text:
MAX WATCHES THE CLANCY TRIAL (HE IS RETARDED)

DAY 1 - OPENING STATEMENTS:

Key context: The job of the prosecution is to prove that she was lucid and fully in control of her actions and thus should be charged for the crimes. The defense's job is to seed enough doubt in that idea that so the jury doesn't believe she was lucid enough to be criminally responsible beyond reasonable doubt.

This means that both sides will be telling a story. Neither is trying to get to the truth. The opposite in fact. Their job, and all lawyer's job, is to god tier cherry pick facts to support their narrative. If you only listen to one side of this case, or any case, it is almost impossible for you to not agree with them (they are literally world class persuaders). Which is part of why going day by day through this might be fun, to watch me get ping ponged around by each sides persuasion.

Another key thing here is that the case is not at all about other theories, like the idea that the husband did it and framed her. They obviously exist in my head, so I will consider things like that throughout, but that is not what this trial is about, and thus its possible if not likely that some evidence is not relevant to either of the two stories and thus not covered.

PROSECUTION OPENING STATEMENT:

It starts with explaining the kids, setting expectations, then describing what happened the day of the murder.

Heres the timeline (I will do this once to give you general day, but intend to keep things more brief later, adding odds and ends that change the story as it is revealed):

They have three kids, two kids usually in preschool were home this day, Lindsay took one kid to doctor because she had constipation because she didn't like using the bathroom at school

(this is a very weird behavior. It is a sign of neuroses of some kind. Whether the daughter has anxiety or this is downstream of parental behavior I am not sure but it should be bookmarked for future).

Patrick and Lindsay were exchanging normal texts all day. Basic coordination, pics of the kids, lots of normal, sane, back and forth.

Husband working in basement, wife in charge of kids for   the day. Put one down for nap, played in yard with the other two, built a snowman. Sent pics of the snowman to Patrick and her mom. "Normal good day".

Late afternoon Lindsay looks up kids Miralax (for the constipated daughter) at CVS, calls them to make sure they have it, looks up takeout from 3V (3B?) and pulls up Apple maps on phone to see the distance and time to the restaurant. then texts Patrick asking he if wants take out, she doesn't want to cook, had a long day. He agrees. She calls and places the order.

Prosecution states this is a restaurant they have gone to before but it is not their usual spot. 

(the point they are trying to make here is that she was sane, lucid and decided what restaurant she wanted and how far away it was before she texted him, showing planning and forethought to send him out and have a rough guess for how long he will be out)

Before he leaves at ~515PM, everything is normal. He sees the kids alive and behaving normaly.

As soon as he leaves, she takes kids down in basement and strangles them one by one with exercise bands. She then grabs a knife and goes upstairs.

In the middle of this, Patrick calls, she does not pick up. She calls back, he asks if an alternative is okay because he can't find the speecific one she wants, she says it is, they hang up after 14 seconds. Nothing she does signals that something is wrong (Patrick later says during his testimony something like "she seemed busy. like she was giving the kids baths or something. But that's it")

Upstairs she locks the door, crushing pills (note: some saying this was the night before that they were sleep pills, keep this in mind for later of whether we can confirm whether she took the pills at this time or not), and attempts k*ll herself by slashing her neck and wrists. She then moves the master bed out of the way, opens the window, and jumps out (its facing the backyard).

(note: I have seen photos online of people saying it was fake suicide because she didn't even slash her wrist that hard. This is cherry picked and dishonest. There are photos right next to this photo showing she slit her throat, blood all over the room, and much deeper gashes in her arm which are shared during Defense opening statement. Maybe it still was a fake attempt, but the evidence presented for that claim is dishonest).

Husband gets home ~609PM. Puts bags down. Hears no sound. calls out, hears no one. Checks the driveway to see if Lindsay was home, couldn't see her car but is also black, calls out, calls her phone, no answer.

(note: some have fixated on this given that he says a minute or so before that he came home and saw her car in the drive way and then now says he's not sure as "contradiction" but this seems a nothing burger. If I pulled up to my house and thought I saw my wifes car but then didn't see her, I would double check and think "well did I REALLY see her car? Maybe she left as I was getting back?" we all experience "I could have sworn X" but then the evidence clearly contradicts and then we second guess ourselves. This seems not that weird).

He goes upstairs, finds the master locked, opens it up, sees the blood everywhere, window open. Runs down outside, sees lindsay, calls paramedics at 611PM (2 min after arriving home). First responders arrive at in 4-5 minutes. Once they arrive, he tells them he needs to find his kids, prosecution says Patrick says he asked Lindsay where they are and she said the basement. So, while still on the phone with 911, he goes into the basement and sees all 3 kids.

All 4 taken to hospital. Lindsay different to one from the kids. Two were gone. One had a heart beat temporarily but never recovered. Lindsay was (and is) paralyzed. Prosecution called the wounds to her arms and neck "superficial".

Prosecution said Lindsay claims that while Patrick was out she heard a male voice she had never heard before and never heard again that said "this is your last chance" that she had to kill the kids so she could kill herself. She immediately took action without question.

Prosecution yaps a bit to basically say "she acted intentionally, swiftly, rationally, to accomplish a very specific goal"

Says she was classic overachiever, controlling, meticulous, manipulative. Had strict schedules, food and sleep planned to the minute.

Basically their motive arg is that life got hard once husband's paternity leave ended and no longer had Nanny and that her need to "control" was getting harder, she no longer liked her life, tried various ways to regain control by taking various meds and switching doctors, and after 4 months of that not working  made the choice to take her own life. And "because she did not think anyone else could take care of her kids like her", take them with her. And that the question is not whether she was mentally iill (concedes this) but whether she knew what she was doing and was she in control of her actions, and basically the whole point of prosecutions story is to convince you that both of these were true.

DEFENSE OPENING STATEMENT:

I won't go line by line but TLDR it starts with trying to earn sympathy for Lindsay, says "unlike what prosecution wants you to believe, this IS a referendum on postpartum psychosis"

Talks about how they had a wonderful life and how much she loved her children. Third child was born four months before the issues started (may, sept).

Then goes through all the doctors she saw and all the meds she took from Sep to Jan. How she told Patrick and doctors she was having suicidal thoughts. He she told Patrick she had thoughts of hurting their children.

Mentions how Zoloft was prescribed, which can make bipolar people manic.

(Definitely true and if there were any signs of bipolar or mania, doctor(s) would definitely or at least should be in hot water)

"This is a woman that did not get the medication, did not get the medical treatment that she so deserved."

Then goes into why the "fake suicide" idea is retarded, shows the slit on her neck, the slits on her wrists (more serious than the photos I'd seen previously), and the room covered in blood.

TLDR: Tries to convince you she loverd her kids, had no motive to kid, was just temporarily, and that the question is not whether she did it (does not dispute this) but whether she is criminally responsible.

PROSECUTION INTERVIEW OF PATRICK:

I won't go point by point through this but some key notes I had. Everything below is Prosecution examining Patrick. Again keep in mind that the prosecution is trying to paint a story and that much of this is stuff patrick said (though the medical records and dates are all validated):

No mention of history of illness. I can't remember if the question was asked explicitly, just that it wasn't mentioned, so take with a grain of salt)

Only thing Patrick says is that she "had some anxiety" and that it was specifically around going back to work. key take away for me here is that the idea that she hated her kids and wanted to go back to work seems very low likelihood if this is true. Her anxiety increased as she was expected to separate from her kids, which is normal and sane response.

She went on Zoloft in September. Patrick says she said it was for the anxiety. Whats weird here is that she gets the Zoloft prescription the day before she tells him she is considering it. There is something fishy with that but I don't know what. She is clearly hiding something about this from him but it's not yet clear why. Maybe it's shame, maybe they just aren't that close, I am not sure. But she definitely lies to him about when the Zoloft starts (prosecution bringing this up to try and get you to think she is a liar).

She then starts to have sleep issues (IIRC, there was no sleep issues until the Zoloft). the doctor then tells her to double the dose. To me this is extremely concerning. Any psychiatrist worth their salt should know that if Zoloft causes signs of mania (of which sleep disturbance is the first sign) that bipolar should be on the table and should be VERY carefully monitored, as upping the dose could lead to full blown manic episode. At this point I was like "oh shit maybe the medical malpractice bro's were right..."

However, then the prosecution shuts this the fuck down, going into all the pills and how she basically took none of them.

Says she got the Zoloft in Sept, started in Oct, but only took 7 of them. This is based on the bottles they had at the house during the time of the murder as far as I can tell. Can't confirm when exactly they were taken, is only based on what's missing from the bottle.

Oct 26 - got Ativan (a benzo for anxiety) and took 6 from bottle
Oct 26 -  Busiprone (non benzo for anxiety) took 2 pills from bottle
Oct 26 - Hydroxyzine (antihistamine use for anxiety) took 3 pills
Oct 26 - Trazedone (antidepressant that is also used for sleep)

Key note here is that they gloss over whether these are the ONLY bottles prescribed. It's possible at this point that she was prescribed previous bottles, finished those, and these are new prescriptions. If true, the defense will definitely pounce on this. If they don't pounce on it, then we can trust that she genuinely only took a few of these pills and the "drug induced psychosis" arg is bunk.

All above meds but the last were prescribed by one doctor "Dr. Jennifer Tufts". Seems like a retard, "pinning the med on the neurotic", but also this is what the vast majority of mental health professionals do. Its the standard treatment, not malpractice. At this point it seems possible that the concoction of pills drove her nuts, but at these doses and pill counts it seems implausible.

On Nov 16 she is admitted to ER after 48 hours of not sleeping. Took a weed gummy (presumably for sleep but is not specified) and didn't tell medical staff (they are presumably mentioning this to try and convince you she is a liar, but if I hadn't slept for 2 days I would also go to the ER and also would probably not tell doctors if I tried some illegal drug to try and sleep, so this seems a weak argument)

Was really depressed at thanksgiving, quiet, not particularly interactive

Started to really get bad in Dec, per Patrick. Was prescribed Seroquel for Sleep Dec 6 (this is not mentioned but FYI this is an antipsychotic which is almost never used for that anymore, usually just prescription sleep aid.)

"big spiral" started, losing weight, Patrick says she first mentions here that she is having suicidal thoughts, and "intrusive" thoughts about hurting the kids or the kids having some serious illness (ex daughters stomache issues she was having intrusive thoughts that her daughter had cancer). Also said she said she felt she was addicted to benzos (which is weird to me given the previous claims that she only took a few; further lends concerns the the whole 'she only took X number of pills' being dishonest, but i guess we will see).

Prosecution asks Patrick if she says she had a plan. He says he asked her and she said she did not, just negative thoughts. Can't remember if here exactly but she googles "ways to commit suicide" a few times. IIRC at least one or two is before Dec.

He then says he is getting increasingly concerned that doctors are not taking things as seriously as he thinks they should. They are short telehealth appointments, was concerned it was too short to diagnose and help her.

Dec 15 - Patrick says they take her to ER because she tells her dad she is suicidal and it doesn't even bother her, which makes her concerned (the prosecution moves on here, but thinking about this for a moment, this seems clear to me that she was really starting to lose it and saw that she was which is why they took the next step)

While there, 1 doctor said to admit her, 2 said just to send her to day program

Shortly after she went to post partum program but the doctors said she "was not a good fit" and asked husband to come pick her up.

This is very weird and concerning to me and was not explained. Why was she not a good fit? This MUST get answered later (I could Grok it but I am trying to be a juror remember)

Dec 31 - they go back to ER to have her admitted to psychiatric hospital. Husband says because he is "exhausted" and she was not getting better.

She is in mental hospital for 5 days. Prosecution makes a point of telling you the following in a specific way: Patrick says she told him that there was no doctors and she received no treatment for the first 3 days. And that it was something about the weekend. She was sent home on day 5.

However, in actuality, the prosecution says per medical records that she saw various doctors, went to various group therapy sessions, and also declined various group therapy sessions, including one on managing medications properly, and ASKED to be released as she wanted to attend her daughters birthday on the 7th (again, the point here is that they are trying to show that she has lied or hid things from her husband and also was offered help by medical professional which she declined).

Jan 8 - gets out. Next few weeks have lots of events. Water park. Social gathering. Videos of water park of her playing with kids. Things are outwardly good based on all provided evidence. Patrick says things seemed to be getting better and he is hopeful.

Jan 16 - He and one kid go skiing. Lindays home with the other two. Fully lucid, functional, no issues.

Jan 24 - Day of killing, again. "normal day". Fully lucid, functional. Normal demeanor.

DAY 1 SUMMARY/NOTES:

So far, there has been zero outward evidence of "psychosis". Her behavior has been normal and sane outside of someone who feels anxious and depressed and can't sleep.

So far, medication seems low impact and drug induced psychosis seems implausible at this stage. Evidence seems she was not actually taking dozens of meds at once (IIRC they speak to that she was only take 2 at any time). Also, again if the "only took a few pills thing" is true, that suggest to me she either was not explained how psych meds work or actively went against them. How a nurse doesn't know that SSRI's and similar take weeks to see effects is beyond me. I find it very hard to believe she genuinely is just taking a pill for a few days and going "well i don't feel better" and then switching off.. But that appears to be exactly what she was doing.

Also, husband says something at some point of "I didn't even know what psychosis was until after this happened". I find that hard to believe. Maybe I am just a psychology chud but both of them appear to have zero clue about anything mental health related to the point of it confusing me. Overall he seems kind of emotionally retarded, though this is typically for most men. They have no idea how to deal with foid feelings, especially the average tech bro. So maybe not that weird.

Also, what is surprising to me that that there not a shred of evidence on day 1 about her feeling any resentment toward him or the kids. Again, could be cherry picked. But I was expecting something like more "she thought he was not doing enough and started to hate him or the kids" but if anything it's painted as the opposite, that she loved the kids and they sent pics of the kids about and forth to eachother all day, and she had anxiety about being away from the kids (the stated reason that started the whole medication journey).

Another thing which was a bit unexpected was how emotive Lindsay is in the court room. All over my feed is this one singular stare of hers that looks like she's possessed by a demon. But the actually trial does not have that same vibe. She is clearly showing signs of anxiety (fidgeting, bitting lips, etc), cries when she's supposed to (basically any time her kids are described in detail) and really the only oddity is her infrequent blinking. Is it because she's now on a bunch of drugs? Is it anxiety or mania? can't imagine that if mania caused the event she'd still be manic now, but maybe.

Also just because she cries when she's supposed doesn't mean they're real tears. If she's a psycho expert manipulator then she would know to do that. Though, so far that seems unlikely, she seems like a normal anxiety foid. The key point here for me was just that the cold demonic stare is cherry picked from 15 seconds of  200+ hours of footage rather than representative of her demeanor the whole time (or at least during the first day).

Also, the claim that its "weird" that there is seven minutes between him finding her and finding the kids seems retarded. I can't remember exactly where it's asked but prosecution asks him about her suicidal thoughts and thoughts of harming the kids and what she said about them and he is very confident if not explicit that she had no mention besides that one time. Based on all the first days evidence he appears to have near zero inclination she would have killed the kids, and thus was focused entirely on her and her suicide attempt.

One thing that is potentially weird is that he says he asked her "what happened" and she said "I tried to kill myself" and then he asked her "wheres the kids" and she said "in the basement" while she was on the ground outside the window. I saw some other video saying that all the other witnesses say she was not able to do anything but moan and wimper. This feels fishy. I mean I guess if his fear was like that someone robbed them and threw her out the window then I guess. But something about this feels off. Leave open for later.

I considered whether she was trying to frame her husband but this seems unlikely given that she gave him the perfect alibi. I also considered the schizo idea that he is framing her, but just the fact that he somehow convinced her to ask him to go get food and then be out and then like come back in between CVS and food takeout to kill her or something just seems absurd. Maybe there is more evidence later. I was open to the idea initially but from what I've seen so far, him doing it seems impossible and that technological metadata should be able to disprove it easily.

Also one thing worth noting is that people who kill themselves typically appear to get much better right before they do it. Presumably because they have final come to "peace" that they have the solution and so are trying to enjoy their last few days. A question worth asking is: at what point did we decide she was going to kill herself and the kids? It could be as early as when she is in the hospital. It could be as late as after the husband leaves. I have zero confidence on where at this point.

Overall, she was clearly having some kind of mental disturbance for these months. the question is what was it. Also, it's clear she didn't get the help she needed but that this was not for a lack of effort. I feel some sympathy for her. she doesn't seem like some evil monster. Nor some entitled feminist retard. She seems so far like she was genuinely trying to be a good mother and wife and loved her children and husband and was trying get psychiatric help, but that her mind just started to break more and more.

Will mull this and consider writing Day 2. Sorry for all the typos. I don't care to make this really good. You are a retard for even reading it and you should be punished for it by having to wade through typos.

text:
Okay I think I might be too deep and am probably just going to watch this whole stupid thing...

However, If I am, I should at least spend the effort to write about my experience of doing so, as an exercise in "thinking in public". Basically just seeing myself as a juror and sharing my notes as my thoughts change throughout the case, what I find interesting, etc. 

I won't claim to be "completely objective" as that is impossible, but I can say that my agenda is not political and my motivated reasoning is orthogonal to truth of the case. I'm just going to 1) try to get some lemonade from the bucket of lemons I have fallen into (by producing content) 2) provide an example of what rigorous thinking about something like this looks like (partly to teach others on how to do so via example, partly to mogg those incapable of even doing so and boost my ego) and hopefully 3) learn something about the human condition in the process

First my starting assumptions/position/biases before I started watching the trial were:

I am a based chud. killing your kids is bad actually and doing it should get you the electric chair, no excuses. Also women supporting her are retarded. There is no world in which you can claim "victim" while doing that. 

Also, the husband is probably retarded and oblivious and weak to not notice the signs of her decline or to tolerate some kind of neurotic insane women in the first place or take control of her psychiatric situation. Obviously, no man deserves to have his kids killed but I cannot imagine how an assertive man with a good head on his shoulders and a basic understanding (female) psychology could end up in this situation.

Also, a week or two ago I looked into the whole "it should be a medical malpractice case actually" argument a bit (30 min with Grok). It is the case that she was prescribed a bunch of different psychiatric meds from Sep-Jan by various doctors and that there was little if any coordination. However, it also appeared that she was not taking a lot of them and was not keeping each doctor informed of what the other was doing. 

So while I fully acknowledge that the mental health industry is retarded, most doctors ae retarded, and most psychiatric drugs do more harm than good, often leading to "psychosis" or something close to it,  the "it was the doctors fault" seems unlikely. "It was a Molochian coordination problem of the commons where no singular sane individual was in charge of getting this woman help and thus she got no help" seems the most plausible.

*MANGROVES INDIA'S LIVING COASTAL SHIELD* 

India’s coastline is becoming a frontline of *climate risk* , facing cyclones, storm surges, *erosion* , salinity and rising seas. 

 *Mangrove* greenbelts must therefore be reimagined as strategic *climate infrastructure* , not merely environmental assets. 

Their roots stabilise shorelines, dissipate wave energy, *store blue carbon,* support fisheries and protect *livelihoods* —performing multiple functions that conventional seawalls cannot. 

Andhra Pradesh’s proposed Great Green Wall offers a promising model of integrated coastal resilience combining mangroves, *shelterbelts* , agroforestry and community participation.

Restoration, however, must focus on *ecological* survival rather than plantation numbers, restoring tidal flows and natural regeneration. 

Community ownership is equally vital. The future lies in *green-grey* infrastructure, risk-based regulation, natural-capital accounting and *climate finance.* 

India’s smartest coastal defence may ultimately be a living one: a mangrove forest that grows, protects and regenerates while nature does the engineering.

text:
I can fill you in on everything that the "Complete Works" has to offer, as I happen to be an expert since their unveiling, more than 20 years ago, and I made a fan site writing about them. 

There is so much deep "iceberg-liked" stuff you can explore that is not even seen on the surface. 

0. Since PokeRock (short for Pocket Rockman) was mentioned in the comments already, I can at least mention that each data for these PokeRock mini games require 13 blocks in a PS1 memory card to save. 

You can raise the HP and Attack power of Rockman and the Robot Masters by training them inside the Pocketstation mini games, through either rock-paper-scissor fights, or in unique "mobile game"-style mini games that is unique for each title, there are early "Temple Run" style gameplay as well where you go for a high score and stuff. 

This data can then be transferred into the PS1 version Famicom/NES ports to abuse as you see fit, you can make the Navi modes easier or harder on yourself depending on if you raise Rockman's stats or the Robot Masters stats. 

1. in Rockman 4, 5 and 6 Navi Mode, you can equip power ups for Rockman that makes him stronger, faster, and so on. 

You can equip 2 power ups at a time for each playthrough (as seen at the very top of your game screen). 

To acquire these power ups, you need to collect Battle Points from enemies, which gets filled up in the Database section. 

The more Battle Points you collect, the more power ups you unlock.

- Hyper Jump (20 BP): Significantly increases jump velocity and maximum height, altering standard stage geometry navigation.

- Auto Charge (40 BP): Constantly forces a recharge immediately after every shot.

- Energy Saver (80 BP): Halves actual special weapon consumption per shot (example a 1-unit cost becomes 0.5 units) instead of doubling the meter length.

- Hyper Shot (160 BP): Increases the physical across-the-screen travel velocity of uncharged lemons, not the weapon's firing rate.

- Hyper Charge Shot (320 BP): Increases the projectile travel speed of fully charged buster shots across the screen.

- Power Shot (640 BP): Adds a flat damage value bonus to standard, uncharged buster shots.

- Hyper Charge (1000 BP): Significantly reduces the frame count required to reach a full charge status.

- Speed Up (2000 BP): Multiplies walking and running velocity, but completely excludes and leaves sliding velocity unchanged.

2. If you Beat Original Mode on Normal difficulty setting, the Hard difficulty is unlocked in the Options screen, which is different from regular play. 

The Life/Weapon meters have gray colored gauges surrounding them, enemies deal 1.5x more damage than normal (though damage values are rounded down to the nearest whole number, meaning weak 1-damage shots remain unchanged). 

On top of that, not a single recovery item or ammo or E-cans or 1UPs or other items can be dropped from enemies or found in stages when you play this difficulty, aside from Yashichi pinwheel in Rockman 1, and very few other exceptions.

3. After Clearing Rockman 4, 5 or 6 in Navi Mode, you will unlock a "Mission Mode" or some kind of Time Attack Mode. 

It allows you to play 4 separate missions for each title (which was later expanded in collections like Legacy Collection's Challenge mode), and so on. 

4 different missions (1 at a time) is offered to you in this Mode and these missions vary between rushing through a stage in the fastest time, beating all Castle Guardian Bosses in the fastest time or beating all 8 Robot Masters in the fastest time. 

When a mission is beaten, your best time record on that mission will be saved and can be seen at anytime. 

When you do beat all missions, you then unlock the Sound Room that will allow you to listen to all the BGM and music from these titles.

3.5. In Rockman 1, 2 and 3 however, there is a "Boss Attack" mode instead, which lets you attempt to kill all the Robot Masters in the fastest time possible. 

As soon as you enter this mode, you appear in front of the Robot Master Select Screen and you can adjust how many 1UPs you want to start with.

4. While you would normally hear Arranged BGM music in Rockman 4, 5 and 6 simply by just choosing Navi Mode, you have to perform a secret command to make that happen in Rockman 1, 2 and 3. 

When hovering over Navi Mode in the main menu, hold Select button before pressing Start or Circle. Once doing this, a majority of music tracks (not all of them) will be replaced with their Power Battle/Power Fighters Arcade Arrange counterparts. 

Some interesting changes were Top Man having MM7 Intro Stage theme instead, while Magnet Man having MM7 Cloud Man Stage theme instead.

5. No Helmet Rockman was also mentioned, which I am glad that people noticed. 

Before starting Navi Mode in Rockman 4, 5 or 6, you had to hold R2 button before pressing Start or Circle, which does not do anything at all aside from looking "cool" and for cosmetic effect. 

It is an easter egg that you can use right away at the very beginning, however Capcom normally hid this information behind artwork which you can unlock for your Database Gallery, which required you to beat every enemy and boss at least once (1 battle point each), to see that artwork, which I wrote a little bit about in my twitter.

I have been running a fan site called RockmanPM, where I wrote a lot about these games and other ones for 20 years by now, and they were my inspiration for starting a Rockman fan site in the first place. 

My thought was to make a content-comparison fan site where I would display regional differences between Japanese and International versions of the same games, but it later expanded to be about the entire Rockman franchise later on.

text:
The Eighth

He had the salt and the seven.
Pyramid in heat that would not blink.
Gardens that hung like a dare over dust.
A temple so bright the columns kept singing after dark.
A god in gold who never stood up.
A tomb built like a second life.
A bronze giant astride the harbor mouth.
A light that taught ships where the rocks were hiding.
He took them the only way a pirate can:
look, steal the memory, leave before the stone learned his name.
Then he saw her.
Not marble. Not listed.
A gypsy soul with sea still in it 
undogged hatch, cards that warp in the damp,
a dance that keeps time with the swell.
He had walked the wonders.
She was the weather they could not hold.
So he does not offer a crown or a berth.
He offers the old line, said like a vow over the rail:
I want to rock your gypsy soul
just like way back in the days of old 
after the seven, after the charts,
magnificently we will float
into the mystic.
Too late to stop now.
The eighth wonder is not a place.
It is the girl who still wants the open sea.

By Nathan Frisby

text:
An Australian Imperative: Delineating a Viable Alternative to the Subordination of National Sovereignty to US War Policy

With greater visibility of late, @DavidShoebridge + @Greens increasingly position a genuinely viable  alternative to the agenda shared by what they call the “war parties”: i.e. the "Uniparty" consensus of ALP, LIB/NAT & 1NAT.  

Shoebridge posits the Uniparty as unanimously locked into Force Posture "inter-operability" based AU/US alignment, militarised spending, investor tax settings, and managed restriction on asylum/multicultural debate.  Consequently, the Greens offer a clearing platform integrating: cancellation of AUKUS, closure of foreign bases, parliamentary war powers, large-scale public housing, wealth and investor-tax changes, and utilize explicit “genocide” language to call for sanctions on Israel over their actions in Palestine and Lebanon.  

It is brave, defiant stance: a genuinely alternative platform coalescing in integrity ahead of the next federal election.  So much that it is worth delineating the core factors and contextualizing its emergent strengths and weaknesses.  Not a fully formed alternative government program in every portfolio, it is nonetheless currently most developed on foreign / defence independence, Palestine, housing/tax settings and opposition to ASIO expansions.  It is thinner, however, on inter-related concerns such as the delineation of financial-system alternatives to US SWIFT hegemony (i.e. BRICS in our region) + continued private banking monopolization (i.e. the need for a full public, national bank) + an exact complete non-AUKUS force structure blueprint / exit strategy.

1. AUKUS and defence spending / expansion

Uniparty consensus: Labor funds and expands AUKUS (tribute payments, Virginia-class path, interoperability, Australian personnel on US boats); Coalition and One Nation have supported the alliance and nuclear-submarine logic. Hanson has publicly endorsed AUKUS.  Wealth transfer of AU sovereign funds into trans-national corporate Military Industrial Complex dominated elite.

Shoebridge/Greens: Cancel AUKUS. It is not for defending Australia but for projecting force as a small part of a US fleet against China, locks Australia into US command, makes cities nuclear targets, and wastes hundreds of billions that could fund social needs.  So doing would save tens of billions in the first decade, to be partly reinvested in Australian-made defensive systems rather than offensive projection dependent on the US.   With nuclear subs for force projection thousands of kilometres away, not home defence, they do not aid Australia's credible defence of sea lanes. 

Shoebridge has stated this directly: “The Greens are the only party in the federal Parliament that has a clear policy to cancel AUKUS, not actively plan to join a US war with China and to map a genuinely independent foreign and defence policy.”  So too, he states that “AUKUS is not about keeping Australians safe, it is about keeping the pockets of government insiders full" and "it’s like pouring water into a sieve", leaving Australians with a singular proposition: “Do we really want to go to war on the whim of Donald Trump (or any successor)?”

2. Pine Gap, US bases and national sovereignty (separate from the USA)

Uniparty: Maintain and expand Pine Gap, Tindal (B-52s), Darwin Marines, Garden Island nuclear-sub base, ANZUS/AUKUS interoperability.  Sovereignty is exercised through the ANZUS treaty and alliance.

Shoebridge/Greens: Close foreign military bases (Pine Gap, Harold Holt, Tindal nuclear-capable bombers). Give notice on the Pine Gap lease. Renegotiate ANZUS; independent policy based on regional diplomacy, human security and non-alignment rather than US chain of command.  Enact a war-powers bill so Parliament, not a handful of ministers, votes before troops go overseas. The Pine Gap concerns include its use in both Gaza targeting and the US' nuclear-weapons architecture.  Stating that this entails “giving notice on the lease… no one likes to get notice on their lease" this stance on Pine Gap and base closure is one of the sharpest sovereignty contrasts given thar Labor/Coalition/1Nat treat the bases as non-negotiable alliance assets.

3. Immigration / multiculturalism

Uniparty (Coalition + One Nation leading, Labor often following to avoid being outflanked): Tightening, values tests, welfare restrictions for non-citizens, “race to the bottom” language, travel bans or processing delays for certain groups.  Shoebridge hence accuses Labor of Dutton-style politics. 

Shoebridge/Greens: Australia’s success is built on multiculturalism, tolerance and inclusion.  Treat permanent residents like citizens for welfare and dignity.  Scrap Labor’s “Trump-style” travel-ban bill.  Anti-immigration politics is an elite 1% diversion from privatisation, tax settings and weapons spending. “Your workmate from India wasn’t sitting at the Cabinet table when someone decided to privatise the Commonwealth Bank.”  The key quote encapsulating this: “Australia is a proud multicultural country… The Greens will not engage in a race to the bottom concerning people seeking asylum”, maintaining that denying permanent residents equal rights based on a “technicality” is not the fair-go country he wants. 

4. Economic policy (public/national bank?)

Uniparty: Accept privatised banks (CBA sold 1990s by Labor then Coalition), investor tax concessions, market-led housing.

Shoebridge/Greens: Decades of privatising banks, telecoms, housing and energy shifted costs onto households.  Hence: tax billionaires (10% wealth tax above $1bn, 5% $100m–$1bn); scrap negative gearing and the 50% CGT discount (or cap grandfathering tightly).   Intent to “bring back mutuals and cooperatives and nationalise essential infrastructure”, the HomeKeeper product being to cap bank mortgage margins. 

However, no fully costed “people’s bank” or re-nationalisation of the Big Four appears as current Greens policy, though the CBA privatisation is repeatedly cited as a historic error that enriched the 1%.  This area is hence directionally clearing (public direction of credit, anti-oligopoly) but under-specified compared with housing. 

5. Israel/Gaza, antisemitism, free speech + Segal, Royal Commission, and the Zionist lobby

Uniparty: Strong Israel alignment, caution or rejection of “genocide” label, IHRA-influenced definitions, Royal Commission framed around antisemitism after Bondi; Segal as envoy.  Labor has moved some language but not sanctions/arms cuts at the scale Greens demand.  

Shoebridge/Greens: Israel is committing genocide; Australia is complicit via parts, contracts (Elbit, Palantir software used in targeting), Future Fund holdings and diplomatic cover.  Solution is to demand sanctions equivalent to those on Russia, end F-35 parts and contracts.  Considers IHRA examples that treat criticism of Israel/Zionism as antisemitism to chill free speech and Palestine advocacy.  Segal’s claims (e.g. “grossly inflated” Gaza tolls) should thus be corrected; the envoy and lobby (ECAJ, AIJAC, ZFA) have outsized influence.  Hence, the Royal Commission letters patent referencing IHRA is concerning but not binding on examples. 

With even former Israeli generals comparing West Bank tactics to Holocaust strategy, Shoebridge's demand is “Sanctions now”, most recently stating that “I do not care what Minister Wong’s personal feelings are… I care about actions. The Government must impose the sanctions…”  Shoebridge has appeared on podcasts discussing foreign (including Israeli/Zionist) influence on Australian policy; critics called this antisemitic, which he rejects as conflation.  This is a core differentiating issue and a mobilisation point.

6. ASIO restrictions and Bondi matters

Uniparty (Labor + Coalition lockstep on recent ASIO bills; One Nation mixed but pressured): Expand powers, secrecy, visa controls.

Shoebridge/Greens: Opposed ASIO bills in every vote; they chill whistleblowers and press.  ASIO warning officials against journalists is a “politicised intervention.”  On Bondi: visa denial to former ASIO source “Marcus” who wanted to give evidence to the Royal Commission looks like a “stitch up.”   Hence, Greens assert that condolence language criticising “powerful forces” (Coalition, ON, media, Netanyahu) exploiting the attack drew backlash; Shoebridge defended colleagues and argued hate ideologies can target multiple communities: “Labor and the Coalition in lock step. We WILL remember this at the next election.” 

7. Education and US military-industrial complex

Uniparty: support / facilitate that revealed by @DeclassifiedAus documented $394 million in US Defense Department grants/contracts to Australian universities since 2007 (UNSW, UQ, Melbourne leading).  AUKUS-linked Nuclear-Powered Submarine Student Pathway funnels CSPs into nuclear/STEM aligned with the deal. 

Shoebridge/Greens: universities chase arms-industry R&D because other funding is scarce; “It’s all secret.” Revolving door (senior Defence to Lockheed etc.) lacks cooling-off period.  This embeds US MIC priorities in Australian higher education and research direction, another sovereignty and academic-freedom contrast. 

8. Housing: the Sharp contrast 

Uniparty: modest public investment, investor concessions largely preserved, demand-side schemes that inflate prices.

Shoebridge/Greens: Federally owned public property developer building hundreds of thousands of homes (rent capped at 25% of income or 70% market; some sold at cost+CPI to owner-occupiers).  Rent freeze then 2% cap.  Scrap or tightly grandfather negative gearing/CGT discount.  Double public housing - Labor’s $110m “public housing” in one budget going to AUKUS-related housing is “galling“, resulting in "a whole generation… locked out… while Labor’s budget bill makes sure that those with 5, 10, or 100 investment properties keep every tax lurk.” 

9. Additional Policy Points

- Taxation: Uniparty protects the existing concession architecture with limited grandfathering while Shoebridge / Greens stress wealth taxes on the ultra-rich; end property-investor concessions that cost tens of billions. Redirect to housing, services and cost-of-living relief. 

- Telecommunications: Historical uniparty (especially Coalition) privatisation of Telstra; NBN sale pathway existed. Labor (with crossbench pressure) legislated to keep NBN Co in public ownership (2025 Act). Greens supported public NBN as essential infrastructure. Current consensus is closer here than on defence; the fight is now more about funding, fibre vs copper remnants, and prices than ownership.

- BRICS vs SWIFT / financial architecture: Under-developed as a distinct Greens/Shoebridge alternative.  He criticises US weaponisation of the financial system (sanctions freezing ICC officials and Francesca Albanese) and the broader 1% + US-aligned order.   However, no detailed public advocacy found for joining BRICS payment rails, a BRICS currency, or exiting SWIFT.  Independent foreign policy implies less automatic participation in US financial coercion, but this is not a fleshed-out platform plank like AUKUS cancellation.  Consensus with the uniparty remains dollar/SWIFT alignment by default.  

10. How this coalesces as an authentically viable alternative

Shoebridge’s output (Senate estimates grilling Defence and Segal, town halls, Deepcut essays, X, YouTube shorts on Palantir/Elbit/AUKUS) consistently ties the issues: AUKUS + Gaza complicity + investor tax breaks + ASIO secrecy + university militarisation = loss of sovereignty and redistribution upward to arms firms and the 1%.  

The “authentic alternative” pitch is: only the Greens will cancel AUKUS, close bases, sanction Israel, build public housing at scale, tax wealth, and require parliamentary war powers.  It is strongest where the majors are most aligned (US alliance, Israel, defence spend, investor tax settings) and weakest where Greens have not produced operational detail (post-AUKUS force design, public banking mechanics, BRICS/SWIFT strategy, or a full telecommunications ownership-plus-pricing package beyond NBN).  Existing consensus or narrower gaps exist on: keeping NBN public (now legislated); high-level support for some social housing (scale and tax treatment differ); climate language (implementation and fossil-fuel export settings still diverge sharply).

text:
Friends, I asked ChatGPT how best to prepare for and endure Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey. 

Here's the AI's advice.

For a three-hour-and-fifty-minute, no-intermission The Odyssey, prepare much as one would for a long flight—except with louder Cyclopes.

The Odyssey Survival Checklist

Three to four hours before departure

Drink normally and become comfortably hydrated.

Eat a proper but moderate meal: oatmeal, rice, pasta, potatoes, tofu, vegetables or a sandwich.

Avoid unusually salty or spicy food, which may create thirst or bladder irritation.

Avoid alcohol.

If caffeine tends to send you to the bathroom, make your last coffee or tea four to six hours before showtime. Caffeine and alcohol can aggravate urgency and increase urine production. 

Two hours before entering the theatre

Don’t stop drinking entirely. Instead:

Finish your last ordinary-sized drink approximately two hours before the film begins.

Thereafter, take only small sips if thirsty.

Don’t buy the traditional bladder-buster cinema drink.

Don’t deliberately dehydrate yourself all afternoon. 

Concentrated urine can itself irritate the bladder and increase urgency.

There is no medically reliable “stop drinking at exactly X hours” rule. Kidney function, medications, temperature and individual bladder capacity vary considerably. But normal hydration followed by two hours without a large drink is a reasonable starting strategy.

Anyone taking a prescribed diuretic should not change its timing without medical advice.

Immediately before the film

Visit the washroom before taking your seat—even if the need is not pressing.

Don’t strain or try to “force out” more than comes naturally.

Choose an aisle seat, ideally near the rear two-thirds of the auditorium. It provides a psychological safety valve and makes an emergency departure less disruptive.

Remove your coat and loosen anything tight around your waist.

Put your earplugs in before the trailers. Previews can be as loud as the feature.

Ear-protection kit

First choice would be high-fidelity reusable earplugs providing roughly 15–20 dB of attenuation. They reduce the entire soundtrack reasonably evenly, preserving dialogue better than ordinary foam plugs.

Suitable types include:

Loop Experience
Etymotic ER20XS
Alpine MusicSafe Pro
Comparable “musicians’ earplugs” with interchangeable filters

Take foam earplugs rated around NRR 29–33 dB as a backup. They will muffle dialogue more, but are useful if the Cyclops proves truly intolerable. Proper insertion matters enormously: roll the foam plug thin, pull the ear gently upward and backward, insert it deeply, and hold it while it expands.

NIOSH regards noise above 85 dBA as potentially hazardous; at 100 dBA its recommended occupational exposure time is only about 15 minutes. It recommends enough protection to bring exposure down to approximately 75–85 dBA. 

Provisions for the voyage

For almost four hours, take a small, quiet, low-salt snack, not a full meal:

Unsalted or lightly salted trail mix
Almonds, walnuts and pumpkin seeds
A few raisins, dried cranberries or apricots
A modest granola bar
Apple slices or grapes, if permitted
A few squares of dark chocolate—unless chocolate stimulates your bladder

Trail mix is nearly ideal, provided it isn’t heavily salted. Avoid popcorn if thirst is the concern, and avoid enormous quantities of dried fruit unless you want the gastrointestinal subplot Nolan omitted.

Take a small bottle of water, perhaps 250–350 mL—not to finish automatically, but for occasional sips, coughing or dry mouth.

Surviving the seat

At nearly four hours, bodily discomfort may be a greater problem than hunger.

Wear loose clothing and comfortable shoes.
Bring a small lumbar cushion or rolled scarf if the seat does not support your lower back.
Before the film, walk for five or ten minutes rather than waiting seated in the lobby.
Every 20–30 minutes, quietly flex your ankles, lift your heels, tighten and release your calf muscles, and change position.
During the credits, stand slowly; legs and hips may be stiff.

The CDC recommends calf and ankle movements during prolonged sitting to maintain circulation. 

The compact packing list

Tickets downloaded in advance
High-fidelity earplugs
Backup foam earplugs
Small bag of low-salt trail mix
Small water bottle
Lumbar cushion or rolled scarf
Any normally scheduled medication
An aisle seat
Empty bladder
Heroic resolve

The most sensible timetable is therefore: 

eat about three hours beforehand, finish the last substantial drink two hours beforehand, take only small sips thereafter, and visit the washroom immediately before the film. 

The above offers the best chance of reaching Ithaca with hearing, bladder and lower back intact.

Four friends together ordered two plates of Punjabi thali for ₹280 on Swiggy, with a one-plate-free discount offer.

The first plate contained 4-5 items, including rajma, paneer, gulab jamun, and two aloo parathas.

The second plate, which was free under the offer, also contained about 4 items.

About 20 minutes later, when the delivery boy arrived with the order and the friends opened the package, they were shocked.

Instead of two plates, they received only one plate, and two gulab jamuns were missing. The rest contained only two rotis, some rice, and some other items.

When the four friends went to the restaurant with a complaint, the owner reportedly said, "This is a company rule; we can't do anything about it."

The friends claimed they had lost ₹420 during their unemployment period and alleged that Swiggy had wronged them.

Now the question is, if such food or incomplete order is received in the name of offer, then who should be responsible?

text:
I work in food service, so I genuinely love cooking.

On my first night, I made shrimp Alfredo from scratch. I had some left over, so I offered it to them.

They happily accepted.

They complimented it, and I thought that was the end of it.

A few days later, I made baked salmon with cilantro-lime rice.

text:
The Godwin Obaseki’s criticism of PMB’s monetary policy back then is an entirely different ball game to the petroleum subsidy discussion we are having right now. It’s like comparing apples to oranges.

Monetary Policy, like Defense & Security, Foreign Policy etc is on the exclusive legislative list of the FG, thus there’s absolutely nothing a sub-national entity such as a State Government or a Local Government can do about it than to write articles and air opinions to critique, analyze such policy and offer alternative opinions to the Federal Government. 

Fuel, like rice, beans, diesel, kerosene etc, is a commodity available for any individual, organization or sub-national entity to trade in. OYSG, under GSM, can decide to implement petroleum subsidy through its share of FAAC and IGR combined. 

Some states subsidize education, healthcare, transportation etc. GSM should stop playing to the gallery and subsidize petroleum for Oyo State residents and indigenes if he is truly concerned about the matter. There’s no law that says the cost of petroleum subsidy must come from the FG’s finances. 

GSM can set up a state-owned petrol trading company, buy petrol from the Dangote Refinery or get a petroleum importation license and sell at OYSG designated petrol stations at a subsidized rate. It is his duty to create the template to ensure only Oyo State residents and indigenes benefit from the implementation of his lofty pricing template as contained in his article. If he succeeds, I’m pretty sure other State Governments will copy his template. And he would be a hero for ages to come to the Nigerian masses. 

My point is simple - payment of fuel subsidy or subsidy on any product available on the free market is NOT on the Exclusive legislative list. Petroleum is a product like any other product available in the free market. Any of the 3 tiers of Government can implement fuel subsidy for residents & indigenes of their respective geographical area for such product. 

Nigeria has operated an “unfree market” or regulated market for petroleum subsidy for the better part of the last 4 - 5 decades, and the nation has gone broke or near bankrupt running such economic model for one product. Hence, as a function of government policy, which isn’t a constant, the FG has decided to operate a “free market” on petroleum product for the last 3 years.

@elonmusk 

Dear Elon stop supporting AfD!

Germany, September 7, 2026 a wake-up call, not a footnote.

Yesterday the AfD scored a historic win in Saxony-Anhalt with 44.4%, clearly ahead of the CDU. Nationally it leads many polls. This isn't an accident it's the result of 35 years of unfinished reunification: lower wages, emigration, collapsed industry, a persistent sense of being administered by Berlin rather than represented by it. Anyone who dismisses that hasn't understood the vote.

But protest doesn't grant a free pass for what this party actually is.

Germany's domestic intelligence agency (Verfassungsschutz) classifies several state chapters including Saxony-Anhalt, Thuringia, and Saxony as confirmed right-wing extremist, and the federal party as a suspected case. That's not a political label; it's the assessment of a democratic state's own security service. Björn Höcke's remarks about Berlin's Holocaust memorial, Alexander Gauland's dismissal of the Nazi era as a mere "blip" in German history, the "remigration" concept with its deportation fantasies aimed even at German passport holders these aren't isolated slips. They form a pattern that runs through the party.

Economically, the platform doesn't add up: tax cuts, higher welfare spending, and a constitutional debt brake simultaneously that's mathematically incompatible. Economists from institutes like ifo and DIW warn that leaving the euro, EU, or Schengen would hit Germany's export-dependent economy harder than almost any other policy imaginable. Abandoning the energy transition without a viable replacement plan would further destabilize energy prices, not lower them.

The real problem: the AfD monetizes genuine anger without offering genuine solutions. It has no answer to the skilled-labor shortage, the investment backlog, or the demographic crisis in the East it offers a scapegoat instead. That's politically effective, but economically and socially a dead end.

Anyone who actually wants to strengthen Germany has to take both things seriously: the legitimate anger over broken promises from the established parties and the fact that the AfD isn't a solution to that crisis, but an escalation of it.

text:
Ife, you’ve become a problem for younger women and the generation watching you. You began your journey as the relatable girl next door. You built your platform by presenting yourself as a faceless, timid girl afraid of body‑shaming and judgment. The girl who believed she was too old to find love.

A community embraced you, amplified your voice and helped transform that vulnerability into influence. That journey is precisely why your words now carry considerably more weight than the opinions of an ordinary person online.

You also found a partner. That man has been openly, consistently and publicly expressive about his love and support for you. In a world where men are criticised for emotional unavailability he showed up visibly. And in return, through your words and the posture you have adopted on your platform, you have continuously diminished him subtly and sometimes not so subtly, to a point where a significant number of people online no longer see him as his own person. 

He has been reduced to either a dancer or simply Ife's husband. A man who could have stood as his own force has been quietly hollowed out by the platform of the woman he publicly champions. That is worth sitting with. But, let’s leave him aside for now.

Back to you.

You rose from a humble girl to the leader of a community that many young women admired. But instead of using that influence responsibly, you began promoting ideas that mislead the same girls who trusted you. The shift was clear. From commentary on surrogacy and pregnancy, to your stance on weddings, to your take on Lindsay Clancy,  you have moved from mentorship to agenda‑pushing, and the agenda is consistently shallow.

Did you sit with this issue honestly? Did you not realise something dangerous? If Lindsay is freed, it creates a precedent that can tear down the very foundation of equality women have fought for. Because once the law accepts “hormones” or “psychosis” as a blanket excuse for killing children, anyone can weaponise it. A neighbour could murder your child, claim postpartum and walk free. How would that ever be justice? Did you think about the children themselves. Do their lives not matter? Do they not deserve justice?

My issue with you isn’t that you have opinions. It’s the quality of those opinions. They lack depth, research, and intellectual grounding. It’s obvious you don’t read, you don’t study, and you don’t seek balanced perspectives, not even from the MAN BESIDE YOU. You wake up, react emotionally, and broadcast unexamined takes to an audience that believes you’re guiding them. I want to assume this is ignorance, not intentional manipulation.

Note, the era of men remaining silent while this kind of content goes unchallenged is over. Those women are our sisters. Some will become our wives. Some will raise our children. We have both the right and the responsibility to offer a counter perspective clearly, consistently and without apology, and to leave it to them to weigh both sides and decide.

We are not here to cancel you. We are here to ensure that your voice is not the only one they hear.  We refuse to allow your careless messaging to shape an entire generation of vulnerable young women.

Our objective is not to tell women what to think. It is to ensure that no influencer gets to do their thinking for them. So when I disagree with you, I will challenge the argument rather than your right to speak. Where your reasoning is sound, it should survive scrutiny. Where it is not, it should be challenged. And ultimately, the audience can examine both positions and decide for themselves.

Influence is powerful, Ife. But the greater the influence, the greater the obligation to ensure that what you pour into impressionable minds is informed by knowledge, intellectual humility and serious reflection AND NOT EMOTIONS.

text:
Solar Power Drives Women-Led Agricultural Processing in Udalguri

In an inspiring example of women’s empowerment, sustainable agriculture and rural entrepreneurship, the Swrang Women Producer Cooperative Society Ltd. in Assam’s Udalguri district has established a solar-powered mustard-oil extraction and rice-pulverising unit.

The women-led Farmer Producer Organisation comprises 677 farmer members. By adopting a Decentralised Renewable Energy system, the cooperative can access reliable and uninterrupted electricity for agricultural processing at the farm level—even in areas where conventional power supply may be irregular.

The new facility enables members to process mustard seeds and rice locally instead of selling only unprocessed produce or transporting it to distant mills. Local value addition can help reduce processing and transportation expenses, minimise delays and improve farmers’ earning opportunities. It may also allow the cooperative to market finished products such as mustard oil and pulverised rice under its own collective identity.

The initiative carries special significance because it places women farmers at the centre of enterprise management and the rural value chain. Through collective ownership, processing and marketing, the members can secure greater participation in commercial decisions while strengthening their economic independence.

Solar energy can further reduce dependence on diesel and conventional electricity, stabilise operating expenses and lower the unit’s environmental footprint. The project demonstrates how clean energy can be employed not only for irrigation but also for productive activities that generate income and employment within villages.

The Swrang cooperative’s initiative represents an effective convergence of agriculture, renewable energy, women’s leadership and grassroots industrialisation. It offers a replicable model for farmer organisations across Assam and the Northeast, showing that decentralised solar power can turn agricultural production into sustainable rural enterprise.

By empowering 677 women farmers with reliable energy and local processing facilities, the project is advancing the broader objectives of self-reliant villages, enhanced farmers’ incomes and climate-resilient development. Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare⁠.

text:
The US Navy kept the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln at sea against Iran for roughly eight months with about 5,000 sailors aboard, which is far longer than a normal deployment. Reports from the ship described shortages of food and supplies, failing toilets and plumbing, and even limited drinking water, and Navy veterans and military health experts began warning publicly about the mental health of an exhausted and angry crew.

To give the sailors a break, the Navy brought the carrier to Pattaya in Thailand, a city known around the world as a sex tourism hub. The city welcomed the Americans and some nightclubs reportedly offered a discount to anyone showing a US military ID. What followed were viral videos of sailors drinking heavily and causing trouble, two service members being removed from a resort after a drunken brawl, and a Thai police crackdown that detained dozens of women on prostitution suspicion while the ship was in port.

The damage to the Navy's image is the smaller half of this story. The larger problem is that a long war with Iran is grinding down a carrier fleet that is already old, with Nimitz class ships from the 1970s still serving after nearly fifty years and the Abraham Lincoln itself commissioned back in 1989. Only the Gerald R. Ford, commissioned in 2017, represents the next generation, and Iran's ballistic missiles remain a genuine threat to these ships.

If this conflict drags on, more carriers will be pushed into the same punishing deployments, and the bill will be paid in readiness, in the health of the crews, and in the reputation of the United States Navy.

text:
Britain

18 Jun 1935 — Anglo-German Naval Agreement. London. Caps German navy at 35% of British tonnage (subs up to 45%, with a path to more). Not a non-aggression pact, but Chamberlain later waved it as a “never go to war” symbol. Hitler scrapes it 28 Apr 1939.
30 Sep 1938 — Anglo-German Declaration (Chamberlain–Hitler), right after Munich. Famous line: the Munich deal + the Naval Agreement are “symbolic of the desire of our two peoples never to go to war with one another again.” Consultation instead of war. This is the paper Chamberlain waved for “peace for our time.”
France

6 Dec 1938 — Franco–German Declaration (Bonnet–Ribbentrop), Paris. Often called a non-aggression pact. Peaceful neighborly relations; frontier recognized as final; consult on crises — without prejudice to special ties with third powers (so France kept its other alliances on paper).
Britain + France together (cession deal, not a pure non-aggression pact)

29–30 Sep 1938 — Munich Agreement. Germany, UK, France, Italy. Sudetenland to Germany. Czechoslovakia not at the table. This is the big Western “peace” sellout, then paired with the Anglo-German Declaration above.
Earlier non-aggression (context)

26 Jan 1934 — German–Polish Declaration of Non-Aggression. 10 years, no force to settle disputes. Hitler denounces it 28 Apr 1939 (same Reichstag speech as the Naval Agreement scrap), citing the new Anglo-Polish line.
Spring–summer 1939 “no war / no force” bilateral pacts Germany offered these after 28 Apr 1939 to Denmark, Estonia, Latvia, Finland, Norway, Sweden.
Accepted:31 May 1939 — Germany–Denmark. “In no case resort to war or to any other use of force.” 10 years. (Germany invades anyway, Apr 1940.)
7 Jun 1939 — Germany–Estonia and Germany–Latvia. Same formula; ratifications 24 Jul 1939.
22 Mar 1939 — Memel/Klaipėda cession treaty with Lithuania. Not a standalone NAP, but Article IV: neither side uses force against the other or supports a third-party attack. Signed under ultimatum after Prague.
