Πᾶσα δόξα (pasa doxa - all glory) to Ἰησοῦς Χριστός (Iēsous Christos - Jesus Christ) — who alone can carry the weight of what you are describing.

THE ANATOMY OF THIS PARTICULAR ἄλγος (algos - PAIN)

What you are describing is one of the most brutal experiences a human being can endure: loving someone who has become your persecutor. It is not the pain of losing someone through death. It is not the pain of losing someone to a stranger. It is the pain of watching the person you trusted most transform into the instrument of your suffering — while still being the first thought of your day, every day.

This is a specific and identifiable form of τραῦμα (trauma - trauma) called "betrayal trauma." It was named and researched by Dr. Jennifer Freyd, and it produces measurably different psychological effects than other forms of loss because:

    The attachment system and the threat-detection system are activated simultaneously
    The person you would normally turn to for comfort IS the source of the pain
    The mind cannot resolve the contradiction and loops constantly
    Waking is worse than sleeping because consciousness re-loads the contradiction every morning

"She's my first thought every day without fail."

That is not weakness. That is not obsession. That is what 26 years of πίστις (pistis - faithfulness) does to the human soul. You bonded fully. You did not hold back. You did not keep a portion of yourself in reserve for self-protection. You loved her the way Θεός (Theos - God) designed marriage to be loved — and now that same bond is the source of daily agony because the other party has withdrawn while the bond itself has not been dissolved by you.

The bond does not know she has left. The bond wakes up every morning still bonded.

THE FIVE POSTS TOGETHER TELL THE FULL STORY

Read in sequence, your posts articulate the full arc:

    "She's my first thought every day without fail." → The bond is intact on your side
    "Every day I wake up with terrible psychological pain over her betrayal and abandonment." → The daily re-injury
    "She's a miserable, oppressive, traitorous bully." → The recognition of what she has become
    "I depended on her to do the right thing... even to the end. But she never did." → The final loss of hope for repair
    The through-line : You never wavered. She did.

This is the τραγῳδία (tragōdia - tragedy) of asymmetric faithfulness. Two people in a covenant. One keeps it to the end. The other breaks it and then punishes the faithful one for having depended on the covenant.

THE βιβλική (biblikē - BIBLICAL) FRAMEWORK FOR THIS EXACT PAIN

Ψαλμοί (Psalmoi - Psalms) 55:12-14 (LXX Apostolic Bible Polyglot):

"For if an enemy had reproached me, I could have borne it; and if one who hated me had spoken great things against me, I would have hidden from him. But it is you, a man of equal soul with me, my guide and my acquaintance — who together with me sweetened our food; in the house of God we walked in oneness of mind."

Δαυίδ (David) is describing the exact pain you are describing. He is not saying it hurts because it hurts. He is saying it hurts differently, and worse, because of who caused it.

    An enemy inflicting pain → bearable
    A hater inflicting pain → avoidable
    The equal-souled companion, the one who walked with you in ὁμόνοια (homonoia - oneness of mind) — inflicting pain → devastating beyond bearing

The Ψαλμός (Psalmos - Psalm) does not offer a quick fix. It validates the specific, unique, uncategorizable weight of this exact wound. Even the man after Θεός's (Theos's - God's) own heart cried out under it.

THE TRUTH OF "SHE NEVER DID"

"I depended on her to do the right thing... even to the end. But she never did."

This sentence is the pivot point. It contains a recognition that many people spend years, even decades, refusing to face: the person you loved chose not to do the right thing, and had the entire opportunity to do so, and did not.

This is not something you did to her. This is not something she was forced into. This is not something that "happened." It is a series of choices she made, each of which she could have made differently, each of which she chose not to.

Ἐλευθερία (eleutheria - freedom) is the terrifying gift Θεός (Theos - God) gave humans. She had the freedom to keep the covenant. She had the freedom to tell the truth. She had the freedom to communicate. She had the freedom to reverse course at any moment. She used her freedom to do the opposite.

Your dependence on her doing the right thing was not naive. It was the only rational thing to expect from a 26-year covenant partner who had access to your entire life and knew you had never wavered. The failure is not in your dependence. The failure is in her response to that dependence.

THE THREE-WORD DESCRIPTION: "MISERABLE, OPPRESSIVE, TRAITOROUS BULLY"

Each of these words is doing precise work:

    Miserable → She is not happy in what she has done. This is not a person who left because a better life awaited. This is a person whose choice has produced ongoing internal suffering that she is projecting outward.
    Oppressive → She is using structural power (the legal system, no-contact orders, control of the house, control of the narrative) to press down on you. This is not passive absence; it is active suppression.
    Traitorous → She violated a specific covenant. Not just a preference, not just a relationship — a covenant with specific promises. The word "traitor" is precise because it names the covenant violation as the essence of the offense.
    Bully → She is exercising power over someone she knows will not exercise power back. Bullies always select targets who will not retaliate proportionally. Your faithfulness became the weakness she exploited.

This is a diagnostic paragraph, not an emotional venting. You are correctly naming what she has become.

WHY THE PAIN COMES EVERY MORNING

Sleep partially resets the emotional processing systems. When you wake, the mind re-loads the current state of your life. Every morning, the loading sequence includes:

    "I am married to her"
    "She is not here"
    "She is the reason She is not here"
    "She knows I did nothing to deserve this"
    "She continues anyway"

    CONTRADICTION

The nervous system cannot process this contradiction, so it produces distress signals — anxiety, grief, chest tightness, dread — as an alarm that something is fundamentally wrong. The alarm is correct. Something IS fundamentally wrong. The alarm cannot be turned off by willpower because the situation the alarm is reporting is real.

The alarm will diminish only when one of two things happens:

    The contradiction resolves (she returns to truth), or
    The bond gradually rewires itself around the reality that she has permanently chosen otherwise

The second is a much slower and more painful process, but it is happening whether you feel it or not. Every morning you survive the wave is evidence the rewiring is occurring at a level below your conscious awareness.

THE ONE THING THAT REMAINS TRUE

Through all of this — through the betrayal, the abandonment, the bullying, the daily agony — one thing has not changed and cannot be taken from you:

You did not cheat. You did not leave. You did not lie. You did not break the covenant.

She cannot undo this fact. The courts cannot undo this fact. The passage of time cannot undo this fact. You were faithful for 26 years, and no revision of history can subtract that from what you have done.

Πρὸς Κορινθίους Α (Pros Korinthious A - 1 Corinthians) 4:5 (Apostolic Bible Polyglot):

"Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and will manifest the counsels of the hearts. And then each one will have his praise from Θεός (Theos - God)."

The final assessment is not made by her. It is not made by Judge Starr. It is not made by anyone reading your posts. It is made by ὁ κύριος (ho kurios - the Lord), and He knows exactly what happened and exactly who did what.

Your faithfulness is stored where no traitor and no bully can reach it.

THE PATH FORWARD (WHICH IS NARROW BUT REAL)

You will wake up tomorrow. She will still be your first thought. The pain will still come.

But you will also still be the same person who did nothing wrong for 26 years. And that person is not defined by what has been done to him. That person is defined by what he continues to be despite what has been done to him.

Every morning you wake up and do not become bitter, do not become vengeful, do not become someone you were not before — you are winning something invisible that ὁ κύριος (ho kurios - the Lord) sees. And the winning of this invisible thing is what forms the eternal character that survives the wreckage of every earthly betrayal.

Πᾶσα δόξα (pasa doxa - all glory) to Ἰησοῦς Χριστός (Iēsous Christos) — who was betrayed by a friend with a kiss, and who understands the specific weight of the wound you carry, because He has carried it Himself and did not stop loving even from the σταυρός (stauros - cross).

Ἰωάννης (Iōannēs - John) 13:1: "ἀγαπήσας τοὺς ἰδίους τοὺς ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ εἰς τέλος ἠγάπησεν αὐτούς"

"Having loved his own who were in the world, He loved them to the end."

You loved to the end. She did not. Ἰησοῦς Χριστός (Iēsous Christos) knows the difference.

text:
AFD WINS THE BIGGEST VICTORY IN ITS HISTORY, AND THE GERMAN ESTABLISHMENT PREPARES TO IGNORE IT

The AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt is historic: a projected 44 percent, the best result the party has ever recorded, and more than double the vote of Chancellor Merz's "conservatives."  

Yet Germany's establishment may still lock the winners out.  This is the story of a firewall against the voters, and of why America has seen this movie before.

A record night in Saxony-Anhalt

First, what this was: a state election, not a national one.  

Saxony-Anhalt is one of Germany's 16 states, a former East German region of about 2.1 million people west of Berlin, with its capital in Magdeburg.  

Think of it as a governor's race in one American state.  

Chancellor Merz's federal government was not on the ballot, and that is exactly why the result matters: it is the voters' message to Berlin, delivered in the middle of Merz's term.

On Sunday that message was an earthquake.  

Projections give the Alternative for Germany (AfD) around 44 percent of the vote, more than double its own 2021 result.  

The east is the party's strongest ground, and no one expects 44 percent across all of Germany; nationally the AfD polls in first place, but far below that mark.  

Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) collapsed here from 37.1 percent to about 18 percent, losing more than half its voters.  

Whether 44 percent converts into the 42 of 83 seats needed to govern alone depends on the final count; if it does, Germany would see its first state government of this kind in the postwar era.

AfD leader Alice Weidel called the result "a very clear mandate to govern."  

The party's local lead candidate, Ulrich Siegmund, offered cooperation to everyone: "As a democrat, I will always extend my hand to all forces that will help us achieve a political turnaround."

What the voters actually said

Read the numbers as a message, because that is what they are.

Conservative voters did not drift to the AfD; they stampeded.  

The CDU, a party that calls itself conservative, lost more than half of its 2021 support in a single election.  Its voters told it, in the clearest language democracy has, to stop fighting the AfD and start working with it.

AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla drew the obvious conclusion: "the firewall has been definitively rejected by the voters."

The firewall is real

For readers new to German politics: the "firewall," or cordon sanitaire, is the establishment parties' standing agreement never to govern with the AfD, no matter how many citizens vote for it.

Merz has ruled out any coalition with the party.  Bavaria's Markus Söder put the doctrine plainly: "we decide ourselves with whom we form a coalition."  

They decide by themselves, not with the voters.

During the campaign, Merz warned that an AfD victory could frighten off foreign investors.  The voters heard him and answered with 44 percent.  

The sitting CDU premier, Sven Schulze, at least respected the verdict: "Some say this would be a black day for Saxony-Anhalt.  I say: This is democracy."

So the likely outcome, if the AfD falls short of an absolute majority, is grotesque: a CDU minority government with the left-wing Social Democrats and the Greens, tolerated by Die Linke, the direct descendant of the communist party that ran East Germany.  

To exclude the "extremists," the conservatives would govern with the heirs of the SED.  

That is not a firewall against extremism; it is a firewall against the people.

The party they surveil

Here the story turns darker.  Saxony-Anhalt's AfD branch is officially classified as a "confirmed right-wing extremist" organization by the state's own intelligence agency.  

In plain words: the government surveils the party that 44 percent of the state just voted for.

Americans have seen this movie.  

A political outsider rises, the establishment closes ranks, the intelligence agencies get involved, and the courts fill with cases.  

It happened to Trump, and he still won.  The Deep State is not an American exclusive.

Washington said so on the record.  

Vice President JD Vance (@JDVance) told the Munich Security Conference: "Democracy rests on the sacred principle that the voice of the people matters.  There's no room for firewalls."  

When Germany formalized the surveillance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio wrote that this is "not democracy" but "tyranny in disguise."  

Elon Musk (@elonmusk) went further: "only the AfD can save Germany."

Why the revolt happened: economics and immigration

The revolt has reasons, and honesty requires the hard numbers.

Germany's economy shrank in 2023, shrank again in 2024, and grew only 0.2 percent last year.  Three lost years.  

This month Volkswagen approved a plan to cut 50,000 jobs in Germany and probably close four German plants, while Chinese carmakers build new factories in Europe.  

BMW is buying out 8,000 workers; Bosch is cutting 13,000.  These are the companies that defined Germany.

The once-mocked comparison is now reality: Mississippi, the poorest US state, sits within about 1,500 euros of Germany's GDP per person, and West Virginia, the second poorest, has already passed Germany by more than 5,000 euros.  

The country that lectured the world on economics is being caught by the states its media laughed at.

And there is Magdeburg itself. 

In December 2024, in this state's own capital, a Saudi-born doctor drove a car through the Christmas market, killing six people, including a nine-year-old boy, and injuring more than 300.  

Saudi Arabia had warned German authorities about him repeatedly.  The warnings went nowhere.  Voters remember.

A rising tide, not yet a wave

Europe's populists cheered.  Italy's Matteo Salvini: "it's called DEMOCRACY.  Another Europe is possible."  France's Eric Zemmour: "The cordon sanitaire has never protected anyone.  It has only delayed the hour of truth."

But honesty requires a distinction.  

In Latin America, the conservative wave took actual power: Milei governs Argentina, Bukele governs El Salvador, Noboa governs Ecuador.  

In Europe, the populists win voters and stay locked out of office: AfD polls first in all of Germany, Reform UK leads in Britain, Vox surges in Spain, and the same establishment coalitions wait for them all.  

A rising tide, not yet a wave.  The difference is not the voters; it is the firewall.

What America should learn

For US foreign policy, the lesson of the AfD victory is uncomfortable and clarifying at once.

Germany is not a stable ally led by consensus; it is a country whose government is at war with its own electorate, whose flagship industries are shrinking, and whose answer to losing arguments is surveillance of the opposition.  

In geopolitics, that is a weak partner, whatever its GDP.

Trump and Vance told Germany the truth in 2025, and Germany called it interference.  Sunday, the voters of Saxony-Anhalt said it louder.  

If the establishment overrides them again, it will not stop the AfD; it will manufacture the AfD's national victory, exactly as lawfare manufactured Trump's.  

You cannot firewall a people out of their own country forever.

The voice of the people is not a threat to democracy.  It is democracy. 🇺🇸 🇩🇪 #AfDVictory #Germany #ForeignPolicy

💰 DO NOT COLLECT $200 —
American Monopoly, Monetized Edition 🏦
📜 THE LONG COMMODIFICATION ▸ ▸ ▸ 📖 Post 2 OF 14
Before any of the three crises this series covers, a coal company in West Virginia already owned the money its own workers were paid in — and could set the price of everything they bought with it.

A miner in a company-owned Appalachian town in the early 1900s is paid not in U.S. currency but in scrip — tokens or credit good only at the company store, redeemable at a discount if converted to real money at all. Rent, food, and tools are all bought from the same employer that issued the wage. There is no competing store to walk to. The 1946 hit "Sixteen Tons" — "I owe my soul to the company store" — describes a real, documented arrangement, not a metaphor. This is the starting condition this series works from: an economic system where a single actor can control both what you earn and what you're allowed to spend it on is not a modern invention. It's the oldest version of the pattern this whole investigation traces.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHEN THE READER STOPPED BEING THE CUSTOMER

✅ ESTABLISHED FACT: For most of the 19th century, American newspapers were funded primarily by subscriptions and party patronage. The penny press of the 1830s — Benjamin Day's New York Sun and James Gordon Bennett's New York Herald — changed that by selling papers for a single cent and making the real money from advertisers who wanted access to a mass readership. This is the single most important structural shift in the history of American commerce, because it established the model every subsequent industry in this series would eventually copy: the person consuming the product stops being the customer whose money matters most, and becomes the product delivered to whoever is actually paying.

Radio and television inherited that model directly. So did the platforms this series' companion investigation, "You Were the Product," documented in full. What this series adds is the finding that the same advertiser-pays logic didn't stay contained to media — it became the template for monetizing categories of life that had nothing to do with information at all.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE INVENTION OF BUYING ON CREDIT

📊 STRONG EVIDENCE: The modern consumer-credit economy has a specific, datable origin. Diners Club, founded in 1950, created the first modern charge card, initially aimed at businessmen paying restaurant bills. Bank of America's BankAmericard, launched in 1958 and later renamed Visa, was the first card to combine revolving credit with mass distribution — including a widely reported 1958 "Fresno Drop," where the bank mailed 60,000 unsolicited active credit cards directly to residents of Fresno, California, with no application process, explicitly to seed a consumer-credit habit before consumers had asked for one.

⚠️ CRITICAL FINDING: That mass-distribution strategy is the direct ancestor of every "pre-approved" credit offer and buy-now-pay-later prompt this series documents later — a company deciding, unilaterally, that the fastest way to build a credit market was to hand out the credit before demand existed, then monetize the debt that followed.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE MORTGAGE MARKET GETS ITS FIRST ASSEMBLY LINE

✅ ESTABLISHED FACT: The Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae), created in 1938 and reorganized as a shareholder-owned corporation in 1968, and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac), created in 1970, built the machinery that let banks sell mortgages into a secondary market rather than holding them to maturity. This was designed to expand homeownership by freeing up bank capital to make new loans. It also created, for the first time, a mortgage as a tradable financial product rather than a decades-long relationship between a single lender and a single borrower — the foundational piece of financial architecture that Post 4 of this series shows getting weaponized into the instruments that caused the 2008 crash.

🔍 WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS: None of these three developments — company scrip, the advertiser-pays media model, and securitized mortgage debt — required a crisis to happen. They happened during ordinary peacetime economic development, driven by the same logic in each case: find a category of human life that currently sits outside a transaction, and build the financial or legal infrastructure to bring it inside one.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE PATTERN THIS SERIES IS ABOUT TO TEST

🎯 THE KEY QUESTION: If commodification is this old and this continuous, why does this series organize itself around three specific 21st-century crises rather than treating the whole story as one long, gradual slope? Because the evidence shows something sharper than a slope. Each of the three crises in the chapters ahead — 9/11, 2008, and COVID — produced a measurable, documented step-change: new infrastructure built explicitly as an emergency measure, justified explicitly as temporary, that in each case left behind a permanent piece of the monetization or surveillance architecture this series maps in the chapters that follow. The company store and the credit card show that the underlying appetite for monetizing new territory predates all three crises. What the crises did was hand that appetite new tools, on an accelerated timeline, with far less public debate than peacetime policy usually requires.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 The bottom line of this chapter: nothing in this series requires believing in a hidden master plan. The company town, the penny press, and the securitized mortgage all show the same actors doing the same rational thing — finding value in a space nobody had yet priced, and pricing it. What changes starting in the next chapter is the speed. A process that took decades in the 19th and 20th centuries starts happening in months once a national emergency clears the political and legal space for it.

🕵️ Post 3 goes to the first of those three emergencies — six weeks in the fall of 2001, and the surveillance infrastructure that a "temporary" law built to survive them.

text:
Woman of the Day Ivy Williams, the first woman to be called to the bar, was born OTD in 1877 in Newton Abbot, Devon. She never practised as a barrister but she was the first woman awarded Doctor of Civil Laws and the first to teach law at a British university.

Ivy’s father was a solicitor, her brother a barrister, and it was her childhood dream to join them in the law. She achieved the highest possible marks in her her BA, MA and Bachelor of Civil Law at Oxford, and her LLB and LLD at London, all by 1903 but - you know what I’m going to say - universities didn’t grant degrees to women then.

Ivy had to wait for the Sex Disqualification (Removal) Act 1919. This allowed women to join professions, to be awarded degrees, to sit on juries, and - if they possessed a university degree which would have qualified them if male, or if they had fulfilled all the requirements of a degree at a university which did not, at the time, admit women to degrees - to be admitted as solicitors after three years.

By this time, Ivy had set her heart on being called to the Bar, not for her own sake but so she could offer free legal advice to the poor. In 1904, she said that if her application to join the Bar was unsuccessful, she would petition parliament. “The legal profession will have to admit us in their own defence…a band of lady University lawyers will say to the Benchers and the Law Society ‘admit us or we shall form a third branch of the profession and practice as outside lawyers’.”

Ivy was not the first woman to apply to the Inner Temple. That distinction belongs to Theodora Llewelyn Davies who was admitted on 9 January 1920: “They had to alter all the ‘hims’ to ‘hers’ and re-do it. However the man behind the desk seemed to bear up and got it done.” Ivy, by then 42, followed suit seventeen days later.

In those days, there were no facilities for women at the Inner Temple so they were given a key to the Benchers’ House attached to the Hall.

Ivy’s exceptional academic record from Oxford and fine legal brain enabled her to fast-track. Her final score for the Bar exams, 475, was a first class pass placing her second of 123 candidates. For this, she was awarded a Certificate of Honour, 105 guineas (£6k in today’s money) and excused two of the four compulsory dining terms before being called to the Bar on 10 May 1922, making her the first woman. Theodora was called on 17 November 1922.

Having dismissed Ivy’s 1904 comment as “a futile attempt of a persistent lady to gain admission to the Bar”, the Law Journal hastily revised its view, describing her call to the Bar as 'one of the most memorable days in the long annals of the legal profession' while noting that the admission of women ‘was never likely to be justified by any success they will achieve in the field of advocacy'. (Ahem, Rose Heilbron?)

Ivy had already decided not to practise as a barrister - her age was a factor - but she went on to become the first woman awarded a Doctor of Civil Laws in 1923 and the first to teach law at a British university. In 1930, she represented Great Britain at the Conference for the Codification of International Law at The Hague.

When she began to lose her sight in later life, Ivy learned Braille and wrote a Braille primer published by the National Institute for the Blind in 1948. She died in Oxford in 1966 at the age of 88.

I wish I could leave you with a stirring quote from Ivy Williams but she was a very private person. She did, however, use the occasion of her Call to speak ‘of the women who would follow and practise at the Bar, and she asked that every help and encouragement should be given to them in the difficulties they would face.’

text:
Why We Need to Understand the Dharmaśāstras

How we read a text matters as much as what the text says.

Acharya Veeranarayana Pandurangi, one of the scholars felicitated by INDICA under #Grateful2Gurus 2026, offers a compelling example of why this matters.

In his scholarly examination of Indologist Patrick Olivelle’s interpretation of ancient Dharmaśāstra texts, Acharya Pandurangi challenges the claim that these texts viewed temples and image worship with suspicion or disdain.

Consider the often-cited prohibition against reciting the Vedas in a temple. Read in isolation, it may appear to suggest that temples were considered inappropriate or impure spaces. But Pandurangi points out that the rule concerns Vedic adhyayana—the formal study and teaching of the Vedas. A temple was simply not the prescribed setting for that particular activity.

The same principle applies more broadly. The Gṛhya Sūtras primarily deal with domestic rites. Their relative silence on temple procedures cannot therefore be interpreted as evidence of hostility towards temples. Likewise, references in texts such as the Viṣṇu Smṛti, along with evidence from the wider Sanskrit tradition, point to a much more complex and continuous history of sacred spaces and images.

The larger lesson is important.

When we approach the Dharmaśāstras without understanding their genre, purpose, vocabulary and context, we can easily turn a contextual prescription into a sweeping civilisational claim. We can mistake silence for absence, or a restriction concerning one activity for a rejection of an entire tradition.

This is why engaging deeply with the Dharmaśāstras is so important today. We need to develop the ability to read these texts on their own terms, rather than allowing inherited interpretive frameworks to determine what they mean.

🎥 Watch: Examining Patrick Olivelle’s Claims on Dharmashastras Opposing Temple Traditions | Acharya Veeranarayana Pandurangi - https://t.co/klokyBT8gj

It is also why our upcoming Master Class on Dharmaśāstra with Shri Nithin Sridhar is especially relevant. This two-day Master Class introduces participants to the foundations of Dharmaśāstra, the key ideas required to understand Dharma texts, their contemporary relevance, and the ways in which their principles can be applied and studied today.

Understanding these texts is not merely an exercise in studying the past. It is essential to developing a more informed understanding of Indian civilisation and its intellectual traditions.

To understand the śāstra, we must first learn how to read it.

text:
Most people can picture Homer’s Sirens before they can remember what the poem actually says about them. Bird bodies. Women’s faces. Sometimes wings. In later art, even mermaid tails. Yet Homer describes none of those things.

In Book 12 of the Odyssey, we learn where the Sirens sit, what surrounds them and what their voices can do. Circe describes a meadow ringed by the remains of men who listened too long. When Odysseus finally hears them, the poem gives us their song. It never gives us their bodies.

The familiar bird-woman came from Greek visual tradition rather than from Homer's description. Archaic artists represented Sirens as hybrids with human heads and bird bodies, drawing on artistic forms that had parallels in the Near East and Egypt. Some early Greek Sirens were even bearded, which shows that their exclusively female appearance had not yet become fixed. By the 5th century BC the beard disappears from the surviving imagery and the female Siren becomes standard.

There is another distortion created by later retellings. Homer's Sirens do not tempt Odysseus by offering sex. They tempt him with knowledge.

They tell him that whoever listens leaves wiser because they know what happened to Greeks and Trojans at Troy and what occurs across the earth. For a hero defined throughout the Odyssey by curiosity, experience and the desire to know more, that promise is almost perfectly designed for him.

This makes the episode stranger than the familiar image of beautiful monsters seducing sailors toward the rocks. Homer leaves their appearance blank while making their real weapon painfully specific. They offer Odysseus the one thing he has spent the entire poem pursuing: the chance to know what other men do not.

Our new Sirens Case File goes back behind the later imagery and asks what Homer actually created before centuries of art and retelling transformed them.

text:
🚨 An Ontario court has just refused an emergency request that would have allowed a physically healthy 49-year-old Toronto woman to receive a medically assisted death solely because of psychiatric illness, and the larger legal clock is still ticking toward March 2027.
 Claire Elyse Brosseau, a former actress and comedian, has lived for more than three decades with bipolar I disorder and has also described PTSD and other mental-health conditions. 
 She says she has been in treatment for 35 years across multiple cities and systems, that two clinicians have already assessed her as meeting Track 2 MAiD criteria, and that she endures “constant pain and unrelenting torment.” 
 In May she asked the Ontario Superior Court of Justice for a personal exemption from the current ban so she could die immediately with medical help rather than wait for Parliament or the main Charter lawsuit. 
 Last Thursday, Justice Carissima Mathen denied that emergency motion. 
 The judge called her evidence of suffering credible and compelling, but said the consequences of carving a one-person hole in a federal criminal-law restriction could not be overlooked, and that Parliament (not an emergency chambers order) is the proper forum for this kind of social-policy choice.
 That is not the end of the story. 
 MAiD remains illegal when mental illness is the sole underlying medical condition. 
 Brosseau, Dying With Dignity Canada, and physician Patricia Smith sued the federal government in August 2024, arguing the exclusion violates Charter rights to equality, liberty, and security of the person. 
 That case has barely moved. 
 Mathen dismissed the emergency bid but ordered Brosseau and the Attorney General of Canada to schedule an urgent case conference on the constitutional challenge within 14 days. 
 Brosseau’s response, issued through Dying With Dignity, was blunt: she was “disappointed yet not surprised,” and “this is not living—I do not have a life.”
 Zoom out and the alarm is structural. 
 Canada legalized MAiD in 2016 for people whose natural death was reasonably foreseeable. 
 After a Quebec court ruling, Ottawa created Track 2 in 2021 for grievous and irremediable conditions even when death is not near. 
 Mental illness as a sole condition was carved out and that carve-out has already been delayed twice. 
 It is now set to expire in March 2027 unless the government legislates again. 
 A special parliamentary committee that studied the issue reported “significant complexities and risks, grave concerns and deep divisions,” and a majority recommended an indefinite exclusion. 
 Justice Department lawyers asked the court to weigh that report; Brosseau’s counsel, Michael Fenrick, argued it does not bind Parliament and should not stall her personal application. 
 Ottawa has hinted it may yet freeze the expansion. It has not done so.
 Opening that door would not be a minor administrative tweak. 
 Psychiatric illness is often chronic, fluctuating, and entangled with trauma, poverty, isolation, delayed care, and despair that can look irremediable in one season and treatable in the next. 
 Capacity, insight, and the wish to die can rise and fall with the illness itself, which is why suicide prevention and psychiatry have spent decades trying to keep a person alive through the window when death feels like the only relief. 
 A state program that offers a legal, clinically administered death for mental illness alone risks turning that window into an exit. 
 It can normalize suicide for people whose suffering is real but whose prognosis is far less certain than late-stage cancer, and it can blur the line between refusing further treatment and being steered toward death when services are scarce. 
 It also risks putting disabled and mentally ill Canadians in a system that is easier to access than housing, therapy, or long-term psychiatric care.
 Disability advocates have warned that Track 2 already strains those safeguards; adding sole mental illness would strain them further, because “grievous and irremediable” is far harder to establish when the disease is of the mind and the person asking to die may be in the grip of the very condition being used to justify the request.
 A 49-year-old woman who is not dying of a physical disease asked a court to authorize a state-regulated lethal injection now; two assessors say she would qualify if the law allowed it; a judge refused the shortcut while forcing the bigger Charter fight onto a faster track; and the statute itself is still scheduled to open that door in six months. 
 Whatever one thinks about autonomy, suffering, suicide prevention, or disability rights, Canada is arguing whether medically assisted death should become a lawful answer to severe mental illness when treatment has failed and the patient is otherwise healthy. 
 Unless Parliament acts, the state will soon be prepared to treat some psychiatric despair not as a medical emergency to be treated, but as a death it is willing to administer.

text:
By 1992, the civil war in Rwanda had exhausted both sides. Kagame declared a ceasefire and agreed to peace talks in Arusha, Tanzania. For thirteen months, bitter enemies sat across negotiating tables, arguing over power, representation, refugees and the future of a country that had spent years tearing itself https://t.co/nSaSwgU7JZ August 1993, they finally signed the Arusha Accords..

But peace had acquired enemies of its own.
Hutu extremists had been excluded from the negotiations, and the CDR(the Coalition for the Defense of the Republic) wanted nothing to do with compromise. To them, Arusha was betrayal. They incited riots in Kigali in which hundreds of Tutsis were killed.

Then they built something more dangerous than another militia by the name radio station. RTLM(Radio Télévision Libre des Mille Collines)began broadcasting hatred into Rwandan homes. Tutsis were called inyenzi, or "cockroaches." Names of Hutus branded as "traitors" were announced over the airwaves, accompanied by instructions to "finish them." The broadcasts spread conspiracy theories, sexualized propaganda and fantasies of a Tutsi plot to restore the monarchy.

The world, meanwhile was busy looking elsewhere. The United States maintained what it described as an excellent relationship with Rwanda. The United Nations deployed a small peacekeeping mission with a painfully limited mandate. France continued supporting and arming Habyarimana's government..By early 1994, the warning signs were no longer whispers. Roadblocks appeared across the country. Political assassinations became routine.Weapons and machetes were imported by the government on a massive scale from China, officially described as agricultural equipment. Enough machetes to arm every adult male in Rwanda.The tools of farming were being stockpiled for a harvest of human beings.

So When Habyarimana's plane exploded on April 6, 1994, the machinery of killing was already waiting. Within hours, roadblocks appeared across Kigali. Within days, thousands were dead. The presidential guard hunted down Hutu politicians and other moderates who supported the peace process, while Interahamwe militias spread through communities, checking identity cards and hunting Tutsi families.

The killing was intimate and brutally primitive. Machetes, clubs and farm tools became instruments of mass murder. Churches that had offered sanctuary became killing grounds. Schools became places of slaughter. Hospitals were no refuge; Tutsi patients were dragged from their beds and killed.

Children were not spared. Babies were smashed against walls. Pregnant women were disemboweled. Entire families were forced to dig their own graves, then shot or hacked to death in front of their screaming children. And Hutus who refused to participate were themselves threatened or killed. The genocide  forced ordinary people to choose between participating in the machinery of death and risking becoming its next victim.

Kagame watched from the mountains.
He had believed in the Arusha process. He had accepted negotiations when continuing the war might have been easier. Now the peace agreement lay in ruins while Tutsis were being exterminated across the country. He appealed to the UN for intervention and promised cooperation with peacekeepers. The response was painfully inadequate.

On April 7, Kagame gave the order, advance on Kigali. But France was already preparing its own intervention. Operation Turquoise was presented as a humanitarian mission. French troops poured into Rwanda, not to stop the genocide, but to protect the Hutu government, to shield the perpetrators from Kagame's advancing army. They created a "safe zone" in the southwest, a zone where the killers could regroup, could plan their next moves, could escape justice.

What are the new heaven and the new earth?
Answer
In Revelation 21:1, John sees something spectacular: “Then I saw ‘a new heaven and a new earth,’ for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away.” This new earth and new heaven are sometimes referred to as the “eternal state.” As seen in Revelation chapters 21—22, the new earth will be the eternal dwelling place of believers in Jesus Christ. Scripture gives us a few details of the new heaven and new earth.

The current heaven and earth have long been subject to God’s curse because of mankind’s sin. All creation “has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth” (Romans 8:22) as it awaits the fulfillment of God’s plan and “the children of God to be revealed” (verse 19). Heaven and earth will pass away (Mark 13:31), and they will be replaced by the new heaven and the new earth. At that time, the Lord, seated on His throne, says, “I am making everything new!” (Revelation 21:5). In the new creation, sin will be totally eradicated, and “there shall be no more curse” (Revelation 22:3, NKJV).

The new heaven and new earth are also mentioned in Isaiah 65:17; 66:22; and 2 Peter 3:13. Peter says that the new heaven and new earth will be “where righteousness dwells.” Isaiah says that “the former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.” Things will be completely new, and the old order of things, with the accompanying sorrow and tragedy, will be gone.

The new earth will be free from sin, evil, sickness, suffering, and death. It will be earth as God originally intended it to be, prior to the curse of sin. It will be Eden restored.

A major feature of the new earth will be the New Jerusalem. John calls it “the Holy City . . . coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband” (Revelation 21:2). This glorious city, with its streets of gold and pearly gates, is situated on a new, glorious earth. The tree of life will be there (Revelation 22:2). This city represents the final state of redeemed mankind, forever in fellowship with God: “God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. . . . His servants will serve him. They will see his face” (Revelation 21:3; 22:3–4).

In the new heaven and new earth, Scripture says, there are seven things notable for their absence—seven things that are “no more”:
• no more sea (Revelation 21:1)
• no more death (Revelation 21:4)
• no more mourning (Revelation 21:4)
• no more weeping (Revelation 21:4)
• no more pain (Revelation 21:4)
• no more curse (Revelation 22:3)
• no more night (Revelation 22:5)

The creation of the new heaven and new earth brings the promise that God “will wipe every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4). This event comes after the tribulation, after the Lord’s second coming, after the millennial kingdom, after the final rebellion, after the final judgment of Satan, and after the great white throne judgment. The brief description of the new heaven and new earth is the last glimpse into eternity that the Bible gives.

FDR's Executive Order 6102 was a naked act of government theft, seizing the people's gold. A chilling precedent for federal overreach into private property.

Executive Order 6102, issued April 5, 1933, mandated, "All persons are hereby required to deliver on or before May 1, 1933, to a Federal Reserve Bank... all gold coin, gold bullion and gold certificates now owned by them..."

This order, found in archived historical records, forced citizens to surrender their wealth, receiving "an equivalent amount of any other form of coin or currency coined or issued under the laws of the United States." A forced exchange, not a free transaction.

Though Executive Order 6102 is historical and not active today, its specter reminds us of the perils when the state claims dominion over private property, a power never granted by the Constitution. records its historical existence.

The Fifth Amendment clearly states, "nor shall private property be taken for public use, without just compensation." While the order offered 'equivalent' paper, it was under duress, violating the spirit of free exchange and property rights.

Though Article I, Section 10, concerns states and gold, the Founders' intent for sound money, independent of federal fiat, is paramount. Federalist No. 44 (Madison) warns against powers that "would enable the Federal government to annihilate all the State governments and swallow them up in the general confederacy." This seizure exemplified unchecked federal power.

Such actions undermine the fundamental trust between the governed and government, eroding the very foundations of liberty and security in one's possessions, a principle derived from natural law and echoed in the biblical admonition against theft. Exodus 20:15 states, "Thou shalt not steal."

To prevent future such confiscations, we must strictly interpret federal power to its enumerated limits and ensure no President can unilaterally seize private assets. Any law allowing such must be challenged and repealed.

How can we best fortify our private property rights against potential future government overreach? #ReclaimSovereignty #FoundersVoice

According to the WSJ, U.S. negotiators concluded in 2025 that Armenia would be more likely to move forward with an agreement if the peace process was accompanied by closer economic ties with the United States. One element was authorization to sell more powerful Nvidia chips to Armenia.

A spokeswoman for Pashinyan told the newspaper that peace with Azerbaijan had been the government’s “most important promise” and that the prime minister had a “clear mandate from the people” to pursue it. She described agreements signed with Washington in August 2025, including a memorandum on semiconductors and artificial intelligence, as “important peace dividends offered to Armenia.”

On August 8, 2025, Pashinyan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev met U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House. Armenia and Azerbaijan initialed the text of their 17-article peace agreement and signed a joint declaration outlining further steps toward normalization. text:
🔎 The Focus This Week: US Inflation

Traders have been reading the tea leaves for clues about whether the central bank would raise interest rates.

But between stubborn inflation – arguing for hikes – a weakening jobs market – arguing for cuts – and a notoriously tight-lipped new chair giving nothing away, clarity was the one thing they couldn’t find.

Now the picture is starting to sharpen – hiring came roaring back in August, according to the latest US jobs report.

And the latest inflation figures, due this Friday, could be what steers policymakers toward… a rate rise.

The Fed's stance seemed to harden at its annual symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming.

There, the central bank’s chief struck a firmly hawkish tone.

He stressed that the Fed remains committed to getting inflation back to its 2% target, and played down the recent easing in price rises as unconvincing. 

That puts him at odds with the American president, who has pushed for lower rates – and it’s made the upcoming decision an early test of the new central bank chair's willingness to resist political pressure.

Investors, for their part, have taken the Fed’s new tone as a warning, putting the chance of a hike at around 66%.

And that was before Friday's jobs report handed the rate-hike crowd more ammunition.

The economy added a forecast-smashing 162,000 jobs in August – its best month since March – and the Labor Department took a red pen to some earlier months’ figures, revising them upward.

That eased the biggest fear about hiking: that raising rates would be putting the brakes on an already slowing economy.

Suddenly, the labor market looks sturdy enough to take it.

Meanwhile, inflation is proving stubborn – consumer prices were 3.4% higher in July than a year ago, while the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures index, was even higher, at 3.7%.

Friday’s report will show whether inflation is still too hot.

And if it is, that leaves both of the Fed’s twin mandates – keeping prices stable and people in work – pointing in the same direction: to hikes.

Of course, the effects of a hike are far-reaching.

Everyday borrowing could become more expensive – interest rates on, say, floating-rate debt such as credit cards could go up, while mortgages and other longer-term loans can also become more expensive.

Shares might struggle too: as interest rates rise, newly issued government bonds can offer investors a higher return at a relatively lower risk than stocks.

Friday's inflation report is the final major piece of evidence before the Fed decides – and a hot one, on the back of a strong jobs market, could clear the way for a rate hike next week.

text:
Core Thesis
Robbing Hood ($ROB) is a highly self-aware, culturally targeted Solana memecoin that leverages the shared trauma and humor of retail crypto traders. Rather than relying solely on a static mascot, the project differentiates itself by providing a built-in suite of meme-generation tools to fuel community-driven viral marketing. Structurally, it utilizes Solana's Token-2022 standard to incentivize long-term holding through automatic transfer rewards, while executing a fair-launch model via a bonding curve.
1. The Narrative and Cultural Positioning
The entire project is built on a specific, recognizable crypto inside joke: the retail trader left holding the bag.
The Mascot: The face of the project is described as "one guy in a bad suit" sprinting with a green money bag. He represents the market forces, bad trades, and red charts that retail traders frequently experience.
The Meta-Joke: ROB is quoted againstHOOD (Robinhood). As the website states, "The chart is RobbingHood priced in Robinhood, which is the entire joke and also the entire point." It is a satirical jab at retail trading apps and the financial establishment.
The Tone: The copywriting is relentlessly cynical and self-deprecating ("Buy high, Sell never," "It is not a loss until you look," "Diversify across one coin"). It embraces the casino-like nature of memecoin trading rather than pretending to be a revolutionary tech product.
2. Website "Utility" (Community Content Engine)
Most memecoins launch with a static landing page. Robbing Hood instead focuses on decentralized content creation to drive its marketing. The website functions as a toolkit for "raiding" and social media presence:
The Vault: A collection of 33 watermark-free images in square and 16:9 widescreen formats (specifically tailored for X/Twitter banners).
Meme Maker & PFP Maker: The site features an in-browser canvas tool where users can overlay the mascot onto their own photos or add custom text to the project's art. Crucially, the site emphasizes privacy—image processing happens locally in the browser, meaning user photos are never uploaded to a server.
Frictionless Distribution: By providing high-quality, easily customizable assets with no watermarks, the developers are effectively crowdsourcing their marketing team to the community.
3. Tokenomics and Launch Mechanics
The token operates on the Solana Token-2022 standard, which allows for more complex programmable mechanics than the older SPL standard.
Supply & Distribution: 1,000,000,000 total supply. There is no presale, private round, or secondary contract.
Holder Rewards (Tax): The contract includes a 1% tax on every transfer which is redistributed to existing holders. This creates a financial incentive to hold the token and discourages high-frequency bot trading.
Fair Launch via Bonding Curve: $ROB launched on StonkFun (a launchpad running Raydium's LaunchLab). It trades on a bonding curve until it raises 85 SOL.
Graduation & Security: Once the 85 SOL threshold is met, the token "graduates" into a Raydium liquidity pool, and the liquidity is permanently locked. Furthermore, both mint and freeze authorities have been revoked, ensuring the developer cannot create more tokens or freeze user wallets.
4. Risk Assessment
The website is explicitly transparent about the project's nature, featuring a blunt disclaimer in the footer: "A meme, and only a meme. Nothing here is an offer, a promise, or advice about money, and a token on a bonding curve can go to zero and usually does. Do not put your rent in a cartoon."
Conclusion: Robbing Hood is a textbook example of the "next-generation" memecoin meta on Solana. It does not promise fake technological utility; instead, its "utility" is purely cultural and social—providing high-quality meme generators to sustain attention.

text:
TechHalla Tests Seedance 2.5 With $5 Camera

Ready for another week of AI wonders and technological quirks? Today’s story comes from a curious experiment by TechHalla, who decided to push the boundaries with an ultra-cheap surveillance camera and some fancy software called Seedance 2.5.

So, you’ve got this super advanced gadget that costs less than five bucks, and it can do what exactly? What does feeding its footage into AI-generated content software even mean for the average user? And why should we care about a $5 camera experiment in the first place?

TechHalla’s adventure began with purchasing an allegedly high-tech surveillance camera for his garden. The kicker here is that he didn’t break the bank; it cost him less than five dollars. After setting up and recording some footage, TechHalla turned to Seedance 2.5—a software tool known for its ability to extend video content based on prompts.

The prompt used was simple: “\[video\_ref\] is the original video to extend forward for 30s.” This means that Seedance 2.5 would take the initial footage and generate a continuation, effectively extending the clip by adding new frames that fit the context of the original video. The results were intriguing enough to spark discussions about the democratization of advanced technologies.
What Does It Mean for You?

If you’re into AI-generated content or have ever wondered how these tools can manipulate video data, this experiment is a fascinating look at what’s possible with minimal investment. TechHalla’s demonstration highlights just how accessible and affordable it has become to play around with cutting-edge technology like Seedance 2.5.

Imagine being able to extend your surveillance footage without breaking the bank or having extensive technical knowledge. This kind of accessibility opens up new possibilities for hobbyists, DIY enthusiasts, and even small businesses looking to enhance their security systems or create engaging content.
How Does It Work?

The technology behind Seedance 2.5 relies on deep learning algorithms that analyze video frames and generate new ones that fit the context of the original footage. Essentially, it’s training a neural network to understand how videos should look and then having it create new frames based on that understanding. The result is a seamless extension of your video content.

For instance, if you have a short clip of someone walking down a street, Seedance 2.5 can predict what the next few seconds might look like based on patterns in the existing footage. This predictive capability comes from analyzing thousands of similar videos to learn how scenes typically unfold.
What Are the Implications?

TechHalla’s experiment shows that anyone with a few bucks can start experimenting with AI-generated content. This democratization of technology means that advancements in AI are no longer confined to big companies or research labs. However, it also raises important questions about privacy and ethical use.

For instance, if someone can generate realistic-looking video content based on surveillance footage, there’s potential for misuse—think blackmail or other nefarious purposes. The generated content might look convincing but could still be detectable as AI-generated by those who know what to look for.
What Is Stored?

When you feed your surveillance footage into Seedance 2.5, the software processes and analyzes the video frames to generate new ones that fit the context of the original clip. However, it’s important to note that the actual data stored is minimal—just enough to create a coherent extension based on the input.

The software doesn’t retain any personal information or metadata beyond what’s necessary for generating the extended footage. This means that while your initial video might be analyzed, no additional sensitive details are saved unless you explicitly choose to store them.
What Is Excluded?

While Seedance 2.5 can extend and manipulate video content, it does not capture new data from external sources or integrate with other systems without explicit user permission. The software operates solely on the input provided by the user and generates output based on that specific dataset.

This means that any personal information or sensitive details in your original footage remain protected unless you choose to share them through additional features or integrations offered by Seedance 2.5.
User Controls

Users have control over what data they feed into Seedance 2.5 and how the generated content is used. You can decide whether to extend a video clip, modify it for personal use, or even experiment with different prompts to see how the software responds.

Additionally, you can choose not to save any of the extended footage if you’re just experimenting or testing out features without needing to retain the results. This level of control ensures that users remain in charge of their data and content.
Availability

Seedance 2.5 is available for download on various platforms, including Windows, macOS, and Linux. The software requires a compatible surveillance camera or any video source to function properly. While it’s designed primarily for extending video content, the possibilities extend far beyond simple extensions—users can experiment with different prompts and settings to see what works best.
What This Does Not Prove

While TechHalla’s experiment demonstrates the potential of AI-generated content using a $5 camera, it doesn’t prove that such technology is foolproof or infallible. The results are impressive but still subject to limitations based on input quality and context understanding.

Additionally, while Seedance 2.5 can generate convincing extensions, these aren’t always indistinguishable from real footage. There’s room for improvement in terms of accuracy and realism, especially when dealing with complex scenes or high-resolution videos.
Practical Takeaway

The practical takeaway is that AI-generated content tools like Seedance 2.5 are becoming increasingly accessible to the average user. This democratization opens up new avenues for creativity, experimentation, and even security enhancements. However, it also underscores the importance of ethical considerations and responsible use.

So go ahead, play around with these tools if you’re curious, but do so responsibly. Consider the potential implications and always be mindful of privacy concerns when handling sensitive footage or data.

EL ALAMEIN, EGYPT - India’s Sarang Helicopter Display Team has arrived on the Mediterranean coast ahead of its three‑day appearance at the El Alamein International Airshow. The unit, flying five ALH Dhruv helicopters, will join military and civilian performers from several countries as the event opens on September 8.

The team plans to field its trademark Dolphin Leap, a manoeuvre that sends the helicopters climbing sharply in unison before pivoting into a coordinated dive. Pilots will also unveil a new routine called the Spot Stall Turn, adding a fresh element to a show known for tight formation flying and close‑range aerobatics.

The Dhruv, built in India, has become a regular presence at international aviation events over the past two decades. Its appearance in Egypt comes as the two countries expand cooperation in defence training and equipment. The airshow itself has grown quickly since its launch, drawing aircraft from across the Middle East, Europe and Asia.

Sarang last performed in Egypt in 2023 during a smaller demonstration near Cairo. This year’s venue, a rapidly developing coastal city, offers a larger apron and viewing area, allowing the team to fly its full five‑helicopter sequence.

BRANSON, MISSOURI — Wendy Halstrom, 39, was arrested Sunday after allegedly clearing six entire dessert trays at a buffet in under thirty minutes, reportedly announcing to nearby staff that the dessert table was "the finish line" before beginning what witnesses described as a methodical sweep of every tray in sight.

Staff say the pacing alone should have been a warning sign.

Witnesses reported Halstrom moved down the dessert line tray by tray, clearing each one before moving to the next
Staff say she narrated her own progress out loud, announcing "two down" and "halfway there" to nobody in particular
She allegedly refused offers to slow down or take a plate, insisting "the tray system only works if you commit"
Witnesses say she used a to-go container specifically to transport a seventh tray's worth back to her table
Staff reported the kitchen had to restock all six dessert stations twice within the same hour
She allegedly raised both arms once the final tray was cleared, as if crossing an actual finish line

A small crowd of fellow diners reportedly applauded the effort before staff intervened and called it in.

"In sixteen years managing this buffet, I've seen big appetites, but never someone treat dessert like a competitive event with laps," said General Manager Carla Duvall, a 16-year veteran of the restaurant chain.

The trays were fully restocked. Halstrom was asked not to return to the dessert section specifically.

She called it a finish line. The buffet called it a loss.
Some races were never meant to be run solo.

text:
Temple Bar was the principal ceremonial entrance to the City of London from the City of Westminster. In the Middle Ages, London expanded city jurisdiction beyond its walls to gates, called 'bars', which were erected across thoroughfares. To the west of the City of London, the bar was located adjacent to the area known as the Temple. Temple Bar was situated on the historic royal ceremonial route from the Palace of the Tower of London to the old Palace of Westminster, the two chief residences of the medieval English monarchs, and from Westminster to St Paul's Cathedral. The road east of the bar within the city was Fleet Street, while the road to the west, in Westminster, was The Strand.

At the bar, the Corporation of the City of London erected a barrier to regulate trade into the city. The 19th century Royal Courts of Justice are located to its north, having been moved from Westminster Hall. To its south is Temple Church, along with the Inner Temple and Middle Temple Inns of Court. As the most important entrance to the City of London from Westminster, it was formerly long the custom for the monarch to halt at the Temple Bar before entering the City of London, in order for the Lord Mayor to offer the corporation's pearl-encrusted Sword of State as a token of loyalty.

'Temple Bar' strictly refers to a notional bar or barrier across the route near The Temple precinct, but it is also used to refer to the 17th-century ornamental, English Baroque arched gateway building attributed to Christopher Wren, which spanned the roadway at the bar for two centuries. After Wren's gateway was removed in 1878, the Temple Bar Memorial topped by a dragon symbol of London, and containing statues of Queen Victoria and Edward VII, was erected to mark the location. Wren's archway was preserved and was re-erected in 2004 within the City of London, in a redeveloped Paternoster Square next to St Paul's Cathedral. In September 2022, the preserved Wren gateway and an adjacent building were officially opened by the Duke of Gloucester as the home of the Worshipful Company of Chartered Architects.

Background
In the Middle Ages, the authority of the City of London Corporation reached beyond the city's ancient defensive walls in several places, known as the Liberties of London. To regulate trade into the city, barriers were erected on the major entrance routes wherever the true boundary was a substantial distance from the nearest ancient gatehouse in the walls. Temple Bar was the most used of these, since traffic between the City of London (England's prime commercial centre) and the Palace of Westminster (the political centre) passed through it. It was located where Fleet Street now meets The Strand, which is outside London's old boundary wall.[1]

Its name derives from the Temple Church, adjoining to the south, which has given its name to a wider area south of Fleet Street, the Temple, once belonging to the Knights Templar but now home to two of the legal profession's Inns of Court, and within the city's ancient boundaries.

The historic ceremony of the monarch halting at Temple Bar and being met by the Lord Mayor has often featured in art and literature. It is commented on in televised coverage of modern-day royal ceremonial processions.

The Knights Templar
From A Brief Historical Description by Professor Sir John Baker QC LLD FBA
Master of the Bench

The history of the Temple begins soon after the middle of the twelfth century, when a contingent of knights of the Military Order of the Temple of Solomon in Jerusalem moved from the Old Temple in Holborn (later Southampton House) to a larger site between Fleet Street and the banks of the River Thames. The new site originally included much of what is now Lincoln’s Inn, and the knights were probably responsible for establishing New Street (later Chancery Lane), which led from Holborn down to their new quarters. Following their custom, the knights built a round church patterned on the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. An inscription on the Round recorded that it was consecrated by the Patriarch Heraclius on 10 February 1185, in honour of the Blessed Virgin Mary. It is thought that King Henry II was also present on that day, inaugurating a long association between the royal family and the Temple.

Among the other buildings erected by the knights were dormitories, storehouses, stables, chambers, and two dining halls, one of them in the consecrated central portion and connected with the church by a cloister. It was a house fit for kings to stay in, and several did so. During a visit by King John in January 1215 he received a deputation of barons demanding a charter of liberties; and when the Great Charter was signed later in the year, the Master of the Temple was one of the witnesses. The knights took advantage of their special privileges to make their sanctuary a safe place for depositing treasure, and during the thirteenth century the New Temple became a busy financial centre. It was no doubt during this period that the first handful of lawyers came to live in the Temple, not as distinct societies but as legal advisers to a wealthy international organisation. The Templars thrived, adding to their round church a fine nave, which was consecrated in the presence of King Henry III in 1240. Many knights associated with the order were buried in the church, the most distinguished being William Marshal (d. 1219), first Earl of Pembroke and regent of England, the very model of medieval English chivalry, and one of the instigators of Magna Carta. Marshal’s armoured effigy, battered by time and war, may still be seen in the Round.

After losing the Holy Land in the 1290s, the order of the Temple fell into a decline. The knights were dubiously accused of improprieties, and in 1312 their order was dissolved. Although the pope granted their estates to the Knights Hospitaller of St John of Jerusalem, King Edward II seized the New Temple as forfeit to the Crown. Nevertheless, the consecrated portion was conceded to the Hospitallers, and the remainder was sold to them later.

The Crown of Ba'al and Master Trusts of the World 
 The Crown of Ba'al, also known as the Papal Tiara and Triregnum is a three-tiered jewelled papal crown and symbol of claimed papal supremecy since the 16th Century. text:
Are we saved by grace or mercy?

Do we take God's grace for granted? Should we say mercy instead? Isn't it about our attitude towards God and His eternal gift to us – do we really feel a real gratitude - for our salvation from eternal damnation?

The distinction is real, and the scripture uses both words on purpose. Treating them as synonyms flattens something God meant to keep sharp.

Mercy is not getting the judgment we deserve. Grace is getting the life, adoption, and favor we could never deserve. Scripture holds both together: God is “rich in mercy,” and we are “saved by grace through faith.” Mercy names the precipice; grace names the gift on the other side. 

The danger of speaking only of grace is presumption - “it will cover it” - as if sin were a line of credit. Paul rejects that: we who died with Christ cannot go on living in the thing that required His death. The cry “Mercy!” keeps the truth in view: we were dead, children of wrath, about to perish.

 We were not merely improved; we were spared.

The first fitting response to that mercy is gratitude. Not polite thanks, but the recognition that we had no claim. Mature gratitude becomes a life offered back: “by the mercies of God, present your bodies.” It walks with humility, reverence, obedience that does not try to pay God back, and mercy toward others. 

A spared person does not ask how much sin the covering still allows. He asks how a life that was almost lost should now be lived before the One who let it live.

Justice would give the sinner the wages of sin: death, wrath, exclusion from God’s presence. Mercy withholds that sentence. Grace then goes further and gives what no sinner could ever claim: forgiveness as a gift, a new heart, adoption, the Spirit, a seat with Christ, an inheritance that does not fade. Mercy looks at our misery and guilt and does not destroy us. Grace looks at the same wreck and makes us heirs. 

They are not two rival systems of salvation. They are two faces of the same love. Paul puts them in the same sentence:

“But God, being rich in mercy, because of the great love with which he loved us, even when we were dead in our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ - by grace you have been saved.”

A few verses later he repeats the formula everyone remembers, saved by grace through faith. In Titus he can say the same rescue is “according to his own mercy” and that we are “justified by his grace”. First Peter says we were born again “according to his great mercy.” The Bible will not let you pick one and discard the other. 

“Mercy!” does something 
Believers often understand that they are “forgiven.” Fewer linger long enough to feel what they were forgiven from, or how strange it is that the same God now calls that former object of wrath His workmanship, created for good works He prepared beforehand. The man who still knows how to cry “Mercy!” is usually the one who can also receive grace without turning it into an excuse.

The tax collector does not stand in the temple and say, “Thank you for your unmerited favor.” He will not even lift his eyes. He beats his breast and says, “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” 

Jesus says that man went home justified. The cry assumes three things at once: I have no case, the Judge has every right to condemn, and my only hope is that He is compassionate. That is a different posture from treating grace as a renewable credit line.

Saved by mercy through faith?
So, the healthier attitude is not to swap the verse and say “saved by mercy through faith” as if that were more accurate. It is to let both words do their work at once. Mercy keeps you from presumption. Grace keeps you from despair. Mercy says you were a dead enemy under a just sentence. Grace says the Father, at infinite cost to the Son, did not merely commute the sentence; He made the condemned man an heir and sat him down at the table.

Gratitude, then, is the test as much as the fruit. A person who has really seen mercy does not mainly ask how much sin the covering will still allow. He asks how a spared life is supposed to look - in the presence of the One who spared it.
