Step into one of Michigan’s best-preserved 19th-century communities in the Marshall Historic District in Marshall, Michigan. The district contains an extraordinary collection of Greek Revival, Gothic Revival, Italianate, and Queen Anne homes, churches, schools, and commercial buildings that reflect the city’s growth during the 1800s.

Marshall was once considered a leading candidate to become Michigan’s state capital, and its prosperous early residents built ambitious homes and civic buildings that still define the community today. Walking through the district offers a rare chance to experience an entire townscape shaped by the architecture and ambitions of the young Midwest.

Little-known fact: Marshall has more than 800 historically significant buildings within its historic district, making it one of the largest concentrations of 19th-century architecture in the United States.

The 5 BC Comet Theory
Ancient Records: Chinese court chronicles from 5 BC documented a bright celestial object or "passing star" that remained visible for over 70 days.
NASA Analysis: NASA planetary scientist Mark Matney used orbital modeling to suggest this comet passed exceptionally close to Earth (within lunar distance).

What does “let them be for signs and seasons” mean in Genesis 1:14?
Answer

In Genesis 1:14, on the fourth day of creation, God declares, “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heavens to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs and seasons, and for days and years” (NKJV). In this way, God established the celestial bodies (sun, moon, and stars) to “be for signs and seasons.” This phrase is theologically, prophetically, and practically significant.

Genesis 1 describes God’s creation of the heavens and the earth. Light was introduced in verse 3, but in verse 14 God established the sun, moon, and stars in the sky. These celestial bodies, in relation to a rotating Earth, mark time, provide signs, and designate seasons. Their movements are accurate to the nth degree. God’s creation is purposeful, orderly, and structured.

The Hebrew word for “signs” refers to visible markers or tokens. In Scripture, signs indicate divine activity. The celestial bodies function as signs in various ways. First, they are instruments of divine revelation: “The heavens declare the glory of God, and the sky above proclaims his handiwork. Day to day pours out speech, and night to night reveals knowledge” (Psalm 19:1–2, ESV). Furthermore, the star of Bethlehem signified Christ’s birth. The magi from the East asked, “Where is he who has been born king of the Jews? For we saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him” (Matthew 2:2, ESV).

In apocalyptic literature, celestial disturbances indicate God’s judgment: “The sun shall be turned to darkness, and the moon to blood, before the great and awesome day of the Lord comes” (Joel 2:31, ESV). When Jesus, the Son of Man, returns, “the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the power of the heavens will be shaken” (Matthew 24:29, ESV).

The Hebrew word for “seasons” is used extensively in the Torah to refer to God’s appointed feast days (Leviticus 23:2, 4). Celestial bodies, then, regulate calendar seasons and days of worship. Passover, the Feast of Tabernacles, and Yom Kippur are based on lunar cycles, as are holidays such as Easter. The sun’s position in the sky determines agricultural and climatic seasons. God ordained times for planting and for harvesting, as Solomon writes, “For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up what is planted” (Ecclesiastes 3:1–2, ESV). Part of God’s covenant with Noah was a promise of seasonal change: “As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease” (Genesis 8:22).

As the Creator, God is sovereign over all He has made. Heavenly bodies fulfill God’s purposes (Deuteronomy 4:19). The sun, moon, and stars reflect divine order. Like a master craftsman, God meticulously placed stars and planets in their courses above (1 Corinthians 14:33). Every aspect of creation declares God’s infinite glory.

The sun, moon, and stars are “lights in the firmament of the heavens” (Genesis 1:14, NKJV) but also function as divine signs and appointed seasons. This celestial order testifies to God’s sovereignty, wisdom, and providence. Creation serves His purposes, not the other way around. Believers should appreciate God’s intricate design and how His plan is infused into creation. Nothing is random but is part of God’s magnificent plan.

What are the new heaven and the new earth?
Answer
In Revelation 21:1, John sees something spectacular: “Then I saw ‘a new heaven and a new earth,’ for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away.” This new earth and new heaven are sometimes referred to as the “eternal state.” As seen in Revelation chapters 21—22, the new earth will be the eternal dwelling place of believers in Jesus Christ. Scripture gives us a few details of the new heaven and new earth.

The current heaven and earth have long been subject to God’s curse because of mankind’s sin. All creation “has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth” (Romans 8:22) as it awaits the fulfillment of God’s plan and “the children of God to be revealed” (verse 19). Heaven and earth will pass away (Mark 13:31), and they will be replaced by the new heaven and the new earth. At that time, the Lord, seated on His throne, says, “I am making everything new!” (Revelation 21:5). In the new creation, sin will be totally eradicated, and “there shall be no more curse” (Revelation 22:3, NKJV).

The new heaven and new earth are also mentioned in Isaiah 65:17; 66:22; and 2 Peter 3:13. Peter says that the new heaven and new earth will be “where righteousness dwells.” Isaiah says that “the former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.” Things will be completely new, and the old order of things, with the accompanying sorrow and tragedy, will be gone.

The new earth will be free from sin, evil, sickness, suffering, and death. It will be earth as God originally intended it to be, prior to the curse of sin. It will be Eden restored.

I believe this technology has the potential to be the next major step in the development of consumer electronics. It offers a fundamentally new way to interact with the digital environment and has the potential to replace many existing devices that accompany people in their daily lives today.

What we once thought was just science fiction is about to become real, but not in a good way! This is not about improving our lives, but controlling them…and they need every bit of information about us to do that.

15-min cities are on the agenda!

By the end of this exercise, they will know everything about us, and I mean everything! Not just our financial information or medical information. Therefore, they will, be able to predict our every movement, how we spend our money and even our thinking!! Human robots under their control.

When they know everything you are going to do, they can plan accordingly and unknowingly force you down certain paths. All of which are profitable to the big companies.

Control and profits are the end goal!

The ‘What’

This is about the centres themselves. They need these gigantic buildings to house and run these massive computers. Sound okay to you? Well, think again, particularly about how they are run. We are not talking housing one or two huge computers, but racks of them,  all stored on top of each other, all gathering information about you and others, then distributing that information to various others centres around the world to be analyzed.

New ones are much larger!

In the USA it has been proved that the heat they generate can even affect local weather, and the water needed to cool them is astronomical, again affecting the water needed by communities to survive. And guess what, if there is a water shortage…guess who gets priority!!…not the people, thanks to the previous deals within SEZs!  

Remember these?

This has been in the planning for years, and the jigsaw is now coming together!

Climate change policies have flown out of the window, replaced by corporate governance and greed.

All this in the name of AI, which has already proven to be unreliable.

So, what do we get out of all this?

In short nothing! Maybe some jobs in construction. 

Do they offer efficiency…well even if they did, does it justify the expense, the secrecy and the environmental damage?

People all over the world are starting to realise the negatives and they are huge and they are saying NO. 

Again, in the States, politicians are being ‘recalled’ and sacked for supporting these centres!

If our FM goes back on his promised moratorium, a stand must be taken one way or another and I’m not sure a protest will cut it.

Dear members of the American press!

Steve Jobs once said, "If you can convince the press of your technology, and the press convinces us, we'll pay attention."

That's why I'm reaching out to you.

For years, the development of personal devices has been driven by advances in smartphones, tablets, and virtual reality technologies. However, all of these solutions still require people to adapt to the device. I've developed a concept based on the opposite principle: the device should adapt to the user and interact with them as naturally as possible.

I believe this technology has the potential to be the next major step in the development of consumer electronics. It offers a fundamentally new way to interact with the digital environment and has the potential to replace many existing devices that accompany people in their daily lives today.

If my assessment is correct, this isn't just another gadget, but a platform capable of transforming the market in the same way that the personal computer, iPod, and iPhone once did. Such opportunities arise extremely rarely, and that's why they deserve independent attention and objective assessment.

I believe Apple has the experience, engineering culture, and vision necessary to turn this idea into a world-class product. Moreover, the successful implementation of such technology could strengthen the leadership of the American tech industry at a time when global competition is becoming increasingly fierce.

I'm not asking you to take my word for it. I'm asking only one thing: help draw Apple's attention to this development and give it the opportunity to be considered by those capable of objectively assessing its potential.

If the technology truly represents the value I see in it, ignoring it could be a missed opportunity. If not, that will become clear after a professional evaluation. But in either case, the idea deserves to be heard.

Thank you for your attention.

Sincerely,

Alexander.

text:
“The Future of Transit”

I rode the steel veins of this country for weeks. Trains first, then buses, then trains again. I sat among the quiet, the tired, the rushing, the forgotten. I watched how a nation moves when no one is filming. I wanted to know if this daily pilgrimage still held dignity, if it still belonged to the people who built the tracks and the roads with their backs and their blood. I wanted to see whether the future generations would inherit something worth boarding.

Out of those rides a story was born. A story that would have made investors lean forward, tourism bloom, and the land of my ancestors shine again. A story that carried culture, memory, and invitation. I spent days carving every sentence so the world would feel it in the chest. I laboured seven days without rest so the dead would finally let me sleep. On Sunday I woke, looked at the sky, and smiled because all I could see was beauty. Labour Day weekend. I had been labouring all week. I told myself I had earned a Guinness.

I drove to @TheBeerStoreON at 301 Dundas St in Whitby. Around 4:55 p.m. a woman behind the counter got my order wrong. I corrected her calmly. What followed was not a mistake. It was contempt. She refused to sell me the Guinness and the Molson. Bad service wrapped in something older and uglier. In that moment I understood why so many of these stores are closing and why 40 something thousand people lost their jobs last month. An institution I once respected enough to edit their posts and create videos for them showed me its true face.

A white woman who had been standing in line saw everything. She followed me outside to the car and apologized on behalf of the land. She offered to go back inside and buy what I had been denied. That small act of decency was the only light in a room that had gone dark. Her kindness reminded me that not every heart on this soil has gone completely cold.

I have no respect for liars. I will always call them out. This land first belonged to my ancestors who walked it long before maps were drawn. The country built on that ground now walks around with its head chopped off, inheriting hatred it does not know how to heal. Everything is falling apart on the ground they once fought to keep honourable. Canada does not deserve the story I carried. I still carry the sacred word that outlasts every closed door and every cruel counter. “The earth is the Lord’s, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.” Psalm 24:1. We were here first and that memory will never be erased from this soil.

The Future of Transit was cancelled because this country does not deserve it right now. I walked away from the counter the same way I have walked away from worse. I still believe in beauty. I still believe in the people who ride those trains and buses every morning with quiet hope. I still believe the land can be worthy again. Until then I will keep speaking. The dead can rest. The living must wake.

text:
We were supposed to go to college together!”
She lunged forward, grabbing my frozen hand and pressing it against her cheek.
“Wes, wake up! Please, wake up!”
Mom’s hand reached out, hesitated, then touched my forehead.
The blood from my wound had frozen into dark red crystals on my skin.
“Wesley…” her voice cracked. “I… I didn’t know. I thought the freezer was off. I thought you were just acting out like you always did.”
She fell to her knees, her fingers clutching my frozen school uniform.
“I was going to let you out after the exam. I just needed you to wait a little longer. I was coming back for you. I swear I was.”
Darren grabbed her.
She sobbed, “I was afraid… afraid that if I let him out, he’d find a way to take the exam anyway… afraid that if he did, the prophecy would come true and you’d die. I had to choose between my sons. How could I choose?”
Dad stood motionless in the doorway. He finally spoke, his voice hollow.
“The prophecy said Darren would die because of Wes’s success. It never said anything about Wes dying because of us.”
Nora let out a choked sob.
“He was at the top of the class. He had scholarship offers from every college. And now he’s dead because…”
“The psychic… the psychic told us… the psychic was wrong,” Darren said quietly. “Or lying. Or maybe you just heard what you wanted to hear.”
He stood up slowly, his eyes red.
“Wes was never the problem. I was never going to jump off a building. I loved him. And you killed him because you were too afraid to see the truth.”
Mom’s hands fell away from me. Her face crumbled into something broken, ancient, hollow.
She looked at my body, frozen in the corner, still reaching for a door that never opened.
“No…” she whispered.
No amount of tears could thaw the ice that had already claimed me.

*"My Dad's Friends Always Calls Me His Wife As A Joke...Until That Night"*

My dad has a close friend whom he trusts a lot. They are very close and usually share their thoughts with each other.

For a long time, I noticed that my dad’s friend would joke about me being his wife whenever he came to our house. Sometimes, if I wasn’t around when he visited, he would even ask my dad, “Where is my wife?” My dad always laughed because he thought he was only joking.

He is married and has children, just like my dad, and our whole family knows his https://t.co/PYbJ4v52O7 night, something happened that completely changed the way I see him.

My parents usually work during the week and come home on weekends, so at the time, it was mostly me and my younger sister who stayed at home. 

One night, he called me around midnight and told me he was outside our house. He said he had just returned from a trip and didn’t want to go home that night.

I initially told him to get a hotel because there was one close to our house, but after some convincing, I allowed him to stay in our parlour because the other rooms were locked.

While he was there, he crossed a boundary with me and made me very uncomfortable. I immediately became afraid that something worse might happen, so I went to wake my younger sister and asked her to stay with me. After that, I made sure we went into our room and locked the door.

The next day, after he left, he contacted me again and offered to send me money and asked me to meet him where he worked. He sent the money, but I blocked him immediately because I no longer felt comfortable communicating with him.

Since then, whenever I see him, I feel completely different toward him. I dislike being around him, and sometimes I even find myself being disrespectful toward him. I honestly don’t know how to handle the situation, especially because he is my dad’s close friend.

I have been keeping this to myself, but I really need advice. What do you think I should do? Should I tell my dad what happened, or should I just stay away from this man and keep quiet?

text:
APPLOVIN $APP REPORTED $1.27 BILLION OF PROFIT LAST QUARTER. THE CASH CAME TO $863 MILLION:

AppLovin APP at $320.56, +$6.98 / +2.23% on Friday. US markets are shut Monday, September 7 for Labor Day, so that is the latest price on every name here. The Palo Alto company sells the software app and game makers use to buy advertising and aim it at the people most likely to install.

Every Len5 has a name at the top of its list and a name one line below it. The top name is usually the one whose argument is over. The one below is where something is still being decided. Six of those today, one per Len5.

AppLovin gets the most words, and the reason is a gap. Its reported profit is compounding faster than almost anything its size. The actual cash is not.

The June quarter, reported August 5:

- Revenue $1.92B vs $1.26B a year earlier, +53%
- Net income $1.27B vs $820M, +55% - about 66 cents kept out of every sales dollar
- Adjusted cash profit, which strips out interest, taxes and the charge for wear on equipment, $1.61B, +58%
- Free cash flow, the cash left after running the business and buying equipment, $863.3M vs $768.1M

Profit rose 55%. Cash rose 12.4%. Of that $1.61B of adjusted cash profit, $863.3M actually arrived - about 54 cents on the dollar, against the 75 cents management maps for the full year, blaming the timing of tax and interest payments.

The Hypergrowth Len5 wants a business both fast and still early. Fast is not arguable at 53%. Early is where it stops short: $107B of market value, and its own map for this quarter is $2.06B to $2.09B of revenue, growth of 46% to 48%, the first time it has pointed below 50%. Holding the case together is the money per customer, revenue per install up 58% while installs fell 2%. What would change it: that step down continuing into next year rather than proving to be a harder comparison.

The price already took a side. On August 6, the session after the report, the stock went $417.80 to $335.67, -$82.13 / -19.7%, then slid to $298.59 by August 24. Friday sits 56.3% below the $733.60 of December 22.

Verdict: the growth is not what is in dispute here, the conversion is. AppLovin has not published its own third-quarter date; calendars point at November 11, and one line settles it - free cash flow against adjusted cash profit. Climb toward 75 cents and the drawdown was about a growth rate. Stay near 54 and it was about the cash.

MOMENTUM LEN5:
- Utz Brands at $14.21, -$0.01 / -0.07% Friday, the Hanover, Pennsylvania maker of Utz and Zapp's snacks. This Len5 wants a price near its twelve-month best with the short and long stretches agreeing, and Utz has the strongest three-month climb here beside a month that went nowhere. The flat month is the answer: on July 20 Germany's Intersnack Group agreed to buy every share for $14.25 cash, roughly 91% above the $7.46 it closed at the day before. Friday sits four cents under the offer. WATCH: the shareholder vote, still undated, the founding family committed to about 42% of the shares. RISK: 0.28% of upside left, against a fall back toward $7.46 if the deal breaks. Verdict: a flawless chart with nothing left in it, because this price belongs to a contract now rather than to a snack business.

QUALITY-VALUE LEN5:
- Visa at $375.07, -$3.68 / -0.97% Friday, the network carrying a payment from a shopper's bank to a merchant's bank and taking a fee each time. This Len5 wants a business nobody could rebuild, priced short of what it is worth, and the first half is arithmetic rather than opinion: the quarter reported July 28 processed 71.7 billion transactions, +10%, and pushed payments volume - the dollars run across the network - past $4 trillion in three months for the first time. Net revenue $11.6B, +14%; adjusted profit $3.32 a share, +11%. WATCH: whether the 2,600 job cuts announced the same day, about 7% of staff, arrive as margin; the fiscal fourth quarter is undated. RISK: price, 2.4% under the $384.14 of August 25, leaving no discount to absorb a slower quarter. Verdict: the moat is settled, and price is the whole reason this one is not first.

DEEP-VALUE AND SPECIAL-SITUATIONS LEN5:
- Copart at $33.72, +$0.14 / +0.42% Friday, the Dallas company running online salvage auctions - insurers hand it wrecked cars, it sells them to buyers worldwide. This Len5 wants a good business marked down after something visible went wrong, and both halves are dated. Marked down: 32.5% under the $49.97 of a year ago. What went wrong is in its own numbers, reported May 21 for the quarter ended April 30 - unit volume fell 2.4%, US insurance volume 4.2%, as households trimmed their coverage. Pricing went the other way, auction prices +4.1% to a seasonal record, and gross margin - what it keeps of each sales dollar after the cost of the sale - reached 46.3%, up 0.71 points. Fewer cars, more money per car. WATCH: Thursday, September 10 after 4:00pm ET, a date Copart set itself on September 1. RISK: a third straight quarter of shrinking volume that better prices no longer cover. Verdict: the markdown is real, and the thing that caused it has not stopped.

GROWTH LEN5:
- BOK Financial at $136.70, -$0.65 / -0.47% Friday, the Tulsa bank lending to businesses and households from Texas to Arizona. This Len5 wants real expansion the price has not already paid for, and the expansion is not in question: loans reached $27.1B at June 30, up $896M in three months and 11.5% on the year, the highest quarterly loan production in the bank's history, with the full-year target raised above 10%. It was built rather than bought - more than 25 bankers hired in the quarter, over 20 in Texas. WATCH: the gap between what it earns lending and pays on deposits barely moved, 2.91%, up a hundredth of a point. RISK: the headline $2.92 a share reads better than the business did - strip a $30.9M gain on exchanging Visa shares and a $4.6M bond repositioning loss and it was $2.59. Verdict: a loan book genuinely compounding, and an earnings line that has not caught it.

INCOME LEN5:
- Global Ship Lease at $46.40, +$0.66 / +1.44% Friday, its best close in twelve months and the only name here making new highs. The London company owns mid-size container ships and leases them to the big shipping lines years at a time. This Len5 wants cash genuinely reaching owners and funded by the business, and the funding is not close: the June quarter, reported August 5, earned $2.48 a share, while the entire year's dividend is $2.50 - $0.625 a quarter, paid September 3, about 5.4% of Friday's price. One quarter of profit nearly covers a full year of the payout. WATCH: the cover is contracted rather than forecast, $3.2B signed at June 30 with all of 2026 and 90% of 2027 chartered out, and that 90% moves first if charter rates turn. RISK: $1.33B ordered for 15 new ships that bill from the shipyard years before they earn. Verdict: the payout is small on purpose, and the reason is still under construction.

A leader is a name whose argument is finished. These six are all still mid-argument, and each has a place where it ends - a shareholder vote for Utz, Thursday afternoon for Copart, a 2027 charter figure for Global Ship Lease. AppLovin's is the widest and the furthest out. It booked $1.27B of profit, banked $863M, and has lost 56% of its price since December. November is when it learns which of those two numbers the market was reading.

Not investment advice.

Tuesday, September 8th- Every day is a wonderful day to celebrate the blessings of grandparents. With the upcoming national day just around the corner, Foley Library is getting a head start on the festivities! If your grandparents visited for the holiday weekend, why not invite them to stay an extra day? Join others this Tuesday from 10 to 11 AM at the Foley Community Library for grandparents' Storytime and craft in the kids' area. It promises a warm morning filled with engaging stories, lively songs, and lots of intergenerational love. After the main story, families can head over to the Maker Meadow to create a special keepsake craft—perfect to give to a grandparent, a loved one, a neighbor, or even a special teacher. Whether you bring your special guest or make something to send later, everyone is welcome.  Enjoy the event and then explore all the wonderful things this brand-new library has to offer!

Grandparents Day Story Time and Craft - Foley

Wednesday, September 9th- Attention all local business owners, entrepreneurs, and community members: the third Coastal Alabama Business Expo, presented by Southern Sands Printing Company and powered by Printing Pros, is approaching this Wednesday. This event provides an excellent opportunity for local businesses and entrepreneurs to showcase their products and services through dedicated booths. Attendees can network, build new connections, and gain insights into the offerings of various businesses. Each booth will feature demonstrations or visuals of what they offer, along with one-on-one interactions with representatives, allowing visitors to learn more about individual businesses firsthand. The expo also offers attendees opportunities to make purchases, schedule appointments, and book with vendors for upcoming events, fostering a spirit of community and collaboration among entrepreneurial neighbors. The event is open to the public from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM and will be held at the Orange Beach Event Center. This is an exceptional occasion to gain visibility for local businesses and strengthen community ties. Do not miss this valuable event highlighting the entrepreneurial spirit of Coastal Alabama.

Coastal Alabama Business Expo - OB 

Thursday, September 10th- Well, we’ve all heard of bull riding, and we’ve all heard of the beach, and most people have heard of Flora-Bama, but have you ever heard of Bulls of the Beach at Flora-Bama? That’s right, toss your sandals to the side and grab your boots for this one, cowboys and cowgirls, and get ready for this 13th annual showdown. Tickets are on sale now, with a portion of proceeds going to St. Jude’s Children’s Hospital. This three-night event starts on Thursday, September 10th. Each night, attendees are encouraged to dress up with a theme for this one-of-a-kind bull riding extravaganza right on the line — that’s right, no dirt here. These bulls are kicking up sand, baby. Thursday night is Camo Cowboy, Friday is Patriotic Tribute in honor of September 11, and Saturday is 90s Country, a fan favorite! Thursday night is also Kids’ Night — children ages 12 and under can participate in a coloring contest for a chance to win a bike, with one lucky boy and one lucky girl. The night concludes with a professional bull event, where Friday and Saturday will feature the professional bull riders in the adult bull riding competition. Come out for the show — whether you’ve been before or not, this is an ultimate experience and one of Flora-Bama’s most anticipated events. This rodeo action draws crowds from across the country, both as spectators and competitors. So giddy up, y’all — it’s time to ride Gulf Coast beach style.

Bulls on the Beach tickets - Perdido Key

Friday, September 11th-Join others this Friday at the National Naval Museum Blue Angels Atrium for a heartfelt commemorative program—“The Service and Sacrifice." This poignant 25th anniversary event honors the bravery and sacrifice of those who lost their lives and those whose lives were forever affected by the tragic events of September 11, 2001. The program will include personal reflections from CDR Steve Scheibner, USN (Ret.), American Airlines Captain (Ret.), “Captain Steeeve," along with VADM John B. Totushek, USN (Ret.), former Chief of Naval Reserve and Commander, Naval Reserve Force, Pentagon Survivor. The Naval Aviation Alumni Choir will also be present, offering uplifting hymns throughout the event. The event will conclude with a wreath-laying ceremony and the sounding of Taps, as a sincere tribute to all who were lost. This free event is open to everyone who registers in advance. All are invited to come together with others for this moment of remembrance and homage from 9 AM to noon. Afterward, please consider exploring the museum. To register, simply visit the link below.

The Service and Sacrifice - Pensacola

Saturday, September 12th- The first full week of September is filled with annual events that deeply unite our community, not just drawing outside visitors but bringing us together through meaningful traditions like the Kenny Vines Memorial Fishing Tournament, which spans two days, starting September 11 at 4 PM and continuing until Saturday, the 12th. This event holds a special place in many local hearts. It honors Kenneth Lane Vines, affectionately known as KV, a passionate and lively fisherman who not only loved to reel in the big ones but also brought joy and laughter to everyone at the docks. A devoted community member, Vines was a founding figure in the Elberta Sausage Festival and the Orange Beach Seafood Festival, and he was active in the Mobile Big Game Fishing Club, as well as in conservation and other foundations. Celebrating all he loved, this weekend event is a heartfelt tribute to his memory. Whether you're participating as an angler, including young, aspiring fishermen, or simply there to watch, the weigh-ins promise to be a lively celebration. The event will be centered at Tacky Jacks Orange Beach on Saturday, the 12th. Scales open at 5 PM, with all vessels planning to weigh in and clear through Perdido Pass by 7 PM. Spectators are encouraged to arrive early at Tacky Jacks, find a cozy spot, grab a menu to dine, and enjoy the evening’s camaraderie. It’s bound to be a night filled with warmth, community, and celebration of a beloved friend.

Kenny Vines Memorial Tournament - OB

Sunday, September 13th- Though the Alabama Gulf Coast hasn’t experienced its last hot, sunny days for 2026, I’m sure you’ve noticed things are getting a little breezier. Don’t get too excited; you still need to pack your water and pray for the wind. However, outdoor strolls are becoming extremely inviting, with fewer folks on the streets, sidewalks, and boardwalks—taking long walks looks good. This Sunday, check out Wade Ward Nature Park located in Gulf Shores. Here, you’ll really get a feel for Hometown Gulf Shores. As you walk along the elevated boardwalks, you can take your time looking east, where you might spot local marshbirds, plants, and even the occasional alligator. Sunrise and sunset are some of the most beautiful times to enjoy the sky; however, any time of day is perfect for exploring these outdoor paths. Whether you lace up your walking shoes, rent or ride your own bike to pedal along, this stroll is sure to please. Make stops if you'd like, or cruise through; there's no wrong way to enjoy. Pack a lunch or stop in at Picnic Beach, Mikee’s, Desoto’s, or many other great spots nearby for lunch or dinner. Enjoy the still warm air, soak up the salty breeze, and don’t forget to bring your camera—you never know what nature might gift your lens. Happy trails.

Wade Ward Nature Park - GS

Well, that’s the week ya’ll! Good times, good people, and plenty of Gulf Coast memory- makers. Now get out there and make some.

Junior is a gorgeous 10 month old Staffy cross English Bull terrier.
His mum was a full staffy and his dad half English Bull Terrier. He is a blue colour.
Junior is needing a new home through no fault of his own. His owner absolutely adores him however as his work has now changed, it means Junior is left on his own for long periods of time.
He can be left on his own, but does love people and would like someone who can spend lots of time with him on walks and giving him attention.
Junior has always lived with kids and loves them. He attends doggy day care and is good with other dogs and new humans. He has never been around cats. He is such a lover to people and adores humans.
Junior is chipped and healthy with no medical issues.
He eats kibble and wainwrights from Pets at Home and loves the green lamb and rice variety.
Junior is crate trained and sleeps in his crate at night. He can be strong on the lead, this may need a bit more work.
He travels okay in the car, its not his favourite but he is ok.
Junior loves treats and is motivated by treats. He is great meeting new people and has lots of energy. His recall is good but may need a bit more work.
Could you offer this lovely lad a new home? If so, please email a bit about yourself to info@help2rehome.com

text:
The surf town of Liwliwa is drowning in monster waves, and the negligence of local authorities and businesses is to blame.

Beachfront resorts in Sitio Liwliwa, Barangay Santo Niño, in the municipality of San Felipe, Zambales, reportedly closed down beginning July, with floods ruining their properties and engulfing entire huts. Parts of the town’s coastline have been consumed by ocean waves, with debris from the buildings and nearby trees floating around.

The town proper, several hundred meters away from the shoreline, has also not been spared from the flooding, with many roads submerged in knee-deep water during storms.

A 24 Oras report from September 5 also notes that a dike enclosing Santo Tomas River, which borders the southern part of Liwliwa, was damaged amid successive storms, making the town more prone to flooding.

Sitio Liwliwa has rapidly risen to fame as an affordable beach destination, often touted as a less crowded alternative to more established spots like La Union.

But Liwliwa was not always a surfer’s paradise. The black sand beach of Liwliwa resulted from ashfall during the 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption, adding a shoreline to the town proper, now called “Old Liwliwa.”

The Mines and Geosciences Bureau said the ashfall added an additional 1 kilometer to the shoreline, deeming the area unclassified land because it had not undergone a proper zoning survey.

“The eruption of Mt. Pinatubo dramatically changed the landscape. Ash rain accumulated on land and lahar found its way to the river dumping a large amount of volcanic materials to the sea. That explains why the beach sand of Liwliwa has a mixture of gray and black sand,” wrote the Olongapo-based blog Playing Tourist in 2019.

DREDGING, OVERTOURISM BEING BLAMED
Extreme flooding was first flagged in July 2025, and locals said it was because of dredging operations at Santo Tomas River. While the Mines and Geosciences Bureau said then that dredging was not to blame, the agency also warned that coastal erosion was due to beachfront resorts putting additional pressure on the land.

“‘Yun pong ating mga resorts diyan are standing on unclassified public lands, accretion po ‘yan, so wala pong titulo ‘yan. Dapat ‘di ‘yan nilagyan ng building diyan,” MGB Region 3 Director Noel Lacadin told 24 Oras in a July 2025 report.
Because the beachfront was molded by volcanic ash, experts also warn that the land is more prone to erosion.

Tourists and locals alike will complain of floods and erosion during typhoon season, but once the weather clears up, more and more resorts will set up shop to take advantage of the growing crowds in the area. And the local government will continue to be slow to act on the similarly emerging issue of overtourism, at the expense of the already-fragile natural environment.

While the municipal government of San Felipe and the provincial government of Zambales have since announced relief operations, suspension of water activities, and the creation of temporary jobs in the direct aftermath of the calamity, there has seemingly been no word on how the authorities will address the failing condition of the beach, which may only worsen as climate change creates stronger, more frequent storms and weather infrastructure fails to keep up.

Similarly, businesses that continue to profit from offering beachfront views despite the growing warnings are not doing anybody a favor. Some of these resorts destroyed by the floods aren’t exactly your hidden gem-type nipa hut stays, but concrete structures that require millions of pesos in capital. Small businesses are definitely in need of support, but the absence of proper land regulations does not excuse greed disguised as resourcefulness or “diskarte.”

Liwliwa is certainly a treasure worth preserving. As tourism to other provinces gains traction, the emerging surf destination offers charming experiences for every type of traveler. But if the beach can just suddenly emerge from a calamity, it can just as easily disappear after another calamity, that of human neglect.

(✍️: Kiara Gorrospe)

News Flashback

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Li Kerong has announced that he will no longer take part in future Xiaomi China GT Championship races after what happened at Shanghai on Saturday.

He was competing in the GTC/GTS races with Phantom Global Racing last weekend, but he is a regular in the Intercontinental GT Challenge this season, leading the Independent Cup standings.

Li was left furious after witnessing Loek Hartog being put into a position where he had to rescue Ollie Millroy. "We cannot rely on fellow drivers to step into harm's way every single time ... On-site rescue response was inadequate after the crash. The organizer failed to offer even basic humanitarian support. All medical burdens have fallen on Ollie's wife, who flew over urgently from the UK. The safety of the drivers is the fundamental bottom line of our sport ... I truly hope motorsport within China will learn to respect human life and move towards better regulation."

Several people have offered to contribute financially to our work. I’m genuinely grateful, but our project already has everything it needs. Your readership, your information and your willingness to share the findings are support enough.

For those who have asked where they could make a useful contribution, I’ve chosen to support @WyvernFellows with a personal donation.

Having spent so much time examining the organisations that influence British public life, I’ve become increasingly conscious of how much catching up our side has to do. 

We have plenty of people identifying what has gone wrong. We also need to give serious support to those prepared to spend their time building something useful.

Wyvern has been established to advocate for the interests of the English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish people. Its founders have worked through months of practical and legal difficulties, committing their own money alongside contributions from early supporters.

It operates on a not-for-profit basis. The founders have pledged that every penny raised will support the organisation’s work or charitable causes, including the Rhiannon Whyte Foundation and charities helping rape-gang survivors.

Getting an organisation established is a considerable undertaking. Keeping it effective requires people willing to back it after the initial enthusiasm has passed. I would like to see worthwhile pro-British organisations develop the resources and staying power to make a lasting contribution.

Please take a look at Wyvern’s mission statement and consider joining or donating if you share its aims.

To everyone who offered to help fund our work: thank you. We’re covered. This is a project I believe deserves some of that generosity.

These stones on the southern slope of Slievemore belong to the Irish court tomb tradition. Most monuments of this kind were first raised in the early Neolithic, around 3700 to 3500 BC. That places the arrangement at roughly five and a half thousand years of age. 

A nearby occupation layer at the so-called Cromlech Tumulus, linked to this tomb by a pre-bog field wall once called the Danish Ditch, has a later Neolithic date of 2619 to 2604 BC. That date speaks to continued life on the mountain after the tomb was already standing, not to the first lifting of these slabs.

The tomb itself has been recorded rather than fully opened. Ruaidhrí de Valera and Seán Ó Nualláin surveyed the Achill megaliths in the mid twentieth century. 

The Achill Archaeological Field School has since mapped and excavated the surrounding landscape: the Deserted Village, Bronze Age roundhouses, the Cromlech Tumulus, and sections of the Danish Ditch. 

Their work includes topographic and GPS survey, trench excavation, lithic study, and radiocarbon dating. The court tomb remains largely as a standing monument in the heather, with its court, jambs, and gallery still readable in the stones.

The bones of those who set these stones do not lie here in any way we can name. Court tombs held selected members of a community, not a complete census of the living.

Their thinking is easiest to approach with patience. The open court faced the living. People could gather, speak, offer, remember. The gallery held a few of the dead and kept them close to the mountain and the view of sea and strand. 

The monument claims a place as well as a lineage. To raise such stones is to say that this slope belongs to memory as well as to grazing and tillage. It is a house for ancestors that the living could still approach. That is a careful, communal way of thinking, not a private one.

Modern scanning can listen to the ground without moving a stone. Drone and airborne LiDAR can pick out low banks, sockets, and field walls hidden under heather and bog. Ground-penetrating radar can search for voids, collapsed chambers, and buried cairn material. 

Magnetometry and electromagnetic induction can show burnt ground and stone settings. Photogrammetry and handheld or tablet LiDAR can build a precise three-dimensional record of every visible slab. 

Thermal drone survey and, more recently, drone-mounted radar have been used on Irish megaliths to look inside mounds without a trowel. Together these methods can map what still lies unseen and leave the monument as it stands.

Walk softly if you go. The stones have already outlasted many weathers and many lives.

The story of Pierce Nagle is interesting. He was the insider the British police had in the Fenian newspaper The Irish People, apparently he was born near Clonmel. He  informed the police about plans for the 1865 Fenian rising, and was given £200 a year by the British Gov. He was later found dear in London. 

I know that an ancestor of mine was in the Young Irelanders and was born near Clonmel as were many other Tipperary Fenians. I am guessing this is why he was trusted by the Tipp Fenians, as they probably knew him since he was a kid. 

This is what Grok said about him. 

Pierce Nagle was a low-level employee of the Fenian newspaper The Irish People who became the government’s key inside informer in 1865. His evidence helped smash the IRB’s Dublin organisation before the 1867 rising.
Background. He was born near Clonmel, County Tipperary. He worked as a national-school teacher and as a parish clerk; he later lost the church post amid an unproved claim that he had taken altar property. He went to America, then came back to Dublin in 1863. He got a job as a folder in the Irish People office on Parliament Street and also taught at the Dublin Mechanics’ Institute. He was sacristan at St Laurence O’Toole’s church on the North Strand. Colleagues treated him as a trusted, if junior, man; James Stephens even sent him on a confidential errand to Tipperary. https://t.co/DSkINAUUU2 
Informer. In New York in 1864 he was reportedly offended by Stephens’s manner and offered his services to the British. In Dublin he was in contact with Superintendent Daniel Ryan of the DMP’s G Division (political detectives). He later said he had taken the Fenian oath in order to inform. In September 1865 he removed a letter from a sleeping messenger in the newspaper office — Stephens writing that 1865 must be “the year of action” — and gave it to Ryan. That letter, plus other papers he supplied, triggered the raid of 15 September 1865. He was arrested with the rest of the staff as cover, then turned Queen’s evidence with another office employee, Patrick Power. https://t.co/kiq41Sbh2x 
Afterward. The government put him on a pension of about £200 a year. He lived in Kingstown (Dún Laoghaire). In 1879 he stopped collecting the money and vanished. Irish and American papers reported that police believed a man found murdered under a railway arch in east London was Nagle; Fenian sources claimed their “vigilance” men had tracked him down after recognising him working again as a book-folder. https://t.co/DSkINAUUU2 
He was not a Fenian leader. He was a clerkish insider whose access to the paper and to Stephens’s correspondence made him valuable. That is why his name stuck: the raid on The Irish People and the 1865–66 trials rested heavily on what he stole and what he swore in court.

text:
THE SPANISH EMPIRE'S DECLINE: A LESSON FROM AN OTTOMAN DIPLOMAT IN 1787
(THE SAME DECLINE THAT THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE WAS EXPERIENCING, IN THE END.)

The text offers a profound historical analysis, as told through the eyes of Ahmet Vâsıf Efendi, an Ottoman diplomat who visited Spain in 1787. His observations provide a timeless warning about the dangers of an economy built on extraction without production, a lesson that resonates today. The story of Spain's decline is a case study in how a state can exhaust its resources and undermine its own long-term prosperity.

THE CURSE OF SILVER AND GOLD

Vâsıf Efendi's core diagnosis is that the vast wealth from the Americas did not create a lasting industry in Spain. Instead, it made the economy "lazy." Rather than investing in domestic manufacturing, the Spanish simply bought everything they needed from England and France. This turned the empire's gold into a river of cash that flowed directly to its rivals, funding their industrial revolutions and enriching them.

THE DESTRUCTION OF THE HUMAN CAPITAL

The diplomat also identified a more profound structural problem. The expulsion of Muslims and Jews, who were the engineers, artisans, and productive backbone of the country, removed the very skills needed to build a modern economy. What remained were fertile lands that lay fallow and a population that lacked the necessary skills to develop them. Spain had effectively destroyed its own human capital.

THE NOBILITY AND THE CHURCH: A DRAIN ON THE ECONOMY

Vâsıf Efendi noted that the Spanish nobility refused to engage in commerce or manual labor. This left thousands of people dependent on the state, contributing nothing to the economy. Similarly, he observed that the vast number of clergy and monasteries, who produced nothing, were a drain on the treasury. This created a massive, unproductive class that consumed wealth without generating it. The system was designed to extract and consume, not to produce and innovate.

A COURT OF BEGGARS

The most striking moment in the account is Vâsıf Efendi's description of the Spanish court's reaction to the sultan's gifts. When he delivered the official gifts for the king, the rest of the royal family openly demanded a share, treating the diplomatic mission like a minor inheritance dispute. They even pressured him to give them his personal belongings. This behavior, Vâsıf Efendi noted, revealed the "moral poverty" and "exhaustion" of a ruling class that had become mere beggars, dependent on handouts, and unaware of its own corruption.

THE COST OF EMPIRE

The diplomat also observed the economic drain of maintaining a vast empire. The cost of defending a map that stretched from the Pacific to the Atlantic was immense, consuming far more than the wealth it generated. The palaces were grand, but the state was decaying from within. He described a system where the ruling class lived in a parasitic world, consuming the empire's wealth but unable to build a lasting foundation for the future.

The Spanish Empire's decline was not caused by external enemies but by its own internal failures. The lesson Vâsıf Efendi documented nearly 240 years ago is still relevant: an economy that extracts wealth without investing in productive capacity, that destroys its human capital, and that allows a parasitic class to drain its resources is ultimately doomed to collapse.

text:
Somewhere, Roy Cohn Is Smiling

NYT Gift Article link
Listen · 7:42 min
07SEP2026
By Carlos Lozada
https://t.co/Ce07EOgU9u

At this point in the Trumpian arc, we’re all too familiar with the president’s methods: Deny everything; apologize for nothing. 

Hog the spotlight. 

Counterattack, counterpunch, countersue. 

Always declare victory, even when you lose (especially when you lose). 

Resentment sells. Nativism sells. 

Cruelty, if not yet normal, becomes the norm. 

Rules and traditions are for suckers; everyone is, if not corrupt, at least corruptible.

These are President Trump’s instincts, yes. 

But before they were his, they were Roy Cohn’s.

Kai Bird’s new book, “American Scoundrel,” written with Susan Goldmark (Bird’s wife and chief researcher), is a biography of Cohn, the sinister 20th-century lawyer who served as chief counsel to Joe McCarthy when the junior senator from Wisconsin was Red Scaring America and as lawyer to Trump when the young real estate developer was deflecting allegations of discrimination against prospective Black tenants. 

“American Scoundrel” is very much a how-we-got-here book, showing how Cohn’s guile, paranoia and shamelessness guided McCarthy, rubbed off on Trump and stuck fast to America.

The day after winning the 2016 election, Trump was on the phone with Roger Stone, his friend and adviser and longtime Cohn ally. 

“Wouldn’t Roy love to see this moment?” the president-elect said wistfully of Cohn, who died in 1986. 

“Boy, do we miss him.” 

And just months later, when the president fumed that Jeff Sessions, then the attorney general, was failing to protect him, an irate Trump demanded, “Where’s my Roy Cohn?”

If he really wanted to find Cohn, all Trump had to do was look in the mirror.

The Cohn-Trump parallels are evident on nearly every page of “American Scoundrel,” so much so that Bird barely needs to point them out. 

From a young age, for example, Cohn traded on the influence of his father, a New York judge, much as Trump would lean on the wealth and connections of his own father, Fred Trump. 

At 16, Cohn got one of his high school teachers out of a traffic ticket by calling the police precinct — “I’m sure you know who my father is” — and later relied on paternal clout to secure a job as an assistant U.S. attorney in New York.

Cohn became obsessed with publicizing his accomplishments — “I didn’t count it as winning if the world didn’t know about it” — and cultivated gossip columnists to stay in the headlines. 

(Not that he needed much help: Cohn’s role in the prosecution of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg established his name in legal and anti-Communist circles, even before his work for McCarthy made him a national figure.) 

To Cohn, “personal loyalty was everything,” Bird writes, and his disregard for legalities was captured in his maxim “Don’t tell me the law. Tell me the judge.”

He was even terrible at paying his bills, “another lesson Trump learned from Cohn,” Bird writes. 

Like his protégé, Cohn was indicted several times and was constantly under I.R.S. audit. 

At his birthday party in 1980, friends presented Cohn with a cake featuring his own scowling visage. 

(No word if T-shirts were available.) 

People who knew both men recognized that some of Trump’s verbal tics — “if you want to know the truth” and “I can tell you” — trace back to Cohn.

Cohn also liked to talk about crowd size. In 1963, after pleading not guilty to charges of perjury and obstruction of justice, Cohn stood outside a Manhattan courthouse and told the assembled reporters that it was the “biggest crowd I’ve seen since the Army-McCarthy hearings.” 

And when he gave a party in Washington celebrating Ronald Reagan’s 1980 election, Cohn boasted about the celebrities in attendance (Barbara Walters and Andy Warhol, among others) and bragged that “we had the biggest crowd.”

Oh, and Cohn sported a permanent tan, too.

Beyond style and temperament, Cohn and Trump shared a political template. 

Cohn “excelled at performative politics,” Bird writes, purporting to stand for the working class while riding around in a Rolls-Royce or hosting parties aboard his yacht, the Defiance. 

Both men saw history “through a lens tinted by conspiracy,” branding their rivals as Communists, radicals or denizens of the “deep state.” 

In a 1978 profile by Ken Auletta, which Bird cites, Cohn assails liberals for believing that “we must be loved by the rest of the world, which happens to hate us,” rather than focusing on national interests. 

“There’s nothing particularly original about Trump’s macho instincts in foreign policy,” Bird argues. They came from Cohn.

“The McCarthyism of the 1950s,” Bird writes, “morphed into a nativist, America Firster politics that transformed the modern Republican Party into a party of resentments against the old establishment, against multiculturalism, globalization and liberal culture” — with Cohn serving as connective tissue between McCarthy and Trump. Reading “American Scoundrel,” I sometimes wondered why the title wasn’t plural.

A journalist who interviewed Cohn at length offered an assessment that could fit Trump just as well: “He harbored a bundle of thinly concealed prejudices that he’d trot out whenever one or more of them worked for him, whenever they were useful.” 

The question for our time is: How long might they prove useful?

“Roy Cohn’s McCarthyism would long outlast McCarthy and would poison the American political landscape for decades to come,” Bird writes. 

Trumpism, too, may mutate and endure, even when Trump himself — weighed down by war, worn down by low public approval, slowed down by age — begins to recede from view.

“Why was McCarthy discredited but not McCarthyism?” Bird asks. 

In part, he concludes, it was because President Dwight Eisenhower declined to attack the senator directly, no matter the entreaties of Eisenhower’s advisers, including his younger brother Milton Eisenhower, who urged the president to “tear McCarthy to pieces.” 

Even as McCarthyism split the country and infected the Republican Party, the president “never took the political risk to ridicule McCarthy’s assumptions,” Bird writes. 

Eisenhower decided that ignoring the senator was better than elevating him through direct confrontation.
How often have we seen such calculations from Republican leaders during the Trump years, with painful and predictable results? 

The slide from amusement to dismay to toleration and finally to capitulation has been short but steep, and we may be stuck at the bottom for a while. 

The paranoia of McCarthyism “persisted as a routine feature of American life,” long after McCarthy exited the stage, Bird writes, leaving “a festering wound on the nation’s psyche.” 

Trump, under the tutelage of McCarthy’s former aide, learned to pick at that wound, making sure it kept bleeding.

Bird is a chronicler of the American establishment; his prior subjects include presidents like Jimmy Carter, advisers like McGeorge Bundy and scientists like Robert Oppenheimer. Cohn lurked around the edges of these stories, the anti-establishment force who both fed off and sabotaged the establishment. 

Now, with Trump, Cohn’s politics have won; the establishment has been dispatched, co-opted, emasculated. 

What remains, Bird writes, is a “subversive counternarrative” of American power.

In an interview with Times reporters early this year, Trump said that the only constraint he felt on his power was, well, himself. “My own morality,” he said. 

“My own mind. It’s the only thing that can stop me.” 

Bird does not make this comparison, but Trump’s words evoke Cohn’s, yet again, from a Penthouse interview 45 years ago. 

“I decided long ago to make my own rules,” he said, “to act according to my own choices, my own judgments and my own conscience.”

Where’s our Roy Cohn? Sitting in the Oval Office.

text:
Somewhere, Roy Cohn Is Smiling

NYT Gift Article link
Listen · 7:42 min
07SEP2026
By Carlos Lozada
https://t.co/Ce07EOgU9u

At this point in the Trumpian arc, we’re all too familiar with the president’s methods: Deny everything; apologize for nothing. 

Hog the spotlight. 

Counterattack, counterpunch, countersue. 

Always declare victory, even when you lose (especially when you lose). 

Resentment sells. Nativism sells. 

Cruelty, if not yet normal, becomes the norm. 

Rules and traditions are for suckers; everyone is, if not corrupt, at least corruptible.

These are President Trump’s instincts, yes. 

But before they were his, they were Roy Cohn’s.

Kai Bird’s new book, “American Scoundrel,” written with Susan Goldmark (Bird’s wife and chief researcher), is a biography of Cohn, the sinister 20th-century lawyer who served as chief counsel to Joe McCarthy when the junior senator from Wisconsin was Red Scaring America and as lawyer to Trump when the young real estate developer was deflecting allegations of discrimination against prospective Black tenants. 

“American Scoundrel” is very much a how-we-got-here book, showing how Cohn’s guile, paranoia and shamelessness guided McCarthy, rubbed off on Trump and stuck fast to America.

The day after winning the 2016 election, Trump was on the phone with Roger Stone, his friend and adviser and longtime Cohn ally. 

“Wouldn’t Roy love to see this moment?” the president-elect said wistfully of Cohn, who died in 1986. 

“Boy, do we miss him.” 

And just months later, when the president fumed that Jeff Sessions, then the attorney general, was failing to protect him, an irate Trump demanded, “Where’s my Roy Cohn?”

If he really wanted to find Cohn, all Trump had to do was look in the mirror.

The Cohn-Trump parallels are evident on nearly every page of “American Scoundrel,” so much so that Bird barely needs to point them out. 

From a young age, for example, Cohn traded on the influence of his father, a New York judge, much as Trump would lean on the wealth and connections of his own father, Fred Trump. 

At 16, Cohn got one of his high school teachers out of a traffic ticket by calling the police precinct — “I’m sure you know who my father is” — and later relied on paternal clout to secure a job as an assistant U.S. attorney in New York.

Cohn became obsessed with publicizing his accomplishments — “I didn’t count it as winning if the world didn’t know about it” — and cultivated gossip columnists to stay in the headlines. 

(Not that he needed much help: Cohn’s role in the prosecution of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg established his name in legal and anti-Communist circles, even before his work for McCarthy made him a national figure.) 

To Cohn, “personal loyalty was everything,” Bird writes, and his disregard for legalities was captured in his maxim “Don’t tell me the law. Tell me the judge.”

He was even terrible at paying his bills, “another lesson Trump learned from Cohn,” Bird writes. 

Like his protégé, Cohn was indicted several times and was constantly under I.R.S. audit. 

At his birthday party in 1980, friends presented Cohn with a cake featuring his own scowling visage. 

(No word if T-shirts were available.) 

People who knew both men recognized that some of Trump’s verbal tics — “if you want to know the truth” and “I can tell you” — trace back to Cohn.

Cohn also liked to talk about crowd size. In 1963, after pleading not guilty to charges of perjury and obstruction of justice, Cohn stood outside a Manhattan courthouse and told the assembled reporters that it was the “biggest crowd I’ve seen since the Army-McCarthy hearings.” 

And when he gave a party in Washington celebrating Ronald Reagan’s 1980 election, Cohn boasted about the celebrities in attendance (Barbara Walters and Andy Warhol, among others) and bragged that “we had the biggest crowd.”

Oh, and Cohn sported a permanent tan, too.

Beyond style and temperament, Cohn and Trump shared a political template. 

Cohn “excelled at performative politics,” Bird writes, purporting to stand for the working class while riding around in a Rolls-Royce or hosting parties aboard his yacht, the Defiance. 

Both men saw history “through a lens tinted by conspiracy,” branding their rivals as Communists, radicals or denizens of the “deep state.” 

In a 1978 profile by Ken Auletta, which Bird cites, Cohn assails liberals for believing that “we must be loved by the rest of the world, which happens to hate us,” rather than focusing on national interests. 

“There’s nothing particularly original about Trump’s macho instincts in foreign policy,” Bird argues. They came from Cohn.

“The McCarthyism of the 1950s,” Bird writes, “morphed into a nativist, America Firster politics that transformed the modern Republican Party into a party of resentments against the old establishment, against multiculturalism, globalization and liberal culture” — with Cohn serving as connective tissue between McCarthy and Trump. Reading “American Scoundrel,” I sometimes wondered why the title wasn’t plural.

A journalist who interviewed Cohn at length offered an assessment that could fit Trump just as well: “He harbored a bundle of thinly concealed prejudices that he’d trot out whenever one or more of them worked for him, whenever they were useful.” 

The question for our time is: How long might they prove useful?

“Roy Cohn’s McCarthyism would long outlast McCarthy and would poison the American political landscape for decades to come,” Bird writes. 

Trumpism, too, may mutate and endure, even when Trump himself — weighed down by war, worn down by low public approval, slowed down by age — begins to recede from view.

“Why was McCarthy discredited but not McCarthyism?” Bird asks. 

In part, he concludes, it was because President Dwight Eisenhower declined to attack the senator directly, no matter the entreaties of Eisenhower’s advisers, including his younger brother Milton Eisenhower, who urged the president to “tear McCarthy to pieces.” 

Even as McCarthyism split the country and infected the Republican Party, the president “never took the political risk to ridicule McCarthy’s assumptions,” Bird writes. 

Eisenhower decided that ignoring the senator was better than elevating him through direct confrontation.
How often have we seen such calculations from Republican leaders during the Trump years, with painful and predictable results? 

The slide from amusement to dismay to toleration and finally to capitulation has been short but steep, and we may be stuck at the bottom for a while. 

The paranoia of McCarthyism “persisted as a routine feature of American life,” long after McCarthy exited the stage, Bird writes, leaving “a festering wound on the nation’s psyche.” 

Trump, under the tutelage of McCarthy’s former aide, learned to pick at that wound, making sure it kept bleeding.

Bird is a chronicler of the American establishment; his prior subjects include presidents like Jimmy Carter, advisers like McGeorge Bundy and scientists like Robert Oppenheimer. Cohn lurked around the edges of these stories, the anti-establishment force who both fed off and sabotaged the establishment. 

Now, with Trump, Cohn’s politics have won; the establishment has been dispatched, co-opted, emasculated. 

What remains, Bird writes, is a “subversive counternarrative” of American power.

In an interview with Times reporters early this year, Trump said that the only constraint he felt on his power was, well, himself. “My own morality,” he said. 

“My own mind. It’s the only thing that can stop me.” 

Bird does not make this comparison, but Trump’s words evoke Cohn’s, yet again, from a Penthouse interview 45 years ago. 

“I decided long ago to make my own rules,” he said, “to act according to my own choices, my own judgments and my own conscience.”

Where’s our Roy Cohn? Sitting in the Oval Office.

Arakhamia, who profits from the production of drones during this war, and his boss, President Zelensky, are posing in a T-shirt that says “Kyiv Regime.”

The joke is built around the word “regime.” In this context, it means a dictatorial or authoritarian government — a non-democratic political system.

Russia constantly refers to the Ukrainian government as the “Kyiv regime,” accusing it of becoming authoritarian, particularly because Ukraine has not held presidential elections, while opposition politicians who advocate peace have been arrested, thrown in prison, killed, or driven out of the country.

Now Zelensky is trying to mock this criticism by essentially embracing the label and turning it into a joke: Yes, we are the “Kyiv regime.” And he is proud of it.

At the very same time, his deputy had been arrested by an independent anti-corruption agency and was being held in pre-trial detention; his other ally, Andriy Yermak, the head of the Presidential Office, was under investigation for corruption; and none of Zelensky’s relatives serve in the army.

*India: Not an Inspiration...but a Warning*Its the Jaichands within thst we need to be careful of.

Its the corrupt officers who allowed the renovation of the building and not the CM or the PM,or HM.

*Japan, a nation decimated by two nuclear bombs, didn't beg for sympathy or aid. It rebuilt itself with pride and an unshakeable sense of self-respect*. In the years since, it has never once stretched out a hand to America for alms.

An Indian man living in Japan for over a decade was about to leave Japan for good. He observed during his stay that no Japanese ever discussed or asked him much about India!

So, he had been a bit curious and asked his closest Japanese friend prior to departure: *What Japanese think about India & Indians in general?*

After a long pause, the friend replied, 
*"We are taught Indian history... not for inspiration, but as a warning."*

Confused, the Indian man asked, "A warning?"

"*Tell me," the Japanese friend continued, "how many British ruled India?"*
The Indian man thought, "Perhaps... around 10,000?"
The Japanese man nodded grimly. "And how many Indians lived there? Over 300 million, right?"
"Then who oppressed your people? Who carried out the orders to whip, torture, and shoot them?" he pressed. 

"*When General Dyer gave the command 'Fire!*' *at Jallianwala Bagh, who pulled the trigger?* The soldiers weren't British; they were Indian."
"Not one turned their rifle on the tyrant. Not one," he said. "*You want to talk about slavery? That was your real slavery. Not of the body, but of the soul."*

The Indian man stood frozen, silent, and ashamed.

*The Japanese friend went on, "How many Mughals came from Central Asia? A few thousand maybe?* And yet they ruled you for centuries. They built empires not with their numbers, but because *your own people bowed their heads and offered their loyalty in exchange for survival... or silver."*

"*Your own people converted. Your own brothers became instruments of their oppression. Your own men handed over your heroes*. Chandrashekhar Azad was betrayed. Bhagat Singh faced the gallows without even a whisper of help from those who called themselves patriots," he said.

"*You don't need foreign enemies. YOUR OWN PEOPLE BETRAY YOU AGAIN AND AGAIN FOR POWER, POSITION, AND PERSONAL GAIN. That is why we keep our distance.*"

"*When the British came to Hong Kong and Singapore, not one native man joined their army. But in India, you didn’t just join the enemy. You served them.* Worshipped them. Killed your own people to please them."

"*Even today, you haven’t changed*. Offer some free electricity, a bottle of liquor, a blanket—and your vote, your conscience, your voice are all sold without a second thought. *YOUR LOYALTY LIES NOT WITH YOUR NATION, BUT WITH YOUR STOMACH*," he said.

"You chant slogans. You march in protests. But when the country needs your character, where are you? YOUR FIRST LOYALTY IS STILL TO YOURSELF AND YOUR FAMILY. EVERYTHING ELSE —SOCIETY, DHARMA, THE COUNTRY —CAN BURN."

*He ended with one final statement:*
"If your nation is not strong, your home will never be safe. If your character is weak, no flag can protect you."

*This is not mockery. It is a mirror.*

Perhaps the time has come for us to stop looking away, because India doesn’t need more patriots in speeches. *IT NEEDS CITIZENS OF UNSHAKEABLE CHARACTER. NOT JUST FREEDOM FIGHTERS, BUT FREEDOM KEEPERS. NOT JUST FLAGS IN OUR HANDS, BUT LOYALTY IN OUR HEARTS*.

It is bitter. But it is true.

HOPE IT Shakes our conscience and please spread the word🙏 one person at a time, can do wonders to this country.

text:
This war must end. Unless one is blind, one can see that the future will bring catastrophe. Zelensky in the first year of the war saved Ukraine’s sovereign independence. The Russian army resorted to digging big holes and jumping in them. 

Ukraine made no progress in evicting Russia over the next few bloody years. How could Ukraine regain momentum?  He chose the strategy that President Biden had red-lined at the inception of the war: striking targets deep inside Russia. Bombarding its capital and crowing about it.

Zelensky knew there would be retaliation, and he knew that his cities could not defend themselves. But he had nothing more to offer than a false hope. Russia’s ability to retaliate was always greater than Ukraine’s ability to strike. And with its European allies supplying funds and weapons and intelligence, Russia increasingly wonders why it does not strike their capitals.

How soon before combat breaks out with NATO? Did Ukraine’s think it could win a ground war by air attack alone? Give the Ukrainian people a chance to vote for the first time in seven years and will they tell Zelensky how they feel? All the enthusiasm about being the world leader in defending against drones disappeared when Russia attached jet engines to its drones.

And the price for ending this epic is to give Russia the rest of Donbas including its Eastern fortresses.  Will this just ease Russia’s way after it regroups and resumed its invasion? It is highly unlikely that Russia will repeat this behavior after being so blooded the first time. And if the rest of Europe agreed to Russia’s rather reasonable request that Ukraine not join NATO, the risk of another invasion drops far below the risk of continuing this war.

I am not a Russian traitor, although I do think highly of Tchaikovsky. The New York City Ballet will present his Nutcracker for the 75th year this Christmas. This is realpolitik, rejecting the fable that this is a good vs. evil affair that can be won. Choose lives over territory, especially when that territory is the part of your country with the most cultural and economic ties to Russia and has been reduced to depopulated rubble after 13 years of conflict.

text:
I wouldn't say, explicitly "unbiblical" but I would say it's an OT anachronysm, so it depends a bit on what 'unbiblical' means.

Judas Maccabeus and his men lived before the cross. They already believed in resurrection and in the possibility that sin still needed to be dealt with after death, so they offered a sin offering and prayed. Once Christ dies and rises, the New Testament presents that offering as complete and final. Hebrews 9:27–28 and 10:10–14 are the usual texts: people die once and then face judgment; Christ’s single sacrifice perfects those who are being sanctified. On this view the Maccabean practice is fulfilled rather than continued, the same way temple sacrifices, the Levitical priesthood, and certain intertestamental hopes are fulfilled.

The sculpture is carved from a massive block of sandstone and is attributed to the period of Kalchuri king Kokkaldev II, around the 10th to 11th century. It measures approximately 8.5 by 3.5 metres. Its immense weight suggests that, although the sculptors completed the carving, they were unable to transport it, leaving it where it was carved.

Until the late 1960s, local shepherds reportedly used it as a sitting stone, while some devotees continued to visit it once a year on particular occasions to offer prayers. There is also a local belief that a similar Ganesha idol lies somewhere nearby.

More recently, the State Archaeology Department has developed a substantial temple at the site.

Labor Day (Mon. Sept. 7) is a federal holiday and all outpatient clinics and administrative offices throughout the VA Maryland Health Care System will be closed. Here are some important reminders for how to connect to important VA health care resources.
Veterans Crisis Line - If you are having thoughts of hurting yourself or you want to speak with a mental health professional, call the Veterans Crisis Line 24 hours a day, 7 days a week at 988, Press 1. 
Emergency - If you have a life-threatening emergency, call 911. The Emergency Department at the Baltimore VA Medical Center is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week – even during Federal holidays. Once the immediate emergency medical care needs have been addressed, the Veteran, a family member, a friend, or a hospital staff member should call the VA’s National Emergency Notification Center at 844-724-7842 within 72 hours.
Urgent Care - The VA offers urgent care services to eligible Veterans at in-network urgent care clinics in the community. You can use the VA’s urgent care benefit to treat minor injuries and illnesses that are not life-threatening. For a listing of in-network urgent care providers in your community, visit https://t.co/7gsVo8lz3P or call VA’s Office of Community Care at 877-881-7618 Monday – Friday between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.
VA Health Connect - If you have a medical concern, please call 1-855-679-0250 and select 3. A Registered Nurse is available to assist you 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Refill Medication/Medication Questions – Contact 1-855-679-0250 and select 1 to refill your prescriptions.
