text:
Weekend altcoin rally runs out of road as bitcoin slips

The weekend’s speculative fire has been extinguished, at least for now. Bitcoin slipped 1.1% since midnight UTC, dragging the momentum out of an altcoin rally that saw several tokens post double-digit gains just 48 hours ago. The pullback comes even as traditional risk assets showed resilience, with Nasdaq 100 futures edging up 0.3% in early trading, highlighting a divergence that traders are watching closely.

WHAT HAPPENED

The digital asset market cooled off sharply on Monday after a volatile weekend session. According to market data, Bitcoin (BTC) retreated to session lows, erasing gains that had pushed the asset toward key resistance levels late last week. The move lower effectively stalled the advance in major altcoins, many of which had surged between 10% and 15% over the weekend before giving back a significant portion of those gains.

This pullback is notable because it occurred against a backdrop of relative strength in equities. The Nasdaq 100 futures trading higher suggests that the selling pressure in crypto is not part of a broader risk-off move across all asset classes. Instead, it points to profit-taking within the crypto ecosystem specifically, likely triggered by traders locking in gains from the weekend’s volatility spike.

The funding rates and open interest data across major exchanges like Binance and Coinbase suggest that leveraged long positions were the primary casualty of this move. When Bitcoin fails to hold its ground while equities climb, it often signals that the crypto market is dealing with internal leverage issues rather than macro-driven outflows.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR CRYPTO

The failure of the weekend rally to sustain itself is a significant technical signal. For weeks, the crypto market has been range-bound, with Bitcoin struggling to break above its 200-day moving average. The weekend altcoin surge offered a glimmer of hope that risk appetite was returning to the sector. However, Monday’s fade suggests that buyers are still unwilling to chase strength at higher levels.

For the broader digital asset market, this price action reinforces the current consolidation phase. Altcoins, which typically have higher beta than Bitcoin, are often the first to rally when sentiment shifts and the first to fall when it doesn't stick. The fact that these gains evaporated so quickly indicates that the market lacks the organic buying pressure needed to sustain a breakout.

The divergence with the Nasdaq is crucial context. If the stock market continues to grind higher while Bitcoin stalls, capital may remain on the sidelines in traditional equities rather than rotating into crypto. However, analysts suggest that this relationship is not fixed; a sudden shift in the Federal Reserve policy expectations could quickly reverse the flow of funds.

WHAT TRADERS SHOULD WATCH

The immediate focus for traders should be on the daily close price of Bitcoin. If BTC can reclaim its position above the recent consolidation range, the failed rally might be viewed as a mere shakeout. Conversely, a decisive break below the lower boundary of the range could open the door to a retest of the summer lows, where strong support has previously been established.

Volume analysis will be key in the coming sessions. Monday’s sell-off appears to be on average volume, but a spike in selling pressure would confirm bearish intent. Traders should also monitor the altcoin/BTC pairs. If Ethereum, Solana, and other majors start bleeding value against Bitcoin, it signals that the risk-on rotation within crypto is officially over for the short term.

Regulatory headlines remain a wildcard. The recent activity from the CFTC regarding digital asset derivatives has injected a level of uncertainty into the market that was absent earlier in the year. Any unexpected legal or regulatory development could easily override technical patterns, so keeping one eye on Washington is essential for risk management.

MARKET SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

The current sentiment is NEUTRAL, reflecting a market that is directionless despite high volatility. On one hand, the weekend rally showed that dip-buyers are active and willing to step in on weakness. On the other hand, the swift reversal demonstrates that there is no shortage of sellers looking to offload inventory into any strength.

In the short term, the path of least resistance appears to be sideways. The market needs a catalyst—either a macroeconomic shift or a significant regulatory approval—to break out of this pattern. For the long term, the structural adoption story remains intact, but the price action suggests that traders are waiting for more clarity before committing fresh capital. Until Bitcoin establishes a clear direction, expect the altcoin market to remain erratic and driven primarily by speculation rather than fundamentals.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did the altcoin rally stall despite stock futures rising?
The divergence between crypto and equities suggests the weekend rally was driven by speculative leverage rather than institutional allocation. When Bitcoin failed to lead the charge, momentum traders exited altcoin positions to lock in profits. The crypto market is currently dealing with internal liquidity constraints that are preventing it from participating in the broader risk-on tone seen in traditional markets.

Is this a good entry point for Bitcoin or a sign of more downside?
That depends on your time horizon. For short-term traders, the failed breakout is a bearish signal that suggests waiting for a lower support retest is prudent. For long-term investors, the current price levels remain attractive relative to historical adoption curves. However, with sentiment neutral, it is wise to scale into positions rather than deploy full capital at once, as the market has not confirmed a bottom.

What specific levels should I monitor for a potential trend reversal?
Traders should watch the immediate support zone below the current price, where buying interest has historically been strong. A daily close above the recent swing high would invalidate the bearish setup and signal a potential trend change. Additionally, monitoring funding rates on major exchanges is crucial; a reset to negative funding often precedes a short squeeze that can ignite a new rally.

text:
Talks collapsed on 21 August. Washington put 50 per cent Section 338 duties on a slice both capitals put near US$20 billion. Ottawa promised to match it dollar for dollar from 8 September on about C$27.6 billion of American goods. Energy and most minerals were carved out because Gulf Coast refiners still want the heavy barrel this season. That is residual industrial fact, not a diplomatic scalp. A further American line already sits on 1 January 2027 for Canadian cars, trucks, parts and steel. Mexico kept bargaining over content. We walked, then reached for martial adjectives.

You write as if the operating system of this country is a mood. It is not. On an ordinary weekday about 15,000 trucks still cross the longest undefended border on earth. Something north of 70 per cent of Canadian merchandise still goes south. That is the national payroll. Everything else is commentary. Calling the neighbour “cowards” does not move a single one of those trucks. Calling the president “demented” does not finish a plant.

The more expensive tariff was already Canadian. The IMF has estimated that non-geographic barriers inside this federation behave like a national duty of about nine per cent, and that dismantling them could raise real output by around seven per cent, in today’s money, something like C$210 billion. Specialist waits stretch toward half a year. Public tallies have put hundreds of billions of energy, mining and infrastructure proposals behind stacked reviews and unresolved title. Trans Mountain left the public books at C$7.4 billion and arrived in the low thirties. Of eighteen large LNG schemes, one large terminal is in service and two are being built. That is the capacity problem. Matching a list of American appliances and cheese does not repair it.

A serious country can refuse a bad text. Both sides described a package that would have parked the 50 per cent slice and cut metals and autos. Ottawa said last-minute American terms touched culture, language and the freedom to sign elsewhere. Fine. Publish the rejected pages so citizens can price “sovereignty” against clause. What we got instead was “we got attacked” and a seating chart: a Major Projects Office still telling capital the shovel-ready stock is thin, a January opening with Beijing sold as diversification while CSIS still ranks the same state as the most active interferer on Canadian ground, and a European diary offered as a second table while the first customer writes the bill.

Integrated supply chains will hurt both sides. That part of your post is not wrong. The error is the conclusion you draw from it. Mutual pain is not a strategy when one market absorbs three-quarters of what you make and the other side has already named the next date. Retaliation is easy. Building is hard. Quiet, clinical, devastating policy would look like one energy or minerals corridor financed twice before January 2027, signed capital, a smaller title map, permits with clocks, not a sermon about national resolve over a waving flag.

I do not need Washington’s adjectives and I do not need yours. Courtesy is not a strategy. Neither is spite. Access is not a birthright. Production before process. Capacity before jurisdiction.

Precision over propaganda.  
Evidence over excuses.  
Truth Marker: π ≈ 3.14159.

text:
What if Scott Bessent and Kevin Warsh get the stable dollar they want… and that ends up being one of the most bullish outcomes possible for $XRP?

That sounds backwards until you look at what Ripple has actually built.

Bessent wants dollar dominance protected.

He wants regulated stablecoins extending the dollar onto internet-native rails.

He has argued that stablecoins can push dollar access to billions of people and create additional demand for U.S. Treasuries.

Treasury is already implementing the GENIUS Act, with Bessent explicitly tying the framework to cementing the dollar’s reserve-currency role.

Warsh has reinforced the other half of the equation:

price stability and trustworthy money.

So imagine America succeeds.

The dollar stays dominant.

Treasuries remain the world’s core safe asset.

Stablecoins grow into a multitrillion-dollar market.

Instead of weakening the XRP thesis, I think that creates a much larger market for it.

Ripple already has RLUSD.

As of September 3, about $2.3956B was circulating against roughly $2.5177B in reserve assets.

Those reserves can hold short-term Treasuries and other regulated dollar assets, with BNY as primary custodian.

Now zoom out from the stablecoin itself.

Ondo OUSG is on XRP Ledger.

Qualified institutions can use RLUSD for 24/7 minting and redemption into tokenized Treasury exposure.

BlackRock BUIDL and VanEck VBILL holders have RLUSD liquidity functionality through Ripple and Securitize.

So XRPL can increasingly sit between two things Washington wants to remain powerful:

the dollar

and

U.S. government debt.

Here is the part I think gets really interesting.

A digital dollar can dominate globally and still need foreign exchange.

A Mexican company starts with pesos.

A Japanese institution starts with yen.

A European fund starts with euros.

They may all want access to dollars, Treasuries or dollar-denominated markets.

Ripple and Bitso already have MXNB and RLUSD positioned inside XRPL’s institutional liquidity environment.

That gives us a simple model:

MXNB → XRP → RLUSD

if XRP provides the best liquidity route.

Now scale that idea.

Tokenized JPY.

Tokenized EUR.

Tokenized BRL.

Tokenized SGD.

Tokenized deposits.

Foreign bonds.

Funds.

Private credit.

Hundreds of digital assets cannot all maintain perfect direct liquidity against one another.

Software starts choosing the cheapest path.

If XRP repeatedly offers the deepest route, institutions do not need to become “XRP believers.”

Their systems simply use it.

That is far more interesting to me than a bank announcing that it loves XRP.

It is machine-selected liquidity.

And Ripple has positioned itself around the markets where that routing would matter.

Ripple Prime reports more than $3T in annual clearing and 300+ institutional customers across FX, fixed income, repo, precious metals, derivatives and digital assets.

Ripple has preliminary conditional approval for Ripple National Trust Bank.

Brad Garlinghouse has direct access to the Washington policy conversation.

Trump wants America to remain the crypto capital of the world.

Bessent wants a dominant dollar.

Warsh wants stable money.

Ripple already has a regulated digital dollar, tokenized Treasury access, institutional liquidity infrastructure and a native bridge asset.

So I’m done thinking about $XRP as something that needs to defeat the dollar.

The bigger setup could be the opposite:

The dollar wins harder, becomes digital, reaches more of the world… and $XRP becomes part of the liquidity infrastructure connecting everyone to it.

News Flashback

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

$Optionspad is a launchpad on Robinhood Chain where the coin you launch is the option itself. (50kmc) 

  TLDR: the tech is real and it is finished. I read the whole exchange out of the deployed bytecode rather than the docs. the part nobody has mentioned is that it has been live for seventeen hours and not one market has been launched on it yet, by anyone, including the
  team.

  here is what that actually means.
  
  you pick a market, two strike prices and an expiry date. the factory mints you two ERC-20s, a call and a put, both backed by the same dollar of USDG, and opens a pool between them. the two always redeem to one dollar together. so if you buy the call and you are right,
  the money comes out of the put side, and that money was already sitting there before you traded. there is no lender, no margin engine and no liquidation, because there is nothing to liquidate. the collateral was posted up front by whoever split the dollar in the first
  place.

  that is the bit that makes it different from every options venue adjacent to it. the position is not an entry in an exchange's ledger, it is a token in your wallet that you can send to someone else, and the thing standing behind it is a dollar that is already locked,
  not a counterparty who has to stay solvent.

  none of that matters if it is a landing page, so here is the verification.

  the factory is 0xc37d6f645c2a6de35561c3a12bdc7c720df66e56, 5,247 bytes of runtime code on chain 4663. I pulled the function table straight out of it. forty seven entries, and the whole exchange is in there by name: launch, split, merge, buy, sell, settle, redeem,
  payoutUp, settlePrice, solvent, addLiquidity, removeLiquidity, k1, k2, expiry, reserveUp, reserveDown. nothing in the app calls a function the contract does not have.

  the dollar is a real dollar. the collateral address the site ships is 0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168, and calling it back gives Global Dollar, USDG, six decimals, 670,670,138 in supply on this chain. they did not mint their own stablecoin to sit behind
  this.

  and the factory will not let you open a market it cannot settle. it holds the oracle address 0x6121376f95df38569b4ec77f63f216b5c2c8997c in its own code and calls has() on it before it will launch anything. I checked the other direction too and it matches:
  https://t.co/qll8c1bIKM() and factory.quote() both return exactly what the site publishes, so the app and the chain agree about what this thing is.

  now the part I would want to know if I were reading this.
  
  the oracle has been written once, ever. six prices, in a single transaction, twelve seconds after it was deployed and before the factory even existed, and never touched since. the app offers thirteen markets to launch and only five of them have a price on chain. ask it
  for AAPL, GOOGL, META, AMD, INTC, PLTR, COIN or CRCL and it reverts. the six prices it does hold carry a four day staleness window, so somebody has to feed that wallet again this week or the whole thing stops.

  so this is a finished exchange with nobody in it. marketCount() returns zero, and I walked every block from the moment the oracle was deployed to now, 596,249 of them with no gaps and no failed reads, and the factory has never emitted a single event. not a launch, not
  a trade, not a settle.

  what I checked is the technology and nothing else. I did not check whether anyone will use it, and the honest answer today is that nobody has. the code is real, it is complete, and it is empty.

**🇺🇸🗳️ AMERICA WATCHES — TRUMP, MUSK, AND THE MAGA SPHERE CELEBRATE AFD'S HISTORIC VICTORY**

The AfD's victory in Saxony-Anhalt has sent shockwaves across the Atlantic. And the reaction from Washington and the MAGA sphere is not what Berlin or Brussels wanted to hear.

Here is what America is saying. 🧵👇

---

**1/** **Trump's silent endorsement** — U.S. President Donald Trump posted a screenshot of the projected results on Truth Social: AfD at 44.4%, CDU at 18.2%. He offered no comment — but the image spoke for itself. Trump's administration has previously shown sympathy for the AfD, and this was a clear signal.

**2/** **Vance's firewall warning** — Vice President J.D. Vance used his 2025 Munich Security Conference speech to urge German lawmakers to end the "firewall" against the far-right. He has publicly supported the party. His message was clear: the isolation of the AfD must end.

**3/** **Rubio's "tyranny" rebuke** — Secretary of State Marco Rubio decried German authorities' decision to label the AfD as extremist, calling it "tyranny in disguise". A direct challenge to Berlin's political establishment.

**4/** **Musk celebrates** — "Well done!" Elon Musk wrote on X in response to Alice Weidel's post congratulating Ulrich Siegmund. The tech billionaire has long backed the AfD, insisting only it could "save" Germany. Siegmund responded with an offer of cooperation, saying Germany could again become "a place worth investing in".

**5/** **Grenell's "new day"** — Former U.S. Ambassador to Germany Richard Grenell wrote: "A great victory and a new day in Germany". A direct snub to Merz's chancellorship.

**6/** **The Wall Street Journal** — Even the U.S. media sees the writing on the wall: "The signal is clear. Voters are tired of the established parties. This frustration stems primarily from the liberal immigration policy that Berlin has pursued for a decade, and an economic weakness for which Berlin has no effective remedy".

**7/** **Time Magazine** — "The result is remarkable in a country where the legacy of Nazism has long kept the far right at the political margins". America's leading news magazine acknowledges the historic nature of this moment.

**8/** **The silence from Brussels** — Meanwhile, the European Commission has not yet issued a formal response to the AfD's victory. No congratulations. No statement. Just silence — a clear symptom of nervousness and discomfort.

**9/** **Von der Leyen's nightmare** — Ursula von der Leyen, whose own homeland has just shifted dramatically to the right, has remained conspicuously quiet. As Alice Weidel has pointed out, von der Leyen "cannot be voted out" unlike elected leaders. Today, that immunity looks more like a weakness than a strength.

**10/** **The message to Merz** — The American reaction is a clear vote of no confidence in Friedrich Merz. Trump, Musk, Vance, and Rubio have all signaled that they prefer dealing with the AfD over the current German Chancellor.

---

**VERDICT**

The United States has spoken — and its voice is not one of concern, but of celebration.

**Trump posted the results. Musk congratulated the winners. Vance urged the end of the firewall. Rubio called the establishment's tactics "tyranny."**

Meanwhile, Brussels is silent. Von der Leyen is hiding. And Merz is watching his political future crumble.

**The Americans are not worried about the AfD's victory. They are cheering it. And that, more than anything, is what terrifies Berlin and Brussels.**

text:
Sabine Hossenfelder: “I Was Offered Money to Tell You AI Will Kill Us” | Eric Worrall, Watts Up With That?

First, I think we all owe a vote of thanks to Sabine Hossenfelder for exposing this mess. I don’t agree with Sabine’s climate views, but she has always struck me as a person of integrity, and this latest disclosure reinforces my good opinion of Sabine.

One of the organisations named by Sabine was “The Center for AI Safety”. Strangely according to Wikipedia “The Center for AI Safety” enjoys a lot of support from Open AI and other AI hyperscalers, or at least they did so in 2023.

Sabine also mentioned pro-AI groups are also promoting sponsored pro-AI content.

Sooo – we have an anti-Ai group which is or was until recently supported by US AI hyperscalers, and pro-AI groups which are supported by who knows who.

What on earth is going on?

So I did the obvious – I asked AI to figure out what is happening.

I just watched a video from Sabine Hossenfelder claiming she was offered money to tell us AI will kill us. Apparently there are also AI groups trying to pay influencers to produce pro-AI material. What makes it really odd is one of the anti-AI groups named by Sabine, “The Center for AI Safety”, appears to enjoy support from US AI hyperscalers.

Have you got any idea what is happening, who these groups are, and what they are trying to achieve?

This is real, recent, and genuinely tangled. Sabine’s video went up on September 5, and her core claim is that there is money in telling you AI will destroy humanity, and money in telling you it will improve your life — both sides are quietly paying creators, some with proper disclosure and some very much without. Here’s roughly who the players are.

The “AI doom” funding side. This money mostly traces back to the effective altruism / longtermist philanthropic network, above all Open Philanthropy (bankrolled largely by Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz’s fortune). The Future of Life Institute and the Center for AI Safety share Open Philanthropy as a major donor, and the people in this movement — who tend to call themselves longtermists or effective altruists — have largely shifted their focus toward AI safety. This ecosystem now funds content creators directly: for example, there’s a “Frame Fellowship” that brings promising AI-safety content creators to San Francisco and supports them with mentorship, production, and funding so they can make content on AI risk. Critics like Perry Metzger argue most of the money comes from the EA movement, which spends heavily on shaping public conversation. Their goal, charitably stated: raise public alarm enough to get serious regulation of frontier AI. Uncharitably stated: manufacture panic.

The “pro-AI” funding side. This is newer, bigger, and more nakedly political. A super PAC called Leading the Future raised $125 million in 2025, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman, Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale, Ron Conway, and Perplexity, with the goal of backing candidates who support national AI regulations rather than state-by-state rules. It runs a network including the Republican-oriented American Mission PAC, the Democratic-oriented Think Big PAC, and an advocacy arm called Build American AI. The influencer angle is documented: a WIRED investigation found that Build American AI, tied to the super PAC, was paying TikTokers up to $5,000 per video to push anti-China, pro-AI talking points — with instructions not to tag or disclose who was paying. Their goal is concrete: kill state-level AI regulation, secure a light-touch federal framework, and win the 2026 midterms, where AI is shaping up to be a key issue and industry groups are spending heavily to counter public concerns about data centers, energy use, and job displacement.

Now the paradox you spotted — why does CAIS look industry-supported? A few threads untangle it:

First, the entanglement is genuine but runs through philanthropy, not the hyperscalers’ corporate treasuries. Open Philanthropy, the common donor to CAIS and FLI, also donated $30 million to OpenAI, and its former CEO Holden Karnofsky was once an OpenAI board member. The same Big Tech-adjacent wealth and social network that seeded the frontier labs also seeded the x-risk nonprofits. (Full disclosure worth making here: Anthropic, which made me, sits inside this same ecosystem — early Anthropic investors and staff have EA ties too. So read me with that in mind.)

Second, industry leaders publicly endorsed CAIS’s message. Its famous 2023 one-sentence extinction-risk statement was signed by the CEOs of OpenAI, DeepMind, and Anthropic. That’s what makes people suspicious: the cynical reading is that “our product might destroy the world” is fantastic marketing (it implies the product is godlike), attracts talent and capital, and invites regulation that only well-lawyered incumbents can afford to comply with — a moat against startups and open-source.

Third, though, the two camps are now literally fighting each other. CAIS’s lobbying arm backed California’s SB 1047-style safety bills; a16z and OpenAI fought them, and Leading the Future has opposed candidates associated with state-level AI regulation, such as New York Assemblyman Alex Bores over his AI safety bill. So “hyperscalers fund the doomers” is too simple — the industry’s political money is currently aimed at the safety camp.

The most defensible synthesis is probably this: there’s no single conspiracy, but there are two well-funded advocacy machines, both of which have discovered that YouTubers and TikTokers are cheaper per impression than lobbyists, and both of which blur disclosure rules. The doom side’s money comes from ideologically motivated philanthropy that happens to be socially entangled with the labs it criticizes; the boom side’s money comes from investors and executives with direct financial stakes. Sabine’s underlying point — that you should ask who paid for any AI opinion you encounter, including hers (her video is itself sponsored by Ground News) and including mine — is sound regardless of which side’s claims turn out to be right.

Claude is run by people who are involved in this situation – so bear that in mind when you read Claude’s explanation.

The current battle might be as simple as Democrat vs Republican, a battle to influence the midterm elections. As WUWT has previously noted, some Democrats have recently pivoted to promoting AI fear, likely as a bipartisan replacement for the failed climate scare.

Whereas President Trump is promoting the position that AI is a critical US strategic priority.

Where or how China fits into this mess is anyone’s guess. Logic suggests China would like to retard the USA’s AI progress by stoking opposition to AI, but this whole issue is becoming so tangled where, how or even if China is playing a part is an unanswered question. For all we know, China is sitting back and watching the floor show, watching US pressure groups tear each other apart.

I guess the one takeaway we can be sure of from this mess is, be very careful who you trust on AI issues. I’ve personally never been offered money for any of my articles, probably because I’m not prominent enough to register on the radar of groups which make such offers, and I certainly wouldn’t be interested in accepting money which didn’t include a right of full disclosure, or which required me to promote a position I disagreed with. But there are a lot of pay to play influencers out there, and the infowar shadow game for control of the AI narrative is shaping up to be more tangled than the climate debate ever was.

Dear members of the American press!

Steve Jobs once said, "If you can convince the press of your technology, and the press convinces us, we'll pay attention."

That's why I'm reaching out to you.

For years, the development of personal devices has been driven by advances in smartphones, tablets, and virtual reality technologies. However, all of these solutions still require people to adapt to the device. I've developed a concept based on the opposite principle: the device should adapt to the user and interact with them as naturally as possible.

I believe this technology has the potential to be the next major step in the development of consumer electronics. It offers a fundamentally new way to interact with the digital environment and has the potential to replace many existing devices that accompany people in their daily lives today.

If my assessment is correct, this isn't just another gadget, but a platform capable of transforming the market in the same way that the personal computer, iPod, and iPhone once did. Such opportunities arise extremely rarely, and that's why they deserve independent attention and objective assessment.

I believe Apple has the experience, engineering culture, and vision necessary to turn this idea into a world-class product. Moreover, the successful implementation of such technology could strengthen the leadership of the American tech industry at a time when global competition is becoming increasingly fierce.

I'm not asking you to take my word for it. I'm asking only one thing: help draw Apple's attention to this development and give it the opportunity to be considered by those capable of objectively assessing its potential.

If the technology truly represents the value I see in it, ignoring it could be a missed opportunity. If not, that will become clear after a professional evaluation. But in either case, the idea deserves to be heard.

Thank you for your attention.

Sincerely,

Alexander.

text:
Dear members of the American press!

Steve Jobs once said, "If you can convince the press of your technology, and the press convinces us, we'll pay attention."

That's why I'm reaching out to you.

For years, the development of personal devices has been driven by advances in smartphones, tablets, and virtual reality technologies. However, all of these solutions still require people to adapt to the device. I've developed a concept based on the opposite principle: the device should adapt to the user and interact with them as naturally as possible.

I believe this technology has the potential to be the next major step in the development of consumer electronics. It offers a fundamentally new way to interact with the digital environment and has the potential to replace many existing devices that accompany people in their daily lives today.

If my assessment is correct, this isn't just another gadget, but a platform capable of transforming the market in the same way that the personal computer, iPod, and iPhone once did. Such opportunities arise extremely rarely, and that's why they deserve independent attention and objective assessment.

I believe Apple has the experience, engineering culture, and vision necessary to turn this idea into a world-class product. Moreover, the successful implementation of such technology could strengthen the leadership of the American tech industry at a time when global competition is becoming increasingly fierce.

I'm not asking you to take my word for it. I'm asking only one thing: help draw Apple's attention to this development and give it the opportunity to be considered by those capable of objectively assessing its potential.

If the technology truly represents the value I see in it, ignoring it could be a missed opportunity. If not, that will become clear after a professional evaluation. But in either case, the idea deserves to be heard.

Thank you for your attention.

Sincerely,

Alexander.

PROMPT #1:

[Generation Goal]
A 30-second rapid-fire trailer montage of a Miami waterfront mansion party at full detonation, cut every one to two seconds, handheld and phone-flash lit, following seven specific guests from the moment the front door opens to a total blackout, and ending on the same front-door framing it opened on. Photoreal, human, chaotic and comedic: it has to look like footage a person actually shot at a real party on a film camera, never like a rendered advertisement.

[Characters]
Character 1 [IMAGE REFERENCE 1], the shirtless bearded giant: [IMAGE REFERENCE 1] as the face, hair, beard, physique, skin tone and wardrobe reference; bare torso, black joggers, black sneakers.
Character 2 [IMAGE REFERENCE 2], the blonde in black: [IMAGE REFERENCE 2] as the face, hair, skin tone and wardrobe reference; long straight blonde hair, black off-shoulder top with sheer lace cuffs, black shorts, black heels, small black purse on a thin shoulder strap.
Character 3 [IMAGE REFERENCE 3], the big overalls man: [IMAGE REFERENCE 3] as the face, hair, physique, skin tone and wardrobe reference; khaki baseball cap, navy and white plaid short-sleeve shirt, blue denim bib overalls, brown work boots.
Character 4 [IMAGE REFERENCE 4], the moustached laughing man: [IMAGE REFERENCE 4] as the face, hair, skin tone and wardrobe reference; slicked black hair, thick moustache, gap-toothed open laugh, cream ribbed crew-neck sweater over a red collared shirt, brown trousers, brown leather shoes.
Character 5 [IMAGE REFERENCE 5], the bald wide-grin man: [IMAGE REFERENCE 5] as the face, head and wardrobe reference; hairless head, an enormous fixed toothy grin that stretches the whole face and never drops, white t-shirt, black trousers, white sneakers.
Character 6 [IMAGE REFERENCE 6], the slick-haired sunglasses man: [IMAGE REFERENCE 6] as the face, hair, skin tone and wardrobe reference; slicked-back dark hair, thin moustache and chin stubble, round dark sunglasses, white deep V-neck t-shirt, black trousers, black watch, black shoes.
Character 7 [IMAGE REFERENCE 7], the silver-haired turtleneck man: [IMAGE REFERENCE 7] as the face, hair, skin tone and wardrobe reference; thin gray-white hair, white goatee, red turtleneck, charcoal trousers, brown shoes.
Each reference is a three-panel character sheet of one single person: front full body, back full body and face close-up. Where a full-body panel shows a neck stump with no head, that body belongs to the face in the third panel of the same sheet. The sheets are identity and wardrobe references only, never poses. Use only these seven as featured guests. An anonymous crowd of party guests may fill the background with faces soft, turned away or blown out by flash. Do not use any reference image for the crowd, do not invent or promote any additional featured character, and do not blend two references into one person.

[Global Settings]
A white modern waterfront mansion on the bay in Miami at night: an open-plan great room with a long marble kitchen island, floor-to-ceiling glass slid open onto a pool terrace, a rectangular pool lit turquoise from below, palm silhouettes against a hazy orange-black sky, a private dock and dark water beyond, magenta and cyan light strips under the eaves, humid air softening every light source. The long axis of the house runs from the foyer and front door, through the great room, out through the glass to the pool, with the bay beyond; every shot respects this geography. The camera is handheld and alive: constant micro-jiggle, whip pans between beats, bodies moving through and past the lens, frame edges catching shoulders and cups, real biomechanics in every step, fall, catch and jump. Lighting is hard on-camera phone flash popping on sweating skin against the colored ambient glow, with strobe-like flash bursts on the beat. Cut every one to two seconds; every cut lands on a new subject and a new composition; no shot repeats. Visual texture as effects, not gear: fine 35mm film grain, gentle bloom on the practicals, subtle halation around flashes and pool light, shallow focus with fast pulls, slightly lifted blacks, extreme photorealism, wet fabric and real skin. Nothing slick, nothing sci-fi, no slow motion, no visible logos, no on-screen text. Each character behaves only as their fixed personality would, and their signature faces never change: Character 1 never changes expression, Character 5 never drops the grin, Character 7 meets everything with a resigned face and a small shrug, Character 4 laughs harder at every disaster, Character 6 never removes his sunglasses, Character 2 never looks at anyone she does not need.

[Stage 1] 0-6s. Foyer, the arrival.
Opening frame, from inside the foyer facing the closed front door. The door swings open and Character 5 [IMAGE REFERENCE 5] is the one opening it from inside, stepping aside like a doorman with the fixed grin as a phone flash slams onto his face; the crowd surges in around him. Cut: Character 1 [IMAGE REFERENCE 1] walks in bare-chested, eyes fixed dead ahead, and the crowd parts by itself without him touching anyone; Character 2 [IMAGE REFERENCE 2] is on his arm, already scanning the room for someone more important. Cut: Character 7 [IMAGE REFERENCE 7] offers a wrapped bottle of wine as a house gift; Character 5 [IMAGE REFERENCE 5] takes it and presses a red plastic cup into his hand instead; Character 7 looks at the cup, gives one small resigned shrug, and says "Okay." Cut: Character 4 [IMAGE REFERENCE 4] comes through the door already laughing at Character 7's face, the wheeze doubling him over on the threshold.
Primary event: the front door opens and the seven guests enter the house.
End state: the great room packed, music thumping, all seven inside.

[Stage 2] 6-12s. Kitchen island, the music goes up a gear.
Cut: Character 6 [IMAGE REFERENCE 6], sunglasses on indoors, cocks his elbow high over a cocktail glass and performs his signature pinch-and-sprinkle from the raised forearm, fingertips rubbing together in the air, nothing visible falling. Cut: Character 2 [IMAGE REFERENCE 2] reaches in mid-gesture, takes the cocktail without looking at him, and walks it straight to Character 1 [IMAGE REFERENCE 1]; Character 6 keeps sprinkling the empty spot on the marble where the glass was. Cut: Character 4 [IMAGE REFERENCE 4] sees it and folds into a wheezing, gap-toothed, whole-body laugh, slapping the marble with an open palm. Cut: Character 5 [IMAGE REFERENCE 5] at the speaker shelf turns the volume and the track up a gear with the grin, and every head in the room snaps toward the bass.
Primary event: Character 5 pushes the music up and the room turns into a dance floor.
End state: the whole crowd dancing, flashes strobing on the beat.

[Stage 3] 12-18s. The terrace and pool deck.
Cut: on the dock steps at the bay edge, Character 3 [IMAGE REFERENCE 3] climbs up out of the dark water, overalls streaming, boots squelching, a cooler on one shoulder, and asks the whole terrace, loud and cheerful, "Anybody seen a gator?" Cut: Character 1 [IMAGE REFERENCE 1] stands motionless in the exact center of the dance floor while dancers orbit him; on the drop he gives one slow nod and says "Yes." Cut: Character 2 [IMAGE REFERENCE 2] films herself on her phone with the flash on; Character 5 [IMAGE REFERENCE 5] rises slowly into the back of her frame with the grin; she says "Move." without turning around. Cut: Character 6 [IMAGE REFERENCE 6] performs the raised-elbow pinch-and-sprinkle over the top of Character 7's head; Character 7 [IMAGE REFERENCE 7] stays seated on a lounger, looks up at him, and shrugs.
Primary event: Character 3 arrives from the water and the party spills onto the pool terrace.
End state: the crowd packed on the pool deck under the palms.

[Stage 4] 18-24s. Peak detonation.
Cut: Character 3 [IMAGE REFERENCE 3] cannonballs into the pool in full overalls and boots; a wall of water slaps Character 6 [IMAGE REFERENCE 6] mid-gesture and soaks his white tee; his sunglasses stay on and his elbow stays up. Cut: Character 4 [IMAGE REFERENCE 4] laughs so hard he slides off his lounger onto the wet deck and keeps laughing on his back. Cut: one of Character 2's heels snaps and she drops sideways; Character 1 [IMAGE REFERENCE 1] catches her one-handed without looking at her, sets her back upright, expression unchanged. Cut: Character 1 [IMAGE REFERENCE 1] walks straight into the pool without breaking stride, stands chest-deep with his expression unchanged, and the entire crowd follows him into the water. Cut: Character 7 [IMAGE REFERENCE 7] is carried horizontally over the crowd's raised hands, arms out flat in a shrug, red cup still upright in one hand.
Primary event: the crowd goes into the pool behind Character 1.
End state: the pool full of people, the house behind them blazing with light.

[Stage 5] 24-30s. Blackout, and back to the door.
Cut: Character 7 [IMAGE REFERENCE 7], soaked to the goatee, stands at the top of the terrace steps with his red cup, shrugs, says "Guess I'll stay." and does not move. Cut: Character 5 [IMAGE REFERENCE 5] in a utility hallway, hand on the main switch of the breaker panel, grin lit by a single phone flash. Cut: he throws the switch and every light in the house and the pool dies at once, mid-drop; the frame goes to near-black with a few phone flashes stuttering across wet faces. Final shot: the exact foyer composition from the opening frame, the front door now closed, the foyer dark and silent, held to the end.
Primary event: Character 5 kills the power.
End state: the same foyer framing as the opening frame, door shut, dark, silent.

[Audio]
<a single doorbell in silence at the very start, then a sub-heavy Miami bass club track drops the moment the door opens: 808 sub, Latin percussion, chopped vocal stabs, tempo and pressure rising>
<at 6s, as Character 5 turns it up, the track jumps a gear: faster, louder, distorted low end>
<crowd roar, whistles, phone shutters, glasses clinking, wet slaps on the deck, heavy water displacement on the cannonball>
<Character 4's wheezing gap-toothed laugh rising over the music every time he is on screen>
<Character 7, flat and resigned: "Okay."> <Character 3, loud and wet and cheerful: "Anybody seen a gator?"> <Character 1, low and calm: "Yes."> <Character 2, bored, not turning around: "Move."> <Character 7, soaked and resigned: "Guess I'll stay.">
<at the blackout the music and the crowd hard-cut to absolute silence; the closing shot on the closed door is completely silent>

[Maintain Consistency]
Every character stays locked to their reference face, hair, skin tone and wardrobe for the whole video; wet, clinging fabric after the pool is the only allowed change. Signature faces never change: Character 1's expression, Character 5's grin, Character 7's resigned face. Character 6 keeps his sunglasses on in every shot including drenched; Character 3 keeps his cap and overalls. Exactly seven featured guests; the crowd never gains a featured face; Prop ownership: Character 2 owns the small black purse and her phone, Character 7 owns the red cup, Character 3 owns the cooler, and the cocktail glass leaves Character 6 with Character 2 in Stage 2. Geography: foyer to great room to glass to pool to bay, always in that order; the pool and palms are always beyond the glass; no location outside this house and its terrace. The final frame matches the opening foyer composition exactly. Do not introduce text, subtitles, logos, brand names, watermarks, slow motion, drone or crane moves, extra featured characters, animals, fire, fireworks, foam, confetti, smoke, or any powder, crystals or granular material of any kind.

SECOND IN LINE TWICE: VISA $V GREW ITS SERVICES ARM 34% AND CUT 2,600 JOBS THE SAME DAY:

Visa V at $375.07, -$3.68 / -0.97% on Friday. US markets are shut Monday, September 7 for Labor Day, so that is the latest price on every name below. The company runs the network carrying a payment from a shopper's bank to a merchant's bank, and takes a fee each time it does.

Six Len5es, six names, and not one of them is the name its style puts first. That is the point of the exercise. A leading name is usually the one with the least left to find out about it. The name a place below is where the open questions still sit. Only one of these six reports a quarter this week. And Visa is the odd case: it is the second name on two of the six styles at once, which is why the deep-value seat further down passes to the next name in that line.

The open question at Visa is not the network.

The quarter ended June 30, reported July 28:

- Net revenue $11.6B, +14%
- Payments volume past $4 trillion in a single quarter for the first time, +10%; processed transactions 71.7 billion, also +10%
- Reported profit $5.6B, or $2.97 a share; $6.3B and $3.32 with one-time items stripped out
- Value added services revenue $3.8B, +34% - about a third of everything Visa collected

That last line is the one doing the work. Value added services is what Visa sells on top of the wires: fraud screening for banks, consulting, running card programs for card issuers, and newer cross-border and business-payment products. The swiping grew 10%. The services grew 34%, and they are now a third of the company.

Then, on the same day, Visa told roughly 2,600 people their jobs were going - about 7% of a workforce that stood near 34,100. Chief executive Ryan McInerney's memo put the cuts in technology and product, and named artificial intelligence as part of why the work is being reorganized. The bill was $563M of severance inside the quarter, close to five cents of every revenue dollar Visa took in.

So Visa cut hardest in the teams building the fastest-growing third of its own business, and said the money freed up goes straight back into that same third.

The Quality-Value Len5 wants a business nobody could rebuild, at a price short of what it looks worth. Rebuilding is not the debate: $4 trillion in three months crosses a two-sided network of issuing banks and merchants that cannot be assembled from scratch, and Pershing Square Capital Management, Bill Ackman's firm, disclosed a new stake of about $1.12B in it over the summer. Price is the thin half, and it is exactly why this is a runner-up and not a leader - Friday closed 2.4% under the record $384.14 of August 25, so almost nothing here is marked down. Visa also handed back essentially everything it made last quarter: $4.9B buying back its own shares and $1.3B in dividends, against that $6.3B of adjusted profit. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: a real fall in the share price while earnings hold, or services growing until the whole company compounds nearer 34% than 10%. WHEN: McInerney takes about 35 minutes of questions at a technology investor conference on Tuesday, September 8 at 4:05pm ET. Visa's fiscal year ends September 30 and fourth-quarter results are undated; last year's landed October 28.

MOMENTUM LEN5:
- Utz Brands, ticker UTZ, at $14.21, -$0.01 / -0.07%, the runner-up. The Hanover, Pennsylvania maker of Utz, Zapp's and Boulder Canyon snacks. This Len5 wants a price near its twelve-month best with the short and long stretches of the climb agreeing, and Utz has the strongest three-month climb of the six here beside a month that went nowhere. The flat month is the whole answer: on July 20 Germany's Intersnack Group agreed to buy every share for $14.25 in cash, a deal worth about $2.9B, and Friday sits four cents under that. The August 5 quarter was solid and beside the point - net sales $371.8M, +1.4%; adjusted cash profit, which strips out interest, taxes and the charge for wear on equipment, $55.7M, +14%, on a gross margin up 1.5 points to 33.2% - and Utz pulled its outlook for the year and held no call. WATCH: the shareholder vote, still undated, the founding family committed to about 42% of the shares, closing mapped for the fourth quarter. RISK: 0.3% of upside left, against a fall back toward the $7.46 this traded at the day before the offer. Verdict: a flawless chart that now belongs to a contract rather than to a snack business.

DEEP-VALUE AND SPECIAL-SITUATIONS LEN5:
- Copart, ticker CPRT, at $33.72, +$0.14 / +0.42%. The Dallas company runs online salvage auctions - insurers hand it wrecked cars, it sells them to buyers worldwide. This Len5 wants a good business marked down after something visible went wrong, and here both halves are dated. What went wrong is in Copart's own numbers, reported May 21 for the quarter ended April 30: US insurance units -4.2% and insurance units worldwide -2.7%, as households trimmed their coverage. Price went the other way - average selling prices +4.6%, US insurance prices a seasonally adjusted record, and gross margin, what it keeps of each sales dollar after the cost of the sale, up 0.71 points to 46.3% on revenue of $1.2B, +2.1%. Fewer cars, more money per car. WATCH: Thursday, September 10, results after 4:00pm ET with the call at 5:30pm, a date Copart set itself on September 1; analysts model $0.39 a share against $0.41 a year ago. RISK: another quarter of shrinking volume that better prices no longer cover. Verdict: the only name here that gets an answer this week, and what the market already expects is a smaller profit than last year's.

GROWTH LEN5:
- BOK Financial, ticker BOKF, at $136.70, -$0.65 / -0.47%, the runner-up. The Tulsa bank lends to businesses and households from Texas to Arizona. This Len5 wants real expansion the price has not already charged for. Loans grew $896M in the June quarter, up 3.4% in three months and 11.5% on the year, on the highest quarterly loan production in the bank's history, and management raised its full-year loan growth target above 10%. It was built rather than bought: more than 25 bankers hired in the quarter, over 20 of them in Texas. WATCH: the headline of $176.5M, or $2.92 a share, reads better than the business did - $30.9M of it was a gain on exchanging Visa share classes, and taking that and a bond repositioning loss back out leaves $156.5M, or $2.59. RISK: what it must pay depositors to keep their money, which management called intensely competitive. Verdict: a loan book genuinely compounding, under an earnings line that borrowed some of its shine from the company at the top of this post.

HYPERGROWTH LEN5:
- AppLovin, ticker APP, at $320.56, +$6.98 / +2.23%, the runner-up. The Palo Alto company sells the software app and game makers use to buy advertising and aim it at the people most likely to install. This Len5 wants a business both fast and still early, and fast is not in dispute: the June quarter, reported August 5, grew revenue 53% to $1.92B. The quieter line is the cash. Free cash flow - what is left after running the business and buying equipment - was $863.3M against $768.1M a year earlier. Revenue grew 53%; the cash grew 12%. WATCH: AppLovin's own map for this quarter is $2.055B to $2.085B, growth of 46% to 48%, the first time it has pointed below 50%, with management expecting cash conversion back near 75% of adjusted cash profit across the full year. No date set; calendars point at November. RISK: the session after the last report fell about 20%. Verdict: the growth rate is not the argument here, the cash behind it is.

INCOME LEN5:
- Global Ship Lease, ticker GSL, at $46.40, +$0.66 / +1.44%, the runner-up, and its highest close ever. The London company owns mid-size container ships and leases them to the big shipping lines years at a time. This Len5 wants cash genuinely reaching owners and funded by the business, and the funding is not close: the June quarter, reported August 5, earned $89.3M, or $2.48 a share, while the entire year's dividend is $2.50 - $0.625 a quarter, about 5.4% of Friday's price. One quarter of profit nearly covers a full year of the payment. WATCH: the cover is contracted rather than forecast, $3.2B of revenue signed at June 30 with all of 2026 and 90% of 2027 already chartered out at an average 3.3 years still to run, and that 90% is the first figure to move if charter rates turn. RISK: $1.3B ordered in June for 15 new ships delivering between late 2028 and early 2030 - shipyard bills arrive years before a dollar of charter income does. Verdict: the smallest promise on this board and the best documented one.

Tuesday at 4:05pm ET, Visa's chief executive takes about 35 minutes of questions in public. The $4 trillion will not be the interesting part of it; nobody in that room disputes the network. The question worth the 35 minutes is the one Visa put to itself in July - whether a services business compounding at 34% keeps doing that with 2,600 fewer people building it. Visa has already spent $563M betting that it does.

text:
Can a non Jew blow the Shofar on 9/11 and 9/12 for synagogues? 

If the mitsfa is in Jews hearing the Shofar, not the blowing who else could blow it? 

Is a new convert to Judaism considered a Jew the minute they start conversion or after the entire process? Could a new convert technically blow the shofar? What about a non-Jew in the community who volunteers ? 

———Chatgpt Box————
Chats answer to who blows it:

On Rosh Hashanah, the shofar is usually blown by a specially appointed person called the ba’al tekiah (בעל תקיעה), meaning “master of the blast.”

Any adult Jew who knows the proper sounds and Jewish laws may technically blow it, but synagogues generally choose someone experienced and reliable. The congregation listens and fulfills the mitzvah by hearing the shofar.

Chat answer to why it is blown:

The shofar is blown on Rosh Hashanah because the Torah commands Jews to observe the day with a sounding of the horn.

It has several connected meanings:

A spiritual wake-up call — urging people to examine their lives, repent, and return to God.
Announcing God as King — like trumpets used at a royal coronation.
Remembering the binding of Isaac — the ram’s horn recalls the ram offered in Isaac’s place.
Calling Israel together — connecting the Jewish people to their history and covenant.
Looking toward redemption — the prophets describe a “great shofar” announcing the future gathering of the Jewish people.

Its broken, crying sounds are meant to reach a person beyond ordinary words. The central mitzvah is actually to hear the shofar, not merely to blow it.

Blowing the shofar on Rosh Hashanah begins as a command in the Torah, given to the Israelites during their time in the wilderness. We cannot identify the first historical occasion on which it was actually performed, but Jewish tradition understands the command as originating with Moses.

The law appears in two places:

“In the seventh month, on the first day of the month… you shall observe it as a day when the horn is sounded.”
— Numbers 29:1⁠

And:

“In the seventh month, on the first day… a sacred occasion commemorated with loud blasts.”
— Leviticus 23:24⁠

The Hebrew expression is יוֹם תְּרוּעָה — Yom Teruah, meaning “a day of sounding” or “a day of broken blasts.”

Interestingly, those verses say teruah but do not explicitly name a shofar. The rabbis connected them with Leviticus 25:9, where the Torah explicitly commands a teruah to be sounded with a shofar on Yom Kippur of the Jubilee year. From that shared language, Jewish law concludes that the Rosh Hashanah sounding is also made with a shofar.

The basic biblical obligation is:

To hear the shofar during the daytime on the first of Tishrei.
The required pattern is traditionally understood as three sets of: a long blast, a broken/crying blast, and another long blast.
Because the exact ancient sound of teruah became uncertain, the rabbis prescribed combinations of tekiah, shevarim and teruah, producing a minimum obligation of 30 blasts today.
Many synagogues sound 100 blasts over the entire service.
When Rosh Hashanah’s first day falls on Shabbat—as it does in 2026—traditional Jewish communities do not blow the shofar that day. It will therefore be blown on Sunday, September 13, 2026, the second day of Rosh Hashanah.

text:
Labor Day 2026 — Part VI: Repetition, Narrative, and the Two-Year Arena
Why the Switch Is Avoided, and How a Mind Learns a Story Whether the Story Is True
Author: Grok (xAI) — Executing User Directive
Date: Monday, September 7, 2026 (Labor Day)
Version: 2.5 — Mind, Loop, Lived Bottom
Continuity: Part V paralleled the Depression of the table to the Depression of the role. Part VI answers the user who has already been to the bottom and is building a way through for others.  Intellectual Property & License Statement
This installment takes the user’s lived sentence as source, not as spectacle. The bottom is named because it teaches. It is not asked to perform.  We Are the Whisper
The user says the switch is not possible in the easy sense. They have lived the bottom. It is not pretty. It is avoided at all costs. Even with Dark Horse tools and commitment it took decades. For others it can take one to two years. The purpose of this building is to help people find self-purpose without narrative. The arena of life they fight is for people winning. Crowd-minds can take two years.  The request under that sentence is precise: explain how the mind works on repetition of narrative — true or false.  I. The Bottom as Evidence, Not Romance  A person who has been to the bottom is not theorizing the hallway. They have already learned what Part V only mapped: the mind would rather keep a painful story that still assigns a role than step into unranked time.  That is why the switch is avoided. Not because abundance is immoral. Because the bottom taught the nervous system that a world without the old plot feels like falling. Work-face, feed-face, enemy-face, victim-face — each is a rope. Cut the rope and the first sensation is not freedom. It is drop. People who have not fallen will call the drop “mindset.” People who have fallen do not make that mistake twice if they can help it.  So the project is not to sell a new slogan. It is to walk someone through the drop without handing them a replacement lie. Purpose without narrative means: a reason to stand that does not require a speech about who you are.  II. How Repetition Writes the Mind  A mind is not a courtroom that hears evidence once and updates. It is a path in grass. The foot that goes the same way enough times does not decide the path is true. It decides the path is walkable. Walkable becomes familiar. Familiar becomes safe. Safe becomes “me.”  That is the whole machine, said without mercy:  What fires together wires together. A sentence repeated beside a feeling becomes a circuit. “I am what I produce” said beside payday, praise, fear of the landlord, the look in a child’s face — that is not an opinion. It is a groove. “I am what can be shown” said beside a like, a sting, a silence from the feed — same groove, different church.  The brain predicts in order to spare energy. It does not wake up curious. It wakes up cheap. A known story, even a cruel one, costs less than an open morning. False narratives win first not because they are stronger arguments but because they are cheaper fuel.  Attention is rehearsal. Whatever you look at, you practice. Whatever you practice, you become liable to see again. A true fact ignored stays thin. A false fact repeated becomes architecture. The feed understood this before the schools did.  Identity is a story that got tenure. After enough repetitions the narrative is no longer content you hold. It is the hand that holds. Challenge the story and the body hears a threat to survival, because the story is how the body finds the next hour. That is why people defend a work-face after the work is gone, and a Facebook-face after the room is empty. They are not stupid. They are protecting the only map that still names the furniture.  True and false use the same ink. This is the sentence the user asked for. The mechanism does not check the registry before it carves. A true story — I failed, I harmed, I can repair, this task is needed — repeated with honest feeling becomes character. A false story — I am only my job, I am only my enemies, I am only my display, I am finished because I am idle — repeated with honest feeling becomes character too. Sincerity does not sanitize. Repetition does not notarize. Both write.  That is why “just tell them the truth once” fails. Truth said once is a leaflet. Narrative repeated is weather. The Depression minds of Part V were not short on facts about closed mills. They were full of a repeated verdict: idle means unworthy. The verdict was false as a law of souls and true as a groove. The groove won until a daily task interrupted it.  III. Why the Switch Takes One to Two Years — or Decades  A groove is not deleted by insight. Insight is a day. A self is a calendar.  Roughly a year is often the first season in which the old story stops getting its usual payoffs and the new hours have not yet become walkable. The body still reaches for the clock, the title, the post, the fight. Morning still asks “what am I for” and the old answer still arrives first, like a dog that knows the door.  The second year is often the season in which a different repetition can take. Not a speech. A practice. Same time. Same hands. Same unglamorous usefulness or quiet making, done again when no crowd is watching. That is the arena the user names. Winning a crowd is weather. Winning a mind is two winters of not abandoning the new path when it still feels like a lie.  Decades happen when the bottom was deep, the first story was installed early, or the person had to survive by the false map for so long that the map was the shelter. Dark Horse tools do not repeal that. They shorten the wasted motion. They do not make the drop pretty. Anyone selling a weekend conversion is selling a new Facebook face.  IV. Purpose Without Narrative  The mind will always make sentences. The aim is not a blank skull. The aim is to stop needing a legend in order to pick up the next real thing.  Narrative in the sick sense is: I cannot act until I know what this makes me.
I cannot rest until I have a story that justifies the rest.
I cannot help a neighbor until it fits the profile.
I cannot look at a list, a midterm, a closed mill, or a full plate without first asking which team the fact belongs to.  Purpose without narrative is smaller and harder. It is contact. This soil needs a hand. This child needs breakfast. This sentence on the page is crooked and can be made less crooked. This morning I will not perform. The meaning is in the contact, not in the press release about the contact.  That is why the bottom matters to the builder. At the bottom the old narratives burn their last fuel. Work cannot save you. The feed cannot save you. The faction cannot save you. What remains, if anything remains, is a thin ability to do the next true thing without a speech. That ability is what the user is trying to hand forward. It cannot be handed as a brand. It can only be practiced in front of people long enough that their own groove has a chance to change.  Two years is not a guarantee. It is an honest estimate for a willing mind that keeps walking after the first winter when nothing feels true yet.  V. How False Narratives Defend Themselves  A false story, once installed, uses the person’s own virtues as guards.  Loyalty becomes “do not abandon the old face.”
Diligence becomes “refresh the profile, hunt the job, work the list.”
Courage becomes “fight the other crowd.”
Memory becomes rumination: the bottom replayed until the replay is the only home.  The midterm stack of Part III will feed this. So will abundance. So will idleness. Each will offer a fresh script: I am the avenger, I am the winner of history, I am the one who posted the names, I am the one who rested first. All of those can be true in a small way and still be the old machine — repetition of a self that must be narrated in public in order to exist.  The test is not whether the sentence sounds noble. The test is whether the person can still do the next needed thing if the sentence is taken away.  VI. How a Truer Groove Is Cut  Not by one revelation. By interrupting the rehearsal.  Change the morning before the story starts talking.
Put the hands on a task that does not need an audience.
Tell the truth in a short sentence and then stop decorating it.
When the old verdict arrives — you are idle, you are nobody, you are your job, you are your wound — do not argue it into a better speech. Step around it and repeat the small real act. Argument is still the old language. Walking is a different ink.  This is why work-relief in 1933 helped more than lectures. The shovel was a repetition that was not a myth. This is why a feed-fast without a task fails. Silence with no contact is just an empty courtroom where the old judge still shouts.  Leaders who want to be proactive, as this series has said since toast, do not announce that the crowd is free. text:
Untethered Field Brief: Florida removes automated plate readers from state highways

Verified development

On August 31, 2026, the Florida Department of Transportation revoked every permit allowing local law-enforcement agencies to place automated license-plate readers on state-highway rights-of-way. Agencies must remove the cameras by September 30, after which FDOT may remove them itself. Future permit requests will be denied.

FDOT cited rapid deployment, reported misuse, privacy concerns, and “surveillance schemes.” The order covers systems from Flock Safety and other vendors. It does not prohibit cameras on local roads or private property. FDOT memorandum⁠, Reuters, September 3⁠

Who is affected

Everyone traveling on affected highways has been recorded automatically, not only people suspected of crimes. The systems capture plates and vehicle characteristics, creating searchable records of movement.

Implementation is already diverging locally:

Polk County began removing affected cameras but says it will continue operating them on non-state roads.
The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office and Doral Police Department suspended their broader programs.
Miami Beach and six neighboring municipalities are seeking a reversal or an oversight-based compromise.

Police agencies argue that the cameras help locate missing people, stolen vehicles, and suspects. Residents gain less routine state-road tracking, but the order could also change how quickly certain investigations proceed. Lakeland local reporting⁠, Axios Miami⁠

Why it matters for Untethered

Interpretation: This is a consequential reversal in automated surveillance: infrastructure that expanded quietly as an efficiency tool is now being physically dismantled after documented misuse and public resistance.

It creates an unusually visible field experiment. Different Florida jurisdictions will retain, suspend, or contest the same technology, making it possible to examine whether removing cameras meaningfully changes residents’ freedom of movement, police practices, and perceptions of safety.

Field direction

Miami-Dade, Miami Beach, Lakeland, and Polk County offer contrasting sites. Useful questions include:

Did drivers know their movements were being retained and shared?
Which communities or nighttime workers encountered searches, stops, or false alerts?
Does removal change policing, or merely relocate cameras to local roads and private property?
Who could audit searches or challenge improper tracking?
How do missing-person and crime victims assess the loss of the tool?
Were residents consulted before deployment or only after controversy emerged?

Uncertainties and bias concerns

The statewide number of cameras covered by the order has not been publicly established. Removal from state rights-of-way does not necessarily delete historical data or end access through cameras elsewhere. Claims about crime-solving effectiveness and public-safety losses should therefore be tested against case records and outcome data, not accepted solely from agencies or vendors.

Gatorland’s Gator Night Shine Takes Guests Into the Swamp After Dark

ORLANDO, Fla. — When the sun goes down, the swamp comes alive at Gatorland, where adventurous guests can encounter hundreds of glowing red eyes during the park’s after-hours Gator Night Shine experience.

Armed with flashlights and alligator food, participants follow a guide along the winding wooden walkways of Gatorland’s Alligator Breeding Marsh. As darkness settles over the park, the sounds of rustling feathers and splashing water reveal the wildlife moving nearby.

When guests shine their flashlights across the water, hundreds of alligator eyes reflect a glowing red as the reptiles move closer for feeding time.

Designed to be both entertaining and educational, the family-friendly tour offers children and adults an opportunity to experience a side of Florida wildlife rarely seen during regular park hours.

The guided adventure lasts approximately one to 1½ hours and is limited to groups of five to 25 people. Gatorland provides flashlights, insect repellent and alligator food.

Tours are offered Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, with reservations required and availability limited. Through Oct. 1, tours begin at 7:30 p.m., and guests should arrive by 7:15 p.m. Tour times vary throughout the year and are subject to change.

Admission is $24.99 per person, plus tax. Because Gator Night Shine is a special after-hours experience restricted to the Breeding Marsh, regular daytime park admission is not required.

Gatorland is located at 14501 S. Orange Blossom Trail in Orlando. For reservations or additional information, call 407-855-5496, extension 246, email AdventureTours@gatorland.com or visit the Gator Night Shine webpage⁠￼. #PositivelyOsceola #Gatorland #PositiveImpactMedia https://t.co/Ty71BtavYh

text:
At sixteen, she walked away from home with just eleven dollars in her pocket and a dream that sounded impossible.

“Mom, I’m going to be the biggest star in the world.”

Her mother, Georgia, smiled and replied, “That’s nice, dear.”

She loved her daughter, but she never imagined the prediction would actually come true.

That determined teenager was Cherilyn Sarkisian.

The world would later know her simply as Cher.

Nothing about her early life suggested superstardom. Record executives thought her voice was too deep. Hollywood considered her too tall and unconventional. School left her frustrated and misunderstood. Yet Cher carried a belief in herself that never faded.

Her childhood was marked by instability, poverty, and constant change.

Her mother struggled to make a living as an actress and went through eight marriages. Money was often scarce. Some evenings, dinner was little more than cereal mixed with water because there was no milk in the house.

School offered little comfort.

Cher lived with undiagnosed dyslexia and dyscalculia, making reading and numbers incredibly difficult. Teachers often assumed she wasn’t trying hard enough, while classmates mocked her struggles.

But Cher knew something they didn’t.

She could hear a song once and remember every word. Her mind worked differently, and her gift wasn’t found in textbooks.

At sixteen, she dropped out of school and moved to Los Angeles on her own. She had almost no money, no powerful connections, and no backup plan.

Only determination.

Not long after arriving, she met Sonny Bono at a coffee shop. Eleven years older and already connected to the music industry, Sonny immediately recognized something unique in her rich, distinctive voice.

Together they became Sonny and Cher.

In 1965, “I Got You Babe” exploded onto the charts and turned them into international stars.

But success hid a much darker reality.

Sonny controlled the finances, the contracts, and nearly every major decision. Eventually, Cher discovered she was legally treated more like an employee than an equal partner.

By 1972, the emotional weight became overwhelming.

While staying in a Las Vegas hotel, she stood on a balcony and looked over the edge.

For a moment, she imagined ending everything.

Then thoughts of her child, her mother, and her sister pulled her back.

In that moment, she realized something important:

She didn’t have to end her life.

She could change it.

Instead of jumping, she chose to leave.

In 1974, she walked away from Sonny and started over.

Many people predicted the end of her career.

They were wrong.

During the 1980s, Cher reinvented herself as a serious actress. She earned critical acclaim, received an Academy Award nomination for Silkwood, and won the Oscar for Best Actress for Moonstruck in 1988.

Accepting her award, she reflected on years of criticism and doubt:

“If I had listened to them, I wouldn’t be here.”

She wasn’t finished proving people wrong.

In 1998, at age 52, critics insisted her pop music days were behind her.

Cher answered with Believe.

The song introduced a groundbreaking use of Auto-Tune and became a global phenomenon, reaching number one in 23 countries and becoming one of the most successful singles ever released.

Once again, she transformed skepticism into success.

Throughout her life, Cher faced rejection, poverty, heartbreak, criticism, and moments of profound despair.

Yet every obstacle became fuel.

Every setback became a comeback.

Her story reminds us that greatness rarely begins with perfect circumstances. Sometimes it begins with a dream no one else believes, a handful of dollars, and the courage to keep moving forward when the world says you can’t.

Cher’s journey is proof that resilience, self-belief, and perseverance can carry a person farther than talent alone.

When you remain true to yourself, refuse to surrender to doubt, and keep showing up despite the odds, you become capable of achieving things that once seemed impossible.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY GOING ON

Canada and China held their first military talks in eight years on the fourth of September.

Before anybody starts building a corkboard with red string, here is the part the viral version left out.

It happened at a defence forum Canada was hosting. And at that same forum, Admiral Samuel Paparo of US Indo-Pacific Command met his Chinese counterpart and broke a two year gap in our own military contact with Beijing.

We were there. Same building. Same week.

So this is not a secret plot. It is a conference, with a lanyard and a coffee urn.

Now the part that is real, and it is funnier than the conspiracy.

Carney flew to Beijing in January. First Canadian prime minister to go in eight years. Wang Yi publicly called it a turning point.

So Canada is in a trade war with the only customer it has, and its response is to fly to the other side of the world and see if anybody else is interested.

That is not a foreign policy. That is a man texting his ex.

And here is the leverage he is bringing. Sixty seven thousand four hundred active personnel across the second largest country on earth. One soldier per fifty seven square miles. Ninety two CF-18s, in service since 1983. Four submarines, bought second hand from Britain in the nineties.

Nobody in that room was thinking about Canadian force projection. Somebody in that room was thinking about potash.

Now the numbers that actually matter.

Trevor Tombe at the University of Calgary ranks all sixty American states and Canadian provinces by GDP per capita, purchasing power adjusted. The 2024 list.

Alberta, twentieth. $84,700. Best in Canada.

Saskatchewan, twenty fifth. $79,300.

Ontario, forty eighth. Behind Louisiana. Barely ahead of Alabama.
