text:
Untethered Field Brief: Court keeps mass voter-screening system offline

Verified development

On September 4, 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit refused to reactivate the federal government’s modified SAVE system while its legality is appealed. The ruling leaves in place a lower-court decision blocking its use for bulk citizenship checks of voter rolls before the November elections. The underlying appeal remains unresolved and will proceed on an expedited schedule. D.C. Circuit order⁠, Reuters⁠

SAVE was originally created to verify individual immigrants’ eligibility for certain public benefits. Its 2025 modification connected it with Social Security records and added bulk searches using names, birth dates, and full or partial Social Security numbers. State agencies could upload voter lists and receive automated citizenship indicators.

Who is affected

Naturalized citizens face the clearest risk because Social Security records may still describe them as noncitizens after naturalization. The court documented cases in which inaccurate results required citizens to produce additional proof or resulted in registration cancellation.

Previous reporting found that more than half of 74 voters flagged in Boone County, Missouri, were citizens. Texas and other states also received corrected results after the system misidentified voters. Texas Tribune and ProPublica investigation⁠

The ruling also limits the exchange of sensitive identifying information between state election offices, DHS, and the Social Security Administration.

Why it matters for Untethered

Interpretation: This is a direct example of institutional access being reorganized around automated screening. A system designed for one administrative purpose was rapidly connected to new databases and repurposed to evaluate millions of people in another consequential setting.

When the automated record fails, the burden shifts to the individual. A citizen may have to locate documents, contact an election office, or correct federal records to preserve access to voting. The system therefore converts a data mismatch into a real-world eligibility problem.

Field direction

County election offices in Texas and Boone County, Missouri, offer documented starting points. Naturalization ceremonies, voter-assistance organizations, and communities with large naturalized populations may reveal how notices and proof requirements are experienced.

Field questions:

How were flagged voters notified, and could they understand what action was required?
What time, travel, documentation, or language burdens were created?
Did election workers treat automated results as evidence or merely as a lead requiring verification?
What happens to people who never receive or cannot answer a notice?

Uncertainty and bias concerns

The decision denies temporary relief; it is not the final appellate judgment. Conflicting litigation involving several states may continue to complicate implementation. Error rates also vary by jurisdiction and remain incompletely documented. Naturalized citizens appear especially exposed, but a full demographic analysis of who was flagged, removed, or reinstated is not yet available.

text:
Untethered Field Brief: Driverless taxis without human controls enter public service

Verified development

On September 3, 2026, Tesla began commercially deploying Cybercabs in limited areas of Austin, Texas. The two-passenger vehicles have no steering wheel, pedals, mirrors, or other conventional controls that a rider could use to take over.

Tesla says rides are available to the public. Texas records listed 45 Cybercabs among the company’s 420 registered autonomous vehicles, although the number actively carrying passengers has not been disclosed. Reuters⁠

On September 4, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an audit covering an estimated 1,000 Cybercabs. It will examine the technical evidence Tesla used to certify that the vehicles comply with federal safety standards. The investigation is not yet a finding that Tesla violated the law. NHTSA investigation record⁠, Associated Press⁠

Who is affected

Paying passengers now entrust the entire trip to software without a physical fallback. Pedestrians, cyclists, nighttime workers, emergency responders, and other drivers encounter the vehicles on public streets whether or not they chose to participate.

Austin has recorded ten incidents or complaints involving Tesla autonomous vehicles since testing began in June 2025. Seven were classified as safety concerns. These reports concern Tesla’s broader autonomous fleet and should not be attributed automatically to the newly deployed Cybercab. Axios Austin⁠

Why it matters for Untethered

Interpretation: Automation has crossed from assisting a driver to removing the human operating position entirely. Public streets and passengers are becoming part of the deployment environment while federal regulators evaluate compliance after service has begun.

This also exposes an institutional-access gap. Texas authorizes autonomous-vehicle companies rather than approving each vehicle model, while Austin itself has little authority beyond emergency coordination. Residents therefore experience the deployment locally without local government holding primary regulatory control.

Field direction

Austin’s downtown service area, South Congress Avenue, pickup locations, and late-night entertainment districts offer useful observation points.

Field questions:

What happens when a rider feels unsafe but has no physical way to take control?
Can riders with disabilities, limited digital access, or language barriers use the service independently?
How are police, firefighters, and roadside workers handling immobilized or unresponsive vehicles?
Do taxi and rideshare drivers see changed demand, hours, or earnings?

Uncertainty and bias concerns

The operating area, service hours, active fleet size, incident rate, and pricing have not been fully disclosed. Early ride accounts came heavily from investors, enthusiasts, and social-media personalities, so they should not be treated as representative passenger experience. Claims about superior safety, employment displacement, affordability, or accessibility remain unverified.

Breaking the Glass Ceiling: How Ishika Jaiswal is Redefining Pan Am Badminton on the Global Stage

The landscape of international badminton is undergoing a subtle yet profound structural shift. While powerhouses like Japan, South Korea, and China continue to dominate top-tier podiums, 23-year-old American shuttler Ishika Jaiswal represents a growing wave of Pan American talent proving that non-traditional badminton nations can hold their own at the highest level.

Reflecting on her run at the World Championships, Jaiswal candidly addressed the psychological barrier of facing icons like Nozomi Okuhara and Ratchanok Intanon:

"I try not to think of them as legends... I was just telling myself constantly: don't feel scared. A little bit after playing, I was like, I can also fight against them. It was a really full-circle moment." 

Jaiswal’s analytical mindset offers a sharp critique of how the global game has evolved, moving away from raw rally endurance toward technical variability, high-level tactical adjustments, and court-reading skills. 

This evolution is central to her development as she transitions from regional dominance to high-level BWF World Tour events.

Beyond her individual growth, Jaiswal highlights a demographic and infrastructural evolution within the Pan Am region. 

The influx of second-generation Asian-American families in hubs like Texas and California, paired with elite coaching arriving in North America, has transformed badminton from an obscure recreational sport into a viable professional pathway. Centers like *Velocity Badminton* in Texas are turning local interest into sustainable development ecosystems for rising talent.

Despite recent tactical setbacks at the Indonesia Masters Super 100, Jaiswal’s intrinsic preparation and long-term vision remain fixed. 

With targets set on breaking into the BWF Top 50, competing consistently in Super 500 events, and representing Team USA at the LA 2028 Olympic Games, Jaiswal stands as a central figure in American badminton's modernisation.

text:
I lived through a category 5 Hurricane known as Ivan on Saturday, September 11, 2004 in the dormitory of St Matthews medical school at the Cayman Islands.  

Some of the student body had taken the school up on a $500 offer on Friday to evacuate to Miami for the weekend, which was just an hour away by commercial flight.  The school package included  airfare and hotel and students were bunking 2 to a room.

Some students opted not to do that.  I was among them.  However, among that subset, they all went to storm shelters on Friday night.  I did not.

In the morning, the first floor was flooded with about 3 feet of water so I went to the second floor and found a security guard there.  We just hung out in a room for a day or so while the storm battered the island.  It suffered a lot of damage and many people died.

🇵🇹 Camino Portugués Coastal Route: what the record shows and what tradition added

🇪🇸 The Pilgrim's Reception Office in Santiago issued 530,987 Compostelas in 2025, its highest annual figure, and the Portuguese routes accounted for 190,344 of them. ComplexDiscovery walks the coastal one this month, Matosinhos to Santiago, with the Variante Espiritual for the final stages.

⛪️ What the route offers, beyond the Atlantic and the granite, is an unusually clear view of how institutions handle their own histories.

👣 A monastery on this walk publishes its founding legend and labels it a legend. A Spanish national archive supports Baiona's Columbus claim, then states in the next sentence that no testimony of the report behind it survives.

📃 Set against those: a heritage decree credited with a property count it never states, a hillfort population that circulates as a figure and was produced as an estimate, promotional superlatives with no institutional origin, and a World Heritage listing the route does not hold.

🔎 For readers whose work turns on provenance, that contrast is the story. The habits that separate a documented fact from an attached tradition are the habits that separate an established finding from a confidently repeated claim.

text:
From a Single Spark to a Golden Harvest: The Remarkable Journey of Sied Mohammed
By: Habtom Tesfamichael

On the scenic outskirts of Adi- Keyh, the administrative center of the Adi-Keyh sub-zone, lies an expansive apiary that defies the rugged appearance of the surrounding landscape. To an untrained eye, this stretch of land might seem ordinary, but for a visionary entrepreneur, it is a sanctuary of industry.

This is the domain of Sied Mohammed, a man whose dedication, foresight, and unwavering work ethic have turned a spark of inspiration into a thriving apicultural enterprise. Today, Sied manages a collection of over 130 modern beehives—a journey that began with a single, wild colony.

Beekeeping is far more than a business in Eritrea; it is an ancient craft woven into the nation’s cultural, social, and economic fabric. For centuries, Eritrean farmers have harvested honey, valuing it not only as a natural sweetener but for its medicinal properties and its role in traditional celebrations and religious ceremonies. Historically, however, the sector relied on traditional cylindrical hives fashioned from mud, stones, and straw. While these methods are a proud part of local heritage, they yielded limited harvests and made hive management labor-intensive.

In recent years, the Eritrean Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) has spearheaded a strategic drive to modernize the sector. By introducing modern frame hives and promoting scientific management techniques, the MoA aims to capitalize on Eritrea’s diverse microclimates. The country’s topography—ranging from cool highland plateaus to subtropical midlands and coastal plains—offers a year-round “bloom calendar,” providing bees with a continuous source of nectar. Sied Mohammed embodies this shift: a forward-thinking farmer who recognized that the “liquid gold” of his region was a resource waiting to be professionally tapped.

Sied’s transformation into a master beekeeper began in 2017 while watching a documentary on Eri-TV featuring a successful bee farmer.

“I was deeply inspired by that program,” Sied recalls. “I learned that bee farming would not only fulfill my goal of self-reliance, but that my local environment was perfectly suited for it. I knew right then that I wanted to pursue this path.”

Sied approached the business methodically. To learn the trade from the ground up, he reached out to an experienced beekeeper in Adi-Keyh, offering his manual labor in exchange for knowledge. For several months, Sied worked as a dedicated apprentice, studying hive management, bee behavior, and the seasonal cycles of local vegetation.

Armed with this practical experience, Sied captured a migrant wild bee colony and settled them in his backyard. Demonstrating confidence in his long-term plan, he invested in several modern beehives before he even owned enough colonies to fill them. A favorable rainy season that year provided lush flora, helping his fledgling venture take off.

Initially engaged in traditional crop farming, Sied realized that beekeeping offered superior sustainability and higher profit margins with less environmental strain, prompting him to pivot entirely toward apiculture.

To build on his practical foundation, Sied sought formal technical training through the Ministry of Agriculture. The MoA courses covered advanced techniques such as queen rearing and colony splitting—a scientific method used to multiply hives by dividing a healthy, populous colony.

“I quickly expanded that first colony into five,” Sied explains. “From there, it was a matter of consistency. By 2021, my count grew from 10 to 20 hives, and today, I manage over 130.”

As his operation grew, Sied adopted migratory beekeeping to prevent his colonies from exhausting local nectar sources during dry periods. Moving his hives across different ecological zones to follow flowering seasons yielded immediate results: last year, Sied harvested 25 quintals (2,500 kilograms) of honey. Thanks to his migratory strategy, he now harvests twice a year.

In the early days, Sied relied on donkeys and camels for transport. As his earnings grew, he reinvested his profits and purchased a pickup truck, allowing him to move his 130- plus hives across the region safely and efficiently.

The enterprise has also become a family effort. Sied’s younger brothers have joined the business, establishing self-sufficiency by manufacturing their own modern hives rather than purchasing them from commercial vendors. This vertical integration has reduced overhead costs and allowed them to customize equipment for local bee varieties.

For Sied, the mission extends beyond personal success. By increasing local supply, he hopes to make honey more affordable for everyday consumers.

“I’m glad to see honey becoming more accessible in the market,” he says. “It should be a common household staple for every Eritrean family, given its health benefits.”

Sied has also diversified into selling bee colonies to aspiring beekeepers, selling approximately 50 colonies over the past year. His technical proficiency now allows him to perform the delicate task of splitting up to 15 colonies in a single night.

Through his journey from an apprentice to an established apiculturist, Sied Mohammed demonstrates how technical training, market adaptability, and sustained effort can turn local natural resources into a thriving enterprise.

Because medical qualifications are universally recognized, practitioners often migrate to capitalist or higher-income countries that offer better pay, modern equipment, and superior working conditions.Loss of personnel: This "brain drain" leaves state systems with severe staffing deficits that training pipelines struggle to replace. Central Planning and Under funding Resource allocation limits: In a state-planned economy, healthcare budgets must compete with other public sectors. Economic downturns or inefficient central allocation lead to chronic underfunding. Material shortages: Hospitals frequently lack basic supplies, medications, and modern technology, which increases workplace frustration and burnout among existing staff. text:
It is a perimeter that has already been walked.

If the same Service 
then announces a return to core mandate on the eve of 2027, two interpretations compete. 

One: a professional DG is pulling the institution back from mission creep. 

Two: the centre is laundering the brand before the bigger contest.

Both can be partly true. That is the problem. 

In a low-trust republic, mixed motives still produce the same 
public conclusion: 
the masquerade now takes instructions.

Compare mandates cleanly. Police handle crime and order. INEC handles ballots. Courts handle disputes. DSS handles threats to the state. When DSS does police work, it becomes a super-police without the police’s visibility rules. 

When it does electoral atmosphere-setting, it becomes an undeclared party organ. 

When it does Bar politics, it amputates 
the one guild 
trained to sue it.

The existential point is not poetry. An INEC result can be petitioned. 

A secret-service preference cannot be cross-examined in the same way, because the investigator is the evidence. 
That is why the phrase “DSS deserved to be DSSed” is crude and also institutionally serious. It means audit, oversight, sanction, and a forced return to the shrine. Not abolition. Discipline.

The DG as Symptom 
and Possible Instrument

Ajayi is not Bichi. 
The record of the last two years includes convictions in terror cases, recoveries of weapons, compensation payments, and a public attempt to separate civil from criminal files. 

A career cadet who has lived the culture may understand, better than an outsider, how the Service commonised itself: too many faces, too many press photos, too many “assistances” that turned ghosts 
into neighbourhood characters.

Respect that. Then apply the elder’s test. Internal knowledge is not the same as independent power. The presidency that appoints the DG also lives with the temptation to use him. EFCC-direction stories in the public square have already taught Nigerians a brutal syllogism: if one agency takes instruction, why would its sister be monastic?

So the question is not whether Ajayi can give 
a good interview. It is whether a field director in a tense state can refuse a “small favour” 
in October 2026 and 
still keep his posting 
in November.

What Restoration 
Would Actually Look Like

Narrow the mandate 
in writing and in punishment. 

Insurrection, terrorism, espionage, threats to constitutional order. 
Full stop. Civil debt, land, professional elections, and partisan “help” 
go elsewhere.

Restore stealth. 
The DG may have a face.
The rest should not. Mystique is not sadism. It is operational hygiene.

Publish, or at least independently review, the NBA-platform detention and the 2023 security-clearance controversies enough to show that files have contents, not just timing.

Accept National Assembly oversight that can bite. A secret service that cannot be examined becomes a state within the state. A secret service that is examined only by its beneficiaries becomes a faction.

Ajayi’s civil-matters directive is the right sentence. 

2027 will decide 
if it was a doctrine
or a costume change.

Closing

Nigeria has survived soldiers who seized radio stations. 

It may not survive intelligence officers who quietly choose umpires and then ask to be trusted as umpires.

The masquerade 
was powerful when it appeared only when the village was in danger. 

It becomes a joke when it attends every naming ceremony.

text:
Labor Day is a U.S. federal holiday observed on the first Monday in September. It honors the American labor movement and the contributions workers have made to the country’s economic and social well-being. 

The first Labor Day parade took place in New York City on September 5, 1882, organized by the Central Labor Union. About 10,000 workers marched from City Hall to Union Square, followed by a picnic, speeches, and fireworks. The idea spread to other cities and states. Oregon was the first state to make it official in 1887.

It became a federal holiday on June 28, 1894, when President Grover Cleveland signed the bill into law. This happened shortly after the violent Pullman Strike, in which federal troops were used to break a railroad workers’ walkout. Some historians see the timing as an attempt to ease tensions with organized labor. Credit for proposing the holiday is usually given to either Peter J. McGuire (co-founder of the American Federation of Labor) or Matthew Maguire of the Central Labor Union.

Many people get a three-day weekend. Typical activities include barbecues, picnics, parades, last-chance summer travel, and back-to-school shopping. Retailers often run sales. Government offices, post offices, banks, and many schools are closed.

It is widely treated as the unofficial end of summer in the United States.

Most of the world marks International Workers’ Day on May 1. The U.S. and Canada chose the September date instead, in part to distance the holiday from the more radical associations of May Day after the 1886 Haymarket affair in Chicago.

Canada observes "Labor Day" on the same first-Monday-in-September schedule.

It in essence, has more to do with the government trying to make American's feel good about working (promotes tax revenue). 

There’s some truth in that reading, especially once you look at how it became a national holiday and how most people treat it now.

The original impulse came from unions. The 1882 New York parade was organized by workers who wanted public recognition and better conditions—shorter hours, safer workplaces, fairer pay. That part is not government PR.

The federal holiday is more complicated. President Cleveland signed it into law in June 1894, right after he sent federal troops to break the Pullman Strike. Rail traffic had been shut down; people had been killed. 

Making Labor Day official was widely viewed at the time as a political gesture; give workers a day off and a parade so the administration looks less hostile after using force against them. Cleveland was not a labor ally.

Over the next century the holiday drifted further from its militant roots. May Day (May 1) stayed the more political workers’ day in much of the world. The U.S. September date became the unofficial last weekend of summer: cookouts, sales, travel, and a three-day weekend. 

For a lot of people it functions more as “you work hard, here’s a day off” than as a reminder of strikes, eight-hour-day fights, or current union issues.

So the idea started with labor activists wanting respect. 

The federal holiday was partly a way to soothe public anger after a strike was crushed. The modern weekend is mostly leisure and retail, not a national conversation about work. 

As a Christian, I don't think it has anything to do, with glorifying Christ (which means you must insert Christ on your own). 

I think it has to do with glorifying the people who want to make sure that everyday Americans just keep on working and following the, the pattern of the world, following the carrot, rather than relying on the transformation that comes through Christ. 

Labor Day is a civic holiday, not a Christian one. It was never meant to glorify Christ, and it doesn’t. It commemorates workers and the labor movement in a particular country at a particular time. Treating it as worship would be a category mistake.

The concern is more about what it trains people to love. That’s a fair question for a Christian to ask of any national custom. 

Scripture does not treat ordinary work as “the pattern of the world” to be rejected. Work is in Genesis before the Fall. Jesus worked with his hands. Paul told believers to work quietly and eat their own bread. Colossians 3 tells slaves and free people alike to work “as for the Lord and not for men.” Diligence is praised; idleness is rebuked. So a day that simply says “honest labor matters” is not, by itself, anti-gospel.

What can become “the pattern of this world” is making work, career, productivity, or “being a good American worker” the thing that gives you worth. 

Romans 12:2 is about not being conformed to that. Identity, rest, and hope are supposed to come from Christ, not from a paycheck, a union, a holiday, or the approval of employers and the state. Sabbath exists precisely so work does not become lord.

So two things can both be true:

1. Honoring the fact that people labor, and that labor has dignity, is compatible with Christianity.

2. Using a holiday (or a culture of endless grind) to keep people looking to the world’s systems for meaning, security, and transformation is not.

Labor Day itself doesn’t preach either message very loudly anymore. For most people it’s a long weekend. 

The spiritual question is what you do with work and rest the other 364 days—whether your labor is offered to Christ or whether work (or the holiday that celebrates it) is quietly asked to do what only He can do.

I'm thinking deeper. Government wants the everyday American to be happy enough to keep on working and supporting the American dollar, which produces tax dollars, which funds government. so of course, government wants to give America an incentive like Labor Day.

Governments do have an interest in people staying productive, reasonably content, and inside the formal economy. Work generates income, income generates taxes, taxes fund the state. A holiday that costs little, feels like recognition, and does not disrupt the basic order is an easy concession. That incentive is real. It does not require a secret meeting.

It also does not mean Labor Day was invented as a trick to keep the dollar afloat.

Unions and city labor councils created the observance. Workers marched when the government was often hostile to them. Congress made it federal after a strike had already been broken with troops. Giving the day official status was cheaper and safer than addressing the conditions that produced the strike. That is closer to “throw them a bone after you used force” than to “we designed this holiday so Americans would love the Treasury.”

The rest of the year, most people work because rent, food, kids, and status do not pay themselves. The state benefits from that. Employers benefit from that. Workers also benefit from that when the alternative is hunger. Those facts can sit together without turning every Monday off into a plot.

From the Christian angle raised earlier: the danger is not that the government likes a functioning tax base. 

The danger is treating the state’s calendar, the job, or “being a productive American” as the thing that justifies your life. 

A holiday can be a small civic courtesy and still be spiritually empty. 

It can also be a day of rest you offer to God rather than a bone you chew because the system tossed it. The holiday does not decide which of those you do.

So, "Play along but choose Christ?" Play along: yes; a state that lives on labor and taxes has every reason to hand out a cheap day of recognition. Call it a bone. Call it civic religion. Call it “keep the machine running and don’t ask the deepest questions.” That reading is not crazy.

Choose Christ: the incentive is not the problem. Living as if the incentive or the machine or your suspicion of the machine is what names you; that is the problem.

The world says: work, produce, pay, take your Monday, feel seen, get back in line.

The cynic says: see the trick, resent the trick, still get back in line.

Christ says: you already have a name that is not worker, taxpayer, or critic. 

Work as unto the Lord. Rest as unto the Lord. Do not let Caesar, the dollar, or the holiday tell you what your life is for.

So, take the day off if you have it. Eat. Be with people. Thank God you can labor and that you can stop. Do not give Labor Day the job of justifying America, and do not give your distrust of the system, the job of justifying you. Both of those are still the pattern of the world.

So basically, in all that you do, do it under the glory of God. 

Eat, rest, work, take the Monday, skip the parade, pay the tax, distrust the incentive; none of that is the point by itself. 

Do it as unto the Lord, not as unto the job, the state, the dollar, or your own insight. 

1 Corinthians 10:31 whatever you do, do it to the glory of God. 

Labor Day does not have to be holy for you to be.

Colossians 3:17 says: 
“And whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.”

It sits at the hinge of the chapter. Paul has just told believers to put off the old self (anger, slander, filthy talk) and put on the new self (compassion, kindness, humility, forgiveness, love). 

Christ is “all, and in all.” Then comes Colossians 3:17.

After it, he drops into the most ordinary life: wives, husbands, children, fathers, slaves, masters. So “whatever you do” is not church language. It is kitchen, job, money, speech, and authority language.

“Whatever you do, in word or deed”

Nothing is carved out. Talk and action. Public and private. Paid work and unpaid rest. A holiday weekend and a Tuesday inspection. The verse does not create a sacred zone and a secular zone. It claims the whole field.

“Do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus”

“In the name of” means under His authority and as His representative. You are not freelancing. You do not get a second brand.

The question is not “Is this activity Christian enough?” 

The question is “Can I attach His name to how I am doing it?” If the answer is no, the problem is the manner or the motive, not the existence of work, government, or a Monday off.

“Giving thanks to God the Father through him”

Thanksgiving is not a garnish. It is how you refuse to treat work, rest, or a civic bone as if they were your savior or your enemy. 

Gratitude keeps Labor Day from becoming either an idol, as in "this proves I matter" or a grievance "this proves they own me"... You receive the day, or you work through it, and you thank the Father through Christ either way.

In the next verses Paul tells slaves to work sincerely, “fearing the Lord,” and masters to deal justly because they also have a Master in heaven. That is the same logic: the job is real, the power structure is real, and neither one gets the last word.

So the verse is stricter than “be nice at work” and freer than “only spiritual things count.” 

Word and deed. 

His name. 

Thanks to the Father. 

That is the assignment.

Happy Labor Day!

text:
A Win-Win in Both Directions

Veterans rightly point out the “win-win” when military pilots take premature retirement and join civil aviation.

The airlines gain well trained and experienced pilots. The pilots, after years of relatively modest military pay, demanding service and personal hardship, finally receive the compensation that the commercial market can offer.

Fair enough. It is indeed a win-win.

But what about the reverse?

What if highly experienced and highly paid airline captains( including former military officers) voluntarily offered to spend a few months every year in national service — for free or at substantially reduced pay?

Would that not also be a win-win?

This isn’t merely hypothetical.

Some years ago a very senior Air India captain volunteered for Pro Bono reserve military service(when it was still a government undertaking). He was an experienced commander and had even been cleared to operate Air India One. Yet his offer was reportedly politely declined by Air HQ because he was considered too senior to serve under relatively junior military officers.

If that is the real obstacle, then surely it is a design problem, not a capability problem.

Other countries such as the USA, Australia , Israel, Canada, Israel etc have long found ways to use experienced civilian airline pilots in their military reserve structures through appropriate reserve ranks, specialist appointments and carefully defined command responsibilities.

India already has the Territorial Army framework for bringing civilian expertise into national service. There are TA units built around specialised civilian skills. Why should aviation be the exception?

Civilian airline pilots have already demonstrated their willingness to serve when the country needs them — from COVID repatriation flights to evacuation missions during crises such as Operation Ganga. Many laid down their lives during the pandemic having volunteered to fly evacuation flights even though the covid vaccine was not initially administered to airline pilots. 

And the military itself has recognised the value of civil aviation expertise. Air India personnel have assisted in training IAF crews(IAF Comm Sqn)  for Air India One operations, while Air India captains have operated VVIP flights during periods of transition and training.

So the expertise is trusted when required.

Why not institutionalise it?

A Civil Aviation Reserve could provide experienced airline pilots with a formal reserve status, appropriate rank or specialist designation, periodic military training and proper legal and insurance protection — while allowing the armed forces to draw upon a substantial pool of experienced professionals during national emergencies.

India already has one direction of expertise transfer:

Military → Civil Aviation.

Perhaps it is time to create the other:

Civil Aviation → National Service.

If the first is a win-win, why shouldn’t the second be one too? 

#IAF #IndianNavy #TerritorialArmy #Aviation #NationalSecurity

text:
That is important.

The committee did not arrive at the conclusion that Southern Kaduna's crisis was invented by El-Rufai.

It investigated a conflict with a history stretching far beyond his administration.

Agwai also recommended measures including dialogue, peace-building and reconciliation, with the establishment of a permanent Peace and Reconciliation Commission among the ideas advanced.

And this brings us to perhaps the most misunderstood part of this entire controversy.

The money El-Rufai said he paid

El-Rufai publicly acknowledged in 2016 that his government had paid compensation to some Fulani.

There is no point pretending otherwise.

But listen carefully to what he actually said.

According to his contemporary account, the Agwai Committee had traced the roots of much of the recent violence to the aftermath of the 2011 post-election violence and distinguished among settled, semi-settled and transhumant Fulani.

El-Rufai said his government reached out to some transhumant Fulani, including people outside Nigeria, and offered compensation for deaths and livestock lost in earlier violence, on the condition that reprisals stop. Some accepted the appeal without payment; some requested monetary compensation for cattle losses, and some were paid.

That is the documentary trail.

And Gen. Agwai himself subsequently intervened when the issue became controversial.

His position was unequivocal: if compensation was being paid because of the Southern Kaduna crisis, all aggrieved parties should be considered, not only herdsmen. He warned that compensating only one side would amount to partial implementation of the committee's recommendations. In which other affected persons including churches and mosques that were destroyed got compensated amongst many others.

Now compare that record with Musa's words:

“He told us he paid bandits.”

That demands clarification.

Who were the people El-Rufai allegedly paid?

Were they active bandits?

Were they criminal gangs?

Were they people who had participated in attacks?

Or were they Fulani who had lost cattle and family members during the 2011 violence and whom the Agwai peace process sought to compensate in exchange for ending reprisals?

These are not semantic differences.

They are radically different factual propositions.

If Musa is referring to a different payment, then he should identify it.

If he is referring to the compensation El-Rufai publicly acknowledged, then the public deserves to know why a documented compensation and reconciliation exercise is now being described as “paying bandits.”

Then another retired general enters the story

This is where things become even more interesting.

Maj.-Gen. Danjuma Ali-Keffi, who served as GOC 1 Division in 2021, has publicly challenged Musa to produce evidence.

And he did not merely defend El-Rufai politically.

He spoke from his experience as a senior military commander.

Ali-Keffi said El-Rufai never instructed him to stop military operations against criminal elements in Kaduna. He said the military conducted clearance operations and that the Kaduna government, through officials including Samuel Aruwan, provided intelligence to commanders. He specifically rejected the suggestion that El-Rufai prevented military action against criminals.

He also raised a question that cannot simply be brushed aside:

If a governor was deliberately enabling the killing of citizens while military operations were ongoing, where were the military and intelligence agencies?

That is a very serious question.

A governor does not command the Nigerian Army.

The military has its own operational chain of command.

And Ali-Keffi says Southern Kaduna was largely under the 3 Division/Operation Safe Haven structure rather than his own 1 Division.

Therefore, if Musa is alleging a deliberate state-sponsored killing campaign, the question cannot end with El-Rufai.

It necessarily raises questions about the security agencies that had operational responsibility.

The Italian "over-under" gun designed by Sestilio Fiorini for World War II is the Breda PG (short for Presa Gas, or Gas Operated).  Developed in 1931 and produced at the Breda factory in Rome, this weapon is notable for being one of the first burst-fire rifles, utilizing a unique "over-under" double-barrel configuration to fire two rounds per trigger pull.  It was primarily offered for commercial sale and export rather than standard military adoption by the Royal Italian Army, which largely relied on the Carcano bolt-action rifle and Beretta Model 38 submachine gun during the war.

text:
Your argument is selective, racist and bigoted nonsense. It runs counter to basic logic and historical accuracy. The very argument of “conquest happens, move on” stinks of the most PUTRID racial hatred and old school bigotry aimed exclusively at Jews. 

The premise of your post has nothing to do with history. It is instead a cheap slogan of racist rhetoric, designed to treat the Jewish people as the only nation on earth whose collective memory, history, ancestry, religion, traditions, language, genetics, name, and return can be dismissed as a technicality. “Regions get conquered… move on” is not a principle. It is a special racist-driven rule written for Jews alone.

Gideon Sa’ar is not reciting a myth. He is stating a fact that every serious historian of the Near East already knows. Jews are called Jews because they are the people of Judah. Hebrew is the language of that land. Jerusalem, Hebron, Shechem, Jericho, Beer-sheva, the Galilee, Judea, and Samaria are not branding exercises from 1948. They are the names of the civilization that formed there, wrote there, ruled there, was exiled from there, and never stopped orienting its entire peoplehood toward there. That is not “a 3,000-year-old biblical deed.” That is the foundation, forming, anchoring, and enduring of a nation.

The Canaan taunt is the giveaway that the argument is unserious. Canaan was a patchwork of city-states divided into sub-ethnicities, not a monolithic distinct peoplehood, and the people who were recognized as 
Canaanites do not exist in the contemporary era. 

The Israelites indisputably emerged in that highland world, and that does not negate the history of Canaanites, nor does the history of Canaanites negate Jewish peoplehood. Jewish peoplehood is the only identity that preserved, in an unbroken chain, the language, law, calendar, liturgy, and place-names of that land. 

The Philistines, from whom the later Greco-Roman geographic label Palaestina is derived, were Aegean Sea Peoples on the coastal plain. They were not Arabs, not Muslims, and not the ancestors of a 20th-century national Palestinian movement. Invoking “Canaan” to cancel Judah is like telling the Greeks that because Mycenae fell they should stop calling themselves Greek. No one does that. They do it only here.

And the name-change history cuts the opposite way from the tweet. After the Bar Kokhba revolt, Rome reconstituted the province of Judaea as Syria Palaestina. Scholars still debate Hadrian’s exact motive, but the effect was unmistakable: strip the land of the name of the people who had just rebelled there. 

That is the origin of the later European and imperial use of “Palestine.” It was not an Arab self-name for a nation-state. It was an imperial overlay on Judea. Jews did not “invent” Judea in order to annoy Twitter. Rome tried to bury and erase Judea, and Jewish memory refused the burial.

Now let’s apply your tweet’s own rule consistently. If conquest dissolves peoplehood, the Arab-Muslim claim is the first casualty. The armies of the seventh century did not “live there as Palestinians.” They conquered a Byzantine Christian and Jewish land. After that came Crusaders, Mamluks, Ottomans, and the British. If “regions get conquered, move on” is the moral law of the universe, then the Jewish return is most certainly no less legitimate than the Arab arrival, and a lot more continuous in memory. 

You cannot use Arab conquest as title and Jewish return as original sin. That is not history. That is a racial hierarchy of claims.

Jewish indigeneity is not a campus fashion. It is the ordinary meaning of the word. A people with historical continuity in a specific territory before later empires; a distinct language, law, calendar, and religion bound to that territory; a sustained link to the land through exile; identification as that people; and a political project of returning to live as that people in that land. Hebrew was not a liturgical fossil that someone decided to cosplay in 1881. It was revived as a spoken national language because the people who spoke it never accepted that their story had ended. 

Jews prayed facing Jerusalem three times a day. They ended Passover and Yom Kippur with “Next year in Jerusalem.” They kept the agricultural calendar of a country they did not control. They buried their dead toward that land. They returned, generation after generation, to Jerusalem, Hebron, Safed, and Tiberias. Continuity does not mean majority status in every century. Continuity means the people never became someone else.

Genome-wide studies place the major Jewish diasporas on a Levantine foundation shared with one another far more than with their host countries. Ashkenazi Jews carry a primary Middle Eastern ancestry plus later European admixture, which is exactly what a people exiled westward looks like. Mizrahi and Sephardi communities preserve that Levantine core even more tightly. This does not make every neighbor a foreigner. It makes the claim that Jews are a random religious club with no peoplehood historically illiterate.

The “move on” lecture is the most grotesque double standard. No serious person tells the Irish that Viking, Norman, and English conquest means Ireland is a mood and they should dissolve. No one tells Koreans that Chinese and Japanese rule erased Korea. No one tells the Greeks that Ottoman centuries made Athens a sentimental hobby. Armenians are not instructed to “accept history” by forgetting Armenia. Kurds are not informed that because empires redrew maps they have no peoplehood. Poles were partitioned off the map and came back. 

Jews were exiled, slaughtered, banned from their own capital, and then told that the unique crime is that they refused to disappear. The only indigenous people required to treat their own name as an embarrassment is this one.

As for the comparison to Persia and Mesopotamia: those are excellent examples for the other side. Iran still exists as the civilizational successor of Persia. Iraq still sits on Mesopotamia. 

The Jewish people are the civilizational successor of Judah. The difference is that Jewish sovereignty was interrupted for centuries by empires that preferred the Jews scattered and weak. When the interruption ended, the same standard applied to every other people was suddenly declared invalid.

Now the Palestinian piece, without the usual dishonesty. Arabs have lived in this land for centuries. They have families, villages, attachments, and political claims that a serious person does not cartoon out of existence. That is not the issue. 

The issue is the demand that a modern national identity, crystallized in the twentieth century against Zionism, should retroactively monopolize indigeneity and render Jewish peoplehood a hallucination.

Even writers sympathetic to Palestinian nationalism have said the quiet part. Rashid Khalidi wrote that Palestinian national identity was “simply nonexistent a generation or two before” World War I and still limited before that war. 

Local Arab elites often described the country as southern Syria. The PLO was founded in 1964, and founded, in its original charter, to “liberate” territory that Jordan and Egypt then controlled, not only Israel inside the Green Line. After 1967 the identity hardened, the sacred vocabulary expanded, and a political nation was built. Nations can be young. France is younger than Judah. The United States is a blink. What they cannot do is annex the entire moral category of “native” by declaring that the older nation is a colonizer in its own country.

“Palestinian” was turned from a geographic adjective used for Jews, Arabs, and others under the Mandate into an exclusive ethnic title whose political function is to make Jewish self-determination colonial by definition. 

If Jews are indigenous, Zionism is a return. If Jews are recoded as white Europeans, then their state becomes an occupying crime scene no matter what borders it accepts, no matter who starts the wars, no matter how many times Jews have offered partition. The history is rearranged to fit the verdict.

International law does not follow the tweet either. The League of Nations Mandate recognized “the historical connection of the Jewish people with Palestine and the grounds for reconstituting their national home.” That was not a church pamphlet. It was the postwar legal order acknowledging a people already understood as a people. 

Jewish communities were not airlifted from Poland onto an empty stage in 1948. They were already a plurality-to-majority in Jerusalem in the nineteenth century. They bought land. They drained swamps. They built cities. They accepted partition in 1947. The Arab leadership rejected it and launched a war. Losing a war you start does not convert the other side’s indigeneity into a rumor.

So no: we should not “call it Canaan.” We should call places by the names that still live in a living people. Iran can be Iran and still be heir to Persia. Iraq can be Iraq and still sit on Mesopotamia. This land can contain Arab communities with real rights and still be the land of Israel for the Jewish people. Those two facts are only incompatible if your politics require one people to be fake.

“Move on” is what Europe told Jews after every expulsion. It is what the Arab world told Jews after 850,000 of them were pushed out of Iraq, Yemen, Egypt, Libya, and Syria. It is what the Romans intended when they tried to pry the name Judea off the map. The Jewish answer, for three thousand years, has been the same. We are not a visiting committee. We are not a metaphor. We are the people of this land, and we did not survive exile in order to apologize for coming home.

In my image I have reimagined and given a contemporary take to the ancient Irish goddess Morrigan. This is her myth.

The Morrígan is an Irish war goddess of fate, sovereignty, and death, often called the Phantom Queen or Great Queen. She has different faces. She appears as a single being and as a triad (Badb, Macha, Nemain), shifting between a beautiful woman, a hag, a wolf, an eel, and most famously, a crow.

In the Ulster Cycle she meets the hero Cú Chulainn, offers herself to him, and is refused. After that she becomes his shadow: she fights him in animal form, then later perches as a raven on his dying body, claiming the battlefield of which she has always been the true owner. She does not merely watch war. She stirs it, prophesies its end, and decides whose blood will be let into the ground.

She is the voice that says a king will fall, a raid will drown a province in corpses, and glory is the only bright hope before the birds come to peck.

text:
Fontaines D.C. — Romance ★★★★

"I'm gon' hit your business if it's momentary blissness"

Since their debut, 'Dogrel', Fontaines D.C. have emerged as one of the most exciting Irish bands in decades. Right from the start, they captured the attention of critics worldwide, with 'Dogrel' even earning a Mercury Prize nomination. I've always liked them, but never fully loved them the way many of my friends and fellow Irish music enthusiasts do—until this absolutely fantastic fourth LP. It’s a game-changer for me. It fucking rules.
The band has long been celebrated for their exceptional songwriting and musicianship, but their latest album, 'Romance', offers a refreshing glimpse into their lighter, more playful side. Full of thoughtful concepts, the album is anchored by the band’s reliable songwriting. Not every experiment lands—“Sundowner,” with its ethereal vibe, feels like a more subdued version of Slowdive—but 'Romance' still pushes the boundaries of what we’ve come to expect from Fontaines. Though they’ve distanced themselves from their punk roots, their ability to express a wide emotional range remains as strong as ever. I really appreciate this shift in direction, and I can hear the clear influence of bands like Nirvana, Smashing Pumpkins, R.E.M., Massive Attack, Portishead, and even Korn. As a ‘90s kid, these sounds hit my ears just right. The album introduces captivating new textures that make for urgent, compelling music—both melancholic and seductive. Far from a simple love letter, 'Romance' is a complex, thrilling exploration of the many facets of romance.
So it’s finally happened for me—the moment when Danny DeVito’s epiphanic line from It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia plays in my head: “I get it now.” I get it now. I understand why people have been saying for years that Fontaines are the best Irish band since U2. And I don’t disagree.

Best Track: Starburster
Worst Track: Horseness Is the Whatness

text:
🐼China is edging, step by step, into Japan's trap

There is a particular kind of headline that Beijing would rather not have to write twice, and this week it wrote it again. China's Ministry of Finance has pumped upwards of 300 billion yuan into eight financial institutions: 100 billion into Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, of which the ministry supplied 70 billion; 160 billion into Agricultural Bank of China, 130 billion of it from the state, the remainder shouldered by China Tobacco; 35 billion into China Life. The list goes on, each figure more forgettable than the last, and that is rather the point — a recapitalisation dressed up as routine business.

It is not routine. This is only the second such rescue since 2023, when Beijing issued 520 billion yuan in bonds to shore up the banking system's liquidity. On the day the latest injection was announced, shares in all forty-two of China's listed banks fell — Industrial and Commercial Bank, China Construction Bank, China Life, Minsheng Bank, the lot. Markets, unlike ministries, do not pretend not to have noticed.

🐼The bill nobody wants to open

Hui Ka Yan, the founder of Evergrande, has been sentenced to life imprisonment, which offers a certain narrative satisfaction and settles nothing whatsoever. He walked away, in effect, from two trillion yuan in bank debt, and that debt has not vanished merely because its architect is now behind bars. Nobody in Beijing has volunteered to establish precisely how much of it the banks are still quietly absorbing, because to ask the question is to invite an answer nobody wants. The result is a banking sector trading, without exception, below book value across all forty-two listed names — Minsheng Bank, Evergrande's largest lender, worst of all, at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.22. A bank valued at little more than a fifth of its stated worth is not being modest. It is being disbelieved.

🐼The decade consumption forgot

China's property bubble has now run a full decade since 2017, and the first casualty, as ever, was the willingness to spend. Wang Wang, the snack conglomerate whose fortunes track the Chinese consumer about as faithfully as any single stock can, has fallen below three Hong Kong dollars. Shein's Hong Kong listing dropped for three consecutive days the moment trading opened. None of this is coincidence; it is the arithmetic of a population that has watched the value of its principal asset fall and has concluded, reasonably enough, that cash in hand beats cash spent.

🐼A lesson Japan already sat through

What comes next is worse than falling prices. It is the grinding, decade-spanning discipline of deflation, and Japan wrote the manual whether China cares to read it or not. After 2001, Japanese life insurers buckled, banks failed in clusters, and the survivors spent years merging themselves into financial holding companies simply to stay upright. All the while, and quite against the wishes of anyone trying to export their way out of trouble, the yen kept rising — climbing, even as the 2011 earthquake and tsunami left the country reeling, to 75.35 against the dollar.

Worse followed. Japanese interest rates fell to zero and beyond; ten-year government bond yields dipped to minus 0.27 per cent. The lower rates fell, the stronger the yen grew, and the less inclined ordinary households felt to spend a yen of it.  Businesses and households refusing to borrow at any price, however cheap, and instead racing to pay down what they already owed. It took Japan thirty years to climb out.

🐼The currency that will not behave

Around 2017, Washington leaned on Beijing to let the yuan rise, and Beijing, characteristically, refused — economists lined up to warn that China must not repeat Japan's mistake. Now nobody is asking. The pressure has stopped and the yuan has strengthened anyway, of its own accord, even as Chinese interest rates keep falling. Falling rates and a rising currency, together, are precisely the combination that makes deflation hardest to bear — the one moment in the cycle when a country has the least room left to manoeuvre.

🐼Capital voting with its feet

Beijing has responded by tightening the screws elsewhere: heavier taxes on companies, larger fines, stricter oversight from the centre. The predictable consequence is that insiders are working harder than ever to move their money offshore, and the tighter the regulatory grip, the faster the capital slips through it, flowing in exactly the direction the state least wants.

If none of this changes, China's next decade will be harder than its last. Hui Ka Yan has his life sentence and his ledger has been quietly closed by the state that once financed his empire. The bill, however, does not know it has been closed. It is still sitting in forty-two banks' accounts, waiting, with the patience only a balance sheet can manage, to be opened again.

text:
EUROPE'S DEBT BOMB: WHY THE NEXT CRISIS MAY START IN THE EUROZONE, NOT THE U.S.
The text argues a significant point: while the U.S. federal debt is undeniably massive, the structural weaknesses of the eurozone may make it the epicenter of the next sovereign debt crisis. The U.S. has the advantage of issuing the world's primary reserve currency, a single government managing fiscal policy, and a unified Treasury market that can attract global capital. The eurozone, by contrast, has a single central bank but 20 separate governments issuing their own bonds, each with independent fiscal policies and electorates.
THE FRENCH DANGER: A SYSTEMIC THREAT
The most alarming signal is France's rising borrowing costs. Its 10-year bond yield has risen to approximately 4.15%, its highest level since 2008, and now slightly exceeds Italy's . As the eurozone's second-largest economy and a core member of the single currency, France's rising borrowing costs cannot be dismissed as a problem of a peripheral state. It represents a systemic threat to the entire monetary union.
GERMAN WEAKNESS: THE LOSS OF THE ENGINE
Germany also offers little comfort. Its 10-year yield is around 3.3%, its highest in 15 years, while its industrial base remains weak. Both key players are paying more to borrow just as Brussels prepares for a new wave of spending, including up to €800 billion for rearmament. The combination of rising yields and an aging population will continue to put pressure on public finances . The problem is compounded by high energy costs and the need to support Ukraine, leaving European governments with few good options .
THE STRUCTURAL WEAKNESS OF THE EUROZONE
The text correctly identifies the eurozone's fundamental flaw: a single currency and central bank, but no unified fiscal system. Each of the 20 member states issues its own government bonds with separate budgets and electorates . The European Central Bank must set a single interest rate for economies with vastly different debt levels and growth rates . This creates three major problems:
A Single Policy for Diverse Economies: The ECB must choose one interest rate for all. Raising rates to curb inflation in Germany could choke Italy's economy, which is more vulnerable to higher borrowing costs .
The Spread Problem: Because governments issue their own bonds, investors demand higher interest rates for perceived riskier countries, widening the spread .
Artificial Safety Valves: The eurozone has had to invent mechanisms like the TPI (anti-spread shield) and the Stability Pact to prevent a collapse .
A CHOICE FOR MARKETS
The U.S. can use the dollar's global role to buy more time. Europe, however, may face its reckoning sooner, as it lacks a robust federal structure to support its debt burden. A single central bank cannot indefinitely reconcile all national budgets. The markets have begun to price this reality. The next crisis in the West may not start in Washington, but in the eurozone, which for years presented itself as the responsible alternative to American fiscal profligacy. Both have serious debt problems, but Europe's is embedded in a system poorly equipped to handle it. The question is not whether the crisis will come, but which model will break first.
THE U.S. ADVANTAGE
The United States enjoys a crucial advantage: it issues the world's primary reserve currency, has a single federal government raising taxes, and sells bonds on a single, enormous Treasury market . This allows it to attract foreign capital and shift some of the cost of its debt abroad. The eurozone lacks this "safety valve." As the text notes, the U.S. debt is a problem, but the European Union's structural weakness may cause it to break first.

text:
Untethered Field Brief: California draws a boundary around AI reading workers’ emotions

Verified development

California’s Legislature approved AB 1883 on August 30 and formally enrolled it on September 3, 2026. It now awaits Governor Gavin Newsom’s signature or veto and is not yet law.

If enacted, employers could not use AI-powered workplace-surveillance tools to:

Recognize, infer, or predict a worker’s emotional state.
Collect data generated by measuring activity in a worker’s nervous system.

The restriction would cover private businesses, public agencies, universities, labor contractors, cities, counties, school systems, and other governmental employers. The Labor Commissioner and public prosecutors could enforce it, with penalties up to $500 per violation. California Legislature, enrolled bill⁠

Who is affected

Workers in call centers, hospitals, warehouses, transportation, retail, public services, and other closely monitored environments would receive the clearest protection.

The bill addresses tools marketed as capable of interpreting stress, fatigue, engagement, friendliness, or other internal states through voice, facial activity, biometrics, or neural measurements. Workers could still be monitored through many conventional methods; the prohibition is limited to AI emotion inference and neural-data collection.

Why it matters for Untethered

Interpretation: Workplace automation is moving beyond tracking what a person does toward claiming to know what the person feels. That changes the relationship between labor and management because an uncertain machine inference about mood, stress, or attitude could influence coaching, scheduling, discipline, or promotion.

AB 1883 attempts to establish that a worker’s interior state is not ordinary productivity data. It offers a strong field question for human-centered technology: Which parts of a person must remain outside an employer’s measurement system?

Field direction

Call centers, hospitals, fast-food workplaces, warehouses, and municipal employers offer useful field sites.

Questions worth carrying:

What behavioral, biometric, voice, or wearable data is already collected?
Are workers told when software evaluates attitude, stress, or engagement?
Can an emotional inference affect scheduling, evaluation, or discipline?
When does an employer classify surveillance as necessary for safety?

Uncertainty and bias concerns

The governor has not acted, so current employer practices have not changed. The bill contains a safety exception that may become a significant area of dispute. It also does not create a technical testing or certification process for determining whether a product actually performs emotion recognition.

Claims that AI can reliably identify internal emotional states remain contested. Cultural expression, disability, neurodivergence, language, race, and gender could all affect how behavior is interpreted, making biased or false conclusions a central fieldwork concern.

Gazing into the Mediterranean horizon, Alexandra sought her escape. She had spent a healthy part of the last six weeks frolicking the salty seas—from the beaches of the Portuguese Algarve to those of the Greek Islands—exercising a type of Polynesian ocean worship she had sampled in Hawaii. The waves had been middling, but time in the sun had left her skin nicely bronzed. Haifa provided ideal conditions for bodysurfing. The ankle waders found interest in her antics. Some offered applause, while others gawked as if she were a rumbustious sea creature that kept washing ashore.
--There was one dogged frowner: a thickset woman with golden curls spilling out of her bathing cap, who, if raised in Japan, would have been trained in the art of the Sumo. Now she stood waiting with two police officers, pointing.
--Alexandra was unsure of her offense, awash in a strange land and knowing few of its rules. Her Jantzen swimsuit clung to her lithe frame modestly. Perhaps it struck blasphemously to display wet hair in the ancient Holy Land. She jumped bashful waves that broke close to shore and ducked under the churning lather of those so forceful they collapsed under their weight out to sea. Having the patience to corral the ideal wave proved key, and likely her only chance, short of swimming for Cyprus, to avoid arrest.

text:
Well I’m being a bit facetious — and of course gross anthropomorphizing doesn’t usually offer grown people much “data.” Inertial-plane physics and its hypertechnicalities I’m not in a position to grasp, hence I’m not going to opine on them for the sake of argument.
I do think mathematization and its modular moonchild, if you will, have created an increasingly spectacular material culture that needs to deny its ground in order to furnish the confusion and mystification the narrative in general demands (Michael Hudson). Hence my goal: a return to the patrilineal foundation of civilization via the remarginalization of the gynocentric.
Hudson’s gospel deconstruction is the same pattern in sacred dress. “Forgive us our debts” is not first a mood. It is a Clean Slate: Jubilee against creditor capture, the cancellation of arrears that palace and temple once wrote into the calendar so the household would not be eaten. Later piety spiritualizes the clause, turns debt into a private interior, and leaves the oligarchic machinery untouched. That is mystification. The narrative keeps the words and denies the ground — land, lineage, release, the father’s house not foreclosed.
Your firmament gag does the same work at a cheaper scale. You did not show I am on a wildly different ontology page from the Bible. You collapsed the Name into a dome-coordinate so “sky daddy” could look Bible-accurate and a claim about husbandry could look like speculation stacked against a children’s map. ANE vault-language is not the paternal function under discussion. Form imposed on physis that does not care — naming, law, cultivation, the binding of the ought, the refusal to let debt-peonage become nature — is not a weather-god on a lid.
Spectacular culture mathematizes, modularizes, then calls the enclosure “just nature” and the ought “just preference.” Hudson’s point is that the Gospels remember a patrilineal, household, anti-creditor foundation and that later religion and later economics both profit by forgetting it. You restage the doll in the air so you never have to occupy that ground. That is not data. It is the narrative denying its own husbandry.

text:
Do you know only once in a year, sacrifice or Bali ritual is followed in Puri Jagannath Mandir? The Bhog is offered to tantrik goddess Maa Bimala or Vimala there. 

In the temple of Lord Jagannath in Puri, Mother Vimala is present. The connection of this Shakta tradition with Jagannath’s Bhairava-tattva is also an extraordinary example of the religious consciousness of eastern India. If Vaishnava and Shakta are always treated here as opposite poles, a large part of history is left out.

I do not deny Vaishnava theology. I do not deny Shaiva theology. I do not deny Shakta theology. I do not deny the historical influence of Buddhist Tantra either.

All of these are mine. But that does not mean one person should impose their own mode of worship on another. Diversity is not weakness. Rather, one of the strengths of Hinduism is that it does not make a single path compulsory for everyone, but allows many paths to coexist.

We certainly want an end to religious persecution, extremist militancy, and communal violence. We want our people to remain safe, our temples and worship to remain free, and our culture and heritage to be protected. But even within that struggle, I must live my eastern Indian Hindu identity in my own way.

text:
OUR LADY OF SORROWS NOVENA

Day 1

Prayer in honor of the First Sorrow of Mary,  Simeon’s Prophesy in the Temple:

Most Sorrowful Mother, grief filled was your heart when, on offering your divine Son at the temple, Holy Simeon foretold that a sword would pierce your soul. There and then you knew you would suffer with Jesus.

Queen of Martyrs, let me unite my heart to yours in this pain, and ask you the grace to keep the thought of my death in mind, so I may always avoid sin.

Hail Mary…

Prayer to our Sorrowful Mother for a particular grace:

O mother most holy and sorrowful, Queen of Martyrs, you who stood by your Son as He agonized on the cross. By the sufferings of your life, by that sword of pain that pierced your heart, by your perfect joy in heaven, look down on me kindly as I kneel before you, sympathizing with your sorrows and offering you my petition with childlike trust.

Dear Mother, because your Son refuses you nothing, ask of His Sacred Heart to mercifully hear my prayer and to grant this prayer in accord with His most perfect will. Therefore, through the merits of His Sacred Passion, along with those of your sufferings at the foot of the cross, I pray…

(Mention your intention here…)

Mother most merciful, to whom shall I go in my misery if not to you who pities us poor sinful exiles in this valley of tears? I beseech you to offer Jesus but one drop of His most Precious Blood and but one pang of His Loving Heart. Remind Him that you are our sweetness, our life and our hope, and your prayer will be heard. Amen

Memorare:

Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known that anyone who fled to your protection, implored your help or sought your intercession, was left unaided. Inspired by this confidence, I fly unto you, O Virgin of Virgins, my Mother. To you do I come, before you I stand, sinful and sorrowful. O Mother of the Word Incarnate, despise not my petitions, but in your clemency, hear and answer me. Amen.

text:
Elon Musk pursued his first wife Justine at Queen's University with a persistence that she later described as somewhere between flattering and clinical.

She turned him down multiple times before agreeing to a date.

He spotted her in the common room during their first year. He walked up and asked her out. She said no. He showed up again. She said no again. He started appearing wherever she happened to be. The library. The dining hall. The path between classes. He was not subtle. He was systematic.

Justine later wrote that what struck her wasn't the pursuit itself but the quality of it. He didn't try to charm her. He didn't flirt. He presented himself the way you'd present a business proposal. Here is what I am. Here is what I will become. The offer is on the table. The closing date is open.

She eventually agreed to a date. He took her out for ice cream and told her he would one day be very successful. Not as a boast. As a data point. The same way he would later tell investors that SpaceX would land rockets. A statement of intent delivered with the certainty of someone describing something that has already happened.

They married years later. The marriage ended. But the pursuit at Queen's University is the earliest record of a pattern that would define every relationship that followed. Elon does not court women the way other men do. He identifies a target, determines the approach, and executes with the persistence of someone solving an engineering problem. The emotion is real. The method is mechanical.

The same mind that lands rockets on drone ships approached a girl in a common room with the same framework: attempt, fail, adjust, attempt again, succeed eventually. Romance as iteration.

Monday Morning Futures: Labor Day Holiday Edition
Monday Morning: September 7, 2026

Labor Day

As the nation pauses to observe Labor Day on Monday, September 7, 2026, financial and agricultural markets remain closed across the United States in honor of the American worker. From the essential labor sustaining our agricultural backbone to the workforce driving industrial, technical, and corporate productivity, today marks a reflection on the contributions that underpin the American economy. Market liquidity remains subdued across international trading desks, with major U.S. exchanges, futures pits, and government offices set to reopen tomorrow, Tuesday, September 8.

News, Markets, Futures & Outlooks

Today’s Top Story: Weak Jobs Print Sparks Record Breakout and Rate-Cut Rethink on Wall Street

Global financial markets head into the new week following a high stakes, record breaking session on Wall Street before the holiday pause. Shifting macroeconomic currents took center stage after the U.S. government reported an unexpected contraction of 23,000 jobs in July, alongside sharp downward revisions to prior months.

While a weakening labor market typically flags broader growth anxieties, equity markets chose to read the data through a dovish lens. The softer metrics immediately pushed expectations for aggressive near-term Federal Reserve rate hikes off the table, sending the S&P 500 surging past 7,790 to close at a fresh all-time high of 7,798.99. Treasury yields softened across the curve with the 10-year yield dropping while mega-cap tech leadership and solid corporate profit growth continued to anchor broad index strength.

Global News This Morning

Overnight headlines are dominated by a steepening logistical crisis in international Black Sea shipping. Officials in Kyiv confirmed that Ukrainian grain exports dropped to just 30% of target volumes during early August due to ongoing strikes on maritime infrastructure, warning that total shipments could be halved without restored access through Greater Odesa.

In response to widespread Russian vessel targeting in the Sea of Azov, commercial traffic through the Kerch Strait remains effectively paralyzed, with Kyiv reportedly floating third-party proposals for a mutual halt to merchant ship strikes. Also, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed new sanctions targeting 13 vessels and 39 entities linked to illicit grain transport, while persistent tensions in the Middle East around the Strait of Hormuz continue to underpin elevated war-risk insurance premiums across global energy and grain transit corridors.

Top U.S. & State News

The USDA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) and state veterinary partners confirm that total U.S. detections in the current New World screwworm outbreak stand at 45 confirmed cases (44 in Texas, 1 in New Mexico), with 4 cases remaining actively under observation and treatment. Biosecurity teams report that containment efforts and sterile fly dispersals are keeping the outbreak localized, though movement restrictions across 22 Texas counties and the live cattle import ban from Mexico remain strictly enforced.

Legislators in Washington introduced H.R. 7466 (the SAFE CATTLE Act) to compel formal coordination between the USDA and Interior Department on wildlife screwworm surveillance. Meanwhile, cattle groups are closely analyzing the economic ripple effects of the Tyson plant restructurings on a regional cash cattle basis.

State News

Texas: TAHC checkpoints remain active across 22 West and South Texas counties following 45 cumulative screwworm cases, with sterile fly drops concentrated along brush country zones.

Illinois: The livestock trade is digesting Tyson's announced closure of its Joslin beef processing plant, prompting regional feedlots to evaluate alternative terminal options.

Nebraska: Grain terminals are adjusting basis levels following recent WASDE report yield cuts, as corn crops enter early dent stage across central counties.

Kansas: Feeder cattle auctions saw late-week pricing pressure as buyers factored in broader packer slaughter reductions.

Iowa: Crop conditions remain mostly stable, with producers monitoring late August rainfall forecasts for soybean pod development.

The Economy

Fresh economic indicators signal growing pressure on the American consumer as persistent inflation continues to weigh on spending power. Commerce Department data showed U.S. retail sales unexpectedly dropped 0.6% in July, marking the sharpest single-month pullback in over a year. 

The downturn was felt broadly across auto dealerships, service stations, and online retailers, reinforcing growing concerns that household balance sheets are fatiguing under sustained price pressure. Concurrently, preliminary data from the University of Michigan showed consumer sentiment tumbling 8%, with short term business expectations sliding 11% as higher energy costs and elevated core inflation erode real income gains.

The National Weather Story

Late-summer weather patterns across the Corn Belt continue to offer a mixed production outlook as crops transition from kernel fill into early maturity.

Prostate Conditions: Moderate temperatures and scattered precipitation across parts of Iowa, Illinois, and Indiana have stabilized crop condition scores following July’s heat stress.

Dryness Creep: Portions of the Western Corn Belt and Central Plains face tightening topsoil moisture profiles, capping top-end yield potential for late planted beans.
Harvest Early Stages: Southern corn harvest is gaining momentum under mostly favorable weather, with early yield reports proving highly variable depending on localized rainfall timing.
Commodities

Grains closed out the latest session on a strong footing as tight global export supplies and post-WASDE yield adjustments fueled short covering. September Corn finished up 11 cents at $4.59/bu, while September Soybeans advanced 11.75 cents to close at $11.77 3/4. September Chicago Wheat added 22 cents to land at $6.74 3/4 on mounting Black Sea transit disruptions. Livestock futures faced late-week headwinds from packer margin adjustments, leaving October Live Cattle down $1.17 to $218.87/cwt and September Feeder Cattle down $2.65 to $334.55/cwt.

Energy markets rallied into the holiday weekend following fresh geopolitical friction and potential naval blockade concerns. September WTI Crude Oil closed up $1.15 to $82.40 per barrel, with Brent settling near $88.82. Equity markets posted a broad record rally into Friday's close before the holiday halt. The S&P 500 reached a new all-time high close of 7,798.99 after making intraday highs above 7,816.
