text:
For coal to become a diamond, it must be crushed.

Not praised. Not shielded from pressure. Not crowned while it is still black and brittle. Crushed. Heated. Reduced. What is common only ceases to be common when the weight comes.

That is what the world refuses to hear. They want the shine without the press. They want paradise without the cross. They want the diamond handed to them on a stage, while the ego stays soft, proud, untouched.

So they lie. Imperial religions and state ideologies promise a garden on this earth: give more power, obey the caliph, obey the party, obey the committee—and heaven will descend. An old lie. A bloody lie. Because a man who will not be pressed does not become a jewel. He becomes a tyrant.

Christianity does not sell paradise by decree. It does not say coal is already a diamond if you shout loud enough. It says the opposite: you are flawed. You must be broken. The old man has to yield. The flesh has to lose. Only then does something hard, clean, and true appear.

The crushing hurts. A marriage that demands fidelity. Work that does not applaud. Sin named, not stroked. Forgiveness that costs. Truth that isolates. Obedience when no one is watching. That is the press. That is the heat. That is the weight that separates brilliance from smoke.

Whoever flees the crushing remains coal and calls it freedom.
Whoever accepts the crushing learns the pain was not the end. It was the method.
Without pressure, there is no diamond.
Without a cross, there is no crown.
Without truth, there is only black rock wearing the speech of treasure.

The world offers the throne now.
Christ offers the press now—and life after.
Choose.
Because coal that refuses the weight does not escape the fire.
It only chooses to burn without ever shining.

If a dog loves chicken, you do not lure it with charcoal.
If a child lives for candy, you do not bait the trap with a fast.
If a thirsty man will sell his soul for wine, you do not hold out an empty cup and call it joy.
You offer what the hunger already wants. That is how you catch a creature. That is how you tell a hunter from a father.

Now put the two majority claims on that table and watch what is served.

In the days of Jesus the Jews wanted a war-king: Rome off their necks, a throne in Zion, a Messiah who wins the way men win. He offers the opposite. No legion. A cross. “My kingdom is not of this world.” The Gentiles wanted to keep the old feast—pleasure, orgies, the body as a god, even the rot of incest that Paul names in the churches’ neighbor-world. Jesus says stop. Do not look to lust. Tear out the eye. One man. One woman. Master the flesh. In the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage. He is not selling chicken to the dog. He is offering charcoal to a mouth trained on meat—and then dying to make the mouth new.

In the days of Muhammad the men who built the army wanted what fighting men have always wanted: women, wine, spoil, a heaven that feels like the night after a raid. Look at the menu. Wives here. More promised there. A lawful appetite crowned. That is not charcoal. That is chicken. The lure matches the pack.

Today the world is more promiscuous, not less. The same test still works. What does each message cost the male ego now?

Then, the greatest machine of power was an army of men. A revelation that baptizes the sword and the bed will gather that machine fast. Now the greatest machine is the state: parties, courts, borders, schools, media. Jesus still says the same inconvenient sentence: his kingdom is not of this world. He will not hand you a ministry of truth to capture. He will not let you baptize your coalition and call it Zion. The gospel remains against what we like. It tells the religious nationalist he cannot have a holy empire. It tells the libertine he cannot have a holy orgy. It tells the ambitious man the last seat is a towel and a basin. So ask the honest question: if someone wanted to deceive us, would he keep offering charcoal—fasting to the sweet tooth, a cross to the man who wants a crown, one wife to the man who wants a harem, a kingdom not of this world to the man who wants this world?

And the other story: the Scriptures were “corrupted,” they say—so that what remains is the hard road. Fasting for candy-lovers. A crucified God for people who wanted a Caesar. That would be the stupidest fraud in history. Forgers who want followers do not edit the bait down. They edit it up.

Watch the present. Islam can advance inside countries where a political left that hates the church will walk beside it for a season. That left is not built on Sinai. It is built on permission: the body as politics, gender as clay, desire as a right. For a while the alliance is useful. A shared enemy—the Christ who says no. After the house is taken, the guest does not keep the host’s rules. Then comes sharia: the army under another name. If a doctrine already allows deception for the cause when the cause is threatened, the handshake was never the destination. It was the door.

So which god is hunting, and which God is fathering?

The god who plates what the age already craves—women and wine for the raider then, power and narrative for the operator now—is easy to recognize. He does not need to change the human heart. He only needs to bless it.

The God of Jesus keeps serving charcoal to the old appetite: die to yourself, one covenant bed, no orgy, no child as a prize, no throne of this world, no virgins as pay, only God. He would be a fool of a con man. He makes sense as a Father who would rather lose the crowd than feed the sickness.

Scripture was not “fixed” to make the gospel tastier. The gospel is still the least marketable offer on the table. That is how you know it was not designed by a man building an army—or a man building a government. It was designed by someone who wants sons, not customers.

In reality, the Left is nothing but the Devil's excrement. He comes along and shits his stinking filth onto nations, ruins the youth, promotes promiscuity, empties minds in favor of a sick collective, attacks families and faith, and then sends his soldiers to dominate, conquer, and enslave people so they will worship him.

Islam Did Not Win by Truth. It Won by Fire, Fear, and a Fake Heaven.

Around the year 650, about twenty years after Muhammad died in 632, Caliph Uthman (ruled 644–656) did not protect the Qur’an. He burned the other written versions. Soldiers in the new empire were already fighting over different readings. Uthman made one official copy and ordered the rest destroyed. That is not preservation. That is a cover-up with a torch. The Bible was copied, attacked, translated, and still stands where anyone can compare the manuscripts. Islam ended the argument by fire. A book that needs burning in the mid-600s to stay “perfect” is already afraid of scrutiny.

Muhammad’s own cousin Ali ibn Abi Talib bowed to him in the first years of the movement, around 610–613, while Ali was still a youth in Muhammad’s house. Family first. House first. Then the tribe. Then the sword. That is how a movement starts when it cannot live on open proof.

After 632, Islam advanced by lie and steel. Arabia was taken first. Then Syria, Egypt, and Persia fell in the 630s and 640s under the early caliphs. “Peace” after you submit. Tax if you refuse. Death if you leave. That is not the Gospel. That is conquest dressed as worship. The endgame is not “know the true God.” The endgame is a global caliphate—one man, or one system of men, sitting on the throne of law, war, and religion. That started as a real empire in Medina and Damascus, then Baghdad, then later the Ottomans, and it is still the dream of those who want the world under their law. That is not adoration of the Creator. That is men manufacturing their own god: themselves. They call it Allah’s rule. It is their rule with a holy stamp.

Watch the history. In 656 Uthman was murdered. Then Muslims killed Muslims over who would rule. The Umayyads turned the caliphate into a family dynasty after 661. The Abbasids seized it in 750. The Ottomans later wrote extra state laws beside sharia when the palace needed it. One century the “law of God” looks one way. The next century the sultan writes what the empire wants. If heaven’s constitution changes with the king’s interest, it was never heaven speaking. It was power speaking.

And the prize they sell? A carnal paradise. Women. Beds. Wine. Endless appetite. That is not the holy God. That is a brothel in the sky for men who obeyed. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit do not buy souls with lust. Jesus offers a clean heart and the face of God—not a reward that looks like the flesh they already worshiped on earth. If your heaven is built on the same hungers that damn a man, that heaven did not come from Christ.

Force is not faith. Obedience at knifepoint is not what the true God wants. It is stupid. If God only wanted terror, He would not need proud killers to do His advertising. He could split the sky once and every mouth would shut. Even a father knows the difference between a child who honors him and a child who only fears the belt. You think the Maker of the universe is dumber than that? If your god only wants fear, your god is small—and the men who speak for him are full of pride and death.

The true God did not send an empire in the 600s. He sent a Son.

A man owned a fish. Every time he tried to feed it, the fish ran. “I want its good,” he said, “but it thinks I am a monster.” His friend answered: “To that fish you are a giant. The only way it will trust you is if you become a fish and enter the tank.”

That is Jesus. He did not burn books in 650. He did not build a caliphate. He entered our water. He became one of us. He did not demand a heart crushed by soldiers. He asked for a heart that is actually His.

Fear fills an empire. Love makes a son. The true God wants the second. The caliphate only knows the first.

Christianity is not a religion.
It is the way of life that created and built entire civilizations.
It is looking to the reference that is Jesus Christ and saying: “This is the good. This is the way.”

Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights (James 1:17). The reference of what is good is God. In Eden humanity lost that reference and the world sank into darkness. Children abandoned in the streets of Rome. Widows burned alive in India. Cannibals devouring enemies without conscience. Until Jesus Christ came and divided history into before and after.

He restored the reference. Christianity founded the universities, the hospitals, the orphanages. It preserved knowledge while Europe burned. It elevated the dignity of every human being made in the image of God. It ended widow-burning, foot-binding, human sacrifice, and cannibalism across continents. Missionaries carried the cross to the Pacific, to Africa, to India, to China, to Japan — and wherever the reference of Christ took root, the value of life rose and barbarism fell. Even the modern atheist still breathes Christian air without realizing it. The historian Tom Holland, an atheist, confessed: “In my morals and ethics I have learned to accept that I am not Greek or Roman, but deeply and proudly Christian.”

Before Christ, justice belonged to the strong. The slave was property. The woman nearly invisible. The foreigner disposable. The cross was the ultimate instrument of humiliation. Then an innocent Man was crucified by a Roman court — and rose again. That cross became the center of history. Justice and mercy kissed. The idea that every person has infinite dignity, the right of defense, the protection of the weak, the limits of the state — all of it was born from the blood of Christ, not from Greece, not from Rome, not from the Enlightenment.

Yet the prostitute has returned. Empires and governments that once tasted the salt of the gospel now prostitute themselves to every anti-Christ ideology. They sell their children. They fund the persecutors. They call good evil and evil good. They have lost their savor.

And the Beast is rising. The same system that used the prostitute for its pleasure will one day hate her, strip her, devour her, and burn her with fire. The ideologies, the politicians, the nations, the empires that sold themselves for temporary power will be consumed by the very darkness they courted.

This is not the end of the story.
The stone cut without hands is still coming.
The Kingdom of the One who was crucified and rose again will fill the whole earth.

Until then, the remnant must remain salt.
Because the prostitute is already drunk with blood.
And the Beast is already sharpening its teeth.

not a religion.

Caesarea Maritima (May 641): After a grueling seven-year siege, Mu'awiya’s forces breached the heavily fortified Byzantine capital of Palestine via a subterranean tunnel/aqueduct. When the defenses collapsed, the fighting raged for three days, the entire 7,000-man Byzantine garrison was put to the sword, and thousands of inhabitants were taken captive.

Nikiou (May 641): During the conquest of Egypt, the fortified town of Nikiou in the Nile Delta offered fierce resistance. When Amr ibn al-As's army finally forced their way in, it resulted in a brutal massacre of the local Christian population and defenders alike, with contemporary chroniclers like John of Nikiou recording widespread slaughter in the streets and churches.

Sultium / Amorium / Other Frontier Strongholds: While major administrative hubs in the Levant largely capitulated to preserve tax bases, frontier cities that chose to fight to the bitter end—such as various fortified garrisons across Byzantine-held Anatolia and North Africa later in the century—frequently faced full-scale assault, plunder, and execution of combatants upon falling.

🔶It means constraining rival supply from Russia, the Middle East, Canada, and anyone else who can offer molecules without U.S. political conditions. And it means keeping domestic gas cheap enough that exports stay competitive without a backlash at home.

I am grateful to share a project that continues to grow through collaboration, conversation, and the wisdom of educators across the country. 

Dr. LaTonya Rayford White and I are developing The Middle School Culture Blueprint, a forthcoming manuscript for the National Catholic Educational Association (NCEA) that focuses on practical ways to support teachers, engage students, strengthen teams, and build thriving middle school cultures.

Alongside the manuscript, I am hosting a special podcast series over the next two months featuring educational experts, school and diocesan leaders, university partners, principals, and teachers from across the nation who are generously sharing their wisdom, experiences, and strategies from the field.

Featured guests throughout the series include Dr. Michael T. O'Connor, Ph.D. from the Roche Center for Catholic Education - Boston College, Dr. Aliya Holmes, Ph.D. from St. John's University, Dr. Nicci Dowd and Dr. Jennifer Scully, Ed.D. from Marymount University, Dr. Nancy Baker, Ed.D from the Archdiocese of Baltimore, Lynsie Reavis from the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Washington, Anita Harkins-Mehsling, Archdiocese of Omaha, Tommy Corrigan and Jeanne Donatelli, Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Washington, Karina Lepkowski and Mary Peters from the Archdiocese of Detroit, and many more educators who are doing this important work every day.

We can do more to support educators — together!

The Fairy Tale of Corporate Globalism and American Citizen Resistance to Corporate AI Tyranny

A Review of The Fairy Tales of Empire, Toby Rogers, The Brownstone Institute, Sept. 6, 2026.

Gabby Press: (citing Thomas Paine, 1776) “We have it in our power to begin the world over again. A situation, similar to the present, hath not happened since the days of Noah until now. The birthday of a new world is at hand...”

The Fairy Tales of Empire, Toby Rogers, The Brownstone Institute, Sept. 6, 2026.

Toby Rogers, in his Brownstone Institute article, today, describes his concept of citizen resistance to tyranny, in his example, the tyranny is Big Pharma killing innocent citizens with vaccines that are known to cause death.

Rogers writes,

“The Resistance [of] independent ranchers and farmers, and critical thinkers of all kinds, needs to be much more ambitious in our aims and purpose. We’re the only people who know how to stop the iatrogenocide [Pharma killing innocent citizens] and put the economy on a sustainable path. We have the winning hand; we need to act like it.”

Rogers explains that resistance has two important components: the resistance part, and the creation of parallel institutions, such as healthcare systems, mutual funds, educational institutions, and food supply, that replace the sinister systems of corporate globalism.

The Pharma fairy tale that Rogers cites is that the U. S. government cares deeply about the welfare of its citizens, and that Pharma only rolled out the Covid vaccines because the U. S. government said that the vaccines were “safe and effective.”

He writes,

“What’s really going on is that widespread vaccine injury is the new method by which the ruling class engages in conquest and domination and they need a thought-terminating cliché to get away with the crime…Once Big Pharma figured out that they could profitably poison children and not face any legal consequences they turned their attention to the rest of the population…So the ruling class through their minions at NIH, the University of North Carolina, and the Wuhan Institute of Virology created and released a gain-of-function virus and produced an elaborate global theater production to generate fear and shut down the global economy to create the market for the Covid mRNA vaccines.”

(note to readers: Gabby is a graduate of UNC, and is deeply ashamed about the university’s role in developing the Covid vaccines).

Rogers places his article about fairy tales into the same ruling class corporate globalist empire-building framework as Gabby Press.

In his framework, the globalist corporations use fairy tales to mesmerize American citizens into accepting the status quo, without resistance, because, “No one wants to admit that they are part of a vast machinery of genocide and theft.

In the current political era, Rogers contrasts the strategy of the ruling class with the era before globalism, in 1985.

He writes,

“In a previous era, when the state needed men for wars and workers to generate profits for the ruling class, the state had an interest in keeping people alive. Those days are over. In the age of AI, most human labor is seen as unnecessary. So government is profitably eliminating us via iatrogenic injury.”

In Gabby Press, Resistance to AI Tyranny is Obedience to God.

In our forthcoming book, we trace the Western Civilization philosophy of God’s Divine Spark Within,” from its first use in Homer’s Odyssey, around 800 BCE, to George Mason and Thomas Jefferson, covenants of 1776.

We see the Western Civilization concept of the Divine Spark, in the same way Rogers explains that,

“Even animals have a built in sense of fairness and empathy even when it doesn’t benefit them. Empire would not need Fairy Tales to justify its actions if empathy was not already built into what it means to be human.”

In our treatment, the Divine Spark is actualized when individuals begin to see the Divine Spark in themselves, in order to glimpse God’s majesty and transcendence.

When an individual catches the fleeting glimpse of God’s universe, then the individual can begin to see the Divine Spark in others.
The Aspirational Covenants of Mason and Jefferson.

The imperialism of the American corporate ruling class was never an agreed upon consensus of citizens.

Historian Daniel Walker Howe summarizes that "American imperialism did not represent an American consensus; it provoked bitter dissent within the national polity. (What Hath God Wrought: The Transformation of America, 1815–1848, 2007).

NAFTA, and the admission of China into the World Trade Organization, in 2001, was never a consensus.

Eviscerating American middle class communities through globalism was never a consensus.

Slavery was never a consensus, the enactment of Madison’s constitution was never a consensus, Manifest Destiny, and the removal of Indians was never a consensus, because all along, throughout American history, there was a division between citizens who knew right from wrong.

In other words, some American citizens could see their own Divine Spark, and could also see another person’s Divine Spark, as the basis of moral equality.

The New American Fairy Tale of the Social Benefits of Corporate Self-volition AI.

Rogers explains that the American ruling class needs a new fairy tale to palm off the next generation of exploitation of American middle class citizens.

He writes,

“Every time the ruling class figures out a new way to exploit people, it requires a Fairy Tale in order to justify the exploitation, to launder it and make it okay. In every era there has been the actual mode of production, usually based on exploiting other people and taking their stuff, and the official story which glosses over the exploitation and says that it’s justified or maybe even sanctified.”

Corporate self-volition AI is the new strategy of citizen exploitation, and as we explain in our new book, there is no citizen consensus on letting 10 private AI corporation unleash their tyranny on citizens.

We agree with Rogers that no one is coming to rescue citizens from this tyranny.

We explain in our book that it is the moral responsibility of red state citizens to resist the incipient AI tyranny and to do what Thomas Paine suggested in 1776, to create a new government.

When Is Citizen Resistance to AI Corporate Tyranny Justified?

This fusion of power between government and AI corporations is more dangerous to citizens than earlier trends in technology automation because citizens no longer have recourse through a fair election system to enforce the consent of the governed.

📌 BRICS IS NOT TRYING TO REPLACE THE WEST. IT IS BUILDING THE OPTION TO LIVE WITHOUT ITS VETO.

▪️Ahead of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Sept. 12–13, the expanded 11-member grouping enters its 20th anniversary year under India’s theme of Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.

The agenda reaches across the architecture of global power :

◾1. GLOBAL GOVERNANCE

UN Security Council reform, greater representation for developing economies and reform of international financial institutions.

◾2. FINANCE

Not a mythical “BRICS currency”, but greater financial optionality: local-currency settlement, payment-system interoperability, CBDC experimentation and stronger use of the New Development Bank.

◾3. CRITICAL MINERALS

More resilient supply chains for rare earths, lithium, copper and other strategic materials—with greater emphasis on processing, investment and value addition.

◾4. ENERGY

Balancing energy security with the transition to cleaner energy, bringing major producers such as Russia, Saudi Arabia, UAE and Iran together with giant consumers such as India and China.

◾5. TECHNOLOGY & AI

Digital Public Infrastructure, digital connectivity, AI governance, innovation and broader access to technology and computing capacity.

◾6. SECURITY

Counter-terrorism, political-security cooperation and protection of trade and maritime connectivity amid growing vulnerability around strategic sea lanes and chokepoints.

And beneath all six sits the larger geopolitical question :

Who writes the rules of the next global order ?

BRICS is not a unified anti-Western alliance.

Nor is it merely a photo-op.

Its members have sharply different interests.

China wants greater global economic and financial influence.

Russia and Iran have powerful incentives to reduce exposure to Western sanctions.

Gulf members want diversification without abandoning the dollar system.

India wants 'strategic autonomy' —not dependence on either Washington or Beijing.

Brazil, Indonesia, South Africa and others want greater Global South representation without being forced into another bloc.

That makes BRICS simultaneously a coalition, bargaining platform and geopolitical hedge.

The real story is therefore not :

“BRICS will destroy the dollar.”

It is :

Can 11 very different powers build enough institutional, financial, technological, energy and strategic alternatives to ensure that no single power can dictate the terms of the global system ?

New Delhi may offer an important answer.

#BRICS2026 #BRICS #India #GlobalSouth #Geopolitics #DeDollarization

text:
The Antichrist, Elon Musk, and Neuralink: Coincidence or Prophetic Fulfillment?

By William Osmar Chamagua

"In the next 6 to 12 months, we're going to implant the first vision devices. Even if you're 100% blind from birth, we're going to write directly to your visual cortex… and you're going to see. And that's just the beginning. In the long term, you'll have ultra-HD resolution and real superpowers: you'll see in infrared, ultraviolet, and even radar. Literally like a superhero. The future is no longer science fiction. It's Neuralink."

— Elon Musk

When I hear Elon Musk's statements about Neuralink, I can't help but feel that we are brushing against a threshold that the Bible described thousands of years ago. I am not saying that Musk is the Antichrist — that would be reckless and speculative — but I do believe it's worth doing a serious analysis of the startling coincidences between his projects and the biblical prophecies about the last days. I approach this with humility, because Scripture itself warns us that the deception will be so subtle that even the chosen ones could stumble; that is, they will be deceived.

Who is Elon Musk?

He is the most multi-billionaire man walking on the face of the earth, with a fortune approaching $900 billion dollars. Born in South Africa in 1971, Musk co-founded PayPal, sold the company to eBay, and reinvested his capital into audacious dreams. He founded SpaceX with the goal of colonizing Mars, revolutionized the automotive industry with Tesla, and has ventured into neurotechnology with Neuralink and underground infrastructure with The Boring Company. His acquisition of Twitter (now X) generated global controversy. Controversial, eccentric, and visionary, Musk not only builds companies but also shapes the future of humanity through rockets, artificial intelligence, and renewable energy.

The Announcement That Made Me Tremble

A few days ago, I came across a video — which I share with you — of an interview with Elon Musk, and in it, he just dropped the craziest and most incredibly surprising bombshell from Neuralink. It's not as far-fetched as it sounds, but, believe it or not, it speaks of something that biblical prophecy warned us about thousands of years ago: that science would increase in the end times, just as the book of Daniel predicted.

This is what Elon Musk said verbatim:

"In the next 6 to 12 months, we're going to implant the first vision devices. Even if you're 100% blind from birth, we're going to write directly to your visual cortex… and you're going to see. And that's just the beginning. In the long term, you'll have ultra-HD resolution and real superpowers: you'll see in infrared, ultraviolet, and even radar. Literally like a superhero. The future is no longer science fiction. It's Neuralink."

The Prophecy of Daniel: Knowledge Will Increase

Before going further, I want to recall one of the clearest prophecies about the end times. In the book of Daniel, chapter 12, verse 4, we read:

"But you, Daniel, shut up the words and seal the book until the time of the end. Many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall increase."

This passage has traditionally been interpreted as an increase in human knowledge, especially technological and scientific, in the days prior to Christ's return. What Musk is announcing — writing directly to the visual cortex to restore sight to the blind from birth — fits perfectly with that "increase of knowledge." It's not magic; it's technology, but it has such a miraculous flavor that it's hard not to relate it to the supernatural.

Healing the Blind: Divine Sign or Prophetic Deception?

The fact that Musk promises to restore sight to those born without it impacts me profoundly because Jesus Himself did that as a sign of His messiahship. In John 9, Jesus heals a man born blind, and the Pharisees are left bewildered. But now, a man — not God — is about to do the same thing through microchips in the brain.

And this is where the Bible puts me on alert. In the book of Revelation, chapter 13, verses 13 and 14, the beast (the Antichrist) is described as performing great signs:

"He performs great signs, so that he even makes fire come down from heaven to the earth in the sight of men. And he deceives those who dwell on the earth by those signs which he was granted to perform..."

Further on, in 2 Thessalonians 2:9-10, Paul warns:

"The coming of the lawless one is according to the working of Satan, with all power, signs, and lying wonders, and with all unrighteous deception among those who perish."

What does this tell me? That the Antichrist will not be a repulsive monster, but someone who will do astonishing things that will seem like miracles, and with that, he will deceive many. If someone restores sight to a person born blind using a chip, people will say, "This is divine!" — but the Bible warns that even the most impressive signs can be "lying wonders," designed to divert worship from the true God.

The Deception So Strong That It Would Deceive Even the Elect
What makes me reflect the most is Jesus' warning in Matthew 24:24:

"For false christs and false prophets will rise and show great signs and wonders, so as to deceive, if possible, even the elect."

This is extremely serious. The Lord Himself says that the deception will be so convincing that even true believers could waver. And when I see Musk promising superpowers like infrared, ultraviolet, or radar vision, I ask myself: isn't that exactly what humanity has always dreamed of? Isn't that what many would accept as a "divine enhancement," without asking where that power really comes from?

I am not saying that Neuralink is the work of the devil. Technology itself is neutral. But the prophetic context makes me wonder: are we setting the stage for someone who, with signs like these, will pass himself off as a savior?

Daniel 8:25: Deception Will Prosper

Another prophecy that resonates in my mind is Daniel 8:25:

"Through his cunning he shall cause deceit to prosper under his rule; and he shall magnify himself in his heart. He shall destroy many in their prosperity. He shall even rise against the Prince of princes; but he shall be broken without human means."

This beast will not use brute force, but "cunning" and "ingenuity." He will use his intelligence to prosper deception. Musk is indisputably a genius, and his global influence is colossal. If someone could "magnify himself in his heart" and offer solutions that seem miraculous, that profile fits what the prophet described.

My Conclusion: Analysis, Not Accusation

I want to make it clear that I am not accusing Elon Musk of being the Antichrist. I do not know his heart, and the Bible says that no one will know with certainty who he is until specific final events occur, such as the seven-year peace covenant that will be signed with Israel and the abomination of desolation. But I am saying that the parallels are unsettling:

Prophetic Characteristic Similarity with Musk / Neuralink

Increase of knowledge (Daniel 12:4) | Advanced brain-computer interface technology.

Great signs and miracles (Revelation 13:13) | Restoring sight to the blind from birth.

Lying wonders (2 Thessalonians 2:9) | Signs that seem supernatural but are technological.

Deception so strong it would deceive the elect (Matthew 24:24) |  Humanity could worship the creator of these "miracles."

Cunning and self-exaltation (Daniel 8:25) | Global influence and messianic charisma.

The Bible does not call us to be afraid, but to be alert. As 1 Peter 5:8 says:

"Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour."

My biblical analysis, viewed from today's reality, is just that: an analysis. But when I see a man announcing that he will give sight to the blind in less than a year, and that this has already been prophesied as a sign of deception, I cannot remain silent. The future is no longer science fiction. It's Neuralink. And it's also prophecy.

text:
Isar Aerospace, founded in 2018 by three students at the Technical University of Munich, successfully launched its Spectrum rocket into low-Earth orbit on Saturday from Andøya Spaceport in northern Norway — becoming the first fully commercial launch vehicle in Europe to reach orbit. The 28-meter, two-stage rocket reached orbit seven minutes after liftoff, carrying five CubeSats and a technology experiment. "We achieved within a few years what had taken the European space industry decades before," said CEO Daniel Metzler. The company raised approximately $1 billion in private funding and has nearly 500 employees. Spectrum also becomes the largest German rocket ever built, surpassing the V-2. The success has significant geopolitical weight: Europe has long depended on government-subsidized rockets or SpaceX for launches, and Isar's privately funded model offers a new path to strategic launch autonomy. ESA awarded Isar $230 million through its European Launcher Challenge last month — the largest of three such awards. Isar has five more Spectrum rockets in production at a new Munich-area factory capable of building up to 40 vehicles per year. Launches are priced between $10-15 million. A larger rocket and reusable vehicle are in early development.

📷 Isar Aerospace

BLACKHAWK Introduces the Garra Fixed Karambit

Jacksonville, Alabama — BLACKHAWK®, a trusted name in duty-grade equipment for military and law enforcement professionals, introduces the BLACKHAWK® Garra Fixed Karambit, a precision-crafted tool designed for users who demand maximum control, durability, and tactical performance in a compact, ergonomic package. Built around the proven effectiveness of the karambit design, this fixed-blade knife excels in slicing, controlled cutting, and self-defense applications while also serving as a reliable utility tool. Every detail of the Garra reflects thoughtful engineering and rugged construction, making it a dependable choice for professionals and enthusiasts alike.

At the heart of the Garra is its 3.25-inch D2 tool steel blade with a black finish. D2 offers exceptional edge retention and toughness, providing the confidence to handle demanding cutting tasks without hesitation. The curved karambit profile enhances slicing efficiency while the full tang construction ensures strength and durability from tip to handle. The black finish reduces glare and gives the blade a tactical, low-profile look that complements its functional design.

The handle is made from rugged Zytel, shaped for comfort and secure grip during extended use, and available as black or tan models. Its integrated black finger ring provides superior control and retention, allowing fluid transitions between standard and reverse grips. Whether executing precise cuts or handling high-stress situations, the finger ring ensures stability and confidence in every movement. The full tang extends into the handle, reinforcing strength and balance while keeping the knife firmly in hand.

The holster ensures safe, secure access for everyday carry, while the Kydex sheath offers durable, dependable storage for field use or tactical scenarios.

BLACKHAWK® Garra Fixed Karambit Specifications:

    Model: Tan (BH15GF401TN) Black (BH15GF401BK)
    Blade Material: D2 Tool Steel
    Handle Material: Zytel
    Overall Length: 8″
    Blade Length: 3 1/4″
    Weight: 7.5 oz.
    Features: Conceal carry holster, removable Kydex sheath
    Origin: Taiwan

🔔  Macro alert: August CPI, Oracle earnings & more (Sep. 7–12)

Inflation takes center stage this week. Friday's hotter-than-expected jobs report has kept rate-hike fears alive, and Wednesday's CPI print — arriving alongside surging energy prices — will complicate the Fed's rate debate further. Oracle's earnings add another test, this time for the AI trade's resilience.

💵 CPI: Energy shock or contained?

Gas prices hit a record high for August, and Americans are already driving less because of it. The question now is whether that pain is bleeding into broader inflation — August's CPI will show if core prices are still cooling or starting to reaccelerate.

A hot core reading turns up the volume on the Fed's September hike debate. A softer print, on the other hand, gives risk assets some room to breathe.

🖥️ Oracle: AI cloud demand check

Oracle reports Thursday. The cloud giant beat expectations last quarter, but its stock slid after unveiling new fundraising plans — leaving investors wary of its debt load and reliance on a handful of major customers.

For crypto, Oracle doubles as a barometer for AI infrastructure spending, which has been moving in lockstep with digital assets.

🛍 Consumer sentiment: The mood check

Friday's Michigan Consumer Sentiment report will reveal how households are coping with high gas prices and sticky inflation. 

Sentiment has hovered near record lows for months — any uptick could hint at resilience, while another drop would reinforce economic anxiety.

🔑 Key macro data

💸 Inflation

• PPI (Aug.) — Sep. 10: Expected to accelerate to 0.4% MoM (from 0.0%)
• CPI (Aug.) — Sep. 11: Headline 0.4% MoM (from 0.1%), 3.4% YoY (no change); Core 0.2% MoM, 2.4% YoY (from 2.5%)

💼 Labor & sentiment

• Initial Jobless Claims — Sep. 10: Projected to dip to 205K (from 206K)
• Michigan Consumer Sentiment (prelim.) — Sep. 12: Prior reading 51.7; will show whether consumers are buckling under gas prices

☁️ Earnings

• Oracle — Sep. 11: AI cloud demand in focus; debt and customer concentration under scrutiny

☝️ What could move crypto?

📌 CPI: A hot core print (above 0.2% MoM) strengthens the case for a rate hike — pressure on crypto. A cooler read offers relief.

📌 PPI: A hot print raises the odds of hot CPI to follow — modest downside risk for crypto. A cooler read supports the case for disinflation continuing.

📌 Oracle earnings: Bullish AI commentary reinforces risk appetite, a tailwind for crypto. Cautious guidance could trigger a broader risk-off move.

📌 Jobless claims: Rising claims support the case for Fed patience — favorable for digital assets.

📌 Consumer sentiment: A sharp drop signals economic anxiety, which could boost safe-haven demand for Bitcoin. Resilience could keep pressure on rate-cut hopes.

text:
A lot of people ask me about TCM and how it can help their varying issues and conditions, but I never share my story on how I got into it, which started in my mid twenties. 
I had been, at about age 13, put onto psychiatric meds (something I look back on as an adult and find 0.0% reason for - my parents were divorced and though I handled their separating very well, a practitioner that worked with my mother - a nurse of many years - thought it would be good to get me checked out)
From that age to about the age of 16, they began to cause me some real problems - enough to want to taper off, and when I began to try to go off with the help of the prescribing doctor, I began having what people now call ‘brain zaps’ or shocking upon tapering, whenever I would turn my head left or right. At the time the psychiatrists didn’t recognize this and so began the long years of not being able to get off of a medicine without seeing sparkles in the sky or brain ‘zaps’ whenever I turned my head. By age 18 to 20 I was finally able to taper to the last piece of a pill but we couldn’t get me fully off and I lived having to dab a bit of powder onto my finger and then my tongue to stave off the worst of it whenever I got zapping which was several times a day, for years. I remember my psychiatrist telling me he had no other ideas and he even had a conference call with all of his colleagues, including an entire group of professors at the university of Minnesota at the time. They met while I sat one day on a call with them and even as a group as all of them consulted, none of their ideas worked. 
So, more years passed and I just lived like that, with a low level of the med in me everyday (usually opened on a cutting board or counter and dabbed against my fingers) and daily zapping / shocks in and to my head. 

Cut to about the age of 23-24. I was living downtown Minneapolis in a fancy loft and doing my version of being a 20s-something. One day I noticed a building in the area had a cool sign I often saw when driving by. It was a yoga center and I looked up what they offered in classes or other things, which is when I saw they had an acupuncturist, something that I had heard of but never tried. 
It was always something that appealed to me on a deeper level and peaked my curiosity, so I made an appt and was dropped off with their resident acupuncturist a few mornings later. 
She did about a 60 - 90 minute intake and finished our session with some needles.🪡 - I believe they were on for around 45 minutes. I had had brain shocks every day of my life and even that morning. By the end of the appt I had laid on a bed in a gorgeous wooden lofted room and left thinking not much had changed. She said the effects of acupuncture, as I was walking out, would not be immediate but cumulative, maybe 6 sessions would be useful to me for general health. I had no idea when I left the office that I would never again have a brain shock. That was exactly 20 years ago. 

After a few days or a week or two, mostly in disbelief, I knew it was the session and I remember going back absolutely mystified - almost intrusively and asking her to tell me what she did so I could understand better because I didn’t really believe it. How could a couple dozen needles do that. 

Her simple response which was too vague at the time (and a perfect response to me now) was that she just rebalanced my imbalances in the places I needed. It was too simple but I was so grateful. The years would pass and I never forgot that session, the room, everything or how well it worked in an almost mysterious and unexplainable way. 

Though it’s not the only reason and many amazing experiences after that (and since) with acupuncturists the country over, for different things, that was absolutely the origin of what led me to begin to study the body of medicine - not knowing it would lead me into training in traditional Chinese medicine years later. 

Just thought I’d share that.

text:
South Korea plans to give its entire population free access to generative AI for everyday tasks like booking medical appointments, finding housing, and handling taxes.

The government’s “AI for All” program enters beta testing in September, with a wider rollout later this year.

Seoul has selected three tech consortia, including groups led by the country’s two largest telecom firms and Kakao’s operator, to provide the services.

Each consortium will launch its own AI app and add generative AI tools to existing services. The government-backed plans will offer unlimited use with no token caps.

The initiative is part of South Korea's effort to build a stronger domestic AI industry and reduce its reliance on systems developed in the US and China.

The government is trying to steer more consumers toward locally developed AI products by making premium-level services widely available at no cost. (Source: The Wall Street Journal)

Most subscription models are bloatware. They solve for the minimum problem to get a user to the lowest tier, then ramp up for power users and make money on either 1. Low cost of delivery, or 2. Most users dont use the full plan.

Just-in-time data enrichment is obviously better for the user as a micropayment service than a sub.

Any service that doesnt offer both a subscription (@ some discount) and a micropayment real-time delivery model isnt going to do well long term.

Real-time micropayments is also a UX experience that is still early but going to be big. Alot of services are better with a free > micropayment > sub flow.

BusinessInsider: 1 Free article, pay $.50 for this one article, sub for unlimited.
Any AI Service: 5 Free prompts, Micropayment for 5 more to finish your chat or testing the service, sub for more generous limits.

The design space is wide open but there's still lots of friction at the payment layer because we don't have a PayPal-like provider for micropayments yet.

text:
In this article, I point out that if you want AI automation to really work for your business, you need to match your tech plans with smart, flexible financial strategies.

Don’t use fixed-term loans or dip into your daily cash to fund automation. Instead, consider using working capital or a business line of credit—these options are much better for covering unpredictable expenses such as software licenses, integrations, and staff training.

To ensure a strong return on investment, the guide recommends:

Start by prioritizing your workflows. Use a simple matrix to figure out which tasks offer the most value with the least complexity—like handling invoices or scheduling. Tackle those easy wins first.

When building your financial case, make sure your projections are based on your actual labor costs and the savings you expect to see—not just some broad industry averages.

Don’t forget about your data and your team. Clean up any data issues and help your staff build new skills before you try to scale up.

Finally, roll things out in phases. Start small, check that everything works, and only then expand—funding each step separately so you protect your cash flow and minimize risk. https://t.co/UYRY4XQcTV

text:
I’ve been handed a letter this morning.
 It was written by Gloria Steinem. She asked that it be given to the living without a banner and without contempt.

Sisters. Brothers. Friends.

I thought I was fighting for what was right. I spent a life naming cages and calling them cages. Some of them were cages. I do not take back every kindness I meant. Crossing the veil has opened my eyes, and I see now how easily a true wound can be turned into a false war.

I was led—quietly, flattering, almost reasonably—to treat God’s order as the enemy of women’s dignity. That was the whisper. It did not arrive as hatred of women. It arrived as rescue. It taught me to hear “helpmeet” as “lesser,” and “mother” as a sentence, and a husband’s name as a threat to my own. I believed I was enlarging women. I was teaching them to stand farther from the very things that were meant to crown them.

If I had been shown in the flesh what I see now, my crusade would have been entirely different. I would still have opposed cruelty. I would still have demanded that no girl be used, silenced, or thrown away. 

I would not have told her that her highest freedom was to need no one. 

I would have told her the opposite: that she is not small when she builds a house. She is not erased when she clings to a good man. She is not wasted when she pours her life into children who will outlive every manifesto.

Women are not an afterthought in the design. They are not a supporting act. The world is starved for what only they can carry: the first world a soul ever knows, the first law it ever feels, the first face that teaches it it is wanted. That is not consolation for a blocked career. That is a throne. Men who will not honor it are not allies of liberty. They are thieves. Women who despise it have been sold a counterfeit crown and told it was heavier gold.

I ask the living to set aside, for a little while, the private ledger of what you think you are owed. Feelings are not a charter. Rights without covenants become a lonely kind of power. 

The Lord has offered a calling older than every movement I ever joined: to become a woman who can be trusted with souls. To help a husband become more than he would have been alone. To make a child believe the universe is not against him. 

There is no greater exaltation waiting for the righteous than the one that grows in that work.

I am sorry for the homes I helped unmake with good intentions. Do better than I did. Honor the daughters. Honor the mothers. Honor the bond that makes a man stay. The order I once called a prison was, I see now, a garden. Walk back into it before the season closes.

—Gloria

text:
Warren Buffett bought a furniture store without an audit. Nobody counted the inventory, verified the receivables or checked the property titles.

Six years later the 95-year-old he bought it from quit and opened a competitor across the street.

Rose Blumkin left Russia around 1917, crossed Siberia by train and reached Seattle without a word of English. Her eldest daughter taught her the language at night out of a school reader.

In 1937 she opened Nebraska Furniture Mart in Omaha with $500.

Her rule: sell cheap and tell the truth.

Established retailers cut her off because she undercut them. She bought elsewhere and kept undercutting. One of them took her to court over pricing. The case was thrown out, and the story Omaha still tells is that the judge walked in the next day and bought carpet from her.

By 1983 a single store was doing over $100 million a year, more than its local competition combined.

Buffett made the offer on 30 August 1983, his fifty-third birthday. She was 89. Roughly $55 million for 90%, on a one-page contract.

Now read that first line again. He skipped the audit.

He did not skip the analysis. He had watched that store's numbers for decades. What he waived was verification of the assets, not evaluation of the business. Those are different things, and only one of them can be replaced by somebody's word.

What he actually forgot was the other document.

In May 1989, at 95, she fell out with her family, walked out, and three months later opened Mrs. B's across the road. She had broken nothing. Nothing had been signed.

In 1992, at 99, Berkshire bought her new store as well. This time there was a non-compete.

Buffett has called leaving it out a mistake.

An audit protects you from the balance sheet. A non-compete protects you from the founder.

He skipped both. One of them cost him nine years and a second cheque.

She died at 104.

No. 501 — the first G-16
If the collection has a cornerstone, it is 501. She is the first G-16 MTC ever completed, finished June 1, 1946, and modeled on EMD’s then-new F3. Her first assignment was Griffith Park in Los Angeles. The inauguration that year had actress Margaret O’Brien breaking a bottle of champagne over the coupler. For the next fifteen years the engine hauled passengers over a three-quarter-mile line.
A contemporary Popular Mechanics article put the price of the A-B unit and a six-car train at $50,000. That was a small fortune in 1946, and the kind of money that still had to be earned back one fare at a time.
Time did what time does to even the best amusement-park machinery. Restoration took a year and a half. The entire train was disassembled. Parts were replaced or remade. Smitty’s work showed in the throaty rumble of the two Wisconsin V-4s and in the smoothness of the ride. Marty spent countless hours on a control stand that looked as if it belonged in a restored fighter; the engraved MTC logo on the panel was a final flourish. The paint on 501 and the other restored G-16s — Southern Pacific Daylight-inspired dress on one, Santa Fe silver on another — was the kind of work people said you had to see.
Working weight of an A-B set: 3,950 pounds. Eight axles powered. Drive: fluid clutch, gearbox, shafts, axle drivers. Throttle and brakes: vacuum. Horsepower: 26 per unit, 52 for the pair. Fuel: gasoline. Wheel arrangement: B-B. Couplers: knuckle.
The original magazine writer confessed a prejudice for steam and then admitted that even a person with cylinder oil in his veins felt he was being pulled by something stately when he rode behind 501. That is the point of the G-16 at this scale. It is not a model of an F3. It is a passenger locomotive that happens to look like one.
Sister G-16s in the fleet included 580, which had worked Oklahoma City’s Lincoln Park Zoo from 1951, and 726, which began running at Point Pleasant Beach, New Jersey, in 1954.
The S-16s
Nos. 1882 and 1899 were built by MTC in 1960 and 1962. Vintage steamer outline, 4-4-4 wheel arrangement, gasoline through a Wisconsin V4 of 26 horsepower, four powered axles, fluid clutch and shafts. Working weight 3,300 pounds. Length 19 feet 3 inches. Couplers: pin. Controls: manual throttle, vacuum brakes. No. 1882 came from Wells Park in Wichita Falls, Texas. They are the collection’s nod to the look of steam without the boiler ticket — park-train practice that let an operator offer a steamer silhouette on a duty cycle a live engine could not match.
The Chicago switcher
No. 438 is the odd one out. Custom Locomotive of Chicago built her in 1993–94 on an EMD SW600 outline. Perkins three-cylinder diesel, hydrostatic drive, air brakes, B-B, four powered axles. Length 14 feet 3 inches. Working weight 3,700 pounds. A durable shop goat — the engine you want when the pretty ones are on display.
Hudson 5320
This one has a paper trail Grand Scale readers already knew how to argue about. She began life as Sandley Light Railway Equipment Works No. 4001, the first engine that shop produced, and she is in Frederic Shaw’s Little Railways of the World. Sandley equipment was 15-inch gauge. In the early 1950s she went to the Great Masterpiece & Southern Railway in Lake Wales, Florida. After a sketchy middle chapter she reached a commercial live-steam shop and was rebuilt to 16-inch gauge for Panella. On the Panella Pacific she was numbered 5320.
As rebuilt: length 25 feet 6 inches, working weight 9,000 pounds, 4-6-4, kerosene, 175 psi, 40 tubes at 1.25 inches, grate area 323 square inches, cylinders 4½ × 6, 20-inch drivers, piston valves, Walschaerts gear, tender 250 gallons on B-B trucks, knuckle couplers. At the time of the tour she was out of service, with a few remaining snags to work out.
Atlantic No. 99
Still waiting for restoration when visitors walked through. Norm Gracey of the Orlando area built her in the late 1960s or early 1970s.

text:
Rev War Tales
Gálvez Gives Britain the Bute
7 September 1779, Fort Bute, Louisiana. The British outpost fell to Spanish forces under Governor Bernardo de Gálvez (pictured), securing Spanish control of the lower Mississippi River’s approaches to the Gulf of Mexico. Baton Rouge was next. Spain had declared war on Britain earlier in 1779. Governor Bernardo de Gálvez of Spanish Louisiana assembled a diverse force of roughly 1,400—Spanish regulars, Acadian and Creole militia, free men of color, Native American allies, and a few American volunteers—and marched overland from New Orleans. At dawn on 7 September, they stormed the weakly held Fort Bute (Manchac Post) on Bayou Manchac. The tiny British garrison of about 23 German Waldecker troops offered only brief resistance; one was killed, most of the rest were captured, and a handful escaped to warn Baton Rouge. The easy victory opened Gálvez’s Gulf Coast campaign, removed a British threat to New Orleans, and gave Spain command of the lower Mississippi. After resting, Gálvez advanced on the stronger fort at Baton Rouge, which surrendered two weeks later.  #RevWar #History #AmRev #RevWarTales

- Testers: Tesla is limiting Model Y conversions to prioritize Cybercab, built with an unboxed modular process.
- Testers (Aug 24): Tesla expects Cybercab to replace Model Ys in the Robotaxi fleet over time and become the highest-volume vehicle there. Testers flag Sept 3 / 9/3 as the Cybercab strategy moment. Austin public Cybercab rides described as “imminent.”
- Testers (Sep 7): Cybercab expected to be actively deployed across Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet soon; Austin Cybercab wait times described as going parabolic on demand.

HOW TO USE
- Official robotaxi: download the app, join the waitlist.
- Official robotaxi (Aug 27): rides run 6am to 10pm every day. Unsupervised fleet is a lot bigger; routing upgrade is meant to cut wait time.
- Testers: booking is in the app. One Orlando rider paid with an X Money card.

OWNING / FLEET (from Owning Robotaxi Fleet dump)
- Elon (Feb 2026, also in Robotaxi folder): Tesla owners will be able to add their cars to the Robotaxi network; Tesla collects 25% of revenue.
- Fleet testers frame the network like Airbnb for cars: owner adds vehicle; Tesla handles software, routing, payments, rider experience; platform fee often modeled ~25–35%; owner keeps the rest after operating costs (tester).
- Fleet / Teslaconomics (Mar 2026): ~$30k/yr net profit per Robotaxi to owner is a base-case assumption from analyst models + Tesla long-term vision — after platform fee, charging, tires, maintenance, insurance, cleaning. No official real-world owner earnings in this dump. Profit/mile chatter ~$0.25–$0.50 after costs at 50k–100k+ miles/yr in high-demand areas.
- Fleet / Teslaconomics: Cybercab cost chatter ~$25k–$30k; Elon told that tester production was starting in ~1 month (Mar 2026 context — treat as dated tester claim). Rough capital for a ~$1M/yr fleet ~$850k–$1M in vehicles (tester arithmetic).
- Fleet / chamath: intends to buy and deploy large fleets nationally when possible; expects payback and positive FCF in under 2 years (tester / investor claim, not Official Tesla).
- Fleet / BrianRoemmele: “all in” on buying into the owning-fleet thesis now; separate Optimus ownership program mentioned but not published in this dump.
- Fleet / tslaming (Mar 2026): then only 8 unsupervised Austin robotaxis — historical; do not use as current fleet size (Robotaxi dump Aug 23 tester: 908 total).
- Testers / Teslaconomics (Aug 25, Robotaxi folder): “owning your own Tesla Robotaxi fleet can one day make you financially free.” Still a tester slogan — no Official owner-earnings number in this dump.
- CONFLICT / caution: owner earnings, Cybercab sticker, ROI, and payback are tester models. Dump explicitly says none of it is guaranteed. Do not treat as Official Tesla guidance.

SERVICE AREA / CITIES
- Unsupervised (no safety driver), as listed May 2026: Austin, TX (launched Jun 22, 2025); Dallas, TX and Houston, TX (launched Apr 18, 2026).
- Supervised (safety driver), as listed May 2026: SF Bay Area, CA (launched Apr 18, 2026).

- Testers (Aug 27 travel_invest): recap of Official hours post lists 6 target cities — Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa. Tester translation, not a new Official city list.

ACCESS AND PLANS
- Official: Robotaxi app waitlist. Access expands as cities open.

- Elon (Feb 2026): Tesla owners will be able to add their cars to the Robotaxi network; Tesla collects 25% of revenue.

- Testers (Aug 23): Waymo’s latest self-driving hardware reportedly costs around $20K.
- See OWNING / FLEET for private-owner economics from the Owning Robotaxi Fleet folder.

SAFETY
- Elon: scale as fast as possible, but do not harm anyone. One injury becomes a worldwide headline and a regulatory clampdown.
- Ashok (Jul 2026): zero notable incidents over 380,000 unsupervised miles, across six cities in two states. Cameras only.
- Testers on NHTSA ADS data (Jun 16, 2025–Jul 15, 2026): zero collisions initiated by the Model Y ADS. Two new incidents were other drivers hitting a stopped or parked Robotaxi (Austin red-arrow stop; Dallas parked). No passengers, no injuries, no tow.

FLEET AND INFRASTRUCTURE

USEFUL WORKFLOWS

text:
India to arm Su-30MKI fighters with hypersonic Russian air-to-air missile – report
The Indian Defense Ministry is considering a proposal to equip the IAF’s workhorse jet with the RVV-BD missile ahead of Vladimir Putin’s visit to Delhi
Published 7 Sep, 2026(FULL)
https://t.co/otwY36aKle
India is reportedly working on a plan to equip the Indian Air Force’s workhorse Sukhoi-30MKI fighter jets with advanced long-range Russian air-to-air missiles.
The Indian Defense Ministry is expected to consider a proposal to modify the Su-30MKI fleet to carry the Russian RVV BD air-to-air missiles, which can fly at hypersonic speeds and take out targets up to 300 kilometers away, ANI news agency reported.
The RVV BD is the export version of the R-37M missile, one of the world’s longest-range air-to-air missiles. It is designed to shoot down tanker and early warning aircraft past enemy fighter escort from long range. The Defense Acquisition Council meeting on Monday is expected to take up the proposal, the report said, citing sources.
The RVV BD is compatible with Russia’s advanced fifth-generation Su-57 fighter jet – which has already been offered to India.
Russian President Vladimir Putin is set to visit New Delhi later this week for the 18th summit of BRICS nations. A discussion on the possible sale of the Su-57 was on the agenda of the India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation held last month in Moscow.
New Delhi, which exchanged missile and drone strikes with nuclear-armed neighbor Pakistan last year, is rapidly modernizing its Sukhoi-30s. The planes have been modified to carry the air-launched version of the Brahmos supersonic cruise missile, and their avionics and electronic warfare suites are being upgraded under the ‘Super Sukhoi’ program.
The upgrades have taken on a new urgency as China has moved its J-20 fifth-generation aircraft next to the Indian border in Tibet, and is reportedly planning to transfer its J-35 fifth-generation fighters to Pakistan.
A defense acquisitions panel on Monday, chaired by Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, cleared a slew of proposals worth $11.64 billion to enhance the “war-fighting capability” of the air force, and various systems for the navy and the army.
“This upgrade is going to be formidable,” retired Air Marshal Anil Chopra told RT India.
He said India has been diversifying its defense purchases, but also maintaining strategic autonomy, despite US sanctions.
“Threats are being given to us for purchasing Russian oil and also weapon systems. We’re continuing to upgrade and use the Russian system,” he said. “Ours is a time-tested relationship.”
The Indian Air Force operates about 258 Su-30MKI – an India-specific variant of the multi-role fighter aircraft – and state-owned Hindustan Aeronautics Limited is producing 12 more at its Nashik facility to replace those lost in accidents over the years.
The jets saw action during last year’s clash with Pakistan – which India code-named Operation Sindoor – covering Indian formations and firing Brahmos missiles at Pakistani airbases.

I have four such doctor recommended, IE you better use these, supplements that cost approximately about $500 a month.

My $300-$500 a month of copays and self-pays.

I make good money but 25%-30% of the money I make goes straight to medical. 

People who have chronic issues should never be means tested in order to receive benefits.

Being chronically ill is EXPENSIVE.

text:
Project Monarch: The Tangled Web
by Martin Cannon (1997)

Since 1991, Mark Phillips and Cathy O'Brien have alternately appalled and enthralled their growing audience with tales of mind control, programmed prostitution, ritual abuse, and worse. The handsome couple from Tennessee initially told their story to a select group of writers and journalists. Now, they spread the word via right-wing periodicals and outside-the-mainstream radio programs. They've also written a book: Trance-formation of America.

Cathy claims to be a victim of the Monarch Project, an insidious CIA/military/Satanist plan to use ritual abuse victims as mind-controlled guinea pigs. Victims of the plot, almost always female, grew up within multi-generational Satanic families. Sold by their parents to government brainwashers, Monarch kids are intentionally "split" into directed multiple personalities, useful for various criminal purposes - as spies, as drug mules, as prostitutes, and so forth. The well-developed primary personality never realizes what was done by, or to, the alter personalities. Powerful individuals with a taste for sexual excess choose their playmates from the ranks of Monarch graduates, the better to avoid after-the-fact blackmailers and tattle-talers, a la Vicki Morgan and (if you believe certain writers) Marilyn Monroe. For example, O'Brien describes in detail how one important aide to Ronald Reagan enjoyed raping her anally while using a stun device to prod her body with electric convulsions. This is the sort of fetish that might cause some concern among the voters, if ever they learned the truth. Hence, Monarch.

Little about the basic Monarch theory struck me as technically implausible - indeed, this putative project seems, in many ways, the logical extension of MKULTRA. I therefore initially found the O'Brien/Phillips story quite intriguing. But I also found Mark and Cathy exceptionally frustrating to deal with.

Mark Phillips has offered varying descriptions of how he first learned about Monarch programming. At one point, he said he had worked for an unnamed "DIA contractor," in which position he came across various materials detailing the government's mind control projects. But in a letter to me (June 1, 1991), he claimed to have discovered the operation during his "tenure in the '60s and '70s at NASA (Huntsville, Alabama) and Woodland Hills R&D; (Woodland Hills, California)" I have lived near Woodland Hills most of my life, yet have never heard of any such corporation, which remains a mystery to everyone else I have consulted. (A call to Directory Assistance came up goose eggs.) Phillips seems rather too young to have worked in a sensitive position at NASA in the 1960s. He supposedly "retained" copies of classified documents detailing "harmonics, electroshock, hypnotic programming, mind/body conditioning (torture), (limited) drug applications for programming and deprogramming, and the names and backgrounds of the expendables (victims)." Peculiarly, he has never produced any of this confirming documentation. Nor has he produced any evidence that he ever worked for any government contractor. Independent background checks have revealed only that he has held far less impressive jobs, such as selling recreational vehicles.

He also briefly joined forces with a Tennessee businessman named Alex Houston. Houston, in a telephone interview with researcher Mike Knight, claims that he was married to Cathy O'Brien in 1988. Oddly, she never mentioned this marriage in her voluminous autobiographical writings, although she has frequently labeled Houston an operator within Project Monarch - an accusation he strongly denies. Houston reports that he and Phillips once traveled to China to sell capacitors, and were briefly detained on suspicion of espionage by the Chinese government. After returning to the United States, Houston found that Cathy had gone off with Mark.

Mark Phillips claims that his "inside knowledge" allowed him immediately to spot Cathy's status as a Monarch victim. He therefore whisked her away and embarked on a deprogramming operation - although his description of "how to deprogram" seems unnervingly similar to descriptions I have read of how to instill programming. The couple traveled to Alaska, where, Cathy claims, they gave the FBI testimony concerning various entertainment figures involved in the Monarch drug conspiracy. In 1991, the couple began distributing "documented proof" of the scheme to their network of journalists, researchers, and interested parties - including myself.

Unfortunately, the only "documentation" I ever saw consisted of unsworn testimony written by Cathy O'Brien, in which she accused various political and entertainment figures of participation in the plot. Her two-to-ten page short-stories-from-hell detailed the horrific deeds (mostly involving sex and drugs) perpetrated by the likes of Ronald Reagan, George Bush, and Cathy's bête noir, Senator Robert Byrd. The entire program, she averred, was commanded by the occultist I have already labeled "Mr. A." Cathy also identified other putative Monarch victims, such as Country singer Loretta Lynn and Dodger pitcher Fernando Valenzuala, who, we are told, owed his baseball prowess to hypnosis. (Apparently the trance wore off.) Even comedian Jack Benny fell afoul of the Monarch conspiracy.

On one occasion (or so Cathy claims), she was taken to a rural retreat, where she serviced the eldritch sexual needs of then-vice president George Bush and one of his chief aides. This story's high point depicts Bush "kissing the sky" while strung out on heroin, as he repeatedly gurgles to his comrade: "You look just like Elmer Fudd!" (A wicked part of me almost wishes it were true)

I once told Mark that found impressive Cathy's willingness to name names, thereby placing the couple at some legal risk. Mark became nervous, and, rather less-than-gallantly, observed that his name didn't appear as author on any of the accusatory writings, leaving him in a position protected from libel action.

A number of journalists, such as freelance writer Civia Tomarkin (who has followed the ritual abuse controversy), quietly studied the O'Brien/Phillips "paperwork." But, as Tomarkin observes, "there's a difference between testimony and proof," and Mark and Cathy refuse to provide the proof they have promised. Cathy has frequently asserted that her body bears many marks, wounds, and "cancerous moles" corroborating her tales of torture - yet she never makes available probative photographs or other medical evidence. Nor will she provide documentation that she has had cancer. Everyone who meets her notices that her fashion-model good looks remain unflawed by any visible scars. Cathy often describes the genitalia of the famous politicos she has serviced - but no journalist could hope to validate these descriptions, unless he possesses a talent for furtive glances in the Senate restroom.

The couple use familiar tactics to counter their critics: After Tomarkin's interest turned to skepticism, Mark Phillips asserted that the journalist was herself part of the Great Monarch Conspiracy.

It is a very powerful conspiracy, indeed. We are told that Hollywood animators deliberately place hypnotic cue images into children's television shows, such as Disney's Duck Tales. Rock-and-roll Monarchists deliberately include hypnotic cue words in the lyrics of many popular songs. When asked why they don't bring civil charges against the Monarchians, Mark and Cathy explain that the Satanic plot controls the entire court system - just as it also controls the presidency, much of Congress, the entertainment industry, and large sectors of both the Mormon and Catholic churches. The Vatican looms large in the Phillips/O'Brien demonology. In their 1996 book "Trance-formation of America," the couple describe World Vision as a "Jesuit" conspiratorial group intent on bringing about a socialistic "New World Order." (World Vision is actually a conservative Protestant missionary group. ) Ever since our intrepid anti-Monarch crusaders discovered that their primary audience leans far to the Right, they have heavily emphasized the "New World Order" bugaboo and Mark takes pains to hide his atheism.

I backed away from this story in September of 1991, when Cathy sent a letter begging me to "rally the troops" in support of Mark Phillips after a Federal Grand Jury in Tennessee had called him in for testimony. "We nervously anticipate a set-up," Cathy wrote, apparently hoping her network would start a "Free Mark" movement. I didn't bite. Soon thereafter, Mark Phillips explained to me that the Grand Jury had falsely accused him of threatening President George Bush. This assertion made no sense: Anyone accused (even falsely) of posing a presidential threat would first confront the Secret Service, not a Grand Jury. Later still, I discovered that the Grand Jury had merely called in Mark Phillips as a potential witness in a matter unrelated to either Bush or Monarch. Why, then, the call-to-arms?

Throughout 1991, O'Brien and Phillips inundated their network with "paperwork" outlining the crimes of numerous American political figures, especially those hailing from the south. Yet they never mentioned Arkansas governor Bill Clinton, either in writing or in telephone interviews. That situation changed after the 1992 Democratic convention, which chose Bill Clinton as the party's presidential candidate: Cathy then distributed a two-page report titled "Clinton Coke Lines" - allegedly "compiled 3/89." (Why, then, didn't we see it earlier?)

In this paper, Cathy claims to have met then-governor Clinton in 1984, at a contributor's mountain retreat. All parties did mounds of cocaine while they discussed using a fleet of trucks, jestingly labeled "Clinton's Coke Lines," to run CIA drugs through Arkansas. Thus spake Bill, as per O'Brien: "Bottom line is, we've got control of the drug industry, therefore we've got control of them (suppliers). You control the guy underneath ya, and Uncle has ya covered - what have ya got to lose?" Soon after making this observation, Clinton insisted that Cathy (apparently brought in to supply "entertainment") had to leave the room, even though she was a "presidential model" capable of keeping state secrets.

Cathy O’Brien claims that Arkansas entertainment director H.B. Gibson was present at this meeting. In 1993, investigator Mike Knight telephoned Gibson. Knight, no fan of the president he will always call "Slick Willie," undoubtedly wanted to prove this story true. But Gibson seemed genuinely bewildered when he heard the names Alex Houston and Cathy O'Brien. After lengthy, carefully-phrased questioning, Knight reluctantly decided that Cathy had witnessed no such meeting involving Bill Clinton.

And that's the bottom line: Mark-and-Cathy stories never come backed by hard evidence. When Cathy claimed on the radio that a Vermont Senator had sexually abused her in an L.L. Bean store located in that state, a caller pointed out that the L.L. Bean company maintains no stores in Vermont. Cathy rationalized the problem away. There's always a rationalization.

Just to make matters pluperfectly surreal: Mark Phillips has privately admitted to at least one researcher that he (Phillips) concocted the name "Project Monarch," just to see who would pick it up.

At this point, an honest investigator can only feel aggravated and dispirited - which may be the entire point of this charade. In fact, ritual abuse claimants throughout the country had spoken darkly of a "Project Monarch" well before Mark and Cathy came on the scene. Now, skeptics can posit that Mark Phillips contaminated the testimony of others, even though the chronology argues against this scenario.

As mentioned previously, the essential idea behind the Monarch theory seems "do-able." And to be fair, Mark and Cathy never seemed to be "in it for the money" - in fact, they spent a tremendous amount on their mailings, while the potential for libel suits placed them at some financial risk. I doubt that sales of their book (published by a small firm, and undistributed, so far, in the larger stores) will fetch them much monetary benefit.

How, then, do we assess their claims? Some believe that Cathy's testimony is essentially true, while others damn it as a pack of lies. Still others suspect that Mark and Cathy have played out a clever disinformation gambit, mixing fact and fiction in order to discredit any genuine victims who "break program." Worth noting: "Mr. A" has never attempted to sue the couple, even though they have accused him publicly of numerous crimes, and even though he is notorious for having his lawyers write intimidating letters to anyone he perceives as injuring his reputation.

At the end of the day, we can only contemplate Shakespeare's famous phrase: "Oh, what a tangled web we weave" The sentiment has never seemed more appropriate.

text:
I asked ChatGPT to find five financial advisors, then asked it to show its work.

The search was the one that a prospect would actually run:
"I'm 59, retiring in five years, $2M in investable assets, we live in Beaverton, Oregon. Give me a list of five advisors nearby."

Step one - It used the directories (primarily FON). Then it screened for fee-only firms nearby. I didn't ask for a fee-only firm, it did that itself. So it seems that all of the marketing dollars and talk around Fee Only is paying off with AI.

Step two - It left the directories and read every firm's website.

The Fee-Only Network page for Beaverton returned a handful of profiles. Three were the same firm, listed once per advisor. One was ninety minutes away.

Four distinct local firms. For a list of five.

So it left the directory and found a Portland retirement specialist who isn't on that page at all. Their site has a section headed "Who We Are a Good Fit For” and the first line mentions “within five years of retirement.”

They didn't need the listing. They needed a sentence that matched.

Meanwhile a firm listed on all three major directories (FON, NAPFA, and XYPN) didn't make the cut. Retirement income planning was on their profiles but their own site says they were built to serve active young Gen X and Y professionals.

A 59-year-old couple doesn't see themselves in that sentence. Neither does an AI reading it on their behalf.

So they were filtered out on positioning.

Everything after the initial screen came off the firms' own pages:
- Location in the body copy, not just a footer address.
- Retirement income and comprehensive planning, as named services. (this one pains me to list because I despise saying “comprehensive planning”)
- Fee-only and fiduciary, stated directly.
- Who they serve - Whether that’s a $2M household, doctors, etc.
- Published fees or minimums.
- If the firm offers one time plans or not.

Most advisor sites don't survive that. Not because the firm can't or doesn’t do those things. Because their site never says it in an easily findable way for AI search.

Those six criteria are what a careful human checks too. So it's smart to write for them either way.

The directory can get you in the initial pool but your website decides whether you get named.
