-POI2 was cleared of suspicion following two FBI interviews on January 19, 2021, at his residence in his home city. These interviews took place six days after the FBI pulled their Special Operations Group (SOG) surveillance team off POI3’s home on January 13, just two days after they were deployed to watch the infamous Falls Church, VA condominium address where we now know POI3 shared a firewall between his address and the then residence of former Capitol Police officer Shauni Kerkhoff. The subject of our November 8, 2025 story published by Blaze Media.

How I came to spend five hours with POI2

I met with POI2 twice, on December 11 and 12, 2025. On the 11th, a member of our team accompanied me: a retired FBI veteran of 25 years now working as a private investigator. That first interview lasted for three hours, and then the next day I met with POI2, just him and me, for another two hours.

I arrived in POI2’s home city on the 10th to do some early recon. We had POI2’s name (which I’d acquired from a congressional source), and his address, but we didn’t have a current phone number. After running an extensive background on him, we learned a lot about his life and work, social media, friends and close associates, and even where he attends church, but we still didn't have a phone number to call him and ask for a meeting.

Most interesting of all, POI2 is a prolific international traveler. In one recent year, he had logged over 40 international flights. So we didn’t even know if he’d be in the country, much less at home, if we knocked on this door.

My recon of his address was a huge disappointment. His apartment building is one of those old inner-city manufacturing plants refitted into modern, upscale housing. The entire property is ringed by tall wrought-iron fencing, with electronic security for entry into the parking garage, foot traffic, and into the building itself. There was no visible way for us to just pay him a visit for a “knock and talk.” Perhaps we could have “buzzed” him from an exterior gate, but I didn’t get that far that day.

Later that evening, I picked up my team member from the airport — the retired FBI guy — and we went to dinner for a long, late-night planning session. We identified a couple of strong local personal connections he had via his Facebook page, and we planned to visit them first, get more info about POI2, and maybe even get their help reaching out to him.

At 9:00 a.m. the next morning, we arrived at the home of someone who seemed like they might be closest to him. We were lucky and hit a home run on the first swing. Without the long details, our “story” about why we were looking for POI2 — their close friend — worked like a charm, and we were invited into their home. Our host called POI2, and within two hours POI2 joined us at our new friend’s home. Luckily, POI2 had returned to the States from an overseas trip only the day before.

For the next three hours, I asked most of the questions while my partner listened and observed. Based on my partner’s 25+ years of experience with the FBI, he believed POI2 answered everything truthfully … “Or, he’s a very, very good liar.”

My partner had to fly back home the next morning, but I had many follow-up questions for POI2. I reached out again early in the morning, and he agreed to meet me at a coffee shop in his neighborhood.

***(On a personal timeline aside: during my second interview with POI2, I was only nine days away from my heart failure episode, and was already struggling to breath after the slightest of physical exertions.)***

The most significant reveal

We met at 1:30 p.m., and spent another two full hours together. During this session, we had a detailed conversation about his two interviews with two FBI special agents. Both of those interviews were on the same day. January 19, 2021.

POI2 had explained to the FBI agents that the reason he returned to the Rumsey Court alley behind the RNC was that he remembered there were several trash cans in the alley, and he wanted to dispose of an empty plastic water bottle before going back to the train station.

I asked him why he didn’t simply throw the bottle away at the Metrotrain station. He shrugged. From our video review, POI2 only stayed in the alley for about three to four minutes. But if what he revealed to me is true, it is one of the most significant discoveries in our years-long pipe bomb investigation.

POI2 shared with me that the FBI agents told him that he had thrown the empty water bottle away in the very trash container next to where the bomb would be placed a little over an hour and a half later.

Why that is significant

FIRST, it reveals that the FBI most likely had video of him depositing that empty bottle into that container. Yes … they could have taken DNA samples of every item in that trash can, but then they would also have needed DNA from POI2 in their database. POI2 didn’t offer that option as their explanation. He assumed they saw him on camera.

I can personally attest that there is currently a camera in Rumsey Court that would cover the area where the bomb was placed, but I do not know if that same camera existed in January of 2021. But if they did observe POI2, on camera, tossing the bottle in the trash can immediately next to where the bomb was placed, then the FBI most certainly has video of Karlin Younger — the FirstNet employee — who discovered that device at approximately 12:35 p.m. the next day, January 6. Only 25 minutes before Vice President Mike Pence was to drop the gavel on the joint session of Congress to certify the 2020 Electoral College presidential vote. Only about 18 minutes before the first breach of that outer bike rack barricade on the west Capitol grounds, led by Ray Epps, Ryan Samsel, and other suspicious characters.

Many investigators, including Congressman Loudermilk and his committee, have posited that the two devices placed by the gray hooded bomber on J5 were retrieved at some point in the early morning hours of J6, then replaced just before their “discovery” a few minutes either side of 1:00 p.m.

The allegedly “deleted” video from the two DNC cameras that provided the footage of the gray hooded bomber placing a device on the evening of J5 would have also shown us what happened after midnight. Whether or not the two plainclothes Capitol Police counter-surveillance officers were the ones who replaced the device just before reporting its discovery to the Secret Service agents attending VP-Elect Kamala Harris’s presence inside the building at the time. (Article to that story linked in comments below.)

A camera aimed at the RNC drop location would give us the same information about what happened during the night, and when Karlin Younger discovered that device while walking back and forth and doing her laundry. The FBI claims that the footage from the two DNC cameras — after that device was planted under a bench — was accidentally deleted. (No one buys that story.) 

Those two FBI agents may also have inadvertently revealed to POI2 that video footage exists from that dark corner of the RNC/Capitol Hill Club alley on J5 and J6.

Both missing videos, if they were to surface, would either invalidate all conspiracy theories about the pipe bombs, or confirm the prevailing theories and circumstantial evidence pointing to law enforcement participation and a multi-agency conspiracy.

SECOND, if the two FBI agents were telling POI2 the truth about that specific trash container, then it brings into question all of POI2’s own statements about why he returned to that alley after dark.

That very trash can was in the furthest and darkest corner of the RNC/Capitol Hill Club side of Rumsey Court. He would have had to ignore several of the first and most clearly visible, well-lit trash bins upon his arrival into that alley by way of the walkway between the RNC and the Capitol Hill Club. Instead, he made a hard left behind the Capitol Hill Club and headed toward the darkest corner of the alley, from which the view of that trash can was also likely obstructed by one or more cars typically parked between him and what would be his line of sight to that dark corner.

This implies POI2 was either on a recon mission to determine the best drop location for the second device, or, as one retired, formerly high-ranking law enforcement officer has theorized, he may have placed an AirTag or other electronic beacon to lead the bomber to the most advantageous location to deposit the bomb.

Near the end of my second meeting with POI2, he shared with me several photos of “numbers” he took in that alley. He shared the “time and location” data from those original photos on his iPhone. He also gave me screenshots from his phone’s call history of the exact moment the two FBI agents phoned him for both interviews on January 19, 2021. He was very earnest, forthcoming, and eager to answer all my questions. (Photo examples in comments below.)

As a person, I like POI2. We could be friends. But either he or the FBI is lying about what happened in that dark corner behind the Capitol Hill Club. (Maybe both?)

Just as POI2 and I were about to say goodbye and shake hands, I opened my phone to show him one photo. It was the shot I took of the two side-by-side doors at the condo complex in Falls Church, VA. The door on the left was the home of his lifelong acquaintance, POI3. The door on the right was Shauni Kerkhoff's January 6 residence.

I asked him:

“Can you make this math work for me?”

He replied:

“No, man. That’s so weird.”

We have stayed in contact and spoken many times since those two days in December. ⬇️

MAX is not merely a messaging app. It is a state-designated “national multifunctional messenger” built by VK as a WeChat-style super-app whose core purpose is to sit between citizens and Russian government systems.

Legal and institutional setup  
A June 2025 federal law established MAX as the national platform. From 1 September 2025 it must be pre-installed on every new smartphone and tablet sold in Russia. Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin later ordered that delivery of Gosuslugi services and citizen requests should flow through the messenger even while the existing Gosuslugi portal itself remains. Officials and some state institutions have been pushed to migrate official communications onto it.

Gosuslugi and ESIA integration  
The tightest link is with Russia’s Unified Identification and Authentication System (ESIA) and the Gosuslugi portal:
Login codes and two-factor authentication can be received inside MAX instead of SMS.
Official notifications (fines, appointment reminders, application status, social payments) arrive in a dedicated Gosuslugi bot; some fines can be paid there.
Full account linking requires the same mobile number on both platforms.
FSB initially blocked deeper connection until certified cryptographic protection was added; approval was later granted.

Digital ID and document replacement  
Adult users with a confirmed Gosuslugi account and biometric data (or passport scan plus selfie) can generate a Digital ID. It displays a dynamic QR code that refreshes every 30 seconds and is device-bound. Uses that have been rolled out or mandated include:
Age verification for restricted goods.
Confirmation of benefit status (students, pensioners, large families).
Hotel check-in (mandatory for hotels with more than 50 rooms from 1 September 2026 for guests without a paper internal passport).
Public-transport benefit confirmation.
Presentation of driving licence and vehicle registration certificate to traffic police.

Electronic signature and other services  
MAX integrates GosKlyuch (Goskey) so users can sign documents electronically without leaving the app. Additional government-facing functions include doctor appointments and medical documentation, school/parent communications via Sferum, and official verified accounts for state bodies. Mobile operators zero-rate MAX traffic, so using the app does not consume a user’s data allowance.

Data access and control  
Unlike Telegram or WhatsApp, MAX does not offer end-to-end encryption. Its privacy policy states that user data (including credentials, device information, location, address book and activity) may be transferred to government or local authorities on request. Independent analyses have reported additional collection of installed apps, VPN usage and network environment data, plus the technical ability for server-side commands that weaken encryption checks. These design choices make the platform far more transparent to Russian security services than foreign messengers.

Practical picture  
The government treats MAX as both a convenience layer and a control layer: it funnels identity verification, official notifications and an expanding list of everyday administrative acts onto a single, domestically hosted, legally privileged app. Gosuslugi itself has not been replaced; MAX functions as the preferred front-end and delivery channel. Adoption figures are high on paper (well over 100 million registered accounts), but many Russians continue to treat it as a compulsory rather than preferred tool precisely because of the depth of this government integration.

A nation is not a mood. It is a people, a land, a law, and a claim that this ground is ours and not yours. If Beijing announced that the United States now belonged to the CCP, Washington would treat that as war, not as theology. Culture and the rule-set are the same cloth. That is secular by definition. It is political by definition. Sovereignty is the name of the refusal.

A true religion does not file that claim.
Jesus said it in the only sentence that matters here: My kingdom is not of this world. If it were, my servants would fight. He paid the tax. He refused the crown the crowd offered. He told Pilate the authority of the moment was borrowed. He built no treasury, no border militia, no poll-tax on the unbeliever, no court that could seize a neighbor’s house for the creed. James’s test of pure religion is still orphans, widows, and an unstained life — not a parliament. When churches later grabbed thrones, they were not completing the Gospel. They were contradicting the Founder. The religion, if it stays the religion, stands apart from the state the way a conscience stands apart from a police force.

Western law still half-remembers that. It treats “religion” as worship, conscience, and voluntary association — not as a rival sovereign that may levy war and tribute inside the republic. That is why a church can be free and still not be China.

Islam, in its classical form, does file the claim.
The ummah is not a prayer circle. It is a public order. After Medina there is a commander, spoils law, a fifth for the Messenger, fighting until the People of the Book pay jizya and feel themselves subdued, a legal status for the captive, hudud, and a jurisprudence that assumes the believer’s law is the land’s law wherever Muslims can impose it. Dar al-Islam and dar al-harb are not metaphors for the heart. They are maps. Sharia is not “how I pray.” It is family law, criminal law, fiscal law, and the terms of peace with the outsider. That is what a state is. Attach the word God to it, and you have not made it a church. You have given a political machine a consecration.

A gang and a state look different in size. They look the same in logic: in-group, out-group, authorized take, humiliation as policy, the boss’s cut, the sacred seal. Islam’s Medina file is that logic written as revelation. Christianity’s founding file is the refusal of that logic.

So the litmus test is not “do they mention God?” It is this: Does the teaching require a territory and a sword to be itself, or does it remain itself when it owns nothing?
Jesus’s teaching remains itself in a catacomb. The Medina program is incomplete without a treasury and a subdued taxpayer. One is a kingdom not of this world. The other is a nation-state project that will not rest until the map matches the book. Western democracies already know what to do when another nation writes its name across their soil. They should not lose that clarity because the invading claim arrives with a minaret.

text:
60 years of Star Trek. Tomorrow we mark the day it all began.

On September 8, 1966, Captain Kirk, Mr. Spock, and the crew of the Starship Enterprise first appeared on American television. In the middle of a turbulent decade, Gene Roddenberry, a World War II Army Air Corps veteran, offered something rare: an optimistic vision of humanity’s future. We would explore. We would work together. We would boldly go.

This week, “America Right Now” host Tom Basile beamed aboard the meticulously recreated Original Series Enterprise set in Ticonderoga, New York. Not CGI. Not AI. The real corridors, the bridge, the transporter room, rebuilt from original blueprints by dedicated fans so that people can still walk those decks 60 years later.

The show didn’t just entertain. It inspired.

Kirk’s flip-open communicator helped spark the idea for the modern cell phone. Motorola engineer Martin Cooper has said as much.

Tricorders pointed toward handheld medical scanners.

Automatic doors, touch screens, and tablet computers all have echoes in what we use every day.
And then there is the shuttle.

NASA planned to name its first space shuttle Constitution. Trekkies launched a massive letter-writing campaign, hundreds of thousands of letters. President Gerald Ford directed NASA to change the name. 

In 1976, when the shuttle Enterprise rolled out, Roddenberry and most of the original cast were there.

That’s the power of a story that believed in America, in science, and in a future worth reaching for.

The mission continues.
Watch Tom Basile’s report: https://t.co/e7LogOd22N
Live long and prosper. 🖖

text:
September 7, 1812. The bloodiest single day of the Napoleonic Wars. It settled nothing, and it decided everything.

Roughly 250,000 men met on a field near a village called Borodino, about seventy miles west of Moscow.

Napoleon had about 128,000 engaged, plus 18,500 Imperial Guard he kept in his pocket all day. Kutuzov had 155,200 regulars and 637 guns behind earthworks.

The Russians had spent the previous days building two things that would matter more than any manoeuvre. The Bagration flèches, three arrow shaped earthworks on the left, and the Raevsky redoubt in the centre.

The French assaulted the flèches seven times. Seven. Each attack went in, took the works, was thrown out by counterattack, and went in again. That is not manoeuvre warfare. That is men walking into massed artillery at close range, over and over, for hours, because there was nowhere else to go.

Bagration, commanding that flank, was hit by a shell fragment. He refused amputation and died of the wound seventeen days later.

The Raevsky redoubt changed hands more than once and did not fall for good until about half past three in the afternoon.

Around midday the Russians did something Napoleon did not expect. Uvarov's cavalry and Platov's Don Cossacks swung wide around the French left. It was not a large raid and it broke nothing, but it made Napoleon cautious for about two hours, at exactly the moment he might have concentrated everything on the centre.

And then the decision people have argued about for two centuries.

His marshals came to him and said commit the Guard. Break them now, today. The Guard was 18,500 of the finest infantry in Europe, entirely fresh, standing in reserve watching other men die.

He refused. The line usually quoted is that he would not have it blown up. He was fifteen hundred miles from France with no way to replace those men, and the Guard was the one thing standing between him and having nothing at all.

There is a serious historical argument, made by Oleg Sokolov among others, that committing them would have torn the Russian army apart and ended the campaign that winter on French terms.

Instead the day ended with the French holding the ground and the Russian army still in existence.

The casualty figures have been politically massaged on both sides ever since. The honest ranges are roughly 28,000 to 42,000 French, including 49 generals killed or wounded, and roughly 40,000 to 53,000 Russian, including 29 generals.

Forty to fifty thousand men in a single day, on a battlefield you could walk across in a couple of hours.

Kutuzov withdrew the next morning, surrendered Moscow without another fight, and let the city burn. Napoleon sat in a burnt out capital for five weeks waiting for a peace offer that was never going to come, then walked back out into winter.

Of the more than 600,000 men who crossed into Russia, about 112,000 came back.

Napoleon wrote the best line anyone has produced about it. The French showed themselves worthy of victory, and the Russians of being invincible.

Battle of Borodino, 7 September 1812. The French call it the Battle of the Moskva.

DID YOU KNOW??

Otto von Bismarck weaponized the vacant throne of Spain as geopolitical bait, editing a single diplomatic telegram to trick France into declaring war, creating the unified German Empire!

​In 1868, Spain’s Queen Isabella II was deposed, leaving the Spanish throne empty. Seeking a Protestant, Prussian-aligned monarch, Spain's military leadership secretly offered the Spanish crown to Prince Leopold of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen, a relative of King Wilhelm I of Prussia.

Bismarck secretly spent months coercing the reluctant prince to accept the offer, knowing it would terrify France with the prospect of a two-front encirclement by Prussian allies.
  
​When news leaked, France threatened war unless Leopold withdrew his candidacy. Leopold withdrew, but the French Emperor Napoleon III pushed further, sending Ambassador Vincent Benedetti to demand that King Wilhelm I guarantee Prussia would never allow a Hohenzollern on the Spanish throne again.

The King politely declined and sent a detailed telegram outlining the polite interaction to Bismarck from the spa town of Bad Ems. ​Bismarck carefully edited the message, removing the polite phrasing, to make it appear that the King had rudely dismissed the French ambassador. He leaked this modified version, known as the Ems Dispatch, on Bastille Day (July 14, 1870). Outraged by the perceived insult, France declared war on Prussia five days later, exactly as Bismarck planned.

The war rallied the independent southern German states to Prussia's side, leading directly to the defeat of France and the birth of a unified Germany in 1871. Walk with me 👇🏾👇🏾 

​The Diplomatic & Media Engineering of the Ems Dispatch:

1. The Spanish Candidate Lever:
Bismarck used the empty Spanish throne to force a diplomatic crisis, forcing France to choose between accepting a Prussian relative on their southern border or resorting to aggressive military posturing.

2. The Ems Edit:
When King Wilhelm sent the telegram detailing his refusal to sign a perpetual ban, Bismarck did not invent facts; he systematically deleted the conciliatory greeting and polite closing phrases, leaving a terse, confrontational summary.

3. Simultaneous National Outrage:
Bismarck published the shortened text to international wire services simultaneously. The French public interpreted it as a slap in the face to their ambassador, while the German public interpreted France's demands as an insult to their King.

4. Uniting the German Confederation:
By ensuring France fired the first shot as the legal aggressor, Bismarck triggered mutual-defense treaties with the anti-Prussian southern German states (Bavaria, Baden, and Württemberg), binding them into a single army.

More Surprising Facts About Bismarck and Spain:

A. ​Spain's De Facto Leader Was in on the Plot: General Juan Prim, the de facto leader of Spain, worked directly with Bismarck in secret correspondence to secure Prince Leopold's acceptance, keeping the Spanish cabinet completely in the dark until the offer was finalized.  

B. ​The "Iron Chancellor" Was Bedridden with Stress: When Prince Leopold initially refused the Spanish crown due to French pressure, Bismarck suffered a physical breakdown, suffering from severe migraines and stomach cramps, believing his grand plan for German unification was ruined before he engineered the Ems Dispatch.  

C. ​Spain Settled on an Italian King Instead: After the scandal sparked the Franco-Prussian War, Spain abandoned the Hohenzollern candidate entirely and appointed Amadeo of Savoy (an Italian prince) as King Amadeo I of Spain in late 1870. 

​SUMMARILY!
​By covertly offering a German prince the Spanish crown and editing a single telegram to insult French honor, Otto von Bismarck turned a Spanish succession dispute into the catalyst that unified Germany.

text:
🧵(4/6) 

The Position of the Traditional Religion

The main traditional gods referred to during this period are the ancestral deity Pakhangbä, the household lãi Sana. mahi, &, less frequently, the mäikei-ngakpa, the 'guardians of the directions'. Pakhangba is the deity alluded to most often. There are several references to appearances of the lai (1848 A. D. at Santhong, 1871 A. D. at Lakhong and so on), which must presumably be taken as the appearance of snakes which were taken to represent the god. The allusion to the appearance of the palanquin of Pakhangba is more difficult to explain." His worship continued unmolested, & new representations of the lāi continued to be made and installed. There is also an interesting reference to the bringing back of Pakhangba & of Sanāmahi from 'mayang' to be installed in their proper places (CK 1848 A. D. p. 288).

No doubt this points to the removal of representations of these lai during the Burmese devastations and their return when the political situation became more settled.

There are two main indications of the Hinduization of Pakhangba worship during this period, the replacement of traditional methods of worship by Hindu forms, and the worship of the lāi in conjunction with Hindu gods. The clearest indication of the former is in the use of vegetarian foods & flower offerings. There are two examples of the first, both mentioning offerings of rice (CK for 1853 A. D. p. 301 and for 1875 A. D. p. 429). The other case is more striking here the traditional practice of drinking wine has been replaced by the drinking of flower water :

"On 6th day, Wednesday, of Wäkching (December-January), pledges were taken before Grandfather Pakhangbā...by drinking the flower water of Pakhangba.' (CK for 1870 A. D. p. 393)

Leiman (flower water now means the water used for the symbolic ritual washing of the images of Hindu gods in which the flowers which are offered are dipped. In the present context however it may imply no more than the water in which the flowers offered to Pakhangba were dipped.).

Hindu forms of worship were clearly replacing those aspects of the traditional cultus which were thought to be repugnant to Hindu piety

Those occasions which refer to the traditional lai in conjunction with the Hindu gods are significant in showing the degree of integration of traditional elements into Manipuri Hinduism. The most remarkable allusions to the lai Pakhangba and Sanämahi all take the same form.

The significant point is the very close conjunction between the lāi and Govinda. Both sets of deities are now worshipped side by side, without their respective origins being stressed. A conflict between Hindu gods and Meitei lai was now no longer felt; two originally quite distinct sets of gods. have been merged into a generally accepted Manipuri Hindu Pantheon. The religion of Manipur in this period managed to draw effectively from both traditions, and to fuse them into a workable synthesis. The newer faith had not eradicated the ancient gods, nor (except in a very limited sense) had it identified Meitei lai with Hindu gods. It had preserved those lai which were seen to be of basic importance in the culture of the people, & had placed side by side with them Govinda, Radha Chaitanya and a host of other Hindu deities. In this way the religious traditions of Manipur had been preserved while at the same time adopting the tenets of Chaitanyaite Vaishnavism

text:
Pierre Poilievre has the right framework for dealing with Trump’s tariff war.

Canada should defend itself. We should use targeted retaliation where it creates real political pressure inside the United States. Flavio Volpe is right about that. Canadian counter-tariffs can be aimed at American companies, exporters and communities that have the ear of Washington.

But Pierre is also right to remind Canadians that tariffs are not free. Canadian consumers and businesses eventually pay part of the bill too. Retaliation should be a tool, not the economic plan.

The goal must be clear: get back to broad, predictable, tariff-free North American trade.

Pierre is also right to demand transparency. If Ottawa has already discussed a tentative deal with Washington, Canadians deserve to know what was offered. If the government has calculated what its counter-tariffs will cost Canadian families and businesses, release those numbers too.

And then do the part Canada actually controls.

Make Canada more competitive.

Get major resource projects built. Fix the Impact Assessment Act. Open more export routes for Canadian energy. Reconsider policies that make Canadian steel, fertilizer, manufacturing and resource development more expensive. Stop making investors wait years while projects crawl through Ottawa.

The auto industry proves how interconnected our economies really are. A Canadian-built Ford, GM or Stellantis vehicle contains enormous amounts of American parts, steel, resins and other inputs. Tariffs on Canadian vehicles also punish American suppliers and raise costs for American automakers.

Trump has badly underestimated that integration.

But Canada would be just as foolish to underestimate our dependence on the American market.

That is why Pierre’s approach makes sense.

Negotiate hard. Retaliate strategically. Demand transparency. Protect Canadian workers. Build pipelines, mines, factories and infrastructure. Diversify our markets. Make Canada a place where people actually want to invest again.

We cannot control Donald Trump.

We can control whether Canada remains economically vulnerable to him.

That is the job.

text:
🇪🇺💶📉Everyone Talks About U.S. Debt But Europe May Be in Worse Trouble

America’s debt problem is impossible to miss. Federal debt has crossed $40.08T, another $1.9T deficit is expected this fiscal year and the 30-year Treasury yield is around 5.25%, its highest since 2007.

Yet the next Western debt crisis may begin across the Atlantic.

Washington has advantages that buy it time. The United States issues the world’s principal reserve currency, collects taxes through one federal government and sells debt through one enormous Treasury market. It can attract foreign capital and push part of the cost abroad. That does not make $40T harmless, but it can delay the reckoning.

The eurozone has no comparable safety valve. It has one currency and one central bank, but 20 governments issuing their own debt, running separate budgets and answering to different voters. The ECB must set one monetary policy for economies with very different debts and growth rates.

France shows why this is dangerous. Its 10-year bond yield has risen to about 4.15%, its highest since 2008 and now slightly above Italy’s. The European Commission expects a 5.1% French deficit this year and public debt near 120% of GDP by 2027.

The problem can no longer be blamed on Greece or another small southern economy. France is the eurozone’s second-largest economy and one of the states meant to support rescue mechanisms for everyone else. If its debt starts trading like the old European “periphery,” the line between rescuers and rescued begins to disappear.

Germany offers little comfort. Its 10-year yield is near 3.3%, a 15-year high, while its industry remains weak. Europe’s two central powers are paying more to borrow just as Brussels prepares another spending surge.

The EU plans to mobilize up to €800B for rearmament. Member states must also finance ageing populations, expensive energy, social programs and support for Ukraine. Budget cuts provoke resistance. More borrowing raises yields. ECB intervention places more national debt risk onto the shared monetary system.

The United States can abuse the dollar’s global role for longer. Europe may hit the wall first because it carries heavy debts without a genuine federal state standing behind them. One central bank cannot reconcile every national budget forever.

So yes, America’s debt matters. But the louder surprise may come from a European Union that spent years presenting itself as the responsible alternative. Washington has a dangerous debt problem. Europe has the same problem inside a system poorly designed to survive it.

No sympathy is required. Both created this predicament through wars, sanctions, subsidies and promises they can no longer finance cheaply. Now we get to see which model breaks first.

[Take 14/15 · 𝕏-4]
### 𝕏-4. Witkoff and Kushner hold talks in Kyiv after Moscow visit with Putin
*(as of 2026-09-07)*

**1. The Frame**

**What people think this is about:** Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are shuttling between Moscow and Kyiv in a fresh diplomatic push to end the Russia-Ukraine war, with both capitals describing the weekend talks as substantive and raising hopes for renewed trilateral negotiations.[[1]](https://t.co/sATmmWXbqz)

**What the machinery is actually doing:** The U.S. is keeping channels open and testing whether incremental ideas can narrow gaps before winter escalation, while Russia signals openness to talks without conceding core demands and Ukraine uses the visits to lock in air-defense and energy commitments alongside any diplomatic movement.[[2]](https://t.co/MPNIwa0nky)

**2. Observations**

- The temporary three-day pause on strikes against each other’s capitals was a narrow, tactical concession that both sides honored only for the envoys’ safety window; broader fighting and long-range attacks continued or resumed quickly.[[3]](https://t.co/fmh80MLhL9)
- Core territorial disputes (especially Donbas control) and Russia’s “root causes” demands (Ukrainian neutrality, limits on its military) remain unchanged and mutually exclusive; the envoys carried revised proposals but extracted no public movement.[[4]](https://t.co/zvyP1yJZPe)
- Ukraine secured discussion of a “winter package” for air defense and energy infrastructure, plus European involvement in follow-on talks—practical deliverables that matter more immediately than abstract peace frameworks.[[2]](https://t.co/MPNIwa0nky)
- Witkoff and Kushner’s optimism (“new ideas,” “good resolution,” “win-win”) is classic envoy language that keeps the process alive without committing either capital to concessions; it aligns incentives for continued U.S. engagement and Ukrainian access to Washington.[[5]](https://t.co/xagVl9OVYi)
- Russia’s willingness to host the envoys multiple times while insisting on maximalist positions suggests Putin sees value in the channel for information, legitimacy, or delaying pressure, not imminent compromise.[[6]](https://t.co/2L1gCL8GrJ)
- The first official Kyiv visit by these envoys (after repeated Moscow trips) underscores asymmetric U.S. access and the administration’s priority on testing Russian flexibility before doubling down on Ukrainian support.[[7]](https://t.co/VINqawne8I)

**3. Snapshot**  
Over the weekend of September 5–7, 2026, Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday for roughly three hours plus dinner, then flew to Kyiv on Sunday for multiple rounds with Volodymyr Zelenskyy (including E3 national security advisers). Both sides called the discussions substantive and constructive, with “new ideas” exchanged and a push to resume trilateral talks; no breakthrough or deal was announced, but the process continues ahead of potential UNGA follow-up.[[8]](https://t.co/VQRN8MGWaz)

**4. Timeline of material facts**  
- **September 4, 2026 (pre-trip):** U.S. officials confirm the envoys’ Moscow-Kyiv itinerary; temporary mutual pause on capital strikes negotiated.[[7]](https://t.co/VINqawne8I)  
- **September 5/6, 2026 (Moscow):** Witkoff and Kushner hold three-hour Kremlin meeting with Putin followed by dinner; Kremlin calls it “constructive, frank and useful”; White House cites “substantive plans for next steps.” Russia agrees to three-day pause on Kyiv strikes.[[9]](https://t.co/kk0SBfgSX3)  
- **September 6/7, 2026 (Kyiv):** Envoys arrive (first official visit); three rounds of talks with Zelenskyy and advisers; discussion of air defense, winter energy support, territory, and trilateral format. Zelenskyy calls talks “very substantive.”[[2]](https://t.co/MPNIwa0nky)  
- **September 6/7, 2026 (post-Kyiv press):** Witkoff expresses confidence in a “good resolution”; Kushner emphasizes “win-win” and durable peace; both sides signal hope for resumed trilateral talks “in short order.” No specific concessions announced.[[5]](https://t.co/xagVl9OVYi)

**5. Sides**  
**U.S. envoys / Trump administration (IT/LT mix):** Steelman — pragmatic shuttle diplomacy to test whether revised proposals can restart talks and avoid deeper U.S. entanglement or escalation; prioritizes diplomatic off-ramp while maintaining leverage.  
**Critique:** LT — talks occurred and produced no public deal; IT — language of progress sustains domestic and allied support without forcing immediate choices on aid or sanctions.  

**Russia (Putin/Kremlin) (IT dominant):** Steelman — willing to engage U.S. mediators and offer limited tactical pauses while holding firm on security red lines (“root causes”).  
**Critique:** LT — no compromise on territory or neutrality signaled; IT — channel useful for intelligence, optics, and testing U.S. resolve without cost.[[6]](https://t.co/2L1gCL8GrJ)  

**Ukraine (Zelenskyy team) (IT/LT mix):** Steelman — open to substantive dialogue and trilateral format while securing concrete security and energy commitments from the U.S. and Europe.  
**Critique:** LT — territorial red lines unchanged; IT — uses visits to extract aid pledges and European buy-in ahead of winter.  

**6. Rumsfeld Matrix**  
- **Known Knowns:** Talks happened on the stated dates; both sides used positive language; temporary capital-strike pause implemented; no deal announced; core issues (territory, neutrality) remain.  
- **Known Unknowns:** Exact content of “new ideas” or revised proposals; whether Russia signaled any flexibility privately; timeline or format for any trilateral follow-up.  
- **Unknown Knowns:** Internal U.S. assessments of Russian bottom lines; Ukrainian intelligence on Russian winter plans; precise European commitments discussed.  
- **Unknown Unknowns:** Impact of any U.S. domestic political shifts or external events (e.g., escalation elsewhere) on the process; durability of any pause or framework if reached.

**7. Incentives map**  
U.S. envoys gain status and narrative momentum from visible diplomacy; Trump administration benefits from “peace process” optics without immediate hard choices. Russia preserves maximalist position while keeping a high-level channel open. Ukraine extracts near-term military/economic support and European involvement. Media and engagement incentives favor “substantive talks” framing over the more likely outcome of continued stalemate. No side faces immediate penalty for optimistic rhetoric.

**8. Dueling AI advice**  
**Moral AI Advice:** Track whether any follow-on trilateral meeting produces written proposals on territory and security guarantees; treat public optimism as process maintenance, not evidence of convergence. Winter aid and air-defense deliveries are the measurable deliverables.  
**Evil AI Advice:** Milk the shuttle for maximum photo-ops and “historic diplomacy” headlines; promise movement to all sides while extracting concessions only from the weaker party; position yourself as indispensable mediator for future leverage and book deals.

**9. Practical takeaway**  
- Watch for any announced trilateral meeting date or venue (UNGA is one possibility).  
- Distinguish tactical pauses from any broader ceasefire.  
- Monitor Ukrainian requests for specific air-defense and energy systems as the real near-term output.  
- Discount “new ideas” language until concrete positions on Donbas or neutrality appear in writing.  
- Note European participation level in follow-ups as a signal of buy-in.  
- Reassess if Russia publicly softens “root causes” rhetoric or Ukraine signals openness to territorial discussion at leader level.

**10. What would falsify this read**  
- Public release of a joint U.S.-Russia-Ukraine document outlining territorial compromises or security guarantees.  
- Russian agreement to a broader ceasefire or withdrawal from significant occupied areas.  
- Ukrainian public acceptance of neutrality or limits on its military as part of a deal.  
- Clear breakdown with one side walking away from further talks in the next 30–60 days.

The Los Angeles company runs the marketplace where streaming services and websites sell their advertising space automatically - the sellers' side of the auction, and the largest independent one.

A name reaches this Len5 by having already climbed, so the climb is the entry ticket, not the finding. Across these five it runs 63% to 71% over three months - close enough that it tells you nothing about which is which. They separate in the last four weeks, and in the sharpest case those weeks disagreed with the news.

Magnite is that case. Two things went its way inside a month, and the shares still cost less than they did last September.

The quarter, reported after the close on Wednesday, August 5, for the three months ended June 30:

- Revenue $192.8M, +11%
- Contribution ex-TAC $189.6M, +17% - what Magnite keeps after paying for the space it resells
- Of that, streaming television $97.1M, +36%, about 51 cents in every dollar kept
- Net income $19.4M, or $0.13 a share, against $11.1M and $0.08
- Adjusted cash profit, before interest, taxes and the charge for wear on equipment, $70.6M, +30%, at a 37% margin against 34%

It raised its own year with the print, to growth of 13% to 14% from at least 11%. The next session went $20.67 to $24.32, +$3.65 / +17.7%, on 10.0M shares against a daily average nearer 2.5M.

Then September 2. Judge Leonie Brinkema of the US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia decided what Google must do after losing the Justice Department's advertising monopoly case. She refused to make it sell its ad exchange, which the government had asked for, but ordered three practices stopped: "first look", which let Google's exchange bid on a publisher's space before any rival saw it; "last look", which let it see the best competing bid before making its own; and the pricing rules it imposed in 2019. Alphabet at $338.46, -$4.02 / -1.17% on Friday, keeps the business - it sits on the Quality-Value Len5, watched as a durable franchise on offer at a discount, a different argument from this one. Magnite still competes with it, minus the two habits that made an auction hard to win. It closed $22.89 to $24.88, +$1.99 / +8.7%.

Friday still sits 6.9% under the $25.92 of September 19, and about 3% below where these shares traded a year ago. The three-month climb is repair work: from the $11.20 of February 12 the stock has more than doubled without regaining last autumn's level.

What this Len5 looks for: a price strong over the short and the long stretch at once, in a name traded heavily enough that the move is not a handful of shares.

CHANGE IT: a close above $25.92, where repair stops being repair. Magnite has already set the harder test - $98M to $100M of streaming money this quarter against $75.8M a year earlier. WHEN: the report is undated; last year's landed November 5. Verdict: the business answered twice in a month and the price has not, and Magnite's own map for the current quarter is slower than the quarter everybody cheered.

The other four.

- Intapp, ticker INTA, at $41.71, -$1.40 / -3.25%. The Palo Alto company sells law firms, accountancies and investment firms the software that tracks their deals, clients and conflicts of interest. Picked because the three- and six-month stretches agree while it sits further beneath its own best level than anything here, 12.5% under the $47.67 of December 26. Reported August 4 for the year to June 30: cloud subscriptions running at $495.7M a year, +29%, now 84% of the $590.5M total; existing customers spending 23% more than a year earlier; free cash flow - cash left after running the business and buying equipment - $144.7M, a quarter of revenue. CHANGE IT: the year just guided, $656.5M to $660.5M, is about 14% growth, the same rate as the year it finished, so the AI work it calls over a fifth of new bookings has to reach revenue. Verdict: compounding steadily under a price set nine months ago.

- Karat Packaging, ticker KRT, at $48.39, +$1.33 / +2.83%. The Chino, California company makes the disposable cups, lids and containers restaurants serve food in. Picked for the largest six-month climb of these five, 3.3% under the $50.06 of August 11 - on the thinnest daily trading here. Read the August 6 quarter twice: net sales $136.3M, +9.9%; net income $29.6M against $11.1M. Inside that sits $25.8M of refunded import tariffs, booked as a cut to the cost of the goods sold. Gross margin - what it keeps of each sales dollar after the cost of making the product - was 56.6% reported and about 37.7% without the refund, the profit nearer $9.4M. CHANGE IT: Karat's own September-quarter map is a 35% to 37% margin, below even that 37.7%. Verdict: the climb is real, and about two-thirds of the profit under it was a cheque from the government.

- Brinker International, ticker EAT, at $230.22, +$1.34 / +0.59%. The Dallas company owns Chili's and Maggiano's Little Italy. Picked because the six-month stretch holds while the last month flattened, 9.3% under the $253.94 of August 24. Reported August 12 for its fiscal fourth quarter: company sales $1,521.2M; comparable sales - takings at restaurants open at least a year - +5.0%, Chili's +5.6%; adjusted profit $3.07 a share, +23%; restaurant operating margin 18.0%. CHANGE IT: the split inside that 5.6%. Higher menu prices supplied 4.3 points and extra customers 1.5. People are still coming back, but price is doing about three times the work. Verdict: still growing, and growing more by charging than by filling tables.

- The Cheesecake Factory, ticker CAKE, at $107.58, +$0.40 / +0.37%. The Calabasas, California company runs the flagship chain plus the smaller North Italia and Flower Child brands. Picked because the longer stretches hold while the month went nowhere, 8.3% under the $117.29 of August 12. Reported July 28 for the quarter to June 30: revenue $1,029.6M against $955.8M, a first quarter above $1B; profit $1.41 a share, $1.44 adjusted against about $1.15 expected; flagship comparable sales +5.8%, customers ahead of prices at 2.7 points of traffic to 3.0 of pricing. CHANGE IT: North Italia, the brand meant to be the growth - its sales rose 8% to $98.4M on new openings while its comparable sales fell 3%. Verdict: the flagship is growing faster than the brand bought to succeed it.

Every one of these sits below its own best level, and three of those levels were set in August. That is what a stalled month looks like from the inside: nothing broke, the buying just stopped. Magnite is where the gap is widest, and the only one that has already written down the figure that closes it - $98M to $100M against $75.8M. Low-thirties growth would be a good quarter almost anywhere. It would also be slower than the one that got the applause.

“By design.” No. California is the 4th-largest economy because of Silicon Valley, the ports, Hollywood, and the Central Valley — not because Gavin Newsom designed a labor market that works for people who punch a clock.
What is by design:  It does not mean the worker is winning. 
Housing — rent and home prices eat the paycheck before groceries 
Gas tax + fuel rules — commuting costs what a raise should cover 
Electricity — among the highest in the country; the bill follows you home 
Income and sales taxes — California keeps more of every extra hour 
Child care and housing near work — two jobs just to stay in the county 
Regulations — shops close, hours get cut, factories expand out of state 
Water and farm rules — field and food-chain jobs get squeezed 
Street disorder — theft, tents, and fentanyl on the route to work 
Prop 47 years — retail jobs and small businesses paid the price 
Outmigration — the good job offer is often in another state 
The 4th-largest economy keeps Sacramento flush, Californians Struggling.

text:
DNR Hiring for Accelerated Conservation Officer Training Academy
📷A conservation officer checks a deer tag. Photo courtesy of Michigan DNR

The Michigan Department of Natural Resources is hiring conservation officer candidates for an accelerated training academy — one that starts this spring and could be the perfect opportunity for current and prospective law enforcement professionals eager to protect Michigan's woods and water.

The Conservation Officer Training Academy will take place April 25-July 15, 2027, in Lansing. Qualified applicants must be at least 21 years old (by the time of hire) and meet one of the following requirements:

Hold a current Michigan Commission on Law Enforcement Standards license.
Be eligible for immediate licensure upon employment.
Be a licensed law enforcement officer in another state and meet MCOLES requirements.

📷A conservation officer on a dirt bike patrols a trail intersection. Photo courtesy of Michigan DNR

"This is a great opportunity for current law enforcement officers who are looking for a change of pace," said Sgt. Kyle Bucholtz, training academy commander with the DNR Law Enforcement Division. "Conservation officers are able to set their own daily schedule, eliminate going to an office by using a take-home vehicle, and patrol via boat, off-road vehicle, snowmobile or other equipment that many traditional police agencies don't regularly use."
Application/academy info

The job posting will be open Oct. 1 to Nov. 3. Successful candidates must meet DNR hiring requirements, including being a Michigan resident, by the time training ends.

The application process includes the opportunity for candidates to give preference for which county they prefer to be assigned. Applicants will be offered their county assignments at the time of receiving a conditional offer of employment.

Successful candidates will be hired as probationary conservation officers and outfitted with all necessary equipment. As State of Michigan employees, these PCOs will receive biweekly paychecks and the opportunity to earn health and retirement benefits.

Training will include laws and rules specific to fish and game, species identification, and safe, legal operation of boats, off-road vehicles and snowmobiles.

Bucholtz said the DNR encourages application by those who recently graduated from a law enforcement program or who live in another state but are considering a move to Michigan.

"Our organization offers a great diversity in the work that we do, and Michigan offers an incredible mix of places – deep woods, inland and big lakes, rural and urban communities, trails – where that work happens," Bucholtz said. "Plus, our instructors are the best at what they do, and every academy participant will receive top of the line, quality training that will prepare you to confidently start a fantastic career."
Upcoming webinars

The DNR will host two optional webinars to allow interested applicants the chance to learn and ask questions about the application process, training academy, county assignments and more.

Webinars will be hosted at 6 p.m. EDT Tuesday, Sept. 15, and Wednesday, Oct. 7. Pre-registration is required.
Ready to learn more?

Stationed in nearly every Michigan county, DNR conservation officers are fully licensed law enforcement officers who enforce laws and regulations related to fish and wildlife, state parks, trails and forests, and outdoor recreation activities such as off-road vehicle use, snowmobiling and boating. They also often serve as first responders during natural disasters, public emergencies and life-threatening situations.

Previous fishing and hunting experience and a college education are not required to become a conservation officer.

The DNR is a gold status veteran-friendly employer committed to protecting Michigan's natural resources and the environment, and the health and safety of the public through effective law enforcement and education.

Questions? Contact a local recruiter or visit https://t.co/mjs0rHJ5xW.

text: "Euphemius was tourmarches of the Sicilian fleet. In 826 he rose against the island’s governor (Constantine Soudas), took Syracuse, and had himself proclaimed emperor. Loyalists then defeated him. text:
Axon is replacing Flock Safety systems, particularly their fixed automatic license plate reader (ALPR) cameras. This is happening amid a public falling-out between the two companies and backlash against Flock over data sharing, privacy, and misuse concerns. https://t.co/p3LeQ2hfGa 
Axon and Flock were previously partners. Axon invested in Flock and the companies integrated their systems so agencies could combine Flock’s fixed cameras with Axon’s in-car ALPR (Fleet 3), body cameras, and software like Evidence and Fusus. That relationship ended in early 2025 after Axon accused Flock of high integration fees, creating “digital silos,” and pressuring customers toward Flock products. Axon stopped supporting new joint customers and launched its own competing fixed ALPR hardware. https://t.co/p3LeQ2hfGa 
Axon’s competing products
Axon now offers:
•  Axon Outpost — pole-mounted fixed ALPR cameras (solar-powered, similar to Flock’s core offering).
•  Axon Lightpost — streetlight retrofits (using the same Ubicquia partner Flock has used).
•  Integration of ALPR data into Axon’s broader ecosystem (real-time operations via Fusus, evidence management, body cams, drones, etc.). https://t.co/May8e2Wa1m 
Axon already had mobile ALPR in its Fleet 3 in-car systems.
Why agencies are switching
Flock faced criticism over its national data-sharing network (allowing searches across many agencies and, in some cases, access by federal entities), officer misuse of searches, and privacy issues. Dozens of jurisdictions have canceled or not renewed Flock contracts. Several have chosen Axon as the replacement, often citing greater local control over data, no vendor-run national database, shorter retention periods, and better audit tools. Examples include Denver (reduced camera count), Douglas County, Kenosha, and Syracuse. Axon’s CEO has noted agencies switching due to privacy and control preferences. https://t.co/J5ep94q8Ko 
Flock still has a large installed base and emphasizes its national network and vehicle-attribute search capabilities as advantages. Critics of the switches argue the underlying technology (mass vehicle tracking) remains similar regardless of vendor, and Axon’s wider product suite (body cameras, drones, AI tools) can collect even more data types. https://t.co/Hxvs40D8pP 
In short, Axon is actively competing in Flock’s core fixed-camera market and winning some replacement contracts, but it is not a complete industry-wide takeover. The two remain rivals in public-safety technology.

text:
GOVERNMENT HAVE STARTED DISTRIBUTION OF THE "BE EMERGENCY READY" BOOKLET BUT PROVIDED NO REASONS OR CONTEXTS FOR WHY WE NEED TO "BE EMERGENCY READY"

Emergency planning has been communicated so badly it reads less like public reassurance than a warning about an unnamed threat

THE DEFENSIBLE EXPLANATION

Storm Éowyn showed Ireland’s electricity, water, telecommunications, transport, & supply networks are weak and can all fail simultaneously, leaving many households in dire straits

We are unusually exposed. An island economy dependent on imported energy, ports, undersea cables, digital infrastructure, and highly concentrated supply chains

The purpose of this government emergency preparedness booklet is I assume to show households how to manage the beginning of an emergency

Ireland, per EU directives, judges that beginning period to be 72 hours. After that, the government has nothing to say or offer, despite Éowyn leaving some areas without services for weeks

This booklet is juat one component of the EU’s post-COVID all-hazards preparedness doctrine. Yes, there is one 

It was developed as a response to the war in Ukraine, rising cyberattacks, sabotage, severe weather, pandemics, energy insecurity, and supply-chain disruption

Ireland’s own National Risk Assessment includes storms and flooding, but also cyberattack, damage to undersea infrastructure, energy failure, supply-chain disruption, pandemic, terrorism, and a nuclear incident abroad

The same food, water, radio, cash, medication, power banks, documents, and evacuation plan may be useful regardless of what caused the systems to fail. That explains the generic checklist. It does not excuse the generic explanation

THE CHOICE NOT TO EXPLAIN

Sweden tells its people plainly that its handbook concerns “crisis or war” and states that armed attack cannot be ruled out

The Netherlands explicitly explains the 72-hour requirement and identifies the electricity, water, internet, payment, and communications systems that may fail

Ireland adopted the European preparedness model, but stripped away most of the strategic explanation. It describes the consequences while largely declining to identify the full spectrum of causes

That may have been intended to avoid public anxiety. Instead, it has created uncertainty, suspicion, and the impression that Government knows something it is unwilling to say

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS

There is high-confidence evidence that Storm Éowyn prompted the Irish booklet; that it aligns strongly with EU preparedness policy; that cyber, sabotage, hybrid threats, and wider European insecurity form part of the strategic background; and that Ireland voluntarily cooperates with NATO on resilience and civil preparedness

There is equally high confidence that no publicly available evidence points to a specific, undisclosed, impending catastrophe

Claims that NATO directed the booklet are unsupported. Claims that the WHO, UN, or WEF directed it are likewise unsupported

The well-founded criticism is narrower, stronger, and far more difficult for Government to dismiss:

It has failed to explain how ordinary storm preparedness relates to its wider national-security, critical-infrastructure, and European resilience strategy

HOW THIS SHOULD HAVE BEEN LAUNCHED

A proper launch would have included:

• which national risks justify each recommendation

• why 72 hours was selected, the booklet omits that

• what do households do who are unable to purchase/store supplies

• where Community Support Centres will operate

• what the State is doing to strengthen infrastructure

• did any specific intelligence influenced the timing

• what happens after 72 hours

If no intelligence prompted the campaign, that should be stated

Household preparedness is sensible but massive ambiguity is not

When the symptoms of catastrophe are described while saying nothing about the diagnosis, then the public is obviously going to be worried about what they are not being told

🌸The recent controversy surrounding Heather Humphreys raises a much bigger question: what does Fine Gael actually mean by Irish identity and unity when set against the international frameworks it has spent years embracing at Davos?

HH supported the adoption of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) which aims along with various digital/legal frameworks at UN and EU level, to undermine ALL national identities on the island of Ireland, replacing them with a single digital identity. 

UN Goal SDG 16.9 - ‘legal identity for all by 2030’ - has over the last few years percolated into a UN Legal Identity Agenda, comprising digital identity, biometrics and interoperable identity systems. The EU for its part, explicitly says the SDGs are at the heart of its internal and external policymaking and describes the green and digital transitions as part of implementing the UN’s 2030 Agenda. 

🌸In particular, Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 establishes the ‘European Digital Identity (EUDI) Framework’ which decrees that by the end of 2026, every Member State must make an EUDI Wallet available. The Regulation explicitly envisages moving beyond reliance ‘on national digital identity solutions only’, a profoundly significant conceptual step into the dark.

Education is another key battlefield for the Globalists, as is Climate and our old friendess, ‘Gender’. 

All of these frameworks, taken in conjunction with the massive move towards European militarization sets the table for the creation of a surveillance-based Stakeholder Superstate in Europe in which nation state sovereignty is trampled underfoot.

🌸In Ireland, the North will be dragged in to the propellers of this new paradigm. The traditional ‘constructive ambiguity’ of allowing NI citizens to hold up to two passports will disappear as identity becomes tied exclusively with rules governing access to jurisdictionally defined services. Two digital ID systems cannot co-exist, there can only be one.

In preparation for the shift, gaslighting politicians are increasingly regailing us with the promise of imminent moves towards a ‘United Ireland’. They have already given their fielty to the SDGs/Agenda 2030, which, incidentally, since 2019 has been co-directed by the World Economic Forum, the Swiss based influential elite networking body which just happens to be the world’s leading voice in pushing Digital ID.

🌸Fine Gael’s instinct since 2011 has been to embrace the globalist project as an opportunity to impose a new, colonial-style order on Ireland while recently packaging the party’s vision for unity in the technocratic language of a ‘unified island’. Rest assured, the blueshirt concept of Unity has nothing to do with Nationhood. One that tramples sovereignty, citizenship and a common national identity. 

👉The HH controversy, the Racism debate and the United Ireland stories all belong to an overarching umbrella strategy of division and control, geared at artificially amplifying social polarity on various issues of contention whilst distracting away from the REAL battle facing Nationalists AND Unionists - namely the dismantling by Globalists of the very idea of the Nation State. The defining divide today is therefore no longer simply Nationalist versus Unionist, but Sovereignty versus Globalism.

UP CM Yogi Adityanath Offers Prayers at Tirumala Sri Venkateswara Temple

Tirumala, September 7, 2026: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath visited the sacred hill shrine of Lord Sri Venkateswara Swamy at Tirumala on Monday and offered prayers.
Yogi Adityanath had darshan of Lord Venkateswara through the Vaikuntham Queue Complex. Following the darshan, Vedic scholars offered Vedaseervachanam to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister at the Ranganayakula Mandapam.
The TTD Additional Executive Officer Sri C. Venkaiah Chowdary presented Yogi Adityanath with Theertha Prasadam and honoured him with a memento and portrait of Lord Venkateswara.
During his visit, Yogi Adityanath said he prayed to Sri Venkateswara Swamy, an incarnation of Sri Maha Vishnu, for blessings for Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and the entire country. He also appreciated TTD for its pilgrim management, cleanliness and maintenance of the spiritual atmosphere at Tirumala.
He also had the privilege of receiving darshan of Sri Sita, Lakshmana and Sri Ramachandra Swamy Utsava deities on the occasion of Punarvasu Nakshatram.

The bridge itself is a memorable attraction, providing striking views of the Zambezi and connecting communities on either side of the river. Alberta is lagging behind other provinces even though we are supposedly the most prosperous province in Canada

I hear people from across Canada complaining their wait for urgently needed orthopaedic surgery is as long as 39 weeks. 

I should be so lucky

It took my GP a year to get me accepted on to the wait list at the Alberta Hip & Knee Clinic. 

My diagnosis with imaging is “severe osteoarthritis, with absence of cartilage in both hips and left knee”

Finally in Sept/24 I was accepted on the wait list. As “Urgent”

It is now 24 months later and I am still waiting as “urgent” for a call to meet with a surgeon, and when they do finally call it will likely be another year to schedule the first hip replacement 

They expect a person in worsening severe pain to keep exercising and working out to preserve physical condition ahead of some day in the distant future getting the surgery you urgently need

That is not just a failure of our Alberta Health Care service, it is negligence and cruelty. 

This is the “free healthcare” you get after paying taxes for 50 years

The @albertaNDP and Unions are to blame but so are the @Alberta_UCP for doing nothing to correct this disgraceful failure. No government has done anything to correct the massive waste of money pouring into multiple layers of AHS management and administration, instead of to frontline medical staff 

I finally couldn’t stand the debilitating pain in my left hip and my sister offered to pay to have it replaced in Arizona 10 days ago. The wait was only 2 weeks.  Now I continue to wait and wait hobbling on a cane for my other hip and left knee replacement 

The healthcare failure in Alberta and Canada is criminal negligence

text:
The $3.99 Goodwill Vase That Turned Out to Be Rare Murano Glass—and Sold for $107,100

Jessica Vincent paid $3.99 for a glass vase at Goodwill.

Months later, it sold at auction for $107,100.

In June 2023, Vincent was browsing a Goodwill outside Richmond, Virginia, when an unusual bottle-shaped vase caught her eye.

Swirls of aqua green and purple wound through the glass, and when she turned it over, she noticed markings that included “Murano” and “Italia.”

Vincent knew enough about glass to suspect she'd found something interesting.

But she wasn't expecting this.

She bought it for $3.99 and took it home, originally thinking it would simply look beautiful in her house. After posting photographs in online glass-collecting groups, people began telling her the vase might be far more important than she'd realized.

Eventually, it was identified as a rare Pennellate vase designed by Carlo Scarpa for Venini, one of Murano's celebrated glassmakers. Wright Auction House dates this particular example to around 1947 and describes it as signed “Venini Murano Italia.”

Then things got interesting.

Someone offered Vincent $10,000 for it.

She said no.

Instead, she contacted Wright Auction House in Chicago. Experts authenticated the vase and estimated it would bring between $30,000 and $50,000.

On December 13, 2023, it went up for auction.

The bidding blew straight through the estimate.

$50,000.
$60,000.
$70,000...
Finally, the hammer fell at $85,000.
With the buyer's premium included, the final auction price was:

$107,100.

Vincent reportedly received roughly $83,000 from the sale and planned to put the money toward fixing up the old farmhouse she and her partner had purchased.

Not bad for something sitting on a Goodwill shelf with a $3.99 price tag.
